title: Brock Purdy will soon be the NFL's all-time leader in career passer rating
summary: Brock Purdy will have the highest career passer rating in NFL history, just as soon as he has enough pass attempts to qualify for the record.
full_text: Brock Purdy will have the highest career passer rating in NFL history, just as soon as he has enough pass attempts to qualify for the record. Purdy's career passer rating of 105.4 is higher than the official record, which is Lamar Jackson's 102.7. But to qualify for the record, a quarterback needs 1,500 career passing attempts, and Purdy is currently just short, with 1,495 career pass attempts. So as soon as Purdy throws his fifth pass on Monday night against the Commanders, he'll have the record. Purdy's lead over Jackson is such that even if Purdy were to throw five straight interceptions to start Monday night's game, he'd still have the record: If Purdy throws five picks on his next five passes, his passer rating will fall to 103.7, which is better than Jackson's record. Passer rating is a fairly goofy statistic which the NFL adopted as its official method for ranking passers in 1973. Its weaknesses as a measurement for a quarterback's quality include overvaluing completion percentage, arbitrarily capping the maximum amount of credit a quarterback can get for a certain statistic, and ignoring important variables like first downs and sacks, not to mention the things beyond passing that a quarterback can do, good or bad, like running the ball or fumbling. Still, it's a statistic that roughly measures how good a passer a quarterback is, and in the history of the league, it measures Purdy as the best ever.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Joe Brady: James Cook's ball security has to improve or carries will decrease
summary: James Cook ran for 111 yards and two touchdowns against the Rams on Monday night, but a negative play almost became his lasting memory of the game.
full_text: James Cook ran for 111 yards and two touchdowns against the Rams on Monday night, but a negative play almost became his lasting memory of the game. Cook fumbled just outside the Rams' 20-yard-line a couple of minutes into overtime and the Rams recovered to give themselves a chance to win the game. Greg Rousseau blocked a field goal attempt, however, and the Bills were able to drive for a kick of their own. Tyler Bass made that kick and the Bills won 37-34, but head coach Joe Brady said on Tuesday that the outcome does not overshadow all that happened to get to that point. Cook's fumble was his second of the night, fourth of the season and his 11th dating back to the start of the 2025 season. He's also run for a league-high 2,153 yards over that span, but Brady made it clear that the ball has to stop squirting out of his hands. “He's doing so many good things running the football," Brady said. "I don't want to lose sight of how great he is running the ball right now. But putting the ball on the ground, it's negating all the positive. I have all the confidence in him. That's why I put him right back out there. But obviously, at some point there has to be consequences to when we're putting negative stuff out there .The conversations that we’re having ongoing, James knows it’s important. It's going to cost us football games. It almost cost us one. We can't confuse because we won the game that that's OK. It's got to improve or the carries are going to decrease." Brady noted that Josh Allen also threw an interception on Monday and said the team is generally "putting the ball in harm's way" too often. They got a painful lesson about how that can hurt a team's chances of winning in Denver during the playoffs last season and Brady would like to see his team avoid any similar outcomes in big moments this season.
author: Josh Alper

title: With Odell Beckham Jr. in Minnesota, Jauan Jennings could be traded
summary: The 49ers continue to have injury issues at the receiver position.
full_text: The 49ers continue to have injury issues at the receiver position. And the Vikings have a current surplus of receivers that includes a player who had spent his first five seasons with the 49ers. On Tuesday, Ian Rapoport of ESPNFL floated the possibility of Jauan Jennings being traded to the 49ers, in the coming days. It would not be a surprise. As we explained after the Vikings signed Odell Beckham Jr. last week, OBJ's arrival seemed to be a message to Jennings , who has two catches for nine yards in four 2026 appearances with two starts. As the Vikings enter their bye, it's a perfect time to assess the roster and to see if any moves can be made, either by adding a player or subtracting one. The Vikings seem to believe Beckham can still play, and the Vikings seem to be perplexed by Jennings's inability to contribute to the passing game. In lieu of simply cutting Jennings, there's a possible deal to be made that would get the Vikings something of value in exchange for the balance of his one-year contract, which included a $4.5 million signing bonus with a $1.63 million base salary and nearly $100,000 per game in active roster bonuses and incentives tied to playing time and receptions. If the 49ers are interested in bringing Jennings back, they could wait for the Vikings to potentially release him. But with Deebo Samuel joining the list of the substation's victims (again) with a hamstring injury, time could be of the essence for the 49ers. Or maybe Jennings gets the wakeup call, and it works. Either way, the clock is ticking. And continuing to hit the snooze button isn't a viable option.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jets worked out Matthew Judon
summary: Matthew Judon is trying to catch on elsewhere after the 49ers cut him from their practice squad this week.
full_text: Matthew Judon is trying to catch on elsewhere after the 49ers cut him from their practice squad this week. Judon had a workout with the Jets on Wednesday. The 34-year-old Judon was once among the best pass rushers in the NFL. He was a two-time Pro Bowler early in his career with the Ravens, and when he hit free agency the Patriots signed him to a four-year, $56 million contract and he made two more Pro Bowls in New England. But he suffered a torn bicep in 2023 and missed most of that season, and he has never been the same player since then. Judon played one game for the 49ers this year before they cut him. The Jets also worked out defensive ends Cam Sample and Quinton Bell, and running backs Ian Wheeler and Dante Miller
author: Michael David Smith

title: Drew Rosenhaus still claims a Tyreek Hill deal "could happen at any time"
summary: Rosenhaus comments on Hill's prospects, without addressing the potential impact of the pending NFL investigation.
full_text: Before a civil verdict was entered on Tuesday against free-agent receiver Tyreek Hill, his agent Drew Rosenhaus revisited the question of whether Hill will soon be joining an NFL team. " I think it’s very fluid ," Rosenhaus told Josh Moser of WVSN. "I think a deal could happen any time. We are looking for the right situation, the right contract, the right team, the right fit, the right approach from a medical standpoint. Tyreek's feeling really good health-wise. I did say last week I thought a deal could happen at any time. But in the NFL it really is day-to-day. So we are still working to find the right situation." What are the factors in finding the right situation? "Well, you know, when you sign with a team midseason you'd like to go to a winner," Rosenhaus said. "Number two, as a wide receiver, you'd like to go to a team that needs a wide receiver. Number three, you'd like to go to a team that's got a pretty good quarterback. And number four, Tyreek's gonna bring a lot of impact. We've got to get a fair contract. And that's always complex to negotiate in the middle of a season. "So kind of look at Tyreek as similar to guys that are traded midseason. Can really come in and help a team in the second half of the year. He can help a team advance to the next level." It's still not clear whether Hill has fully recovered from a serious knee injury that he suffered in September 2025, during the Week 4 Monday night game against the Jets. "I don't know that he's 100 percent today, but he's close and he'll get there really soon," Rosenhaus said. "But I think that's probably something you have to wait until he gets out in practices and gets with the team before saying he's 100 percent. But he really is right there." The clip posted online includes no discussion of the pending Personal Conduct Policy investigation, or the potential impact of the then-pending civil trial. With Hill found responsible for two counts of battery, it's a significant complication — both as to how the league will proceed (paid leave becomes a possibility immediately after he signs) and as to whether a team will want to accept the P.R. consequences of adding a player who has just been found liable by a jury for battery of his ex-wife, and ordered to pay her $500,000 in damages.
author: Mike Florio

title: Sean McVay on Alaric Jackson: "He has to consistently do a better job"
summary: On Monday, Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson sucker punched Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb.
full_text: ' On Monday, Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson sucker punched Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb. On Tuesday, the NFL suspended Jackson for two games. After the suspension was imposed, Rams coach Sean McVay addressed the expectations for Jackson. “It is very important to represent the things that we want to be about," McVay told reporters. "He has to consistently do a better job. I think each situation is its own separate entity. I think you want to be careful pigeonholing yourself into a one-size-fits-all. The league made their decision. I want to understand the totality of the situation. "I'm not condoning by any stretch of the imagination, but I want to gather all the information before I make comments. It certainly doesn't help us when we're missing a player of his caliber. He has to make more consistent decisions that are in alignment with being available and representing the things that we want to be about without a doubt." McVay also explained that David Quesenberry will replace Jackson during the suspension. McVay, who said he believes Jackson will appeal the decision, doesn't know what Chubb said to prompt the punch from Chubb. While Chubb's words won't excuse the reaction, California does have a "fighting words" law that prohibits certain comments that are " inherently likely to provoke an immediate reaction ." That would be relevant if the local authorities get involved in the situation. Frankly, they should. The game was over, for several minutes. Jackson's pads were off. He returned to the field for the conversation that led to the altercation. If the situation had unfolded elsewhere and in the presence of a police officer, Jackson would have been (or at least should have been) immediately arrested. In this case, the evidence is on video. Why shouldn't Jackson be charged with battery? Anyone else who sucker punched someone in a public place would be, or at least should be.
author: Mike Florio

title: Dan Campbell says pass protection shows why Jahmyr Gibbs is different from other backs
summary: Gibbs made the key block on a touchdown pass from Jared Goff to Sam LaPorta on Sunday.
full_text: Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs set the NFL record for most touchdowns before turning 25 on Sunday. But Lions coach Dan Campbell says it was a teammate's touchdown that showed what a special player Gibbs is. On a fourth-and-1 touchdown pass from Jared Goff to Sam LaPorta, Gibbs made the key block in pass protection that gave Goff time to pass. Campbell said after watching the film he sought Gibbs out to praise his blocking on that play. "I hit him up this morning," Campbell said. "I said, one of my favorite clips of everything you did — he had a ton of eye-opening plays — was his his protection route on the fourth-and-1, LaPorta's touchdown. That was outstanding. To me, that's why he's different. All this other stuff, of course he's got that and it's rare. It's that. He's unselfish and he's tough and he's willing to do anything for his teammates. And he might as well have scored on that because he's as excited as anybody is that he helped get LaPorta a touchdown and protect Goff so he could make that throw. That's unselfishness." Gibbs ran for 151 yards and caught five passes for 56 yards against the Cardinals, and he's currently leading the NFL with 747 yards from scrimmage and nine touchdowns. But Gibbs makes highlight-reel plays even when he doesn't have the ball in his hands.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Bo Nix: Playing good and playing bad, it’s a narrative and something made up
summary: Bo Nix dismisses the numbers.
full_text: ' Bo Nix dismisses the numbers. The Broncos' quarterback seemingly has had a pedestrian season so far. His numbers are down from 2025 in completion percentage (64.3 to 59.9), yards per attempt (6.4 to 5.8) and passer rating (87.8 to 80.8). The Broncos rank 30th in total offense after being 10th last season. Nix, though, doesn't see it that way. “Playing good and playing bad, it’s a narrative, and I think it’s honestly kind of something we make up,” Nix said after Tuesday’s practice, via Chris Tomasson of The Denver Gazette . “I don’t think necessarily I’m playing any different than what I’m normally playing.” Nix was only 16-of-27 for 123 yards with a touchdown in Sunday's 23-17 win over the Chargers. He had only one completion longer than 16 yards. Nix, though, looks at the positive. “We’re sitting here at 3-2 and having a good start to our season,” Nix said. “There’s things we want to clean up. There’s things we want to fix. We’re leaving some things out there on the field but we’re finding ways to win like we did last year [during a 14-3 season]. I feel strongly that we’re going to continue to do that.”
author: Charean Williams

title: Sean McVay gives special teams coach Bubba Ventrone vote of confidence
summary: The Rams' special teams miscues cost kicker Harrison Mevis his job.
full_text: ' The Rams' special teams miscues cost kicker Harrison Mevis his job. It won't cost special teams coach Bubba Ventrone his. Rams head coach Sean McVay said Tuesday that Ventrone's job is safe. “I have a lot of confidence in Bubba Ventrone," McVay said, via NFL.com. "There’s no changes that are gonna be made there. We’re gonna keep working. This isn’t the first time that we’ve had adversity and the first time that we’ve had some different things that I have to do a better job of.” The Rams fired special teams coordinator Chase Blackburn in December after a series of blunders by the unit in a 38-37 overtime loss to the Seahawks. Assistant special teams coach Ben Kotwica finished the season as the interim coordinator, but the Rams muffed a punt in the NFC Championship Game. The Rams hired Ventrone in January. He was the assistant head coach and special teams coordinator for three seasons on Cleveland’s staff. He has also coached for the Colts and Patriots since concluding a playing career that saw him spend time with the 49ers, Browns and Patriots. Ventrone inherited Mevis, who went 12-of-13 on field goals and made all his extra points last season. Mevis missed two field goals in the Rams' 37-34 overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night. He was wide left on a 50-yard try on the Rams' first possession and had a 48-yard, game-winning attempt blocked by Greg Rousseau in overtime. Mevis had missed four of nine attempts this season. The Rams signed kicker Blake Grupe off the Jets' practice squad on Tuesday.
author: Charean Williams

title: Joe Brady wishes he'd taken two knees before Monday night's game-winning field goal
summary: Week 5 included plenty of examples of how not to best manage the clock in late-game situations.
full_text: Week 5 included plenty of examples of how not to best manage the clock in late-game situations. Most of the coaches who learned lessons did so the hard way, by losing their games. Bills coach Joe Brady learned a lesson while still winning. In a Tuesday session with reporters, Brady expressed regret for attempting the game-winning 45-yard field goal on second down, with two minutes left in overtime. "I didn't want to run two QB sneaks with the fall process of, again, getting — putting the ball in harm's way, taking some shots on Josh, just to get — we knew we were already in line," Brady said. "So it's like, hey, do I just, hey, center the ball and just take two knees? You know, you go back two yards, but you don't give them, you know, they end up worse if you miss. They get 45 seconds to, you know, to go 20 yards for the field goal. Big difference in two-minute, and, you know, the 45-yard field goal and a 47-yard field goal percentages, you should still be good to go, right? "And, you know, so if I had that opportunity again — look, I was convicted about it. You know, [Tyler Bass] was good to go. The conversation we had in the huddle and upstairs was like, 'Let's just go win the game right now.' But, you know, to not give them that shot again, if we do miss, the best thing would be is to take two knees and say, 'Hey, the 45 and the 47 is not of big difference.' Be a completely different story if the ball was a little further back. I'd be no indecision on taking knees if we were a little closer. We were just in that. It is a long field goal. We had just missed an extra point, but had the confidence in [Bass], but that's when I do wish I probably took two knees, and then we kicked the game winner. And if anything, they'd have 45 seconds and not two minutes." Plenty of Bills fans would surely prefer a 45-yard field goal try to a 47-yard field goal attempt. For obvious reasons . Regardless, the thought process is another example of the decisions coaches need to make in real time, with the clock ticking. If the kick had missed from 47, the Rams would have had less than 40 seconds to gain enough ground to try another potential game-winner. A miss from 45 would have given the Rams triple that amount of time.
author: Mike Florio

title: Chargers agree to terms with QB Jake Browning
summary: With Trey Lance on injured reserve with a groin injury, the Chargers needed quarterback help.
full_text: '' With Trey Lance on injured reserve with a groin injury, the Chargers needed quarterback help. They worked out quarterbacks Jake Browning and Kyle Trask, along with cornerback Jalyn Armour-Davis, wide receiver Ronnie Bell, wide receiver Luke Grimm, wide receiver Chris Hilton, wide receiver Tejhaun Palmer and wide receiver JuJu Smith-Schuster. They signed Grimm to the practice squad, and Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports that the team has come to terms with Browning. It is unclear whether Browning is signing with the practice squad or the active roster. Justin Herbert and DJ Uiagalelei are the only quarterbacks on the 53-player roster. Browning, 30, was with the Bengals the past four seasons before joining the Bucs in free agency this offseason. Tampa Bay cut him out of the preseason. He has appeared in 17 games with 10 starts and has completed 68.5 percent of his passes for 2,707 yards with 18 touchdowns and 15 interceptions.
author: Charean Williams

title: James Thrash upholds Dre Greenlaw suspension for head-butting incident
summary: The 49ers won't have linebacker Dre Greenlaw for Monday night's game against the Commanders.
full_text: The 49ers won't have linebacker Dre Greenlaw for Monday night's game against the Commanders. The NFL has announced that hearing officer James Thrash, a former NFL receiver, has upheld the one-game suspension imposed Monday on Greenlaw. During the second quarter of Sunday's game between the 49ers and Seahawks, Greenlaw applied a head butt to Seahawks linebacker Ernest Jones IV. Greenlaw was wearing a helmet; Jones was not. Greenlaw was ejected. It was his third ejection since 2022. Last year, he was suspended for one game for his behavior toward referee Brad Allen after a game between the Giants and Broncos, Greenlaw's team in 2025. Greenlaw will forfeit $136,388 in base salary for the game. He'll also lose a $23,529 active roster bonus. The 49ers could be able to seek partial repayment of his $2.5 million signing bonus, too. The lost reps also will make it harder for Greenlaw to earn a $750,000 incentive based on 75-percent playing time for the season. If earned, the amount doubles if the 49ers make the playoffs.
author: Mike Florio

title: NFL has been "monitoring developments" in Tyreek Hill case
summary: On Tuesday, a jury entered a mixed verdict in the civil lawsuit filed against free-agent receiver Tyreek Hill by his former wife, Keeta Vaccaro.
full_text: On Tuesday, a jury entered a mixed verdict in the civil lawsuit filed against free-agent receiver Tyreek Hill by his former wife, Keeta Vaccaro. The verdict comes at a time when the NFL is investigating Hill for the allegations Vaccaro has made. "We have been monitoring developments in the matter which remains under review of the personal conduct policy," an NFL spokesperson told PFT on Tuesday night, after the verdict was returned. The civil verdict is not binding on the league, as to either the counts on which he lost or the counts on which he won. The NFL's investigation is independent of that process. The key question is whether Vaccaro will cooperate with the NFL. It has no power to issue subpoenas; if, for example, the verdict leads to a prompt settlement, a confidentiality provision could prevent her from talking to NFL investigators. Regardless, the verdict becomes evidence that the NFL could utilize, along with the transcript of Vaccaro's sworn testimony. It's unclear when the NFL's investigation will conclude, or whether the civil verdict would prompt the league to place Hill on paid leave as the investigation proceeds.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jury returns mixed verdict in Tyreek Hill civil battery case, awards $500,000 to ex-wife
summary: Hill lost on two counts, won as to the rest.
full_text: The civil lawsuit brought by Tyreek Hill's ex-wife alleging multiple counts of battery and related legal claims has resulted in a verdict. Via Diana Moskovitz of Defector Media , the jury found Hill responsible for two counts of battery . He was found not responsible on the remaining counts. The jury awarded Keeta Vaccaro $500,000 in compensatory damages. The jury did not enter an award of punitive damages. The jury's decision not to award punitive damages is curious. Battery is an intentional tort. In Florida, however, the law requires " clear and convincing evidence " of intentional misconduct. It's possible, in theory, that the jury found evidence of battery under the lower "preponderance of the evidence" standard but not "clear and convincing" proof, which is a higher bar. The outcome becomes relevant to the NFL's ongoing Personal Conduct Policy review arising from the allegations Vaccaro initially made against Hill in a divorce filing. The findings represent a neutral determination that Hill more likely than not committed battery, twice. However, the Personal Conduct Policy does not automatically subject a player to discipline based solely on a civil verdict; the league will still need to perform its own investigation and reach a conclusion through the collectively-bargained process. Regardless, the finding of two instances of civil battery, plus a $500,000 verdict, could cause one or more potentially interested teams to refrain from pursuing him. Especially since the league could still find that Hill violated the policy as to the two incidents on which Hill lost — and all incidents on which he prevailed.
author: Mike Florio

title: It's official: Rams LT Alaric Jackson suspended two games
summary: The NFL has made the two-game suspension of Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson official.
full_text: ' The NFL has made the two-game suspension of Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson official. Jackson is set to miss games against the Cardinals and Raiders. He can appeal, with either Derrick Brooks, Jordy Nelson, Ron Rivera or James Thrash hearing Jackson's appeal and rendering a decision. Jackson threw a right hook to Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb after the Rams’ 37-34 overtime loss on Monday night. ESPN’s cameras caught Jackson exchanging jerseys with Bills defensive lineman Deone Walker at midfield when Chubb appeared to say something to Jackson. Jackson punched Chubb in the face with his right hand before Rams tight end Colby Parkinson pulled Jackson away. Chubb called it “just emotions” after the game. Jackson has started all five games this season and missed only one game last season.
author: Charean Williams

title: DE Sai'vion Jones estimated as full participant, the only change to the Broncos' report
summary: The Broncos had another walkthrough Tuesday as they get ready for their Thursday night gamea against the Seahawks.
full_text: ' The Broncos had another walkthrough Tuesday as they get ready for their Thursday night gamea against the Seahawks. They had only one change to the report from Monday, estimating defensive end Sai'vion Jones (shoulder) as a full participant. Cornerback Riley Moss (ribs) was again listed as limited participant. He did not play Sunday against the Chargers but appears on track for a return this week. Safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) and cornerback Pat Surtain II (ankle) were both listed as non-participants a second consecutive day. Hufanga exited Sunday's game, while Surtain did not play after his injury in Week 4. Safety Brandon Jones (foot) and guard Ben Powers (biceps) were estimated as full participants.
author: Charean Williams

title: Saints waive CB Jayden Price, sign CB Decamerion Richardson
summary: The Saints waived cornerback Jayden Price two days after he fumbled the opening kickoff in the second half against the Vikings.
full_text: The Saints waived cornerback Jayden Price two days after he fumbled the opening kickoff in the second half against the Vikings. He made three tackles in five games, playing 112 special teams snaps. The Saints also cut undrafted rookie Brock Rechsteiner, who was on the reserve/suspended list and never played. Rechsteiner, the son of WWE Hall of Famer Scott Steiner, was suspended six games by the NFL. The team terminated the contract of long snapper Cal Adomitis, and it re-signed cornerback Decamerion Richardson. Richardson, a fourth-round pick of the Raiders in 2024, originally joined the Saints off waivers from Las Vegas. He played two games for the Saints and totaled one special teams tackle. The Saints also cut running back Ulysses Bentley and wide receiver Trey Palmer from the practice squad.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jaxson Smith-Njigba, Leonard Williams listed as limited practice participants again on Tuesday
summary: The Seahawks released another estimated practice report on Tuesday and it didn't feature a change in status for wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba or defensive tackle Leonard Williams.
full_text: The Seahawks released another estimated practice report on Tuesday and it didn't feature a change in status for wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba or defensive tackle Leonard Williams. Both players were listed as limited participants due to ankle injuries for the second straight day. The Seahawks will release injury designations for Thursday's game against the Broncos on Wednesday. The only change from Monday's report was guard Beau Stephens (shoulder) moving from limited to full practice participation. Linebackers Chazz Surratt (calf) and Drake Thomas (ankle) were listed as out of practice. Running back Zach Charbonnet (knee) and quarterback Drew Lock (right forearm) remained in the limited category while wide receiver Irv Charles (knee) and running back George Holani (ribs, knee) were listed as full participants.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bears activate DE Shemar Turner from PUP
summary: The Bears activated defensive lineman Shemar Turner off the reserve/physically unable to perform list, the team announced Tuesday.
full_text: The Bears activated defensive lineman Shemar Turner off the reserve/physically unable to perform list, the team announced Tuesday. His 21-day return-to-practice window was set to expire Wednesday. Turner's return is perfect timing for the Bears with starting defensive end Montez Sweat suspended for two games for violating the NFL's policy on performance-enhancing substances. Turner will take Sweat's spot on the 53-player roster. Turner, a second-round pick in 2025, tore the ACL in his right knee last season. He had moved from defensive tackle to defensive end in the Week 5 off week last season. In five games as a rookie, he totaled six tackles, including two for loss.
author: Charean Williams

title: Chiefs put WR Tyquan Thornton on IR, sign LB Cam Jones to active roster
summary: The Chiefs did not replace Tyquan Thornton on the active roster with another wide receiver.
full_text: ' The Chiefs did not replace Tyquan Thornton on the active roster with another wide receiver. Thornton was placed on injured reserve Tuesday due to the dislocated ankle he suffered in Week 4. He'll have surgery on the ankle and is expected to be sidelined for 3-4 months. Linebacker Cam Jones was signed off of the practice squad in a corresponding move. Jones signed with the Chiefs over the summer and joined the practice squad after being part of the team's final cuts. Jones played 38 regular season and playoff games for the Chiefs in 2023 and 2024. He played in 10 games for the Jets last season and has 43 total tackles. The Chiefs also confirmed that they have signed wide receiver Justin Watson to the practice squad. Watson and Jones were teammates during Jones's time with the team and Watson spent three seasons with the Chiefs before moving on to the Texans last year.
author: Josh Alper

title: Giants sign LB Malik Harrison to active roster
summary: The Giants elevated linebacker Malik Harrison from the practice squad three times in the first five weeks of the season and they made a more permanent move with him on Tuesday.
full_text: The Giants elevated linebacker Malik Harrison from the practice squad three times in the first five weeks of the season and they made a more permanent move with him on Tuesday. They announced that they have signed Harrison to the 53-man roster. Linebacker Dawuane Smoot took Harrison's spot on the practice squad. Harrison had two tackles in the season opener against the Colts and he recovered a fumble in the team's Week 3 win over the Titans. The 2020 third-round pick has also played in 76 games for the Ravens and 11 games for the Steelers. Smoot worked out for the Giants on Monday. He has 27 sacks in 127 career games.
author: Josh Alper

title: Micah Parsons: "Jayden Daniels probably cost Dan Quinn his job"
summary: Packers LB minces no words about QB's role in clock disaster.
full_text: Micah Parsons still isn't ready to play after last year's knee injury, but he still knows how to mix things up. Parsons recently said on his podcast, The Edge with Micah Parsons , that quarterback Jayden Daniels is to blame for the game-clock clusterfudge at the end of overtime in the Giants-Commanders game. "Jayden Daniels probably cost my man Dan Quinn his job , to be honest with you," Parsons said, via Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic . "To be honest with you. And, like, I'm a big Jayden Daniels fan. But the reality is, he probably cost a lot of people their jobs this past weekend. . . . "All respectfully, we get coached so much on these situations that, like, I'm a defensive player, and this shit's programmed to me. I even know what to do in those situations. There's no way I'm taking a sack with 14 seconds left and no timeouts. . . . And, mind you, it'd be different if Jayden Daniels was a rookie. This is your third year. This is your third year. You've been to the NFC Championship game. You've been in big moments before. And to me, like even after a sack, you're casually getting up." Parsons made it clear that, in his view, quarterbacks are expected to always know what's going on. "This is your job, bro," Parsons said. "This is your job to be prepared to understand the game and understand situations. That's in your job profile. And you're telling me, 'Oh, we're gonna want to pay this guy eventually $60 million? This cannot happen. . . . I'm a big JD5 fan, but that's inexcusable, bro." Parsons said that the Packers work on situational football "every day," What happened at the end of the Giants-Commanders game should have required no discussion, frankly. "This is a lack of preparation, a lack of mentality, and a lack of urgency," Parsons said. "That just can't happen." Parsons isn't wrong. The fact that it did happen raises plenty of questions about the level of preparation and attention to detail, as created by the coaching staff. It speaks to potential cultural flaws, perhaps one in which Daniels hasn't been challenged or held as accountable as he could have or should have been, given his standing in the organization. It would be a lot easier to make sense of all of this if the Commanders had recorded and preserved the relevant communications. And Daniels surely will face even more questions on this topic the next time he speaks to reporters. The fact that the outcome was so bizarre, so jarring, and so downright surreal becomes a horrible moment for everyone involved. As to the ultimate consequences, Parsons hit the nail on the head — Daniels's failure to take charge of the situation in the moment will probably cost Quinn his job. But Daniels will continue to be the starting quarterback because, even if he made an inexcusable mistake as to one of the easiest parts of the job, he does the hard parts better than most of his peers.
author: Mike Florio

title: Saints owner Gayle Benson: I won't accept this level of play as our standard
summary: Seats are starting to heat up in New Orleans.
full_text: Seats are starting to heat up in New Orleans. The Saints lost to the Vikings in Week 5 to fall to 1-4 on the season. The last three losses came in a row and all three came at the Superdome, including a Monday night drubbing at the hands of the Vikings on a night when the Saints celebrated the 20th anniversary of their post-Katrina return to the stadium. On Tuesday, owner Gayle Benson said that loss "truly disappointed me" during a speech at the Greater New Orleans Quarterback Club Luncheon that left no doubt about how disappointed she is with the team's performance in general. Benson said fans "are right to expect more than we have delivered" through the first five weeks of the season. “As the owner, the responsibility does start with me,” Benson said, via Rod Walker of NOLA.com. “I will not make excuses and I will not accept this level of performance as our standard. I am committed to making the decisions necessary to improving this team. Everyone on this organization understands the urgency. We must prepare better, execute consistently and correct mistakes that are costing us the games.” Benson didn't issue any ultimatums about a more acceptable standard of play, but she did vow to hold people accountable if the Saints are not able to right their ship in the coming weeks. “Kellen Moore and his coaches are responsible for preparing our players to perform," Benson said. "Mickey Loomis and our football staff are responsible for building a roster capable of sustained success. The players are responsible for their preparation and execution. I am responsible for holding this organization accountable.” Moore is in his second season as the head coach while Loomis has been the General Manager since 2002. The Saints are 7-15 since Moore was hired in 2025 and it sounds like that record will need to get a lot better in order for anyone to feel secure about returning in 2027.
author: Josh Alper

title: NFL is expected to suspend Rams LT Alaric Jackson two games for postgame punch
summary: Jackson punched Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb in the face on the field after the Rams' 37-34 overtime loss Monday night.
full_text: ' The NFL is expected to suspend Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson for two games for a postgame punch Monday night. But Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that the league has yet to notify the team and the NFLPA. Jackson threw a right hook to Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb after the Rams' 37-34 overtime loss. Jackson will miss games against the Cardinals and Raiders unless he appeals and wins. ESPN's cameras caught Jackson exchanging jerseys with Bills defensive lineman Deone Walker at midfield when Chubb appeared to say something to Jackson. Jackson punched Chubb in the face with his right hand before Rams tight end Colby Parkinson pulled Jackson away. Chubb called it "just emotions" after the game. Jackson has started all five games this season and missed only one game last season.
author: Charean Williams

title: Browns place Raheim Sanders on IR, sign Audric Estime off Vikings practice squad
summary: The Browns have made a couple of moves at running back and on the practice squad.
full_text: The Browns have made a couple of moves at running back and on the practice squad. Cleveland announced the club has placed running back Raheim Sanders (hip) on injured reserve. As a corresponding move, the club has signed running back Audric Estime to the 53-man roster off of Minnesota’s practice squad. Sanders was injured in Sunday’s loss to the Jets. He served as the primary kick returner for Cleveland, averaging 29.3 yards per return. Estime appeared in seven games with one start for New Orleans last year, rushing for 198 yards with a touchdown. He caught 12 passes for 103 yards. He previously appeared in 13 games for Denver in 2024. Additionally, Cleveland signed tight end Devin Culp and guard Vershon Lee to the practice squad and released cornerback Myles Bryant and receiver James Proche II from the practice squad.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Dolphins claim WR Jared Wayne off of waivers
summary: The Dolphins are making a change at wide receiver during their bye week.
full_text: The Dolphins are making a change at wide receiver during their bye week. They announced that they have claimed Jared Wayne off of waivers from the Texans. Ryan Miller was waived to create room for Wayne on the roster in Miami. Wayne played in all five Texans games this season, but was the odd man out after the team acquired Marvin Harrison Jr. in a trade with the Cardinals. He had four catches for 65 yards and also saw time on special teams while with Houston. Wayne played in four games for the Texans over the previous two seasons. He had two catches for 20 yards in those contests. The Dolphins also announced that they have signed defensive lineman Jordan Jefferson to the practice squad and that they have released defensive lineman Mazi Smith in a corresponding move.
author: Josh Alper

title: Seahawks activate WR Irv Charles
summary: The Seahawks will have wide receiver Irv Charles available for Thursday night's game against the Broncos.
full_text: '' The Seahawks will have wide receiver Irv Charles available for Thursday night's game against the Broncos. Charles was activated from injured reserve on Tuesday afternoon. Running back Velus Jones was released in a corresponding move. Charles went on injured reserve in order to continue working his way back from last season's torn ACL. Charles was playing for the Jets when he was injured and he was traded to the Seahawks for a conditional 2028 draft pick this offseason. Charles mostly played special teams for the Jets and had 14 tackles in 25 games for the AFC East club. Jones had two tackles and two kickoff returns in four appearances this season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jaguars put Anton Harrison on injured reserve
summary: A report on Tuesday morning said Jaguars left tackle Anton Harrison is headed for arthroscopic knee surgery and that his timeline for return won't be known until the operation takes place.
full_text: A report on Tuesday morning said Jaguars left tackle Anton Harrison is headed for arthroscopic knee surgery and that his timeline for return won't be known until the operation takes place. The Jaguars revealed on Tuesday afternoon he'll be out at least four games regardless of what's determined during surgery. Harrison was placed on injured reserve and that could be where he spends the rest of the season. Per Tuesday's report, one of the potential outcomes is that Harrison misses the rest of the season. Walker Little is set to replace Harrison against the Texans in London this week. The Jaguars have a bye in Week 7 and then face the Colts, Ravens and Titans. Jacksonville filled Harrison's roster spot with the previously reported signing safety Kaevon Merriweather off of their practice squad. They also announced that they have signed long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer to the practice squad. Ross Matiscik was forced out of last Sunday's game with a shoulder injury and defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton was pressed into service in that role.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bears' Montez Sweat suspended two games for performance-enhancing substance violation
summary: The Bears will be without starting defensive end Montez Sweat for the next two games.
full_text: The Bears will be without starting defensive end Montez Sweat for the next two games. The NFL announced today that Sweat is suspended without pay for two games for violating the NFL policy on performance-enhancing substances. Although the NFL does not disclose the specific reason when a player is suspended for a violation, a two-game suspension is typically the penalty for a first offense of a player testing positive for a stimulant, diuretic or masking agent. Players who test positive for anabolic steroids are typically suspended at least six games. Sweat will miss Sunday's game against the Falcons and the following Thursday night game against the Patriots. He will then be eligible to return Week 8 against the Seahawks on Monday Night Football. The 30-year-old Sweat, who arrived in a Chicago via trade from Washington during the 2023 season, has started all five games and played 69 percent of the Bears' defensive snaps this season. He has two sacks.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Prisco's Week 6 NFL picks: Seahawks over Broncos on Thursday night, Buccaneers upset Steelers
summary: Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 6 picks, including the Packers over the Cowboys on 'Sunday Night Football'
full_text:
After a horror show in Week 4 with my NFL picks , I got back on track in a big way this past week. I was 10-4-1 straight up and 9-6-1 against the spread. That brings my season record straight up to 48-30-1 and the ATS record to 34-43-2.
The ATS mark will be a slow climb to get back above .500 after that really bad Week 3. But I felt good about the picks this week.
Time to build some momentum. Two good weeks in a row?
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
The Seahawks lost a tough one to the 49ers last week and now face a short week on the road against Denver. The Broncos ' offense has struggled, even with Sean Payton taking over as the play-caller. Bo Nix has to pick it up, but this is a tough defense to try and fix things. Seattle takes a tough road game.
Pick: Seahawks 23, Broncos 17
The Jaguars will have been in London for two weeks, which makes this a challenge for the Texans , who went this week. Houston won for the first time on the road last week and now their division chances probably rest on this game. The Jaguars were sloppy last week, which will get them back focused. Jaguars will win a tight one.
Pick: Jaguars 24, Texans 20
The Bears are off a horrible showing in Green Bay, in which the defense was shredded. But the Falcons lost in overtime to the Ravens and quarterback Michael Penix was hurt. He will likely play here, and that's a good thing since he can light up the Chicago defense. Falcons win it.
Pick: Falcons 27, Bears 21
There is a chance that Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will be back for this game after missing last week with an ankle injury. Even if he isn't, I think the Ravens defense will be up to the task of slowing down the Browns offense. If Jackson is back, the Ravens offense will move the ball.
Pick: Ravens 24, Browns 13
The winless Titans head out on the road to play a Colts team that has been inconsistent. The Colts' defense has improved in recent weeks, which will challenge Cam Ward and the Titans' limited offense. Look for the Colts to get a division victory as Jonathan Taylor has a big game.
The Patriots have turned their season around with consecutive victories as Drake Maye has come alive. The Jets played better on defense against Cleveland last week with eight sacks, but this is a bigger challenge. Look for Maye to keep it going as the Pats win a third straight.
Pick: Patriots 28, Jets 13
The Saints have lost three straight and have fallen to 1-4. They didn't play well against the Vikings last week, but this is a chance to get right. The Giants tied last week, but Jameis Winston played well. I think this will be about defenses. Giants in a close one.
Pick: Giants 19, Saints 16
The Panthers are off a bye, while the Eagles are off a trip to London where they lost in brutal fashion to the Jaguars. This is desperation time for the Eagles, but the injuries have piled up. Somehow, though, they will get off the deck to win this behind their defense.
Pick: Eagles 23, Panthers 20
Both of these teams righted the ship a bit with victories last week. The Bucs badly needed it after losing their first four. Tampa Bay ran it with Bucky Irving to beat the Cowboys and I think they can do that here as well. The defense played better in that game and will limit Aaron Rodgers somewhat. Bucs win it.
Pick: Bucs 26, Steelers 21
The "Dream Team" Rams are 2-3 and haven't looked the part of a Super Bowl champ. The offense got it going against the Bills , but the defense was a non-factor in the fourth quarter and overtime. They will play better here against the Cardinals . Meanwhile, Matt Stafford will have a big day.
Pick: Rams 35, Cardinals 20
The Chargers limp into this one at 0-5, while the Chiefs are undefeated off a bye. The Chargers are desperate and need a win or their season will be over. This is not a good place to try to get that first victory. Look for Patrick Mahomes to play well. Chiefs coach Andy Reid is outstanding in his career off a bye.
Pick: Chiefs 28, Chargers 21
The Bills are playing consecutive road games, but they stayed on the West Coast after beating the Rams in overtime Monday night. That was a tough, physical game, which will make it a challenge on a short week. The Raiders were awful against the Pats, but they will play better on offense here. They just won't stop the Bills.
Pick: Bills 35, Raiders 21
The Packers blew out the Bears Sunday as Jordan Love lit up the skies. Look for more of that in this one against a bad Dallas secondary. The Cowboys struggled on defense against the Bucs, and that will continue in this one. Love continues to play well. Packers win a shootout.
Pick: Packers 31, Cowboys 27
This is a long road trip for the Commanders off a brutal tie last week to face the league's best team right now. That's a tough combination. They can only hope for a letdown by the 49ers after they beat Seattle last week. It won't happen. The 49ers continue to roll as Brock Purdy continues to make a claim as a legitimate MVP candidate.
Pick: 49ers 30, Commanders 21
author: Pete Prisco

title: Bills' Joe Brady threatens playing time 'consequences' for James Cook III over fumble issues
summary: Cook coughed the ball up twice against the Rams in Week 5 and has four fumbles on the year
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills defeated the Los Angeles Rams in overtime to conclude Week 5, but they escaped a close call that could have been avoided if their star running back took better care of the football. James Cook III fumbled twice in the 37-34 victory, and the second nearly cost the Bills the game. His ball security issues are an ongoing issue and one that seems to be wearing on coach Joe Brady, who threatened to reduce Cook's playing time if they persist.
The second of Cook's fumbles on Monday came on the opening possession of overtime. The Bills were within field goal range and threatening to begin the extra period with a touchdown after a 57-yard completion from Josh Allen to Khalil Shakir . On the ensuing play, Cook ran up the middle and lost the ball when Rams linebacker Nate Landman punched it loose and Aaron Donald fell on it.
All Los Angeles needed to win at that point was a field goal, but a blocked 48-yarder kept the Bills alive and led to an eventual game-winning field goal of their own.
Cook's fumble marked the second of two Buffalo turnovers, as Allen previously threw an interception.
"Right now, we're putting the ball in harm's way," Brady said on Tuesday . "We know the way that we lose football games is we turn the ball over. Our two best players turned the ball over last night. James put the ball on the ground. Look, he's doing so many good things running the football. I don't want to lose sight of how great he's running the ball right now. But we're putting the ball on the ground, and it's negating all the positive."
Cook has been fantastic as a runner in 2026 with a blazing start to the season in which he averaged 106.4 yards per game over his first five outings. That continues a hot streak which dates back to last season when he won the NFL rushing title with 1,621 yards and the season prior when he led the league with 16 touchdowns.
Fumbles are a byproduct of his heavy workload, though. He is already up to four on the year, and he lost the ball six times a season ago. No non-quarterback has more fumbles in 2026, and only Cam Skattebo matched his total at the running back position through five weeks.

Geno Smith , Jared Goff , Josh Allen, Daniel Jones , James Cook III , Cam Skattebo
"I have all the confidence in him," Brady said. "That's why I put him right back out there. But at some point there has to be consequences when we're putting negative stuff out there. The conversations that we're having are ongoing. James knows. It's important to him. But that can't happen. It's gonna cost us football games. It almost cost us one. But we can't get confused because we won the game; that's OK. It's gotta improve, or the carries are gonna decrease."
Any decrease in playing time for Cook would mean an uptick in opportunities for one or both of Ty Johnson and Ray Davis . They have a combined five carries for 8 yards on the year and factor more heavily into the pass scheme with 12 catches for 166 yards.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Rams' Alaric Jackson suspended for punching Bills' Bradley Chubb
summary: Alaric Jackson hit the Bills' pass-rusher with an apparent sucker-punch following Buffalo's wild Monday night win
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills picked up one of the wildest wins of the season on Monday night with an overtime victory over the Los Angeles Rams , and somehow, things actually got even wilder after the game. Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson threw a punch at Bills edge rusher Bradley Chubb and appeared to make contact with his face.
The NFL suspended Jackson two games for the incident. He will be eligible to return to the active roster on Monday, Oct. 26, which sets him up to miss the Week 6 matchup with the Arizona Cardinals and Week 7 contest against the Las Vegas Raiders . His first game back from suspension will be on Nov. 1 against the Los Angeles Chargers .
Following Buffalo's 37-34 win, several players from both teams stayed on the field to do a jersey exchange and that's when the drama started. Jackson was trading his jersey with Buffalo's Deone Walker and while that exchange was going on, Chubb was talking trash to Jackson.
The Rams offensive lineman clearly didn't like what Chubb had to say because he walked straight over to the Bills' pass-rusher and got in his face. Jackson and Chubb then started yelling at each other, and that's when things got ugly.
At that point, the two players had to be separated by their teammates. You can see a video of the incident below.
Alaric Jackson threw a punch at Bradley Chubb after Bills-Rams. pic.twitter.com/diJunklKBe
"After the game, as players were shaking hands and exchanging jerseys, Jackson struck Buffalo linebacker Bradley Chubb in the face after a brief confrontation, violating Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, which applies to 'any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship,'" the NFL said in a statement.
As you can see, Jackson's punch was pretty blatant, and the suspension is unsurprising given the historical precedent for that punishment.
During the 2025 season, Lions safety Brian Branch got hit with a one-game suspension for instigating a post-game fight following a loss to the Chiefs . That altercation actually took place on Oct. 12, 2025, exactly one year before Jackson's punch.
Jackson was suspended for two games in 2024 for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy, so this is not his first time standing under the league's watchful eye.
Based on post-game video, it appears that Chubb was talking trash to anyone and everyone.
Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb had to be restrained by teammates following Monday night’s game against the Rams. pic.twitter.com/f5ltQs1xin
After he left the field, Chubb was asked about the altercation.
"Just emotions. You know what I mean," Chubb said of what happened, via the California Post . "Emotional game. It was a close game."
In the video, you can see that Chubb put his hand in Jackson's face just before Jackson threw the punch and that may have instigated the situation.
"They always catch the second guy, so I let him swing and my teammates held me back, so I just chilled," Chubb said.
Chubb was also asked if he was quarreling with anyone specifically and it appears that Jackson wasn't the only Rams player he was talking trash to.
"It was just the whole team," Chubb said.
Chubb finished the game with just two tackles, but his team won and that's what matters.
author: John Breech

title: Saints owner Gayle Benson voices frustration with 1-4 record, emphasizes 'urgency' to improve
summary: Benson turned up the heat on the Saints' coaching staff and roster during their three-game losing streak
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints opened the 2026 season with a promising two-game start in which they fought back from a 21-0 deficit against the Detroit Lions to force overtime and defeated the Baltimore Ravens on the road. But since then, they have lost three consecutive games and dropped the last two by double digits. That stretch of football did not sit well with owner Gayle Benson.
Speaking at the Greater New Orleans Quarterback Club on Tuesday, Benson lit a fire under the team when she expressed her disappointment with the 1-4 start.
"That is not acceptable to me, and it falls short of what our fans truly deserve," Benson said . "I hear the frustration directed toward our team and our organization. It is not lost on me. Our fans invest their time, their money and their hearts in the Saints. They are right to expect more than we have delivered.
"As an owner, the responsibility does start with me. I will not make excuses, and I will not accept this level of performance as our standard. I am committed to making the decisions necessary to improve this team. Everyone in this organization understands the urgency. We must prepare better, execute consistently and correct the mistakes that are costing us the games. Words will not restore our fans' confidence; our performance must do that."
The first two losses aged poorly, as the Lions went on to lose two of their next three games following the overtime thriller and the Las Vegas Raiders dropped both of their two ensuing contests. The third loss stung particularly hard because it came by 21 points to a division rival, the Atlanta Falcons , on the day the Saints celebrated the 20-year anniversary of the Superdome's reopening, no less.
The most recent defeat was perhaps the most frustrating yet, because the typically prolific passing attack fell silent in a game where the defense played some of its best football of the young season. Quarterback Tyler Shough passed for a season-low 96 yards against the Minnesota Vikings and their stout defense after crossing the 250-yard threshold in each of his previous four outings.
If there is anything to build upon, it would be the seven-point win over the Baltimore Ravens in Week 2. That generated no momentum in the moment, though.
"Our obligation to deliver better football remains very clear," Benson said. "To the coaches here today, you all know what leadership requires when your team struggles. You confront the problems, make corrections and hold yourself to the same standard you demand of others. That is what I expect throughout our organization."
Following a promising final stretch of the 2025 season in which New Orleans won four of its final five games, it appeared as though then-first-year coach Kellen Moore was turning a corner. His offensive prowess carried over into 2026, but the wins did not. The Saints rank 16th in scoring (up from 28th a year ago) and 20th in yards (up from 23rd) but stand in a tie for third place in a wide-open NFC South, which they entered the year with hopes of winning.
The Saints are now on pace to finish Year 2 of the Moore era with a worse record than in Year 1.
"To our fans, I hear you very loudly," Benson said. "I understand your disappointment, and I share your determination to see this team succeed. Your support deserves a response you can see on the field. We cannot change the results of our first five games. We are responsible for what we do next. I expect better, our fans deserve better, and I am determined to see that we do it for them."
author: Carter Bahns

title: Jauan Jennings landing spots: Could veteran WR reunite with 49ers after slow start in Minnesota?
summary: With Jennings' trade market reportedly set to heat up, these destinations would be ideal fits
full_text:
This season could be the worst of Jauan Jennings ' career if the wide receiver spends the rest of the year with the Minnesota Vikings . He has not clicked with his new team after he signed with them on a one-year, $8 million contract in free agency and is suddenly a trade candidate as the Vikings potentially seek to get anything they can in return for him before he departs at the end of the year. According to NFL Media/ESPN , Jennings' trade market is expected to heat up before the Nov. 10 deadline.
Despite joining the Vikings on the heels of consecutive highly productive seasons with the San Francisco 49ers , Jennings started only two of the first five games of 2026 and missed another for personal reasons. He has a mere two catches for 9 yards on five targets as an afterthought in the passing scheme.
The hope when Jennings signed with Minnesota was that he could thrive as the second weapon behind Justin Jefferson or the third option behind him and Jordan Addison . Instead, the six-year veteran has been invisible. He struggled to get open in Weeks 1-5, and when he did, quarterbacks Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz mostly either missed him or did not throw his way in the first place.
Jauan Jennings was pissed off he didn’t get the ball when he was wide open in the end zone on Sunday A total of 5 targets in 4 games will do this to you pic.twitter.com/25tacVpI0f
There appears to be a lack of chemistry between Jennings and his quarterbacks, and he is clearly a far worse fit in Kevin O'Connell's offense than that of Kyle Shanahan. For those reasons, and because he can leave of his own volition at the end of the season, the Vikings could work toward a trade over the next month.
These five teams would be ideal landing spots for Jennings should a trade materialize.
A return to the Bay Area almost makes too much sense. It was with the 49ers that Jennings developed from a seventh-round pick into the team's top wide receiver. He was a highly reliable fan favorite who led San Francisco's wideouts in 2024 and 2025 and developed a reputation as a premier third-down weapon and run blocker. His usage would balloon if he got out of a poor situation in Minnesota and returned to the one that made him the best version of himself.
While the 49ers elected last spring to save money instead of retaining Jennings on a multi-year contract extension, he only landed a modest one-year deal anyway with the Vikings. It would seemingly not cost San Francisco nearly as much to bring him back on his current deal as it would have to re-sign him last offseason, and if money is no longer an issue, the reunion is a slam dunk.
Plus, the 49ers are in serious need of wide receiver help. This would not be the addition of a familiar face just for the sake of a reunion. It would be the addition of a capable contributor who can mask the absences of numerous wideouts, including Deebo Samuel (out for multiple weeks with a hamstring strain), Ricky Pearsall (out for the season following PCL surgery) and the trio of De'Zhaun Stribling , Christian Kirk and Demarcus Robinson, who all remain on injured reserve.
The only go-to targets in Las Vegas, and the only ones locked in as part of the future of the franchise, are tight ends. Outside of Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer , the Raiders are without reliable threats in the passing game. The wide receiver group is the clear weak spot of a surprisingly competitive roster and one that needs addressing if the Raiders seek to contend for a playoff spot in Year 1 under Klint Kubiak. And since they stand above .500 through five weeks, they could emerge as buyers at the trade deadline.
Kirk Cousins leads a productive offense, but eventually this will be Fernando Mendoza's team. What if the rookie takes over at some point this year? He needs receivers who will help him settle into his first meaningful NFL action. With Jack Bech and Dont'e Thornton Jr . on injured reserve and Jalen Nailor working his way back from a concussion, Mendoza's supporting cast would be lacking if he were suddenly thrust into action. Jennings is the kind of experienced receiver who can win 50-50 balls and ease the No. 1 pick into a state of comfort.
The offseason acquisition of Kenneth Walker III rejuvenated the Kansas City Chiefs ' offense. The running game has been spectacular thanks to the reigning Super Bowl MVP, but the typically electric passing attack could use a lift considering the cupboard is quite empty at wide receiver outside of Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy . Now that Tyquan Thornton is potentially out for the season with his dislocated ankle, the need for help has never been greater. Not only would Jennings aid in the receiving department, but his run-blocking skills would be a boon to Walker and the already tremendous ground scheme.
Kansas City reunited with Justin Watson and added him to the practice squad, and it has been linked to Tyreek Hill in his attempt at a comeback from his devastating knee injury. Neither of them is on the active roster, though. There is room for Jennings.
The Pittsburgh Steelers ' offense is gaining steam with Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy appearing in vintage form of late, but that momentum is in danger due to a rash of wide receiver injuries. Michael Pittman Jr. is on injured reserve with a foot issue, while Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (neck) are already ruled out for Week 6 and could miss additional time. Jennings could be a plug-and-play replacement for those ailing receivers in an offense that is firing on all cylinders.
The Steelers cannot afford to slow down in the highly competitive AFC North. The Ravens are 4-1 and everyone else is one game back at 3-2. Jennings may be a necessary addition to keep the machine running until, and perhaps after, the trio of receivers returns to the lineup.
The last time the Green Bay Packers traded within their own division was in 2023. The Vikings have not traded with an NFC North foe since 2022. That was also the most recent instance in which the two teams made a deal with each other. Minnesota may be hesitant to assist a division rival that needs immediate help at wide receiver, but if the price is right, perhaps the first-place Vikings will consider it.
It would likely cost the Packers a premium considering the context between the teams, but Green Bay lacks receiver depth with Jayden Reed out for the season. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden have been an excellent one-two punch, but this offense is suddenly feeling the crunch after letting Romeo Doubs leave in free agency and trading Dontayvion Wicks . What once was an overcrowded room is now walking a tightrope from an in-season depth standpoint. Plus, the Packers are in the playoff mix at 3-2 but have not looked stellar offensively outside of their most recent win. They could use an injection of life.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Micah Parsons rips into Jayden Daniels for 'disgusting' OT blunder:  'Probably cost Dan Quinn his job'
summary: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn was Parsons' first NFL defensive coordinator with the Dallas Cowboys, and he's taking Quinn's side after Washington's overtime mistakes
full_text:
Micah Parsons is no longer in the NFC East after being traded from the Dallas Cowboys to the Green Bay Packers ahead of the 2025 NFL season, but he still follows that division closely.
That means he was well aware that Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels failed to keep the clock running for a game-winning field goal attempt at the end of Washington's 27-27 tie vs. the New York Giants on Sunday. Naturally, he has a strong opinion about it.
"Jayden Daniels probably cost my man Dan Quinn his job, to be honest with you," Parsons said on Monday on his "The Edge" podcast on Bleacher Report. "To be honest with you. And, like, I'm a big Jayden Daniels fan. But the reality is, he probably cost a lot of people their jobs this past weekend."
The Commanders can't get the play off in time and this game ends in a tie pic.twitter.com/WmPp6q5hU0
Parsons feels the Commanders blew their chance to upset the first-place Giants on Sunday, and that it will cost Washington head coach Dan Quinn his job, with the team now out to a 1-3-1 start in 2026. The Commanders went 5-12 in 2025 with Daniels missing 10 games due to injury, a year after going 12-5 and reaching the NFC championship game.
It's worth noting Parsons isn't a neutral observer here, even though he is currently a Packer. Quinn was Parsons' defensive coordinator with the Cowboys during his first three NFL seasons, from 2021 to 2023, when Dallas won 12 games in three consecutive seasons. That's why Parsons refers to Quinn as his "OG" and said they would have hard conversations, whether they were "father to son or player to coach" in Dallas.
Parsons' cohost asked if he puts any of that glaring lack of awareness by Daniels and the offense on the Commanders 'coaching staff, and he doubled down on Daniels being the primary party at fault.
"All respectfully, we get coached so much on these situations that, like, I'm a defensive player, and this shit's programmed to me," Parsons said. "I even know what to do in those situations. There's no way I'm taking a sack with 14 seconds left and no timeouts...And, mind you, it'd be different if Jayden Daniels was a rookie. This is your third year. This is your third year. You've been to the NFC Championship game. You've been in big moments before. And to me, like even after a sack, you're casually getting up. ... He's not even urgently getting up. ... That is disgusting, bro."
The 27-year-old edge rusher is well aware of how people squarely pin wins and losses on a team's starting quarterback. As someone who also recently went through a messy contract negotiation with the Cowboys, Parsons is also well aware that NFL players are extension-eligible after their third NFL season. That means Daniels will be able to sign a new, more lucrative second NFL contract in the 2027 offseason should Washington choose to offer him one.
What happened on Sunday won't help the Commanders quarterback at the negotiating table, according to Parsons.
"If people want to say QBs win or lose games, and as you can see, they won or lost the game [tied] on a QB's hands, this is your job, bro," Parsons said. "This is your job to be prepared to understand the game and understand situations. That's in your job profile. And you're telling me, 'Oh, we're gonna want to pay this guy eventually $60 million?' This cannot happen. Jayden Daniels is in a contract year. That's not what I want to put on tape."
Daniels' postgame press conference seemed to rub Parsons the wrong way as well. Daniels said , "We gotta relay that as an offense, it starts from everybody, top down [the coaching staff]. Ultimately, it's on me." But Parsons expected more direct accountability.
"I'm a player, and you know I'm a big JD5 fan, but that's inexcusable, bro," Parsons said. "The lack of urgency, that's something, if I was on [his] defense, I would have had to say something in the locker room. I would've had to come talk to him like 'yo, that's not OK.'"
The Packers work on situational football "every day," according to Parsons. He also inferred that it is the standard operating procedure across practices throughout the NFL. Here's how he described the situational football practice schedule in Green Bay:
Bottom line, Parsons feels Daniels needs to improve his awareness and desire to put his team in a better position. He doubled down that what happened on Sunday for the Commanders is simply inexcusable.
"To me, this is a lack of preparation, a lack of mentality, and a lack of urgency by the [big] man on campus [Daniels]," Parsons said. "That just can't happen."
author: Garrett Podell

title: Bears' Montez Sweat suspended for violating NFL's performance-enhancing substances policy
summary: Sweat will miss two important games before his return in November
full_text:
The Chicago Bears will be without edge rusher Montez Sweat for the next two games. The NFL suspended Sweat without pay for violating the league's performance-enhancing substances policy, the league announced on Tuesday. He will be eligible for reinstatement on Friday, Oct. 23.
Sweat is set to miss Sunday's road game against the Atlanta Falcons and the Week 7 "Thursday Night Football" clash with the New England Patriots . His first game back from suspension is the Monday night trip to Seattle on Nov. 2, when the Bears face the reigning Super Bowl-champion Seahawks .
Across the first five games of 2026, Sweat logged seven tackles and two sacks, the latter of which rank as the third-most on the team. It has been a relatively slow start for the pass rusher, whose 8.8% quarterback pressure rate is lower than any of his season-long marks from 2019-25. His time to sack of 7.18 seconds is also a career worst by nearly two full seconds.
Despite the modest five-game stretch, Sweat remains vital to the Bears' defensive front, which is relatively thin on the edge. Just last season, he led the team in sacks, tackles for loss and quarterback hits, and he paced the squad in sacks for the two years prior. He earned the first and only Pro Bowl selection of his career in 2023 when he opened the year with the Washington Commanders and closed it in Chicago.
Sweat's six turnovers caused by pressure in 2025 were a career best and ranked second in the NFL , per Next Gen Stats.
Sweat has missed only one game since his arrival in Chicago three years ago. The Bears logged three sacks in that 2024 loss to the Arizona Cardinals , but none of the players who recorded them remain on the roster. It will be primarily up to Dayo Odeyingbo and Austin Booker to step up during Sweat's suspension, and the former's status is in question after he left Sunday's loss to the Green Bay Packers with a quad injury. If Odeyingbo cannot play, James Lynch would be the next man up across from Booker.
Booker is the team leader in sacks, quarterback hits and tackles for loss thus far, and he is responsible for a forced fumble, as well. He did all of that despite coming off the bench in each of the five games, so perhaps the pass rush will not regress as he steps into a starting role. Odeyingbo, meanwhile, also ranks ahead of Sweat with three sacks.
The Chicago defense had a long day in Week 5 in its 31-7 rivalry loss, but excelled in Weeks 2-4, allowing a combined 28 points in three games. It may not have to shoulder as much of the load moving forward, as quarterback Caleb Williams is on track to potentially return from his hamstring strain on Sunday. The timing of Williams' return could not be more opportune, given Sweat's scheduled absence.
