title: Prisco's NFL Week 6 Power Rankings: 49ers are league's best team, Packers climb 10 spots
summary: Pete Prisco shares his latest Power Rankings for the 2026 NFL season, including some big risers and fallers
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan hasn't won a Super Bowl. That doesn't mean he isn't a great coach.
If last season, in which he won 12 games with an injury-ravaged team, didn't prove how good he is at leading the 49ers, this year is doing just that.
The 49ers are 5-0 after going to Seattle and beating the Seahawks on Sunday, doing it with a defense leading the charge, rather than the Shanahan-led offense.
The 49ers limited the Seattle running attack, forced four turnovers, one of which was recovered in the end zone for a touchdown, and had five sacks, the most they've had in a game since 2024. They did it without star pass rusher Nick Bosa.
First-year defensive coordinator Raheem Morris is using a much more aggressive scheme than past Shanahan coordinators, and it's showing up in takeaways and sacks. The coverage is tighter.
Combine that with Shanahan's offensive wizardry and an MVP-type start for quarterback Brock Purdy, and it's easy to understand why the 49ers sit atop my Power Rankings. Going to Seattle and beating the defending champs sends a loud message to the rest of the league.
As for Shanahan, his greatness as a coach might not truly be earned until he wins a Super Bowl. That's just the way it is. He came close when his Jimmy Garoppolo-led 49ers had a lead against the Kansas City Chiefs in Super Bowl LIV after the 2019 season, only to see Patrick Mahomes rally to win it. They came close again four years later in Super Bowl LVIII, with Purdy and Co. pushing Mahomes and the Chiefs to overtime before losing.
This team, provided it stays healthy, has a real shot at getting back there for Shanahan. For now, they are the league's best team with a schedule that might not be as tough as expected before the season. Plus, they already have victories over division rivals in the Rams and Seahawks.
This could be Shanahan's year to win one.
The bottom of my rankings stays the same. The Miami Dolphins remain at No. 32, but the Tennessee Titans at No. 31 will give them a run for their money this season. Neither team has won a game. Who wins first?
author: Pete Prisco

title: NFL trade deadline buyers and sellers: Cowboys looking to add, possible Chargers fire sale?
summary: These are the teams and names to monitor as trade season heats up in the weeks to come
full_text:
As the sixth week of the NFL season arrives, the gap between Super Bowl contenders and teams vying for favorable positions in the draft has begun to grow. Once teams recognize their spot in the pecking order, they can chart their path forward for the rest of 2026 and beyond, and one of the first decisions to make is whether to buy or sell at the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
That mark is already less than a month out, so there are only a few games left to help front offices decide whether to add impact talent or ship it out in exchange for draft capital.
A few teams have already begun this process. On Sunday, the Arizona Cardinals traded wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr . to the Houston Texans in a move that padded the former's draft coffers and gave the latter a high-upside depth piece on offense who could get his career back on track in a new situation. Before Harrison, Cam Jurgens , Joey Porter Jr . and J.J. McCarthy hit the trade block.
The question is not whether there will be a flurry of moves at the deadline — that is a given. It is more about which teams will make them. Once it becomes clear who is buying and who is selling, the players involved will, in many cases, be quite obvious.
Here are the teams that could buy and sell at the deadline and the players that may be on the move.
Sell candidates: Khalil Mack , Donte Jackson , Quentin Johnston , David Njoku
Why wait until the deadline to move on from obvious trade candidates such as Mack? The Chargers are, shockingly, going nowhere fast at 0-5 and face a grueling schedule between now and Nov. 10, so they may as well get out ahead of the market and sell before they lose even more leverage. This roster and its coaching staff might have simply run its course, because after years of coming up short in the postseason, their chances of even getting back there in 2026 are bleak at best.
Mack is by far the most tradeable player on the roster as a 35-year-old playing extremely well on a one-year contract. That is the exact kind of rental player that defense-needy playoff contenders are in search of every single year.
Teams with holes on the back end of the defense could call about Jackson and his expiring contract, too. He racked up nine interceptions across the 2024 and 2025 seasons, after all. And on the other side of the ball, someone will look past Johnston's drop problems and see his physical attributes as worthy of investment. Meanwhile, Njoku should be a cheap option at tight end.
Buy candidates: Khalil Mack, Josh Sweat , Daron Payne , Zach Sieler
So long as Ben Johnson is around, the Bears will not have trouble putting points on the board. Once Caleb Williams returns to the lineup, Chicago will be back in the mix for prime positioning in the NFC playoff hunt, and it already showed it can stay afloat for however much longer he is on the sideline. In order to maximize the team's upside upon Williams' return, general manager Ryan Poles needs to bolster the defense, especially up front. The Bears rank just 20th in quarterback pressure rate and lack depth on both the edge and interior.
What about a reunion with Mack? He spent four years of his prime with the Bears and clearly still has something to give with three sacks in five games this season. Perhaps they could acquire Sweat instead. They have just enough cap space to bring him in this year before his salary balloons in the final two years of his contract. The edge rusher spot should be a higher priority than defensive tackle since the Bears were mostly quiet at that position in the offseason and just saw Marcus Davenport abruptly retire after Week 4 .
Sell candidates: Tony Pollard , Calvin Ridley , Jermaine Johnson II
If a Titans breakthrough comes during the Robert Saleh era, it does not appear it will happen in Year 1. This franchise is still stuck in rebuild mode and needs to acquire as much draft capital as possible to round out its core of Cam Ward and Carnell Tate with more young prospects. That means cutting bait on what already looks like a lost season, parting with the tradeable veterans, hoping that Ward shows signs of improvement in the second half of the year and making good use of what should be another early first-round pick in 2027.
Pollard is among the biggest names across the NFL who could be next in line to be traded . The former Pro Bowler is on an expiring contract and perhaps in the final stages of his prime. He would be a terrific No. 2 option for a team that already has a standout starting running back.
Ridley already seems to be in the midst of his decline and is no longer a regular starter, but was a perennial 1,000-yard receiver as recently as two years ago. And even though the Titans traded for Johnson in the offseason, they did so knowing he would play 2026 on his fifth-year option and could flip him in an attempt to get something in return rather than watching him leave at the end of his contract.
Buy candidates: Maxx Crosby , Alex Highsmith , Khalil Mack, Josh Sweat
Jerry Jones is in a trading mood already and made a splash when he acquired Joey Porter Jr. The defense still needs help, though. After they added Porter, the Cowboys could shift their focus back toward the front of the unit and continue to address the edge rusher spot, which has been a weakness ever since they shipped Micah Parsons out of town. Jones has not been shy about wanting to shore up the defense through the trade market and is always one for the marquee transaction, so Dallas might not be done big-game hunting.
By the time the deadline arrives, the Cowboys might have just enough cap space to add Crosby to their payroll. They reportedly made three offers to the Raiders prior to the nixed deal that would have sent him to the Ravens , so it does not take much imagination to picture them making another push. The bigger question is whether Las Vegas still has any interest in moving him.
Dallas could also look back to Pittsburgh and try for Highsmith, who could be the odd man out in a three-person pass-rushing system that also features T.J. Watt and Nick Herbig . The Cowboys already pulled off three trades with the Steelers over the last year and a half, so there is a fruitful working relationship between the two front offices.
Sell candidates: Austin Jackson , Zach Sieler, Josh Uche
To climb out of the deepest rebuild in the NFL, the Dolphins have to establish a core around which they can build a roster. There are early signs of one existing in standout first-year linebacker Jacob Rodriguez and rookie wide receivers Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell , but Miami needs another big draft like the 13-pick haul it put together this past spring. While it lacks a volume of tradeable veterans and will have a hard time receiving Day 1 or Day 2 capital in return, there are a couple who could help the Dolphins pile up selections in the later rounds.
Jackson is off to a rough start as the 71st-rated offensive tackle among 72 qualifiers, per PFF, but tackles are always in demand. He would be an affordable half-season rental. Sieler, at 31, is much older than the defensive pieces the Dolphins plan to build around. Uche is the strongest candidate of the three to re-sign with Miami, but even that is no guarantee.
Buy candidates: Jerry Jeudy , Khalil Mack, Josh Uche , Daron Payne, Zach Sieler
The 49ers own the best resume in the NFL with wins over the entire rest of the NFC West, plus the Broncos and Dolphins . They played better over five games than any other Super Bowl hopeful, but with a roster loaded with older and oft-injured players, their ability to stay in the hunt is always tenuous.
San Francisco can never have enough weapons. In order to keep this train rolling, general manager John Lynch should add startable depth at the deadline to prevent any catastrophic drop-offs should injuries further plague his team down the stretch and into the playoffs. He has all the room on his payroll he needs to do so with $41.9 million in salary cap space, which is the most of…
author: Carter Bahns

title: Is it Carson Beck time in Arizona? When Cardinals need to replace Jacoby Brissett with the rookie QB
summary: A look at the Cardinals' quarterback outlook and when Carson Beck should start
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals (1-4) have hit their ceiling with Jacoby Brissett as their starting quarterback in 2026.
Since defeating the now 0-5 Los Angeles Chargers in Week 1, Arizona has lost four in a row, including a damning couple of losses the last two weeks. The Cardinals had a chance to beat the New York Giants in Week 4 with a play at the 4-yard line, trailing by six with 11 seconds remaining. After using their final timeout, Brissett threw a pick-six, the third of his single-game career-high three interceptions that day.
Equally — or perhaps more — damning is what happened on Sunday in Arizona's 45-21 defeat against the Detroit Lions . The Lions entered Week 5 with the league's 31st-ranked scoring defense (31.8 points per game) and the NFL's worst total defense (423.8 total yards per game) and third down defense (52.8% third down conversion rate allowed). After an opening drive touchdown pass from Brissett to tight end Teagan Quitoriano , the Cardinals' next five drives were three-and-outs. That's right. Arizona had five consecutive three-and-outs against the league's worst total and third-down defense. Their next drive ended with an interception. It wasn't until the game was essentially over that Brissett found the end zone again.
That leaves the question: Is it time for Carson Beck to take over in Arizona?
Every quarterback who had played the Lions entering Week 5 stuffed the stat sheet and either beat Detroit or lost to them by one possession. The Brissett-led Cardinals losing to the 2026 Lions defense, which is missing both All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph and Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch , by 24 points is unacceptable.
Quarterbacks vs. the Lions this season
Brissett's production this season — 66.3% completion percentage, 1,110 yards passing, nine passing touchdowns and five interceptions for an 85.2 passer rating — isn't terrible, but it's all empty calories in that it mostly happens with the game's outcome no longer up in the air. The 2026 season isn't an outlier for Brissett either. In 2025, he threw for 3,366 passing yards, the second most in the NFL since becoming a starter in Week 6, but they weren't impactful. Arizona won just one of Brissett's 11 starts in 2025, and it was against the Dallas Cowboys , who owned that season's worst scoring defense (30.1 points allowed per game).
Brissett is what he is: a 33-year-old journeyman on his sixth NFL team in 11 seasons who is limited as a full-time starting quarterback.
A strong case could be made that 2026 third-round pick Carson Beck should begin to receive increased reps in practice before eventually replacing Brissett in the starting lineup. Beck played just one preseason game , the Hall of Fame game against the Carolina Panthers, but he performed well. He threw for 188 yards and a touchdown while completing 15 of his 19 throws.
A rib injury cut short his development opportunities as he missed the final three Cardinals preseason games. Thus far this season, he has been the emergency third quarterback on game day.
"If we think that's what's best," said Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur on Monday when asked about moving Beck to an active role. "We haven't had those discussions. We'll end up having that discussion [Tuesday]."
Sure, a one-game preseason sample size isn't incredibly indicative of a quarterback's long-term NFL potential, but it's worth ramping Beck up to start. The next two weeks are against difficult defenses in the Los Angeles Rams and the Denver Broncos , but Arizona should target Week 8 for Beck to make his regular-season debut.
Why Week 8? That's when the Cardinals will head to AT&T Stadium to face the Dallas Cowboys (2-3), the only team Brissett beat in 2025 and the owners of the NFL's current seventh-worst scoring defense (27.2 points per game allowed in 2026). The Cowboys are fresh off an embarrassing loss to the 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who earned their first win of 2026 with undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels making his second career start.
Arizona needs to get Beck, an older rookie who will turn 25 years old in November, reps for at least the second half of this season. It'll only help to assess what the Cardinals have in him ahead of utilizing another high draft pick in the vaunted 2027 NFL Draft . If they like what they see, the Cardinals can simply go with the "best player available" approach. If they don't, they may need to take a longer look at the upcoming quarterback draft class.
author: Garrett Podell

title: NFL eyeing possible schedule change with Sunday night flex in Week 8, but league doesn't have a lot of options
summary: With Philadelphia and Washington struggling, the league has until Oct. 20 to make a move, but scheduling conflicts across the Week 8 slate leave few viable replacement options
full_text:
You don't usually see a prime-time game get flexed during the first half of the season, but that might actually happen this year.
According to the Philadelphia Inquirer , the NFL is considering whether to flex the Eagles-Commanders game out of Sunday night in Week 8. The NFL loves to put NFC East teams in prime time because of the markets involved, but with the Eagles at 2-3 and the Commanders at 1-3-1, the league might not want to keep the matchup there.
Under NFL rules, any flex for Week 8 has to be announced at least 12 days in advance, so the league has until Oct. 20 to make a decision. That means both teams will get to play one more game before the league decides whether to flex the matchup. The Eagles are hosting the Panthers this week while the Commanders are traveling to San Francisco to face the 49ers on Monday night.
If the Commanders lose to the undefeated 49ers, that would drop them to 1-4-1, and since they have a bye in Week 7, that means Washington would go into the Sunday night game with just one win and the NFL would likely prefer not to see that. As for the Eagles, if they were to lose on Sunday, that means they'd definitely have a losing record going into the Week 8 game (After facing the Panthers in Week 6, the Eagles play the Cowboys in Week 7 before facing the Commanders).
If the NFL is looking to flex the game, the league's big problem is that there aren't many great options. Let's check out the best games on the Week 8 schedule and why they probably won't work:
One other thing the NFL would have to work through is that CBS and Fox are both allowed to protect a game from being flexed.
Now that we've covered the big games, here's the rest of the Sunday afternoon slate in Week 8:
As you can see, there's just not a great option in that group. The NFL could try to do something crazy like moving the Ravens-Bills game to 4:25 p.m. ET and flexing Chiefs-Broncos to prime time, but that would take some serious behind-the-scenes shuffling, and as we mentioned, the Chiefs are on SNF in Week 7, so they might not be a viable candidate to be flexed back there in Week 8.
It could make sense to move Browns-Steelers, especially since this is Aaron Rodgers' final season, but Pittsburgh is playing on Sunday night in Week 10 against the Bengals, so that could throw a wrench in that plan. Based on all the options, the NFL might just be stuck with keeping Commanders-Eagles in prime time.

title: Brian Flores-NFL lawsuit: Recruiting firm memo filled with racial stereotypes, attorneys claim
summary: Flores, Steve Wilks and Ray Horton have an ongoing lawsuit against the NFL for racial discrimination
full_text:
In the latest development in the Brian Flores lawsuit against the NFL for racial discrimination , a recruiting firm memo regarding Flores possessed examples of what his legal team labeled as racial stereotypes and talking points teams use in reference to potential Black head coach hires.
A memo put together for the Las Vegas Raiders by the recruiter Korn Ferry during a recent head-coaching search became unsealed in court on Tuesday. It is part of the lawsuit from Flores — and former head coaches Steve Wilks and Ray Horton —against the league and six teams. Front Office Sports obtained and published a copy of the memo on Tuesday.
In the report, it was noted that he was "polished and a good presenter" despite growing up in Brownsville, Brooklyn, the same area as notorious heavyweight champion boxer Mike Tyson . Flores' lawyers argue the report assumes someone from the predominantly Black area of New York wouldn't have strong public speaking skills. According to the NYU Furman Center , just over two-thirds of Brownsville's population, 67.6%, is Black.
"Polished and a good presenter despite growing up in Brownsville, Brooklyn (same as Mike Tyson)," the memo read, via Front Office Sports . "He was able to build a strong friendship with a billionaire's son which gave him opportunities to socialize and learn how to build relationships with white-collar and upper-class individuals."
Flores' attorney, Michael Willemin, told Front Office Sports that the write-up paints Flores as an "angry Black man." Willemin pointed to the "polish upwards" reference in his "Weaknesses" section as a racial stereotype that downplays Flores' intelligence as a minority.
Other "Weaknesses" comments his lawyers point to in the report read:
Flores, who has been the Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator since 2023, following three seasons as the Miami Dolphins head coach (2019 to 2021), has the Vikings out to a 5-0 start in 2026. Their undefeated record is largely on the strength of his complex blitzing, disguise coverage scheme.
Minnesota has the fewest touchdowns (9) during a 5-0 start since the 2003 Carolina Panthers , while Flores' defense ranks first in the NFL in scoring defense (12.8 points per game allowed) in 2026. Flores' unit also leads the league in quarterback pressure rate (46.4%), sack rate (9.8%), blitz rate (69.8%), completion percentage allowed (53.2%) and passer rating allowed (62.9).
Flores first sued the NFL in 2022 and was later joined by Wilks and Horton. The Tua Tagovailoa comments referenced in the report refer to when the ex-Dolphins quarterback labeled his former head coach as "a terrible person" in 2024. Tagovailoa, who is now the back-up quarterback with the Atlanta Falcons , said Flores shook his confidence that he could be an NFL quarterback.
The current Vikings defensive coordinator responded to Tagovailoa's comments in August 2024 , and he said he used that feedback to grow as a leader.
"Look, I'm human," Flores said at the time , specifically when asked about Tagovailoa's "terrible person" depiction. "So that hit me in a way that wasn't ... positive for me. But at the same time, I've got to use that and say, 'Hey, how can I grow from that? How can I be better?' And that's really where I'm at from that standpoint. Do I feel like that's me? No. But how can I grow from that situation and create a world where that's not the case that anyone says that about Brian Flores?"
author: Garrett Podell

title: Will Chargers trade Justin Herbert? Update on possibility of QB being dealt and possible landing spots
summary: Herbert's name has started to circulate ahead of the NFL's trade deadline
full_text:
With the Nov. 4 trade deadline rapidly approaching, rumors and rumblings have intensified regarding potential players who may be on the move. One of those players is Justin Herbert , the Chargers ' embattled quarterback who has played some of the worst football of his career through the season's first five games. His struggles have coincided with the Chargers' dreadful 0-5 start to the season.
Despite Herbert's struggles this season, the Chargers would be well-compensated if they decided to trade him. ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter said that a high-level executive threw out a hypothetical scenario to him where the Chargers traded Herbert for three first-round picks. Intrigued, Schefter then reached out to the Chargers to see if they would actually consider trading Herbert.
"The person basically cut me off mid-sentence," Schefter said. "Stopped me in my tracks and said, 'Let me be very clear about this. We have never even discussed that idea. The sentence -- should we trade Justin Herbert -- has never once been uttered in our organization, nor will it be.'"
Based on that report, it appears that the odds of Herbert being traded are about as good as Herbert winning league MVP this season. Despite their current predicament, the Chargers apparently still believe that Herbert is their long-term franchise quarterback and is capable of playing high-level football again.
That may be true, but teams often have a change of heart. Nothing can entirely be ruled out in sports, especially in the NFL , where things seem to change on a dime. That's why, even if it is unlikely, the prospect of Herbert being traded can't be dismissed entirely, especially when you consider what the Chargers would get for him.
In that vein, here are several teams that would likely be in play if Herbert were made available for trade:
The Vikings were the first team to come to mind. Despite their 5-0 start, Minnesota's offense remains bogged down by middling quarterback play.
While that is true, it's hard to imagine the Vikings doing anything dramatic unless the team goes into a funk sometime between now and the trade deadline. Kyler Murray , for all his faults, is 4-0 as Minnesota's starting quarterback.
It's worth repeating, however, that the Vikings could decide to pull the trigger on something of this magnitude if the offense continues to lag behind the defense.
If the Jets want any chance of being relevant by season's end, they need to do something drastic on the offensive side of the ball. Trading for Herbert would qualify as such.
Gang Green's defense is currently fifth in the NFL in fewest points allowed. The offense, however, is among the league's worst in several areas, most notably in points scored.
With 10 picks in the upcoming NFL Draft , the Jets have the resources to make a splash at the deadline. That makes this scenario even more likely if the Chargers have a change of heart with Herbert.
It would be hard to blame the Titans if they chose to end the Cam Ward era after less than two years. Ward hasn't made significant strides this season, and it's one of the reasons why the Titans are 0-5.
While he wouldn't change their fortunes that much this year, Herbert would infuse some optimism into a fan base that badly needs it. The Titans could certainly use more optimism as they prepare to open a new stadium in 2027.
Miami can get a do-over after drafting Tua Tagovailoa instead of Herbert in 2020.
The Dolphins are in the first year of Malik Willis ' contract, but anyone who has watched Miami knows that Willis isn't the team's long-term solution at quarterback. Instead of riding it out with Willis, the Dolphins would be better served finding a better option at the most important position in sports.
More so, Herbert's arrival would give Miami's long-suffering fanbase some much-needed hope. The Dolphins, after all, haven't had a quarterback of Herbert's caliber since Dan Marino, who retired at the end of the 1999 season.
As unlikely as this scenario is, it makes a lot of sense for both franchises.
Both Herbert and Jalen Hurts could use a change of scenery. Herbert has regressed in Los Angeles, and the same can be said of Hurts in Philadelphia.
For the Eagles , Herbert could potentially jumpstart their playoff hopes if Philadelphia can find a way to win some games ahead of the trade deadline. Hurts, in turn, would be a better fit in Mike McDaniel's offense.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Rams release kicker Harrison Mevis after disastrous loss to Bills, sign Jets' practice squad kicker
summary: Mevis hit just 55.6% of his field goal attempts this season, which ranks last in the NFL
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are making a special teams change on the heels of their 37-34 overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday night. NFL Media reports the team is releasing kicker Harrison Mevis and signing Blake Grupe off the New York Jets ' practice squad.
Mevis, affably known as "the Thiccer Kicker," made all four of his extra-point attempts on Monday, but missed his two field-goal attempts. His first miss came from 50 yards in the first quarter, and his final miss came in overtime on a 48-yard game-winning attempt — a kick that was tipped by Bills defensive end Greg Rousseau .
GROOOOOOOOOOOOOOOT!!!! 📺: ESPN pic.twitter.com/0EHkuNlfN1
As for the Rams' new kicker, Grupe is one of the smallest players in the NFL , standing at 5-foot-7, 156 pounds. Undrafted out of Notre Dame in 2023, Grupe has kicked for the New Orleans Saints and Indianapolis Colts . The Jets claimed him off waivers in August and had him on the practice squad for all of this season so far.
In 50 career games, he has hit 81.9% of his field goals with a long of 60, and 98% of his extra points. In 2025, Grupe appeared in 11 games for the Saints, hitting 18 of his 26 field goals (69.2%). He also appeared in five games for the Colts, hitting all 11 of his field goal attempts. He hit all of his extra points during the season.
Mevis played 14 games for the Rams over the last two years. He hit 12 of 13 field goals and all 39 of his extra-point attempts in nine games last year, but he was just 5-of-9 on field goals this season. His 55.6% field goal percentage ranks last in the league.
Some of the blame for the Rams' loss to Buffalo rests on head coach Sean McVay, who went conservative in overtime . While L.A. needed just a field goal to win the game, McVay became complacent at the Bills' 35-yard line. On second-and-10, he called a short pass for Puka Nacua , which picked up five yards. On third-and-5, he dialed up a Kyren Williams run that got stuffed at the line of scrimmage. That set the stage for the unsuccessful 48-yard field goal attempt.
McVay's play-calling in this spot was controversial, as the Rams offense had registered three straight touchdown drives to end the fourth quarter.
"I thought offensively and defensively we battled," McVay said after the game. "Thought some of the coverage units, we did some really good stuff. And then the kicking game, especially with our PAT, field goal — not even close to good enough. It cost us the game tonight."
As CBS Sports' Zach Pereles pointed out , the Rams' special teams unit has struggled as a whole over the last two seasons. This year, Los Angeles ranks 29th in yards per kickoff return and 26th in yards per kickoff return allowed. The Rams are also 30th in net yards per punt and 26th in opponent net yards per punt.

title: Josh Allen heaps high praise on Matthew Stafford, says he does this one thing better than any QB ever
summary: Tom Brady has previously given that title to Aaron Rodgers
full_text:
An iconic scene unfolded before the Bills ' dramatic overtime win over the Rams on Monday night. Prior to the start of overtime, Matthew Stafford and Josh Allen , two of the best quarterbacks of this era, faced each other at midfield. It conjured up memories of Tom Brady and Peyton Manning , who faced each other numerous times during their decorated careers.
After the game, Allen opened up about his admiration for Stafford, whose stature as an all-time great has grown in recent years. In fact, Allen said that Stafford does one thing better than any quarterback in history.
"I've got an unbelievable amount of respect for Matthew," Allen told ESPN afterward. "The way he plays the game, the way he's always played it. He's as tough as they come.
"If he's not the greatest thrower of the football of all time, I don't know who is. He spins it. He's a competitor. He's a guy who every quarterback should strive to be like."
“If he’s not the greatest thrower of the football of all time, I don’t know who is.” Josh Allen joins @LauraRutledge postgame and gives high praise to Matthew Stafford 🙌 pic.twitter.com/pwgc6VBPlN
The unofficial "greatest thrower of the football" title has often been given to Aaron Rodgers , who has continued to display his legendary throwing touch during his age-42 season. Brady has routinely called Rodgers the best thrower of the football in NFL history.
"I think there's no greater passer of the football than Aaron Rodgers," Brady said earlier this year. "I mean there's certain people and you're like 'Holy.' You see everyone do it and then you see one person throw the ball that much better. Aaron Rodgers was incredible."
It's possible that Rodgers crossed Allen's mind prior to his postgame press conference. Allen slightly adjusted his response when he was asked about Stafford again.
"In my opinion, if he's not the greatest thrower of the football, he's No. 2," he said.
Josh Allen has nothing but respect for Matthew Stafford pic.twitter.com/GuJ1SjAf1v
Regardless of where he ranks, Stafford's status as an all-time great is no longer a debate. He validated his greatness with a Super Bowl win in 2021, and last year, he became the oldest league MVP in history.
While the Rams' season has been disappointing so far, the 38-year-old Stafford continues to play at a high level. He currently leads the NFL in attempts, completions and passing yards. Against the Bills, Stafford threw for 383 yards and three touchdowns and completed a whopping 74.1% of his passes.
Red zone to end zone for @tae15adams 😮‍💨 📺 @ESPNNFL | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/5Qg0A3DPAj
As great as Stafford was, he couldn't outduel Allen, the 2024 league MVP and current front-runner to win the award again. While he attempted 35 fewer passes and threw for 173 fewer yards than Stafford, Allen was unstoppable on the ground with 121 yards and a touchdown on just 10 carries. He currently leads the NFL with eight rushing touchdowns.
Allen's rushing is what separates him from most other elite quarterbacks, both past and present. He's 16th all-time with 87 touchdown runs and is three away from tying Hall of Famers Eric Dickerson and Curtis Martin.
Stafford may be the greatest passer in the game, but Allen is firmly in the conversation as one of the greatest running quarterbacks in history.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Ranking Week 5 coaching blunders: Did Sean McVay, Jim Harbaugh, or an NFC East coach have the worst gaffe?
summary: From Dan Quinn heating up his hot seat in Washington to Jim Harbaugh owning up to a fourth-quarter collapse in Los Angeles, we rank the week's most brutal sideline decisions
full_text:
Week 5 in the NFL featured some pretty incredible coaching gaffes that directly led to losses. Whether the leaders in charge of their teams just zoned out for a second, forgot what situation they were in or chose the wrong strategy, multiple fan bases were driven to madness by their franchises' decision-makers.
There were coaches who forgot about the clock, coaches who got either too aggressive or too conservative, and a coach already on the hot seat who admitted he cost his team the game. Week 5 almost saw it all when it comes to coaching blunders.
Below, we break down and rank the notable coaching gaffes from this past week in the NFL, going from "That's pretty egregious," to "Sir, what the hell are you doing?"
"I can't think of a time I've ever been more mad at myself"
The 2026 season has been a nightmare for the Los Angeles Chargers . Not only are they 0-5, but the Justin Herbert and Mike McDaniel marriage has not gone according to plan. Plus, injuries are again beginning to mount.
It looked like the Chargers were on their way to winning their first game of the season against the rival Denver Broncos on Sunday. The Chargers held a 17-10 lead early in the fourth quarter and just watched Wil Lutz miss a 42-yard field goal. They had all the momentum, but Jim Harbaugh wanted more.
The Chargers decided to go for it on a fourth-and-1 at their own 41-yard line. Herbert was stuffed, and the Broncos took over on downs. That fourth-and-1 failure marked the beginning of the end for Los Angeles.
The Broncos went 41 yards on five plays and tied the game with a Courtland Sutton touchdown. Then, two plays into the Chargers' next possession, Herbert was sacked and fumbled away the ball. That turnover led to a Broncos field goal, which gave Denver a 20-17 lead. On the Chargers' next possession, Herbert threw an interception on fourth-and-6, setting up another Broncos field goal. Denver won, 23-17.
"The reason [the Broncos] won the football game is because Jim Harbaugh was an idiot! What are you doing?" 😳 @PriscoCBS #NFLPostgame pic.twitter.com/lj9iNV8ufd
"Yeah, it was the wrong decision, I've never — I can't think of a time I've ever been more mad at myself," Harbaugh said after the game.
Jim Harbaugh tells @RealFRamirez of the @SportingTrib that he takes the blame for the failed fourth down call and the loss. pic.twitter.com/Zc7XdX7DZN
Harbaugh is in the midst of his first eight-game losing streak if we include last season's playoffs. It's the longest losing streak of his career as a head coach in the NCAA or NFL.
"It's been a while since I've been this pissed after a game"
The Buffalo Bills at Los Angeles Rams on Monday night was a potential Super Bowl preview, and this game required a fifth quarter to determine a winner. Both teams scored touchdowns in the final two minutes to get the game to overtime, and the drama continued in the extra period.
The Rams won the overtime coin toss and elected to kick since both teams now receive a chance to possess the ball in the extra quarter. It looked like the Bills were well on their way to a touchdown to open overtime, but then James Cook III fumbled at the Rams' 22-yard line. It was recovered by Aaron Donald , and Matthew Stafford took over, needing just a field goal to win.
The Rams quickly got into enemy territory thanks to a 21-yard pickup from Puka Nacua . It was at the Bills' 35-yard line where Sean McVay began to feel comfortable. On second-and-10, he called for a short pass to Nacua, which picked up five yards. On third-and-5, he called a Kyren Williams run that got stuffed at the line of scrimmage. That set up a 48-yard Harrison Mevis field goal attempt for the win.
If "48-yard field goal attempt from Mevis" sounds familiar, it's because he missed a 48-yard field goal just last week against the Philadelphia Eagles . He also missed a 50-yard field goal in the first quarter on Monday. Now, a 48-yard field goal is definitely makeable, but certainly not a gimme. Sure enough, this potential game-winning kick was tipped by Bills pass rusher Greg Rousseau . The Bills then went 35 yards down the field and kicked a game-winning 45-yard field goal to hand the Rams a 37-34 loss.
McVay's conservative play-calling and decision to go for a 48-yard field goal with his struggling special teams was mind-boggling. Consider that the Rams had registered THREE STRAIGHT touchdown drives to end the fourth quarter. That includes a possession where L.A. went 63 yards down the field on eight plays with 1:30 remaining in regulation to send the game to overtime. Now, with the game on the line, McVay is choosing Mevis over the reigning NFL MVP?!
"It's been a while since I've been this pissed after a game," McVay said in his fiery postgame press conference.
This is about as upset as I’ve seen Sean McVay after a game. He blames himself for the conservative third and five call in OT and kicking the long field goal. There will likely be special teams changes this week. pic.twitter.com/Y06H3vLON1
As CBS Sports' Zach Pereles pointed out, the Rams rank dead last in special teams EPA this season:
McVay really trusted this unit over the TOP OFFENSE IN THE NFL. The Rams are now 2-3 because McVay played it too safe.
No one expected it, but the Eagles' Week 5 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London ended up being one of the best games of the week. It looked like the Eagles had registered a massive upset victory at the end of the fourth quarter, but jubilation turned to depression in the span of eight seconds.
With 1:35 remaining in the fourth quarter, down 16-14, Jalen Hurts led his offense 32 yards downfield on nine plays, setting Jake Elliott up for a 48-yard field goal. He nailed it, putting the Eagles up, 17-16, with eight seconds left on the clock.
On the kickoff, the Eagles elected to kick the ball in play instead of kicking it into/out of the end zone, allowing Ameer Abdullah an opportunity to make a play. And make a play he did. Abdullah broke loose for 53 yards to set Jaguars kicker Cam Little up with a game-winning 57-yard field goal.
JAGS HUGE KICK RETURN. They're in range for one more shot at a field goal! @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/XSWbKBTvW2
UNBELIEVABLE. JAGS WIN. WHAT JUST HAPPENED?!?! pic.twitter.com/O7x8JTgPeK
Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni accepted blame for the decision to put the kickoff in play and for the devastating loss as a whole.
"I didn't make the right decision, and I lost us that game, and that's what I said to our guys, and what hurts there is that the guys fought so hard and then I don't make the decision that I should make at the end of the game and I cost us that game," Sirianni said. "I put that fully on me."
Nick Sirianni says it crystal clear: He made the wrong decision on the kickoff and he owns it Wouldn’t go into the reasoning why he decided what he did pic.twitter.com/xy0QiyIF4c
So, why did Sirianni leave the ball in play? One could assume the Eagles wanted to allow a few of the eight seconds to run off the clock as the Jaguars returned the kickoff. The one thing you can't do is allow the returner to break loose, which is what Philly did. The 2-3 Eagles are now under .500 for the first time since 2021. Sunday's loss snapped a franchise-record streak of 76 games where the Eagles were .500 or better, per CBS Sports Research.
"That's my responsibility, nobody else's"
Without a doubt, the worst gaffe of the week — and maybe of the season — goes to Dan Quinn of the Washington Commanders . This is the kind of mistake where you may never look at your head coach the same again. It may be the first thing people point to when Quinn is eventually fired, because it was a sequence that warmed up his seat that much more.
The Commanders and New York Giants went to overtime in a rain-soaked Northwest Stadium with the score tied at 27 apiece. Giants kicker Dominic Zvada missed a 46-yard field goal to begin the extra period, while Washington was forced to punt after picking up just…

title: NFL rules former Ole Miss star, LSU target Zxavian Harris now eligible to join league as free agent
summary: The defensive tackle's return to the field could be coming soon, but fellow Da'Quan Wright is still waiting for news on any changes to his eligibility
full_text:
The NFL Management Council has ruled that former Ole Miss defensive tackle and NFL rookie Zxavian Harris is an eligible free agent and able to work out or sign with a franchise of his choosing, according to a recent memo obtained by Front Office Sports .
He was previously ruled ineligible to join an NFL team in September, but the league reversed that decision after Harris disputed its claim that he played college football this season. Since Harris never practiced at LSU, his intended school after being granted a preliminary eligibility injunction, the NFL has designated him as a free agent. He is free to join any team on its active roster or practice squad.
This comes after more than two dozen athletes who had signed professional contracts attempted to return to college after the NCAA's "five for five" ruling this summer .
LSU coach Lane Kiffin was in pursuit of several players, including Harris, Ole Miss tight end Da'Quan Wright and former LSU edge rusher Jack Pyburn , who's now on a three-year rookie deal with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after starring in the preseason.
LSU was expected to add Harris, a former Ole Miss standout, in August after a brief preseason stint with the New Orleans Saints following the Louisiana court ruling. The ruling allowed athletes from the Class of 2022 to receive temporary restraining orders to gain a fifth year of eligibility.
However, LSU decided not to add Harris and Wright to its roster in September after the SEC threatened to kick the Tigers out of the conference . At the time, CBS Sports reported that the SEC was weighing possible forfeiture of games , a legal challenge in federal court and even possible expulsion if LSU didn't back down.
At the time, expulsion was considered "extremely, extremely unlikely," but it spoke to "the level of frustration within the conference that it had even been uttered." The SEC later filed a federal lawsuit against head coach Lane Kiffin, athletic director Verge Ausberry, the university and others associated with it.
Harris was in training camp with the Saints after going undrafted in 2026. A four-star recruit in the 2022 signing class, Harris really broke out as a senior last fall. He was a key cog in the Rebels' defense — wreaking havoc in the middle of the line to the tune of 58 tackles, nine tackles for loss and three sacks. That was enough to get Harris invited to the NFL Scouting Combine in Indianapolis.
Per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero , Wright is not eligible yet under NFL rules. He reportedly worked out for the Green Bay Packers earlier this month , prior to the league's memo.
Drew Rosenhaus, Wright's agent, told ESPN last month that his client was waiting to hear from the NFL .
"When he left the (Cleveland) Browns , there was no doubt he'd be able to play at LSU," Rosenhaus said on The Pat McAfee Show . "We were very careful during the interim period where LSU was getting heat from the SEC not to sign with LSU at that point. We did not want to lose his eligibility to go back to the NFL. He did not sign with LSU while all this stuff was up in the air, but the league is still trying to decide if they're going to let him try out or join a team.
"We thought we'd be able to, but it's up in the air. I'm rooting for the young man. He just wants to play football."
At the time, Rosenhaus said multiple NFL teams were interested in Wright's services, but the league hadn't cleared him for an NFL return yet. That's evidenced by Wright's workout with the Packers last month .
author: Brad Crawford

title: Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson to miss multiple weeks with injury, per report
summary: Henderson was injured during Sunday's win over the Raiders
full_text:
The New England Patriots will be without one of their top two running backs for a while. According to a report from ESPN , TreVeyon Henderson suffered a high ankle sprain during last Sunday's win over the Las Vegas Raiders and is expected to miss multiple weeks. The injury does not require surgery, and he will not go on injured reserve, but he's going to miss several games.
Henderson missed the first game of the season with an ankle injury, but returned in Week 2. He split time with Rhamondre Stevenson over the last four games, totaling 163 yards and a touchdown on 42 carries while adding two catches for 22 yards.
Henderson totaled 1,132 yards and 10 touchdowns during his rookie season a year ago, but mostly worked behind Stevenson in training camp as the latter reportedly outperformed him. Stevenson was considered the more reliable pass-catcher and blocker, and Henderson continued to trail in snap share during these last few weeks before suffering the injury.
Back in Week 1, without Henderson, Stevenson had an 84.5% snap share during the Patriots' loss to the Seattle Seahawks , with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison working in behind him in limited roles. He took 70.7% of the snaps on Sunday against the Raiders, with the share bumping up following Henderson's departure. (Kiner's fumble may have played a role in that as well.)
The Patriots have games upcoming against the New York Jets , Chicago Bears and Miami Dolphins over the next three weeks. Stevenson should be expected to play a significant lead role during that time, with Kiner working as the No. 2 back and Larison perhaps being elevated from the practice squad for game days.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Who is the best WR in the NFL? How Puka Nacua stacks up vs. JSN, Ja'Marr after historic 'MNF'
summary: Revisiting our list of the top 10 wide receivers in football
full_text:
Before the season started, CBS Sports rolled out its top-10 rankings for players at every position on both offense and defense. Some of those rankings look extremely prescient five weeks into the NFL season. Others do not. That's just the way it goes. Football is an unpredictable game, and even those of us who observe it most closely and get a lot right still get a lot wrong a lot of the time.
We're not necessarily here to debate what we got right or wrong, but to revisit our lsit. Because so many wide receivers are off to such great starts this season and delivering jump-off-the-screen performances in big-time games, we wanted to see if there are any updates we can make just under a third of the way through the season.
So in the space below, we'll detail the updated top 10. Enjoy.
Honorable mentions (in no particular order): Malik Nabers , Tetairoa McMillan , Davante Adams , George Pickens , Garrett Wilson , Parker Washington , DeVonta Smith , Mike Evans , Christian Watson , A.J. Brown
Flowers is off to an insane start to the season. He's only played two full games so far (he missed one, left one early and played only 33% of the snaps in another), and he's yet to play a full complement of snaps with Lamar Jackson under center. Yet, he already has 26 catches for 405 yards and a pair of scores. He leads the NFL with 4.45 yards per route run, per Tru Media, and that number was even higher before he had to play a game with his backup quarterback. He's being used by Declan Doyle in a way that maximizes his skill set, and it's beautiful to watch.
Olave is tied for the NFL lead in catches with 39, and he's already got 537 yards (second) as well. He is a target vacuum in the Saints' high-volume passing offense, seeing a look on 26.3% of his routes, according to Tru Media. He's also generated an explosive play (gain of 15+ yards) on 20.4% of his targets, which is the highest mark of his career to date. He's worked more often on the perimeter this season than last (73.2% of his routes compared with 61.0%), but it hasn't stopped him from being a target hog.
London is a completely different — and absurdly good — player whenever Michael Penix Jr . is on the field for the Falcons. Penix has played in 17 games, starting 15 of them, over the last three years. In those games, London has caught 100 of 154 passes for 1,535 yards and eight touchdowns. He's seen a target on 33% of his routes and averaged 9.97 yards per target. All of those are elite, best-of-the-best type of numbers. Unfortunately, quarterback play has undermined his performance whenever someone other than Penix has been out there, but that shouldn't take away from what he does when he has solid QB play.
Collins is a monster-sized receiver (6-foot-4, 222 pounds) with a monster skill set. Utilized most often as a pure X receiver (he lines up out wide on 88% of his routes, per Tru Media), Collins is tasked with doing the hardest work a receiver can do. He makes it look relatively easy. He's only played in three games this year due to a hamstring injury, but he's gone for 19-249-3 and looked dominant doing it.
I think it's important to note that while St. Brown often gets labeled as "the best slot receiver" in football, he's actually played more often on the perimeter than on the inside in three straight seasons. He does everything, not just the slot stuff. He's obviously absurdly good in the slot, but he's also really good outside. He's gone for 100-plus catches and 1,100-plus yards in four consecutive seasons, and five 10-plus touchdowns in each of the last three. He's on pace to top all of those numbers again this year. He's the model of consistency.
It's easy to forget what Lamb did the last time he was fully healthy and had Dak Prescott under center for a full season: He led the NFL with 135 catches and piled up 1,749 yards and 12 touchdowns while being named a First Team All-Pro. This season, he's reminding people just how good he is. He's tied with Olave for the league lead in catches, and he also has 507 yards and four touchdowns. Had he not suffered a quad injury during last week's game against Tampa, those numbers would be even better. CeeDee does everything, and he does it all at an extremely high level.
Jefferson is another one who has missed some time this year, leaving one game after just seven snaps and missing another with an injury. In his other three games, he has 17 catches for 226 yards and three touchdowns. And one of those games came with a backup quarterback forced into emergency duty, and another came in a driving storm where pass volume was limited. We all know what Jefferson can do when he's healthy and has even adequate QB play. We'll likely see it through the rest of the year.
Stop me if you've heard this before, but we have another guy who has missed time here. Nacua sat out two games, and yet, after Monday night's 17-catch explosion against the Bills , he already has 31 grabs for 337 yards and a score this season. He led the league at 107.2 yards per game last year, and he's topping that this season at 112.3 per game. He's a physical force as a pass-catcher, run-after-catch guy and a blocker. The only thing keeping him from the top of this list is reliability. He misses too many games and too many plays due to trips to the medical tent.
Chase has also missed time this year, leaving one game after just 15 snaps due to a concussion. But he's still at 27-289-4, and he proves every week how much of a freak he is with some of the most ridiculous catches you can imagine. (See his touchdown grabs against the Texans and Dolphins for examples.) He's elite off the line, at the break and after the catch. There's nothing he doesn't do at the highest possible level. He's gone for at least 100-1,200-7 in each of the last three years, and even if he's not on that pace right now, he'll almost surely get there again. It's what he does.
JSN leads the NFL with 583 receiving yards, a year after leading the NFL with 1,793 receiving yards. He's gone for 75-plus yards in every game this season and 100-plus in four of five. He's also scored in four of five contests and has an NFL-high seven receiving touchdowns to date. It's impossible to cover him, and right now, he runs the best routes in the league. He wins so easily both off the line and at the break that it's almost hard to fathom how he's not wide the hell open on every single play. (And he usually is, anyway.) This crown will likely be passed back and forth between the top few guys for a while, but right now, JSN has it.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Five NFL teams getting the most out of their rookie class: Dolphins, Browns leading the way
summary: Miami is on a near-record pace with 14 first-year contributors, while the Ravens and the Chargers also lean heavily on newcomers
full_text:
Week 5 of the NFL season has come and gone, and we have a good sample size of snaps so far, including from rookies. Seven teams had more than one pick in the first round of the 2026 draft: Jets , Browns , Titans , Chiefs , Giants , Cowboys and Dolphins . So, how are those rookie classes performing in relation to others? There are several ways to measure and weigh the impact of rookie performers, but there is no substitute for playing time.
Before getting into the teams whose rookies have played the most, the five lowest snap totals belong to the Broncos (63), Rams (194), Seahawks (283), Eagles (403) and Cardinals (545).
Here are the rookie classes that have played the most snaps this season:
Baltimore's rookie class is headlined by offensive lineman Vega Ioane. He was playing right guard but was forced to start at center in Week 5, and the acquisition of Cam Jurgens will allow the Ravens to get the five best linemen on the field. Ioane is allowing pressure for every 32.4 pass blocking snaps, according to TruMedia.
Rookie tight ends Matthew Hibner and Josh Cuevas have helped the franchise absorb the losses of Isaiah Likely and Charlie Kolar . Wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane saw a significant workload in Week 1, but was then lost for the season due to injury.
Cornerback Chandler Rivers and edge rushers Zion Young and Ethan Burke have also factored into the defensive rotation.
New York made two selections in the top-10 overall: linebacker Arvell Reese and right guard Francis Mauigoa . Those two players have accounted for more than half of the Giants' rookie snap counts. Additionally, 22% of the rookie snap count has been played on special teams.
Reese has looked the part through five games. Mauigoa is allowing a pressure once every 18.7 pass blocking snaps, according to TruMedia. Cornerback Colton Hood has started two games for the team. Wide receiver Malachi Fields has been an asset in both the run and the pass. I wrote about Fields as one of the non-first-round picks who have taken on a large role this season.
Los Angeles is off to an unforeseen and uncharacteristic 0-5 start. The team's issues go well beyond injuries, but those, too, have taken a toll. When veteran center Tyler Biadasz suffered a season-ending injury prior to the season, it forced Day 2 selection Jake Slaughter into the starting lineup. Slaughter is allowing a pressure for every 25.7 pass blocking snaps, according to TruMedia.
Ten rookies have taken offensive or defensive snaps for the Chargers this season. Of the 612 offensive snaps, five offensive linemen have combined for all but 22.
Safety Genesis Smith and edge rusher Akheem Mesidor are fully immersed in the defensive rotation.
All of Cleveland's top-100 overall selections have delivered thus far. Spencer Fano and Austin Barber are starting at left tackle and right guard, respectively. Fano is allowing a pressure for every 23.1 pass blocking snaps, according to TruMedia. Barber is allowing a pressure for every 46.3 pass blocking snaps.
Wide receivers Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion rank in the top three on the team in each of the following receiving categories: receptions, yards and targets.
Safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren has seen his role expand with each passing week. His length and aggressiveness playing downhill have allowed the team to be more creative with personnel and blitz packages. McNeil-Warren often takes on the role of playing single high when the team opts for it.
Cleveland's five other draft selections have a combined 118 snaps; all but three of which have come on special teams.
Miami is on pace for 7,106 rookie snaps played this season, which is just off the pace for the most played in a season over the last decade. The Browns' 2016 rookie class played 7,185 snaps during a 16-game season. I previously wrote about that Browns class and other high-volume rookie classes over the last decade.
Linebacker Jacob Rodriguez leads all NFL players with 57 tackles. He, along with safety Michael Taaffe , cornerback Chris Johnson, and offensive guard Kadyn Proctor , has played 250+ snaps this season. Proctor is allowing a pressure for every 22.9 pass blocking snaps, per TruMedia.
Some of that is born out of necessity, as Miami has arguably the most talent-deficient roster in the league. It is one of three winless teams this season, after all.
Contributions go well beyond the team's first and second round picks, however. In addition to Taaffe, Miami has leaned heavily on rookie wide receivers Chris Bell , Kevin Coleman Jr . and Caleb Douglas , the latter of whom has missed time dealing with an injury.
In total, the team has played 14 rookies this season.
author: Josh Edwards

title: Rams vs. Bills thriller: Josh Allen accomplishes something he's never done before in Buffalo's OT win
summary: Buffalo's star QB snapped an 0-7 slump on Monday night
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills won a potential Super Bowl LXI preview on Monday night, defeating Matthew Stafford and the Los Angeles Rams , 37-34, in overtime. It was a remarkable back-and-forth affair that saw both offenses put up 400+ yards of total offense, both teams score touchdowns in the final two minutes, and both clubs make mistakes in overtime
This matchup proved that Bills quarterback Josh Allen is still one of the best players in the world. He completed 12 of 19 passes for 210 yards, one touchdown and one interception, while adding an incredible 121 yards rushing and another touchdown on the ground. However, the real headline is that Allen accomplished something he had never done before in his career — win in overtime.
Previously, Allen was 0-7 in overtime, the worst overtime record by a quarterback in NFL history (including playoffs), according to CBS Sports Research.
33-27 loss at Tampa Bay Buccaneers
33-30 loss vs. Minnesota Vikings
22-16 loss at New York Jets
37-34 loss at Philadelphia Eagles
33-30 loss at Denver Broncos (playoffs)
37-34 win at Los Angeles Rams
Allen's first overtime win is definitely one he will remember forever. The Rams won the overtime coin toss and elected to kick since both teams now receive a chance in the extra quarter. It looked like the Bills were well on their way to a touchdown to open overtime, thanks to a 57-yard gain from Khalil Shakir to get Buffalo down to the Rams' 22-yard line. But then James Cook III coughed up the ball for the second time, and it was recovered by Aaron Donald .
The Rams now needed just a field goal to win the game. Stafford and Co. got into the Bills' territory with ease, but then Sean McVay started getting conservative. On a third-and-5 from the Bills' 30-yard line, he called a Kyren Williams run that got stuffed at the line of scrimmage. That set up a 48-yard Harrison Mevis field goal attempt for the win.
A 48-yard field goal is definitely makeable, but certainly not a gimme — especially if you're Mevis . He missed a 48-yard field goal outdoors in Philly last week and missed a 50-yard field goal earlier on Monday night. His kick was tipped by the Bills' Greg Rousseau .
With new life, the Bills marched 35 yards down the field on five plays and set Tyler Bass up with a 45-yard field goal to move the Bills to 4-1, and earn Allen his first-ever overtime victory.
