title: Cam Ward isn't getting benched, but should Titans consider drafting a QB in 2027? History offers clues
summary: The former No. 1 pick has struggled through 22 NFL starts. Here's what other first-round QBs tell us about his future, and why Tennessee faces a complicated decision in 2027
full_text:
Cam Ward isn't going anywhere. After Sunday's 26-3 loss to Houston dropped the Titans to 0-5, Robert Saleh made it clear that benching the second-year quarterback isn't on the table. Tennessee remains committed to the former No. 1 overall pick, even as the offense continues to stumble its way through the season.
As CBS Sports' Jordan Dajani explained Monday , benching Ward wouldn't solve Tennessee's many problems. It would only make it harder to determine whether he's the team's long-term answer.
But there's a difference between believing in a young quarterback and seeing evidence he's getting better. Ward is 3-19 through 22 starts, and the numbers tell a story that goes well beyond wins and losses. So what does history tell us about how the future might look? And if Ward and the Titans can't right the ship, would the organization think about drafting a(nother) quarterback with a(nother) top pick?
To find an answer, I looked at first-round QBs since 2000, comparing their first 22 NFL starts with their next 22. The results offer some hope, although there's a pretty big difference between improving and becoming the franchise quarterback Tennessee thought it drafted.
Among 56 first-rounders who started at least 22 games in their first three seasons, Ward ranks tied for 51st in EPA per dropback (-0.15) and 52nd in yards per attempt (5.8). His 38% offensive success rate ranks 49th.
The unusual part? Ward hasn't been reckless with the football. His 1.4% interception rate is among the lowest in the group. But his 2.6% touchdown rate ranks tied for 50th, and he rarely generates explosive completions. Basically, he's avoiding interceptions without making enough plays to move the offense consistently.
Kyle Boller (No. 19, 2003)
Joey Harrington (No. 3, 2002)
Five of the nine quarterbacks in the table were selected No. 1 overall, and seven were top-three picks, a reminder that even the most highly regarded prospects aren't guaranteed immediate NFL success.
Josh Allen and Jared Goff both struggled early in their NFL careers before becoming high-level starters. But after 22 starts, Allen was already at 0.00 EPA per dropback, while Goff was at -0.05, both substantially better than Ward's -0.15. (EPA per dropback measures how much a quarterback's passing plays increase or decrease his team's expected points, with positive numbers indicating more productive plays.) Allen and Goff then made another jump in starts 23-44, improving to +0.14 and +0.13, respectively.
Ward's closer comparisons aren't nearly as reassuring. Of six first-round quarterbacks who had similar struggles as Ward over their first 22 starts, five improved their EPA per dropback. That's the good news. The bad news? Only Bryce Young and David Carr actually climbed into positive territory.
Young does provide some reasons for hope: His EPA improved from -0.20 to +0.02, while his yards per attempt went from 5.5 to 6.4. Alex Smith offers a different lesson. He actually got worse over his next 22 starts before eventually developing into a productive veteran, both later in his 49ers career and after he was traded to the Chiefs .
So patience can pay off. But improvement doesn't automatically mean a team found its long-term starter. What would that improvement look like for Ward? Here's how three quarterbacks performed over their next 22 starts, with results ranging from modest improvement to a significant turnaround.
There's another layer to Ward's story, one I remember from evaluating him in college.
Ward was No. 3 on my final 2025 big board , behind Travis Hunter and Abdul Carter . The arm talent was special, as was his ability to throw accurately off-platform and from any arm angle. And from Washington State in 2022 through his final season at Miami , he became noticeably better at getting through reads, navigating the pocket and playing on time.
Still, the same concerns kept showing up . He could lock onto his first read, pass up an easy completion or leave a clean pocket looking for something bigger. Those plays were often thrilling in college. Against NFL defenses, they can turn into sacks or wasted downs.
The numbers tell a similar story. Entering his final college season, Ward had a First-Round Readiness Score (FRED) of just 6.8 , nowhere near the historical first-round benchmark of 50. (FRED measures how closely a quarterback's college resume resembles those of previous first-round picks.) But after his remarkable 2024 season at Miami, Ward's score jumped to 49.3, an improvement of 42.5 points in one season.
For perspective , Allen had already reached 51.6 before his final college season, while Patrick Mahomes was at 55.7. Ward, meanwhile, went from nowhere near the first-round benchmark to QB1 in one season. That doesn't diminish what he accomplished. It does remind us how much of his evaluation rested on a late breakout, even as his film showed real development.
Now, Tennessee needs Ward to make another jump. But they also have to consider what happens if it never comes.
That brings us to the 2027 draft, where the latest "can't miss" class has been less-than-stellar depending on where you've focused your attention through the first six weeks .
As we sit here in the middle of October, my top four quarterbacks in the '27 class are Darian Mensah , Trinidad Chambliss , Drew Mestemaker and Jayden Maiava , with CJ Carr and Julian Sayin tied for fifth. Dante Moore and Arch Manning , my QB1 and QB2 over the summer, have been inconsistent, and Moore hasn't played since suffering a concussion vs. USC in late September.
By the way, of the names above, only Sayin had a FRED score north of 50 coming into the season. And while those scores are neither draft grades nor indicators of NFL success, they do further illuminate the problem: The Titans could be choosing between a talented quarterback who hasn't yet delivered and another talented quarterback who arrives in town with many more unanswered questions.
Tennessee shouldn't use a first-round pick on a quarterback because Ward has struggled. They also shouldn't pass on one just because they used the No. 1 pick on Ward two years earlier.
If Ward starts the remaining 12 games, as Saleh seems to suggest he will, he'll have 34 career starts by the time Tennessee has to make that decision. The team doesn't need him to become Josh Allen by January -- hell, Bryce Young was benched three games into his second season. He got another chance a few weeks later, and now two years after that, he's playing every bit like a franchise quarterback.
The lesson: These things take time, man.
For the Titans, though, there needs to be more than the occasional glimpse of hope. They need to see steady improvement, the kind that suggests Ward is on his way to becoming that guy .
And if those improvements don't happen, Tennessee will start over. It happens across the league every year. There's a fine line between patience and hoping things to be, mostly because hope ain't a plan. And waiting without evidence of a turnaround? That's something else entirely.
author: Ryan Wilson

title: Top 10 best NFL free agent acquisitions through Week 5: Kenneth Walker III, Mike Evans on top
summary: A look at the biggest game-changing free agents through the first five weeks of the 2026 NFL season and how they've impacted their teams
full_text:
Free agency in the National Football League is different from almost any other North American professional sport. In basketball or baseball, an impactful player going from one team to another is seemingly almost guaranteed to be a very similar player in their new home.
That's not always the case in football with the major differences in how NFL teams organize their schemes, playbooks and play calls. However, the free agents who continue to ball out in their new homes really pop. Obviously, the first two that come to mind are two game-changing contributors to two undefeated teams: Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III and San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans . Walker is extending quarterback Patrick Mahomes ' career with his historic rushing production early on, and Evans is helping Purdy make an early-season MVP case.
Which 2026 free agents stand out as game-changers for their new squads through the first five weeks of the new season? Let's take a look at the top 10.
Contract: Three years, $42 million with $25 million guaranteed
The Carolina Panthers (2-2) are atop the NFC South through the first five weeks of the 2026 NFL season, and it's partially because of Devin Lloyd's playmaking. In Carolina's Week 2 demolition of the Cooper Rush-quarterbacked Atlanta Falcons , Lloyd racked up nine tackles, a sack, two interceptions, a pick-six and three passes defensed. That made Lloyd the first player since Zach Brown in 2012 with multiple interceptions, a pick-six and a sack all in the same game.
Even though the Panthers had a Week 5 bye, their seven takeaways are tied for the 10th-most in the NFL. Lloyd has a large impact on that statistic.
DEVIN LLOYD JUST HAD ONE OF THE GREATEST LINEBACKER PERFORMANCES IN NFL HISTORY 9 TKL, 2 TFL, 2 INT, 1 SACK, 1 TD, 1 QBH, 3 PD Carolina may have landed one of the best defensive pickups of the offseason. pic.twitter.com/4BGRbQ7jxq
Contract: Three years, $26 million with $23 million guaranteed
The signing of linebacker Nakobe Dean added some much-needed playmaking to the Las Vegas Raiders ' defense. In 2025, their 16 takeaways were tied for the ninth fewest in the league. This season, the Raiders have 10 takeaways, which are tied for the second most behind only the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks ' 11.
Dean is a major reason for that with an NFL-most three forced fumbles. It is a little worrisome that the 2026 Raiders are the second team in NFL history, along with the 2007 Denver Broncos, to allow an increasing points and yardage total in each of their first five games of a season, but they're 3-2 through five weeks. That definitely is exceeding all expectations for Las Vegas early on, after they had the first overall pick in the draft in the spring.
Contract: Three years, $49.5 million with $32.39 million guaranteed
The Cleveland Browns have struggled to put together capable offenses for years for a variety of reasons. Cleveland's offense is still bogged down by physically diminished Deshaun Watson at quarterback, but left guard Zion Johnson is playing a strong brand of football, particularly in pass protection.
Through five weeks, Johnson has not surrendered a sack, and he has allowed just three quarterback pressures and one quarterback hit on 184 pass-blocking snaps. That's good enough for Pro Football Focus to grade Johnson as the league's fifth-best pass-blocking guard with an 80.1 pass-blocking grade. Finding quality offensive play in 2026 can be difficult, but the Browns hit on Johnson.
Contract: Three years, $40 million with $26 million guaranteed
Despite losing starting quarterback Jaxson Dart with a season-ending knee injury in Week 2, the New York Giants remain in first place in the NFC East division through five weeks with a 3-1-1 record. Free agency acquisition tight end Isaiah Likely is a big reason why New York has been able to maintain any semblance of a coherent passing game despite fill-in quarterback Jameis Winston ranking second-to-last in the league in completion percentage at 57.6%.
Likely's four receiving touchdowns are tied for the fourth-most in the NFL and rank as tied for the most among tight ends leaguewide. His 19 receiving first downs are the most among all tight ends through five weeks this season. With No. 1 wide receiver Malik Nabers still finding his footing in 2026 after returning from a torn ACL, Likely has been a godsend for the Giants' passing game.
Contract: Three years, $81 million fully guaranteed
The Las Vegas Raiders are 3-2 in 2026, and if the regular season ended today, they would be the last team in the playoffs. Much of their early-season success is because of their No. 9 scoring offense (26.4 points per game). One of the key components of that success has to do with the team's improved offense, anchored by three-time Pro Bowl center Tyler Linderbaum . In 2025, the Raiders allowed a pressure rate of 40.5%, the fifth-highest in the entire league. That rate has declined slightly, down to 38.1% in 2026, but it has made a huge difference, allowing 38-year-old Kirk Cousins to perform like a fringe top-10 quarterback statistically this season.
Linderbaum has been a huge piece of that improvement with Pro Football Focus grading him as the eighth-best pass-blocking center in football with a 72.9 pass-blocking grade.
Contract: One year, $3.095 million with $2.5 million guaranteed
There may not be a better value free agency signing in 2026 than Atlanta Falcons edge rusher Cameron Thomas . The 26-year-old former third-round pick of the Arizona Cardinals had just three starts through his first four seasons after playing for three teams -- the Cardinals, the Kansas City Chiefs and the Cleveland Browns -- in his first four seasons. New Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski brought Thomas with him from Cleveland to Atlanta for cheap, and Thomas has more than rewarded Stefanski's belief in him as an every-game starter in 2026.
Thomas' 22 quarterback pressures are tied for ninth in the NFL, and he also has 2.0 sacks this season. Thomas has multiple pressures in all five games this season and at least three in each of the last four games. His arrival is one of the reasons the Falcons are much more energetic in 2026 than they were in 2025.
Contract: Three years, $60 million with $19 million guaranteed
It has long felt like the Cincinnati Bengals were a few pieces on defense away from getting back to the postseason with Joe Burrow , Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins leading their high-flying offense. That's why the Bengals went on a spending spree defensively this past offseason, trading the 10th overall pick in the draft for defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence and then signing both edge rusher Boye Mafe and defensive tackle Jonathan Allen in free agency.
Mafe has been one of the biggest game changers in football this season. His 3.0 sacks through five games are great, but he's also making a consistent impact as a pass rusher on a regular basis. Mafe's 25 quarterback pressures rank as the sixth most in the entire NFL, just ahead of Danielle Hunter's 23 and just behind Greg Rousseau's 29. He is playing like one of the NFL's best pass rushers through five weeks. That's money well spent.
Contract: One year, $11.3 million fully guaranteed
Kirk Cousins still has his fastball at 38 years old. Cousins' 12 touchdown passes this season are tied with Jared Goff for the second-most in the entire league, and he trails league leader Brock Purdy's 13 by just one scoring strike. His 1,269 yards passing rank as the seventh most in the league, while his 100.7 passer rating is ninth in the NFL. Beyond the box score, Cousins is also providing an intangible impact as 2026 first overall pick Fernando Mendoza's mentor this season. His presence is allowing Mendoza to develop on the bench while easing his way into life in the NFL. The lessons Mendoza is learning from the four-time Pro Bowler now will likely pay dividends for the Raiders' franchise for years to come.
Contract: Three years,…
author: Garrett Podell

title: Who can win Super Bowl 61? Identifying contenders outside of top tier that can hoist Lombardi Trophy
summary: Moving past heavy hitters like the Chiefs and 49ers leaves a dangerous second tier featuring the Jaguars, Bengals and more
full_text:
We are over one-fourth of the way through the 2026 NFL season, and it's going by fast. What have we learned through the first five weeks? Well, the San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks are still pretty good, and the Kansas City Chiefs have reinvented themselves offensively with Kenneth Walker III . Those are three obvious Super Bowl favorites, but which teams offer some value?
Let's examine the "second tier" of Super Bowl contenders. For this exercise, we will eliminate the top six favorites to hoist the Lombardi trophy over at DraftKings Sportsbook. That includes the Los Angeles Rams , San Francisco 49ers, Baltimore Ravens , Buffalo Bills , Kansas City Chiefs and Seattle Seahawks. Now, we are left with teams that have odds of at least +1200.
Below, we will examine the Super Bowl odds for seven teams that should make the playoffs, but could also be considered legitimate sleepers.
Odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook
The Detroit Lions actually have the second-shortest odds to win the NFC North right now, so do with that what you will. Dan Campbell just registered his first road win of the season on Sunday, as Detroit dominated the Arizona Cardinals , 45-21. However, beating up on a bad team doesn't exactly quell all concerns.
The Lions may lead the NFL in sacks (20), but they still rank dead last in total defense, allowing 404.4 total yards per game. Even with the 21 points allowed on Sunday, Detroit still ranks bottom four in scoring defense with 29.6 points allowed per game. This Lions team is unfortunately reminiscent of recent Lions teams. Jared Goff commands a lethal offense headlined by Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown , but it's hard to believe Kelvin Sheppard's defense has the ability to support a legitimate contender. With that said, Sunday's performance against Arizona was good.
It's tough to evaluate the Chicago Bears without Caleb Williams under center. In fact, we got to watch Williams for one game, and then he was injured in a monsoon that made it nearly impossible to move the ball. That one full game was pretty impressive, though. He accounted for four total touchdowns while the offense dropped 552 total yards.
When this Bears team is healthy, they are tough to keep up with offensively. Williams can sling the rock, and D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai make up one of the fiercest rushing duos in the NFL. I do have some concerns about this Bears defense, however. The Green Bay Packers were one of the worst teams in the NFL through four weeks, and then Jordan Love came out and dropped 367 passing yards, two touchdowns and 31 total points on Chicago in a 24-point blowout victory.
Points per game differential
Out of every team on this list, the Denver Broncos are the most frustrating to watch. Take their Week 3 matchup against the Rams, for example. They go down 16-0 at halftime, only to drop 30 points in the second half and win the game. The Rams weren't the Broncos' only impressive victory this season. Don't forget they defeated Trevor Lawrence and the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 2.
Sean Payton took back play-calling duties from Davis Webb this past week, but it didn't help. Despite the come-from-behind victory against the winless Los Angeles Chargers , the Broncos recorded just 224 yards of total offense and went 1 of 12 on third downs. Yikes. Bo Nix threw for just 123 yards and one touchdown.
I feel like all the pieces are in place for the Broncos to eventually become a legitimate contender. Don't forget that they were in the AFC Championship game last year, and probably would have made the Super Bowl if Nix didn't injure his ankle in the divisional round. Nix can make all the throws you want, but he's not seeing the field too well right now and is not quick enough on the trigger. It wouldn't shock me if he starts building some momentum soon. Then, he has some decent weapons around him with Courtland Sutton , Jaylen Waddle and RJ Harvey -- who entered this past week leading the entire NFL in yards after catch. Hey coach Payton, why did you throw the ball to him just once on Sunday?
The Minnesota Vikings have to be one of the most fascinating teams in the NFL. On the one hand, they are undefeated at 5-0 with a defense that ranks first in scoring and third in total defense; on the other, Kevin O'Connell's offense ranks in the bottom six with 283.0 total yards per game. The Vikings have scored the fewest touchdowns (nine) during a 5-0 start since the 2003 Carolina Panthers , per CBS Sports Research.
New quarterback Kyler Murray did have his best game of the season this past Sunday against the New Orleans Saints , completing 80% of his passes for 229 yards and one touchdown while also rushing for 51 yards. Hopefully that's a sign of things to come, because the Vikings can be a legitimate Super Bowl contender if Murray morphs back into his Pro Bowl self. He has legit weaponry around him with Justin Jefferson , Jordan Addison T.J. Hockenson and now Odell Beckham Jr . Watch out.
Drake Maye is back after giving the NFL quite the scare to begin the season. He threw for 374 yards, four touchdowns, zero interceptions and also rushed for a touchdown in the 45-17 beatdown of the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday and became the first New England Patriots quarterback to put up that kind of stat line in a single game. He's accounted for eight total touchdowns and two turnovers over the past two contests, after scoring one touchdown with seven turnovers in the first three games of the season.
I also think this Patriots defense is almost being slept on. For them to do what they did to the Raiders without Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis III was impressive. Then, I feel as though we've seen this defensive front take over at times. The football world isn't talking enough about the impacts rookie Gabe Jacas and Elijah Ponder have made. Ponder has 4.5 sacks over the last four games!
It feels like we are still figuring out what the Cincinnati Bengals are. The revamped defense started hot by forcing turnovers on three of their first four possessions of the season, but surprisingly allowed 30 points in a loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 3. What we can't deny is that the Bengals are 3-2, which is their best five-game start since 2021 -- the year they reached the Super Bowl.
Joe Burrow is still one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL, while Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are still the best receiving duo when healthy. Cincy's defense currently ranks outside the top 20, but there's a real opportunity to make a statement against Lamar Jackson and the Ravens in Week 7 following the bye.
Sunday's thrilling win in London moved the Jaguars to 4-1, but it did reveal some red flags about this team. The Jags probably should have dominated a Philadelphia Eagles squad that was without Lane Johnson , Drew Kendall , Saquon Barkley , DeVonta Smith and Jonathan Greenard, among others, but instead needed a borderline miraculous 53-yard kick return and a last-second 57-yard field goal to win.
The Jaguars' red-zone offense on Sunday was embarrassing. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone vs. Philly, including two trips where Liam Coen's offense couldn't score from the 1-yard line. With that being said, if the Jaguars can clean some of this stuff up, this team could make a serious run. Trevor Lawrence is a legitimate franchise quarterback, and he has a nice supporting cast in Parker Washington , Jakobi Meyers , Josh Cameron and sometimes Brian Thomas Jr. . Bhayshul Tuten is better than I expected as a lead back, and then Anthony Campanile's unit ranks No. 1 against the run and is tied for second in turnover differential.
This is the best team in the AFC South, and no longer some sleeper in the AFC.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: How an initial 2026 NFL Draft embarrassment actually ended up benefitting the Steelers
summary: So far, Pittsburgh has benefited from what transpired back in April
full_text:
Omar Khan's fourth NFL Draft as the Pittsburgh Steelers ' general manager could not have started worse, or at least that's how it initially looked after Philadelphia Eagles GM Howie Roseman swooped in and snatched the player Khan and the Steelers were about to select with the 20th overall pick.
Adding insult to injury was the fact that the entire process was recorded and immediately dispersed into the universe. In a matter of minutes, seemingly everyone had seen Makai Lemon chatting on the phone with Khan before Pittsburgh was leapfrogged by Philadelphia, which drafted Lemon after pulling off a trade with, of all teams, the Dallas Cowboys , a longtime division rival.
The move was viewed as another example of Roseman's excellence at his job. Conversely, it was seen as a complete embarrassment in Pittsburgh.
Inside the Eagles draft room as they’re trying to Makai Lemon on the phone 👀 🎥: Eagles/YouTube pic.twitter.com/E484AsWiKA
#Steelers GM Omar Khan on calling WR Makai Lemon and then getting jumped by the #Eagles : “When the draft happens, there’s a lot of excitement that goes on. There was no ill intent. We made the call… The draft throws curveballs at you in every round, trust me. It happens… https://t.co/qyTNOuoRuo pic.twitter.com/qKIKuEGS6X
That sequence of events looks much different now, however. While it's still too early to say anything definitive, the Steelers are currently benefiting from what transpired six months ago.
The Steelers quickly pivoted to another need. They drafted offensive tackle Max Iheanachor , who was initially described as extremely talented yet extremely raw. Iheanachor, who was born in Nigeria and moved to the United States at 13, did not play football until he joined East Los Angeles College's team in 2021.
Iheanachor quickly developed into one of the top-ranked JUCO players, which led to him joining Arizona State's football team in 2023. He started in five games that season, became a full-time starter in 2024 and was named second-team All-Big 12 in 2025.
Iheanachor was met with early adversity with the Steelers after he sustained an injury during training camp. While the injury temporarily stunted his growth, it didn't stop the Steelers from trading Broderick Jones to the Cowboys in a move that showed how the Steelers felt about their rookie right tackle.
It didn't take long for McCarhty to insert Iheanachor into the starting lineup. In Week 3, Iheanachor came in and helped Pittsburgh rip off 411 yards and 30 points in a win over the Bengals . Since Iheanachor has taken over at starting right tackle, Pittsburgh's offense has averaged 29.3 points, 375 total yards and 119 rushing yards per game after averaging 11.5 points, 249.5 yards and 74.5 rushing yards in its first two games.
"Max is a talented young man. I think that's evident," McCarthy said after Pittsburgh's win over the Bengals. "His injury was a setback in training camp, but he's ready. It was time to give him that opportunity."
After missing out on Lemon and taking a lineman in the first round, everyone in the world knew that the Steelers were going to draft a receiver in the second round. Bernard was projected as the Steelers' best option at receiver entering Day 2 , but the question was whether or not he would actually still be on the board when Pittsburgh was on the clock with the 47th pick.
Fortunately for the Steelers, he was, and Khan was able to draft him without another team swooping in this time.
From a ranking standpoint, there was a considerable drop-off after Bernard (as it turned out, another receiver wouldn't be drafted after him until Antonio Williams went to Washington with the 71st pick). The Steelers, however, remained patient, and their patience was ultimately rewarded after watching two other receivers ( De'Zhaun Stribling and KC Concepcion ) go off the board early in the second round. They would be the last two receivers taken until Bernard was drafted by Pittsburgh.
The 6-foot-1 Bernard didn't put up big numbers in college, which is one of the reasons why seven receivers were drafted ahead of him. What he lacked in numbers, however, he made up for in versatility and reliability, among other things. He was tabbed before the draft as an ideal complementary receiver, which is what the Steelers needed alongside DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman .
Bernard is an excellent route runner, has reliable hands, and can line up on the outside and in the slot. He is also a student of the game, which helped him quickly earn Aaron Rodgers's trust .
The beginning of training camp consisted of Bernard getting limited reps with the first-team offense, while Roman Wilson got the lion's share of the work. He showed his potential in the preseason, however, making a 25-yard catch in his preseason debut and scoring his first career touchdown in Pittsburgh's preseason finale.
Bernard didn't catch a pass in Week 1 and caught just seven passes during Pittsburgh's first four games. On Sunday, though, Bernard stepped up with Pittman inactive and Wilson and Ben Skowronek leaving the game with injuries. He caught six passes for 80 yards while helping the Steelers' record a 34-22 win over the Colts .
Aaron Rodgers showing off the elusiveness @INDvsPIT on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/bUqpkTsr6H
With Pittman, Wilson and Skowronek already ruled out for Pittsburgh's upcoming game, Gernard is expected to continue to get opportunities to shine.
"Football comes easy to him," McCarthy said Monday when asked about Bernard. "I think there's some young-guy mistakes he made yesterday, but you can see it coming. I think he's acclimated very well to the offense, the ability to play all three positions -- he sticks his nose in there in the run game, too. I've been very, very impressed."
The third receiver drafted, Lemon was tasked with helping the Eagles replace AJ Brown , who was traded to New England this offseason. So far, Roseman's rebuild at receiver hasn't worked out.
Through five games, the Eagles' offense is 28th in the NFL in passing. Jalen Hurts is averaging just 187 passing yards per game. In his last two games, Hurts completed 49.3% of his passes, an inexcusable percentage for a high school quarterback, let alone for a former Super Bowl MVP.
Hurts could play better, but the issues go well beyond him. For starters, he's playing for his third offensive coordinator (Sean Mannion) in three years. Philadelphia's offensive line recently saw the retirement of Lane Johnson and the trade of Cam Jurgens . Saquon Barkley , a 2,000-yard rusher two years ago, has missed time due to injury.
Philadelphia's receivers haven't pulled their weight, either. That includes Lemon, who has caught just 15 of 22 targets for 108 yards. He is coming off his most productive game so far, though. He caught five passes for 43 yards in Sunday's loss to the Jaguars .
Excellent hands from Makai Lemon. pic.twitter.com/xNQsFslFk1
From the outside, it appears that Lemon's slow start can at least partly be attributed to Philadelphia's issues around him. In addition to the other issues mentioned above, Lemon isn't getting much help from his fellow receivers in terms of creating space for him. He also faces the burden of being a first-round pick.
The short answer is no. The Steelers ended up drafting two players who are currently making an impact. Iheanachor is a starter, and Bernard currently is too, given Pittsburgh's current injuries at receiver. It's safe to say that the Steelers wouldn't be 3-2 if it wasn't for their two rookies.
Conversely, the Eagles are 2-3 and are in the midst of a disappointing season. Until Lemon and the Eagles turn things around, Roseman, not Khan, will be the one who will have to defend his decisions from Day 1 of the 2026 NFL Draft.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: NFL Week 6 picks and score predictions: Seahawks destroy Broncos, Eagles lose again, Cowboys stun Packers
summary: Here's your weekly dose of John Breech's NFL picks
full_text:
I don't think four coaches from the same division have ever been fired on the same day, but if it's ever going to happen, now would be the time, and yes, I am talking about the NFC East.
If the NFC East ceases to exist, it's because the entire division imploded in Week 5 with possibly the most disastrous week for any division ever:
I feel like the play this week is to ride this wave of incompetence and pick against every NFC East team.
So will I actually do that? Let's get to the Week 6 picks and find out.
Actually, before we get to the picks, here's a quick reminder that you can check out the weekly picks from every CBSSports.com NFL expert by clicking here . If you don't click over, I won't be offended. However, I will be offended if you don't sign up for CBSSports.com's NFL newsletter, which I'm in charge of writing.
If you do sign up, it's like an early Halloween treat for both of us: I get more sign-ups and you get an email from me twice a week. If you want to subscribe, all you have to do is click here and enter your email address . I promise that link takes you to the newsletter sign up page and not to the sign up page for the newsletter about small cats that I'm thinking about starting.
Alright, let's get to the picks.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
If the NFL ever decides to have two head coaches battle each other in a steel cage, I nominate these two. I don't know why the NFL would ever do that, but I just want to get ahead of things in case this happens.
They might not admit it, but there is no bigger coaching beef in the NFL right now than Mike Macdonald vs. Sean Payton and we wouldn't have even known about it if not for a hot mic incident involving Macdonald from earlier this year. During the incident, here's what we found out:
Payton hated everything that happened so much that he essentially banned fans from filming anything at the Broncos' training camp after that.
These signs greet #Broncos fans at training camp. A security official said the great majority of fans are following rules. The official said fans can get a warning initially and nobody is in jeopardy of being evicted unless actions “excessive.” Nobody was said to be tossed Friday pic.twitter.com/cswT91vnvk
Again, this all happened in 2024, and now that you're caught up, that brings us to the fallout (And if you somehow missed this very real story, we've got all the details here ).
Macdonald apologized for the fact that his comments about the situation leaked out and Payton responded to that by pretending like it wasn't a big deal, but it's definitely a big deal. It's been two years, but I still think Macdonald is mad about the fact that another team was going to accuse him of cheating, especially since it came just before he was about to serve as the head coach in his FIRST NFL GAME ever.
OK, now let's fast forward to this week. Going into this game, Macdonald has one of the best defenses in the NFL and they get to face a Broncos offense that can't get out of its own way this year. One reason the Broncos' offense has been struggling is because they keep getting off to slow starts. They've scored just 23 points in the first half this year (4.6 points per game), which is tied with the Titans -- THE TITANS -- for the fewest in the NFL.
Last week, Macdonald was probably thrilled to see that Payton decided to take over play-calling duties in Denver, because that means he can now take out two years of anger on the Broncos' coach. I was going to predict a blowout here for Seattle, but the game is in Denver, and I don't quite trust Sam Darnold against the Broncos' defense, so I'll say a 10-point Seahawks win.
PICK: Seahawks (-3) 27-17 over Broncos
The Jaguars loved playing in London in Week 5 so much that they're sticking around for another game. The Jags will actually be making some NFL history Sunday and that's because they're going to become the first team ever to play back-to-back international "home" games. The Jags have played two consecutive games in London before, but in the past, they've played one as the road team and one as the home team. This time, they'll be the home team in both games.
I have no idea why I'm telling you any of this. I think I just needed to stall so I could decide who I actually want to pick to win this game, and now, I'm ready.
Last week, Robert Saleh called the Texans the best 0-4 team in NFL history and I don't think he was kidding.
If there's one thing I've learned about the Texans over the years, it's that there is no team better than them at losing their first few games of the season and then bouncing back to make the playoffs. In 2023, they started the season 0-2 before turning things around just in time to win the division with a 10-7 record. In 2025, they started the season 0-3 and still somehow managed to make the playoffs.
At this point, I'm starting to think the Texans are just seeing how far they can push things. If they can make the playoffs after an 0-3 start, why not 0-4?
One thing you should keep in mind about the Texans is that they're about five plays away from being 4-1.
Basically, if NFL games were only 58 minutes long instead of 60, the Texans would be 4-1. I will definitely talk to Roger Goodell about possibly making that change on the Texans' behalf, but that seems like a long shot, so if anyone in Houston is reading, please do NOT count on that happening.
The Texans have a chance to completely turn their season around this week. They just traded for Marvin Harrison Jr., DeMeco Ryans just started calling defensive plays again, and if they win here, they'll only be two games out of first place heading into Week 7, which is about all you can ask for when you open a season with four straight losses.
I'm going to say the Texans get their season back on track with a win here.
PICK: Texans (+3) 20-17 over Jaguars
It has been a rough week for the Eagles: They blew a win against the Jaguars, they have no healthy running backs on their roster, and now, they have to fly back from London and face a situation that no team has ever won in.
The Eagles will be going into Week 6 after playing in London and they'll be facing a Panthers team that will be coming off a bye. This will mark just the fifth time in NFL history that a team coming off an international game has had to play a team coming off a bye, and uh, I have some bad news for everyone in Philadelphia: The team coming off the international game has gone 0-4.
And just when you thought it couldn't get any worse for the Eagles, I have more bad news: The team coming off the international trip has averaged just 15.25 points per game, and the ugly part is that they've been outscored 70-30 over the first three quarters in those four games. I feel like the Eagles should file a protest over this part of their schedule, but I'm not sure who they would even file the protest with.
The problem with this specific situation is that the team coming back from Europe usually needs a small adjustment period. The jet lag after the flight back to the United States usually lasts a day or two, which means it can impact practice for your next game.
On the other hand, the Panthers have been sitting at home since Oct. 5 celebrating their Week 4 win over the Lions in the Cat Bowl. I mean, just think about that: Would you rather be dealing with jet lag or celebrating a win in the Cat Bowl? That's a rhetorical question. You don't have to answer. We all have imaginary Cat Bowl celebrations all the time.
Not only do the Panthers have the scheduling advantage here, but they might actually be the better team. Through four weeks, Carolina's biggest weakness is that its defense can't stop the run. The Panthers are surrendering 156.5 yards per game on the ground, which is the second-highest number in the NFL, but if there's one team that might not be able to take advantage of that, it's the Eagles. With Saquon Barkley and Tank Bigsby out, the Eagles were down to their third-string running back (Will Shipley)…
author: John Breech

title: What we learned in NFL Week 5: Mike Evans is perfect fit with Brock Purdy, Josh Allen extends MVP lead
summary: Plus, this NFL Draft class is looking excellent early
full_text:
There are stars on Hollywood Boulevard, so, naturally, when the Rams made not one but two blockbuster trades, acquiring Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie , and the Chargers made the biggest coordinator hire in Mike McDaniel -- both dramatic all-in moves -- plenty of eyes and attention went to Southern California.
The Patriots have run football for much of the 21st century and are coming off a Super Bowl berth, so, naturally, when they traded for A.J. Brown , plenty of eyes and attention went to Beantown.
The Chiefs have run the NFL for much of the last eight years, so, naturally, when they signed Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III to take the burden off a recovering Patrick Mahomes , plenty of eyes and attention went to Kansas City.
We love superlatives: "best" offseason, "worst" offseason, "most interesting" signing, "most surprising" team ... the list goes on.
How about one that just made sense? Mike Evans to the 49ers has been a perfect marriage of talent, tendencies and scheme.
As we sort through who's legit and who's not at this still-early point in the season, we can also group the legit teams into tiers of "playoff legit" and "Super Bowl legit." At 5-0 and coming off a road win at the defending champs, the 49ers are "Super Bowl legit." Evans, who left Tampa Bay after 12 legendary years, is getting exactly what he was looking for: a place where he can contend for a title while being a huge contributor.
As for the 49ers' side of things? Well, after Evans went for seven catches, 113 yards, a touchdown and a two-point conversion against Seattle, Kyle Shanahan put it best:
"That's exactly why he's here."
These are the six lessons we learned in Week 5.
Listen, sometimes you have to toot your own horn: The 49ers signing Mike Evans was one of my favorite moves this offseason . Yes, I understood the injury/age concerns, but the fit was perfect: big, downfield wide receiver for a quarterback ( Brock Purdy ) who's more than willing to give his guys chances downfield.
And in Week 5 against the Seahawks -- a potential NFC Championship matchup -- Evans dominated. On the 49ers' final touchdown drive alone, Purdy and Evans connected four times for 75 yards, plus the two-pointer.
Mike Evans is FEASTING today 💪 @SFvsSEA on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/plnciLv8D5
MIKE. EVANS. AGAIN. @SFvsSEA on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/7OlyUgWcEV
These two plays, within a minute of each other, are perfect examples of why Evans is so valuable. He can win on big in-breaking routes, and he can win on straight-line shots on the outside. What an absolute stud. He's a future Hall of Famer who's showing he still has a TON left in the tank. Last year, the 49ers scored 26 points combined in three games against Seattle (including playoffs). Sunday, they scored 32.
In Shanahan's system, the ability to attack the intermediate and deep-intermediate areas takes things to the next level. Currently, Evans is catching 2.6 passes per game on throws 10-25 yards downfield. It is extremely early, but that would be the highest rate for any player Purdy has played with, just ahead of Brandon Aiyuk . Evans isn't providing the over-the-top, long-speed prime Aiyuk did, but the fact that he's impacting the offense in a similar way is truly amazing.
That's exactly why he's there, indeed.
This was originally going to just be a lesson learned, but it was so bad that we turned it into an entire story you can read here.
How many NFL wide receivers can make both this play ...
PARKER WASHINGTON, WOW. JAGS TAKE THE LEAD. @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ubE4xivDcD
51-YARD TOUCHDOWN FOR PARKER WASHINGTON @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Gf38EGe1Qr
You'd probably think of Ja'Marr Chase , Justin Jefferson , Puka Nacua ... players of that ilk. Well, Parker Washington showed that if he doesn't belong in that superstar group, he's up there among the groups right behind them.
Washington doesn't look the part of today's passing-game-revolves-around-me star wideouts, but he plays like one. Last year, he caught 19 of his 29 contested catch opportunities, the best of any player (min. 25 opportunities). Look at the other guys near the top of the leaderboard.
Best contested catch rate, 2025 (min. 25 opps, reg + playoffs)
Washington has now caught four of his five contested catch opportunities this season already, too.
"We consider him an elite wide receiver, so I don't know what everybody else thinks, but we feel like he's pretty freaking good," Trevor Lawrence said after the game.
I am fine waving away the Bears ' poor offensive performance Sunday with Caleb Williams out. I'm not particularly worried about that side of the ball when at full strength.
I am worried about what I saw from the defensive side. Jordan Love lit the Bears up for 367 passing yards -- the most by any player in the rivalry in the history of Lambeau Field -- and connected on five passes of 30+ air yards. The only other quarterback to hit that many in a single game is Ben Roethlisberger back in 2015. My colleague Garrett Podell had a great story on the Packers coming back to life .
But the Bears? They are the worst team in the NFL defending deep passes ... by far.
And that's despite the Bears having played three of the league's worst offensive teams (Carson Wentz-led Vikings in a downpour, Eagles , Jets ).
There are just so many examples of cornerbacks and safeties getting beat in man and in zone. Love was on a heater Sunday, sure, but there were wide-open dudes deep all day.
Jordan Love had 6 big time throws in Week 5 with 228 passing yards on these 6 throws alone These throws are beautiful pic.twitter.com/loZu2Ee3nQ
If we exclude the overmatched middle three teams on Chicago's schedule, the Bears are allowing 453 yards and 33 points per game this season, with opponents completing 70% of their passes for 10.6 yards per attempt. That's simply not good enough to get where the Bears want to go. All the defensive progress it looked like the team had made Weeks 2-4 appears to have been a product of the schedule.
The 2027 draft class has been getting a lot of publicity, even before the 2026 draft was complete. But the top of the 2026 draft, especially on defense, is looking great.
There have been a lot of fun offensive players -- Denzel Boston , First impressions aren't perfect for projecting the future. But it's so far, so good for debut defenders this season.
The Ravens beat the Falcons in a 30-23 "Sunday Night Football" overtime thriller. It's not only an impressive win for Baltimore, which was without Lamar Jackson and got a late touchdown drive plus a two-point conversion to force overtime, but also the latest example to be considered for overtime strategy.
The Ravens won the toss, chose to receive and then went down the field and scored a touchdown. Then Kyle Hamilton picked off Tua Tagovailoa to seal the win. Through two years of having this rule ...
It's a tiny sample size, and we can't draw any overarching conclusions beyond that. It's the one the NFL was hoping for: There's no "right" choice. Jesse Minter cited the win/loss records as part of his reasoning, but also the flow of the game.
"I did feel like our offense was rolling a little bit, and their defense was getting a little bit tired. And if you go out there, and you get Derrick [Henry] rolling again, now you're out of two-minute mode, and you're back into normal offense, that we could punish them with the run game a little bit, and that's what happened."
The Ravens' overtime drive took over seven minutes and forced the Falcons to use both of their timeouts. That's another advantage of taking the ball first: You don't have to worry about the clock on your opening drive. The Falcons, on the other hand, had to be in hurry-up mode after getting the ball with just 2:50 left and no timeouts.
Another advantage of taking the ball first is the idea of the "third possession." If it's still tied after each team…

title: Question: Why didn’t a Cardinals backup QB play late in the Lions’ loss?
summary: Remember the football movie “Friday Night Lights”? The movie took place in Odessa, Texas, where high school isn’t a sport, but a religion. The flick starred Billy Bob Thornton as the head coach of the Permian High School Panthers. In the Panthers’ very first game, their star running back Boobie Miles was having a magnificent […]
full_text: QB Gardner Minshew #15 and QB Carson Beck #19 (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Remember the football movie “Friday Night Lights”? The movie took place in Odessa, Texas, where high school isn’t a sport, but a religion. The flick starred Billy Bob Thornton as the head coach of the Permian High School Panthers. In the Panthers’ very first game, their star running back Boobie Miles was having a magnificent game, and their opponent had no answer for him. Even though it was the first game of the season, numerous college scouts were in the stands. RELATED: LIONS GET REVENGE ON CARDINALS Into the fourth quarter, Permian had the game well in hand with a huge 42-7 lead, due to the play of Miles. When Coach Gaines called for his backup Comer, to enter the game at running back, he could not find his helmet. He tried to borrow Miles’ helmet, but was rebuffed. So, Coach Gaines sent Miles back in. The next play was “28 sweep” to Miles. As he attempted to turn the corner, a linebacker hit him high and very hard, and he fell over a defender lying on the turf. The high-low tackle produced a loud snap, and Miles suffered a knee injury. Coach Gaines’ offensive prize was now gone for the year. This same scenario played out in the Arizona Cardinals’ 45-21 loss to the Detroit Lions on Sunday afternoon. With 1:05 remaining in the third quarter, Detroit QB Jared Goff scored on a one-yard sneak. The score was now 38-14. On the Cardinals’ next possession to begin the fourth quarter, an eight-play drive ended on the Lions’ 19-yard line when QB Jacoby Brissett was sacked on a fourth-and-one. 12:55 was left in the ballgame. The game was well in hand, and Detroit was leading by four scores. The Lions then drove the field and scored another touchdown. The clock showed 5:03 remaining; Detroit was now up by five scores. Out trotted the Arizona offense, including Brissett. Why wasn’t Brissett pulled? There was no way the Cardinals were going to climb back into this game. What purpose is it to still play your starting quarterback? Why didn’t Arizona head coach Mike LaFleur pull Brissett and send out backup Gardner Minshew? Better yet, the team has got to find out what they have in rookie Carson Beck. Five minutes of live game time would be helpful data. It would also be useful to see if Minshew can move this offense better than Brissett. So far in two seasons, Brissett is 2-15-0 in games that count. Maybe a change of scenery is the answer. Perhaps it’s not, but if LaFleur is hell-bent on Brissett leading this new offense, then why risk him in a lost cause? What if Brissett were to become injured in those last five minutes? Nothing much was going to change the outcome. As it turned out, TE Trey McBride turned a bad throw into a highlight reel with a spectacular catch. That meant the Cardinals lost by four scores instead of five. Yeah, for the home team! Seeing Minshew or Beck would have been a pleasant sight. Arizona has played five games already, and neither man has taken a single snap all season. In soccer, you have to play your backup goalkeeper at some point just to keep him/her focused. The same goes for ice hockey. Play the backup keeper against weaker opponents so that he/she can get some ice time. This was the perfect opportunity to get one or the other some live game action. And if Brissett had gotten injured during that final drive, articles like this would be discussing whether Minshew or Beck should become the new starter going forward.

title: Ravens news: Jesse Minter cracked the NFL’s new overtime rules
summary: Welcome back to Loose Feathers, a regular round-up of the latest news and analysis about the Baltimore Ravens. In today’s edition, we cover the praise for Jesse Minter’s overtime strategy on Sunday night against the Falcons, Tyler Loop flashing his range, and an update on just how good Zay Flowers is this year. Did the […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 11: Head coach Jesse Minter of the Baltimore Ravens looks on before a game against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome back to Loose Feathers, a regular round-up of the latest news and analysis about the Baltimore Ravens. In today’s edition, we cover the praise for Jesse Minter’s overtime strategy on Sunday night against the Falcons, Tyler Loop flashing his range, and an update on just how good Zay Flowers is this year. Did the Ravens reinvent NFL overtime? When Kyle Hamilton won the overtime coin toss, most expected him to announce that the Ravens were kicking off. Conventional wisdom regarding the league’s new(ish) overtime rules dictated that teams wanted to possess the ball second so they had an information advantage. Depending on the results of the first drive, they would know exactly how many points they need to score to win or keep the game going. The Ravens had other plans. Head coach Jesse Minter – aided by game management coordinator Charlie Gelman and others on the staff – wanted to take advantage of a tired Falcons defense that just let Tyler Huntley drive down the field in less than two minutes. Atlanta’s vaunted run defense did not hold up against Derrick Henry and Justice Hill, and Huntley had (finally) settled into a rhythm through the air. Baltimore’s defense had also just injured Falcons quarterback Michael Penix on the final drive of regulation. He said after the game that he could have taken the field if Atlanta got the ball first. But Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle executed a masterful 14-play drive that took 7 minutes (and three seconds) off the clock. In that time, the adrenaline keeping Penix’s pain at bay subsided. He threw on the sidelines, but Tua Tagovailoa instead entered the game. Kyle Hamilton took care of things from there. Not every team is as capable of executing a clock-killing drive as one with Henry in the backfield. It would be interesting to see Lamar Jackson under center in these scenarios; it’s almost hard for him (and Zay Flowers) to not generate explosive plays. Other NFL teams will still try to copycat the Ravens’ success on Sunday night in future overtime games, which could also put the league in position for more ties. The Ravens hacked NFL overtime to beat the Falcons – James Dator (SB Nation) Using a heavy dose of Derrick Henry and short passing from Tyler Huntley, the Ravens executed a 14-play, 7:03-minute touchdown drive that both moved the ball all the way down the field for a touchdown, but critically forced the Falcons to use both of their timeouts, while leaving fewer than 3 minutes left on the clock. Henry ran the ball six times on the drive, the longest pass completion was for 10 yards. So much time was taken off the clock that when Baltimore was at 2nd and goal it was almost as if the Falcons had to the let them score , just to ensure they had a chance to possess the ball. Ben Gretch (Stealing Signals) What happened last night is the Falcons had to use both of their overtime timeouts on defense to preserve time. They got the ball back with just under three minutes, and only the 2-minute stoppage, and it forced them to be one-dimensional. On the broadcast, Collinsworth suggested kicking to force the Atlanta QB situation onto the field quicker. What Baltimore did attacked the Atlanta QB situation more; if Atlanta got ball first, they could’ve tried a run-based offense. They really couldn’t do that with 2:50 and no timeouts. Setting aside the specifics of Atlanta’s QB situation, EPA models look at next-drive success, because that’s crucial in football. What I’m suggesting is missed here is when a team executes like Baltimore did last night, the opponent’s drive success takes a substantial hit because of the clock constraint… …Anyway, Baltimore executed this brilliantly last night, and more teams should take note. Kicking off gives your opponent the ability to execute this. The Falcons didn’t necessarily run well last night, but they’ve been great on the ground in other recent games, and an alternate result last night where they had ball first could’ve been them executing a run-based offense that bled clock and put the Ravens in the situation they found themselves in, with not enough time to run a balanced offense and force to be one-dimensional and throw. Tyler Loop’s big leg is finally showing up NFL Week 5: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday’s games – Jamison Hensley (ESPN) Trend to watch: Ravens kicker Tyler Loop has become automatic from long range. He hit two field goals from 51 yards, improving to 5-of-5 from 50 yards or longer this season. This is a major change from last season, when Loop was 1-of-4 from 50 or longer as a rookie. Ravens news, notes and opinions: Reinforcements on the way, Year 2 growth and Tyler Loop’s range – Jeff Zrebiec (The Athletic) Long-distance Loop Tyler Loop made just one of four field-goal attempts from 50-plus yards last year. While Ravens coaches consistently touted his big leg, he faltered in his limited opportunities from distance. Through five games this year, he’s 5-for-5 from 50-plus yards, and the Ravens don’t win the Cowboys or Falcons games without his ability to come through on long kicks. Zay Flowers’ numbers through six weeks are (still) ridiculous Zay Flowers Is Redefining What a No. 1 Wide Receiver Looks Like – Ryan Mink (BaltimoreRavens.com) There shouldn’t have been any questions about Flowers’ premier status after he finished seventh in the NFL in receiving yards last season. But the same tired “Is he a No. 1?” question arose when the Ravens gave Flowers a four-year, reportedly $140 million contract extension this offseason, ranking him fourth in average annual salary among wide receivers. Flowers has put the question to bed this season. By any metric, he’s been the most productive and unguardable wide receiver on a per-snap basis in the NFL. Flowers’ 405 receiving yards this season ranks eighth in the NFL, but he’s missed two games’ worth of snaps due to a hamstring injury. His quarterback, Lamar Jackson, has also now missed a game and a half. Per route run, Flowers leads the NFL with 4.5 yards. When Jackson has been under center, Flowers has averaged 9.1 yards per route run (and 5.3 yards per play).

title: Ravens release WR Chris Moore with rookie Ja’Kobi Lane nearing return
summary: The Baltimore Ravens released veteran wide receiver Chris Moore on Tuesday, per a team announcement, likely clearing a roster spot for the return of third-round rookie Ja’Kobi Lane from injured reserve. Lane fractured his wrist in Week 1 and underwent surgery shortly after. He is eligible to return to practice on Wednesday. Head coach Jesse […]
full_text: Football - NFL - Baltimore Ravens v Dallas Cowboys - Estadio Maracana, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil - September 27, 2026 Baltimore Ravens' Chris Moore celebrates scoring their third touchdown REUTERS/Brian Snyder | REUTERS The Baltimore Ravens released veteran wide receiver Chris Moore on Tuesday, per a team announcement , likely clearing a roster spot for the return of third-round rookie Ja’Kobi Lane from injured reserve. Lane fractured his wrist in Week 1 and underwent surgery shortly after. He is eligible to return to practice on Wednesday. Head coach Jesse Minter said on Monday that the 6-foot-4 wideout has “done a really good job” staying physically ready to play during his time on the sidelines. “I think he is in a really good place from a conditioning standpoint, from what he has been able to do with the training room and the rehab standpoint,” Minter added. Moore, originally a Ravens fourth-round pick in 2017, returned to Baltimore in July and made a push for the 53-man roster. He was unlikely to dislodge second-year receiver/returner LaJohntay Wester, who would have been exposed to waivers if cut. As a vested veteran, he was not subject to waivers and immediately re-signed to the practice squad. He appeared in four of the Ravens’ first five games and played 97 snaps on offense, primarily as a blocker. He did make a few plays through the air, including a 53-yard catch in Week 1 and a four-yard touchdown in Week 3. The Ravens also released wide receiver Xavier Guillory from their practice squad on Tuesday, clearing a spot for Moore to re-sign on Wednesday. He still has two game day elevations remaining. Baltimore’s receiving corps has been just fine without Lane. Zay Flowers has been the most efficient pass-catcher in the NFL, Rashod Bateman has 233 yards in the last four games, and Devontez Walker is still making an impact play on nearly every catch. However, Lane’s size could be valuable amid the current issues in the Ravens’ tight end room. Durham Smythe is out for the season with a torn Achilles, and Matt Hibner suffered a hand injury in Atlanta, though he returned to the game. Mark Andrews has been struggling with drops and is not the athletic downfield threat he once was. With Smythe sidelined, Andrews is the Ravens’ best blocking tight end. He may need to take on more inline duties with Lane getting looks as a big slot who can find space in the middle of the field. His size could also help with Baltimore’s goal-to-go woes. The former USC standout was the Ravens’ most exciting rookie in training camp with highlight-reel catches almost every day. The team’s two draft picks before him, Vega Ioane and Zion Young, have impressed in the trenches thus far, and a strong comeback from Lane would cement 2026 as one of Eric DeCosta’s best draft classes.

title: Winners and losers from Ravens’ Week 5 win over the Falcons
summary: The Ravens entered Week 5 without Lamar Jackson against a red-hot Falcons team and left with their most impressive win of the Jesse Minter era. There were plenty of winners in this one, while one player stood out as the biggest loser. Winners QB Tyler Huntley: Huntley showed once again why Baltimore has complete faith […]
full_text: The Ravens entered Week 5 without Lamar Jackson against a red-hot Falcons team and left with their most impressive win of the Jesse Minter era. There were plenty of winners in this one, while one player stood out as the biggest loser. Winners QB Tyler Huntley: Huntley showed once again why Baltimore has complete faith in him as Jackson’s backup. He finished with 24 completions on 32 attempts for 201 yards and two touchdowns, with 20 yards rushing and the game-winning score on a quarterback sneak. Huntley was particularly impressive on the final drive of regulation to tie the game on a back-shoulder touchdown pass to Devontez Walker. RB Derrick Henry: Everyone knew it would be a heavy Henry game without Jackson under center, and that is exactly what transpired. Henry rushed for 102 yards on 24 carries while scoring on an 18-yard reception. He also found the end zone on the two-point conversion to tie the game. Henry did not have a run longer than 11 yards, but he was able to grind out the tough yards and wear down Atlanta’s defense in overtime. Offensive line: The Ravens’ offensive line paved the way for 208 total rushing yards, utterly bullying the Falcons’ front at times. Rookie first-rounder Vega Ioane continues to look like a budding star wherever he plays on the interior, allowing zero pressures against Atlanta, per Pro Football Focus. WR Rashod Bateman: Bateman made multiple key plays to keep the offense moving against the Falcons, including three catches for 38 yards on the final game-tying drive of regulation. His 62 receiving yards (on five receptions) led the team for the second time this year after zero instances in 2025. WR Zay Flowers: While Flowers didn’t set off the fireworks we’ve come to expect this year, he still made several important plays throughout the game, finishing with 53 receiving yards on eight catches, plus one carry for 13 yards. He also lost 26 yards from his statline when the Ravens also opted to take a defensive pass interference penalty he drew to save an extra few seconds on the clock. Declan Doyle has fully unlocked the fourth-year receiver, and his numbers should jump back up once Jackson returns to the lineup. WR Devontez Walker: Walker had just two catches against Atlanta, but his second could not have come at a better time as Huntley connected with him on a back shoulder throw in the end zone on the game-tying drive. RB Justice Hill: Hill started the game on the wrong foot with a drop on the opening drive, but followed up with a 21-yard run on the next play to convert on third down. Hill broke off another long run later in the game with a 47-yard gain on another third down. He finished the game with 73 rushing yards on just four carries. S Kyle Hamilton: Hamilton shows up every week for Baltimore’s defense, and he made the biggest play of the day on Sunday. After marching down the field and scoring a touchdown to start overtime, the Ravens’ defense needed a stop against backup quarterback Tua Tagovailoa to win the game. After a 20-yard pass to Drake London, Tagovailoa again went to his superstar wide receiver, but Hamilton was waiting underneath this time to secure the game-sealing pick near midfield. He finished the game with six total tackles as well as two pressures, according to PFF. S Malaki Starks: Starks has begun to stack strong performances after a rocky start to his sophomore season. The former first-round pick had perhaps his best game of the season against the Falcons in Week 5. Starks made several critical tackles against Bijan Robinson, including one that saved a touchdown when he was one-on-one with the ultra-elusive back. Starks led the defense with 10 total tackles, including two tackles for loss. His 70.0 coverage grade was also the second-highest the team, according to PFF. OLB Mike Green: Green is another second-year player who has hit a groove in recent weeks. Without Trey Hendrickson on the field in the last two weeks, Green has stepped up on the edge, both as a pass rusher and against the run. Green had three pressures against Atlanta, according to PFF, to go with a sack. Green’s quick third-down pressure on quarterback Michael Penix forced a throwaway on the Falcons’ final drive of the game, keeping them from winning in regulation with a field goal. OLB Tavius Robinson: Just two plays earlier on Atlanta’s final drive in regulation, it was Robinson who nailed Penix for a sack on first down, causing a fumble and injuring the third-year quarterback. This led to Tagovailoa taking over in overtime and serving up Hamilton’s game-ending pick. DT Nnamdi Madubuike: Madubuike looks more and more like his old self with every week that passes. He was effective on Sunday as a pass rusher with three pressures and against the run with two stops, according to PFF. Madubuike, Hendrickson, and Green should form a formidable trio of pass rushers once all three are on the field together again. K Tyler Loop: Loop was perfect against the Falcons, converting all three field goals including two from 51 yards. Loop kept the Ravens in the game until the offense was finally able to reach the end zone in the third quarter. Loop has now missed just two kicks through five weeks, with one being blocked. Losers: TE Mark Andrews: It’s never fun to point out the negatives during such a feel-good win, but if there was one glaring problem in this game, it was Andrews. The veteran tight end dropped a touchdown on the opening drive of the game and followed that up with a fumble on the next drive that Atlanta recovered and took the other way for a score to go up 7-3. Andrews later failed to secure the catch on a two-point attempt, leaving Baltimore down 17-15 in the third quarter. Andrews then let another pass hit the ground on third down while the Ravens trailed 20-15 with just over six minutes remaining in regulation, forcing a punt to give the Falcons the chance to put the game away. Andrews ended up making several catches on the last two drives of the game to finish with 28 yards, but his blunders were a primary reason that the Ravens were scrambling in the second half. Third-down defense : The Ravens have struggled to get off the field on third down all season, and that was once again a major issue on Sunday, allowing nine conversions on 17 third downs. London in particular gave Baltimore’s defense issues on third down and long. The inability to make third-down stops sullied what was otherwise a strong defensive outing by the Ravens.

title: James Cook and ball security: How worried should Buffalo Bills be?
summary: Picture this, Buffalo Bills fans: the team has an elite running back. That player averages over 5.5 yards per touch. He’s become one of the main focal points of the offense. He’s a threat to score a touchdown every time he touches the football. He can gain tough yards between the tackles, but he also […]
full_text: Picture this, Buffalo Bills fans: the team has an elite running back. That player averages over 5.5 yards per touch. He’s become one of the main focal points of the offense. He’s a threat to score a touchdown every time he touches the football. He can gain tough yards between the tackles, but he also has the breakaway speed necessary to create explosive plays on the ground. The only issue? He fumbles—a lot. In fact, he fumbles once every 50 times he touches the football, which is well above the league average. Should the Bills be nervous? Should they bench him? He has a capable backup running back who has come in and played well in spurts, but that backup is a backup for a reason, which is that he isn’t nearly the overall threat that the starter is. For those of you wondering who we’re talking about, the answer might not be as obvious as you’d assume. The player is question is Thurman Thomas, Hall of Fame running back and 1991 NFL MVP. The backup is Kenneth Davis, a good-not-great running back in his own right who operated as a great change-of-pace back for the Bills. The fumble data is correct, per Pro Football Reference, as it covers the first five seasons of Thomas’ illustrious career. Why discuss Thurman Thomas and his fumbles in the year 2026? Because for Bills fans of a certain age, we’re seeing something close to deja vu all over again in Buffalo’s current top running back, James Cook III. Cook is a dynamic runner who clearly needs to be a big part of Buffalo’s offense. Over the course of his five-year career, he already has three Pro Bowl nods and a Second-Team All-Pro selection on his resume. He led the NFL in rushing touchdowns with 16 in 2024, then followed that up by leading the NFL in rushing yards with 1,621 in 2025. In just four-plus seasons with Buffalo, Cook is fifth all-time in franchise history in rushing yards, trailing only Thomas, O.J. Simpson, Fred Jackson, and…quarterback Josh Allen. He’s fourth all-time in franchise history in rushing touchdowns behind Allen, Thomas, and Simpson. All of the information above is very, very good. Cook is an elite running back, and he is a threat to score every time he touches the football. However, of late, he’s also a turnover waiting to happen. Cook has fumbled 17 times in his career, including the playoffs, and 11 of those fumbles have occurred since the beginning of the 2025 regular season. Given that he has 487 touches in that same time frame, that means that Cook fumbles a dismal once every 44 touches. Yes, that means he’s currently fumbling at a higher rate than Thurman did, and Thurman was a fairly notorious fumbler throughout much of his career. The frustrating issue with Cook is that this problem is definitely a more recent issue. In his first three seasons, including the playoffs, Cook totaled 750 touches. He fumbled just six times, which equates to once every 125 touches. That kind of ball security is elite-level stuff, and the fact that he’s shown himself capable of it raises some questions in my mind. First, is Cook’s recent uptick in fumbles something sustainable? Is there a change in technique that’s led him to fumble more? Have opposing teams recognized a flaw in his game that has made it easier for them to punch the ball out of his grasp? I don’t see a noticeable difference in the way Cook runs or carries the football over the last two seasons as opposed to the first three years of his career, so I think we can rule that one out quickly. Perhaps with more touches comes more scout tape, and that scout tape shows a player vulnerable to the “Peanut Punch.” However, for these fumbles to come in such bunches feels like there must be an element of bad luck involved, too. Despite the horrendous fumble rate over his last 23 games, Cook clocks in at a fumble every 73 touches for his career. That’s better than Thurman Thomas by nearly ten touches, as Thomas fumbled once every 64 times he touched the football throughout his career. Given that he was fumbling once every 50 touches through his first five seasons, we can see that Thomas improved in that area as his career went on. Cook’s career is far from over, but he’s done the exact opposite in taking a sharp downward turn in fumble rate. Maybe you’re sick of a historical comparison and would rather see how Cook’s fumble rate ranks among his contemporaries. Below, here are ten high-volume backs, their total touches over the last two seasons (including playoffs, where applicable), and their total number of fumbles in that span: NAME TOUCHES FUMBLES RATE Jahmyr Gibbs 472 3 157/fumble Derrick Henry 443 4 111/fumble Bijan Robinson 486 6 81/fumble Jonathan Taylor 483 3 161/fumble Ashton Jeanty 431 2 216/fumble Aaron Jones Sr. 269 4 67/fumble Kenneth Walker III 425 1 425/fumble Kyren Williams 444 3 148/fumble Jaylen Warren 353 2 177/fumble Christian McCaffrey 530 2 265/fumble James Cook III 487 11 44/fumble There it is in black and white. Cook, while an elite talent with the ball in his hands, has also turned into a turnover waiting to happen over the last season-plus. His fumble rate is nearly equal to that of New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo, who has five fumbles in 216 career touches, or one fumble every 43 touches. No one doubts that Cook is a better player than Skattebo. However, it’s alarming for the Bills that both players are that close in fumbles per touch. This isn’t a call to bench James Cook, nor is it a backdoor way to say that the Bills need to feed him the football less. Actually, the problem lies in exactly the opposite of those discussion points. Buffalo needs Cook to play, and they need him to play at an elite level. They also need to give him the football, especially as their top receiver, DJ Moore, continues to deal with a lingering shoulder injury. Arguably, Cook is the most important person on Buffalo’s offense whose name isn’t Josh Allen. That’s what makes his fumbles so concerning. Could the Bills give Ray Davis more snaps if Cook continues to give the ball to their opponents? Absolutely. Davis has two fumbles in his NFL career—both of which have come in playoff games. Counting his kickoff returns, Davis has 269 career touches, so he fumbles once every 135 touches. He averages 5.1 yards per touch in the regular season throughout his career; Cook, by comparison, averages 5.6 yards per touch in the regular season. Perhaps Cook’s ball security would improve with fewer touches, as his explosion in fumbles has also come during a two-year timeframe where he has seen a serious uptick in usage. Is it fatigue that’s causing him to be less secure with the ball? Well, if the Bills give their most dynamic non-quarterback offensive player fewer touches, that circles us back to the issue raised above: The Bills need Cook to be successful on offense. Part of being successful, though, is by following head coach Joe Brady’s mantra of making sure that the team can “put the ball down” after each play. Far too often, Cook is putting the ball on the ground rather than giving the offense a chance to put it down. The numbers are there, and they don’t paint a pretty picture for James Cook’s ball security. With a defense struggling as badly as Buffalo’s is, the offense can I’ll afford to give opposing teams more possessions. Cook has to protect the football. The Bills need him to figure out his issues—and fast. All data courtesy of Pro Football Reference
