title: Buffalo Bills record book: Josh Allen, James Cook make NFL history
summary: Some are calling it cinematic, but let’s be honest, Bills fans. That game was a mess from start to finish. Missed connections that turned into missed opportunities, turnovers, and a defense that looked lost far too often. But in the end, it was a win. A very strange, brutal win, but a win’s a win, right?  And […]
full_text: Some are calling it cinematic, but let’s be honest, Bills fans. That game was a mess from start to finish. Missed connections that turned into missed opportunities, turnovers, and a defense that looked lost far too often. But in the end, it was a win. A very strange, brutal win, but a win’s a win, right? And along the way, there were actually some pretty good things that happened. So that’s what we’re going to focus on in this week’s edition of Shout! outs. _____________________________________________________________________________ Josh Allen found a way to make NFL history despite throwing the ball just 20 times. Of course, it helped that he also ran for 121 yards, the second-highest rushing total of his career. When the passing game isn’t working quite right, Allen can just take care of things himself. Josh Allen became the first player in NFL history with 200+ passing yards on 20 or fewer pass attempts and 100+ rushing yards on 10 or fewer rush attempts in the same game. pic.twitter.com/MyX5CPFvft — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) October 13, 2026 _____________________________________________________________________________ For the first time in team history, the Bills had a quarterback and running back each rush for more than 100 yards in the same game. And Josh Allen and James Cook weren’t done there. They also tied an NFL record for the most regular-season games in which both teammates scored a rushing touchdown. This is the first time in team history that the Bills have a QB and a RB both with 100+ rushing yards in the same game. https://t.co/ciBkSinkTb — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) October 13, 2026 _____________________________________________________________________________ Five games, five rushing touchdowns. Josh Allen has found his way into the end zone with his legs in every game this season, becoming the first quarterback in NFL history to start a season with a rushing touchdown in each of his team’s first five games. Josh Allen is now the first quarterback in NFL history to record a rushing touchdown in each of his team's first 5 games of a season. pic.twitter.com/dmnj1rQpWf — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) October 13, 2026 _____________________________________________________________________________ James Cook is putting together quite a start to the season. His 532 rushing yards through five games rank third in franchise history. And with two trips to the end zone Monday night, Cook now has 40 career rushing touchdowns, including the playoffs, joining a pretty short list of Bills who have reached that number. James Cook III’s 532 rushing yards this season ranks third most by a Bill through 5 games in team history. Cook III only trails O.J. Simpson who recorded 813 yards in 1973 and 823 yards in 1975. pic.twitter.com/IB4DWBI6XO — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) October 13, 2026 The touchdown also marked Cook's 40th career rushing TD (including playoffs). He's the 4th Bill to have 40+ rushing TDs, joining Josh Allen (95), Thurman Thomas (81) and O.J. Simpson (57). https://t.co/rivl72sUAV — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) October 13, 2026 _____________________________________________________________________________ Greg Rousseau apparently has a thing for blocking field goals. The last time the Bills blocked one was Oct. 13, 2025, against the Atlanta Falcons. Rousseau got that one, too. Almost exactly a year later, he’s did it again. This time, the end result was better though. Greg Rousseau recorded the first FG blocked by the Bills since October 13, 2025 at Atlanta. That block was also by Rousseau. pic.twitter.com/DQgmIP9adt — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) October 13, 2026 _____________________________________________________________________________ We spent Monday night yelling at our televisions, and we’ll probably spend the rest of the week yelling about coaching decisions. There was plenty to complain about, and I’m sure we’ll get to all of it. But there’s still plenty worth Shout! ingabout, too.

title: Takeaways from Bills instant classic win over Rams on Monday Night Football
summary: I’m working on a few hours of sleep, and I’m actually surprised I was able to fall asleep in the wee hours of Tuesday morning given the mixture of cortisol and adrenaline that were coursing through my veins after the Buffalo Bills 37-34 win over the Rams on Monday Night Football in Week 5. This […]
full_text: I’m working on a few hours of sleep, and I’m actually surprised I was able to fall asleep in the wee hours of Tuesday morning given the mixture of cortisol and adrenaline that were coursing through my veins after the Buffalo Bills 37-34 win over the Rams on Monday Night Football in Week 5. This game had nine lead changes, six-consecutive touchdown drives to end regulation, and was capped with the first overtime victory of Josh Allen’s NFL career to date. Josh Allen reminded everyone who the NFL’s best player is On April 21, 2026, I sent the following tweet, because I realized despite feeling this way for years, I had never actually put it on the Twitter/X record. And nothing is official until that happens right? Josh Allen is the best player in the NFL and has been the best player in the NFL since the start of the 2022 season — Chris Trapasso (@ChrisTrapasso) April 21, 2026 As you can see, that tweet went decently viral… plenty of Bills fans liked it, agreed, etc. Plenty of Ravens/Chiefs fans felt differently. A few months later, I wrote my rationale here at Rumblings. And I’m not a victory lap person. I know how much of a rollercoaster the NFL season is. Keenly aware. BUT MY LORD JOSH ALLEN SURE AS HELL VALIDATED THAT TWEET LAST NIGHT. OK, that is all. Onto the next point. Jim Leonhard’s defense is currently not Jim Leonhard’s defense I’m not going to pretend I know/understand all the calls and concepts in Leonhard’s defensive scheme. But as an avid college football fan, I vividly remember those Wisconsin defenses. They blitzed from everywhere. You just never knew from where. Their secondaries were outstanding despite lacking five-star recruits. They lived in man. They dropped defensive tackles into underneath throwing lanes. Confused the hell out of quarterbacks. And I think these two tweets that resurfaced last night from Anthony Prohaska of Cover 1 that were sent in the offseason tell essentially the whole story right now on the defensive side of the ball for the Bills: Jim Leonhard on the Bills defensive personnel in year 1 for him: “That’s the exciting part of the offseason. I had a vision for what I want it to be, and it might not totally get there in year 1. We have to be real as far as who we have, what their skillsets are, and I have to… — Anthony Cover 1 (@Pro__Ant) May 26, 2026 This doesn’t look or feel like a Jim Leonhard defense with how bland/vanilla it largely is. The aggression and front foot style of play isn’t there. This is a coach whose fundamental principle is dictating to offenses and not being a counter puncher. And they’re playing almost… — Anthony Cover 1 (@Pro__Ant) October 13, 2026 Couldn’t have written it better myself, Anthony. Whether it’s because Leonhard doesn’t trust his secondary loaded with youth and newcomers to Buffalo, or they’re simply still learning all of the intricacies of it, the Bills secondary is a major problem entering Week 6. No question about it. I do happen to think the more reps this secondary gets together, the better it’ll become. And the more they’ll understand what Leonhard is asking of them. I’m also of the belief more youngsters should see the field in the back seven — like Kaleb Elarms-Orr and Jalon Kilgore. And for as much as I initially want to write that Leonhard might be meddling/micro-managing too much… again, Buffalo’s defense, in its current state schematically, does not resemble the Wisconsin defenses he coordinated with great aplomb and perennial success. Joe Brady is learning too… I didn’t hate the Bills wasting time for the end of the first half before trying to move the ball. I did not like the timeout after they let the clock bleed inside 40 seconds. If you’re going to take that route — milk the clock so you’re legitimately with the ball last before halftime — you can’t then stop the clock yourself because you can’t get into the right play. Unequivocally a mistake. Brady owned it postgame. Maybe could’ve used a timeout on the final defensive drive of regulation too right? When it seemed like the defense was gassed. However, Brady doesn’t operate in a vacuum as the NFL’s sole head coach. Sean McVay, a head coach since 2017, didn’t exactly ace his game-management test before sending out Harrison Mevis in overtime last night. And things could be worse on this front… ask Commanders fans. Yes, the Bills probably should’ve tush pushed Allen twice to get the clock inside two minutes in overtime. But you know what? Even if that was technically the smarter thing to do, and I’m all for attempting to make the most prudent decision at all times, the tush-push plan to “waste time” in case of a miss would’ve been focusing too much on the worst-case scenario occurring and attempting not to lose. And I’m glad, for a change, the Bills coach was concerned with one thing… winning. …but his game plan was masterful The Bills were down their two best outside separators at receiver for this game. That cannot be overstated in its importance. We’ve seen many offenses, even early in 2026, completely crumble without their No. 1 wideout. So the Bills pounded the rock. Utilized two perfectly executed running back screens. Called an exquisite — and legal — pick play on the Keon Coleman touchdown. Schemed open a two-point conversion! And let Allen be Allen as a runner. Now, of course, Brady didn’t necessarily plan for Allen to run it 10 times for 121 yards. But Brady understood those vertical routes were going to draw defenders out of the intermediate level of the field to give his quarterback ample room to morph into an agigtated moose with And 1 mixtape agility in space. The Bills (passing) offense went into this game with one hand tied behind its back, and Brady’s game plan helped Buffalo escape with a win. Lastly, he clearly very much understands if the Bills are to go to where they intend to this season, James Cook will be an integral facet of this team. Brady going right back to Cook after his overtime fumble will go a long way with the running back himself and the rest of this Bills team. The Bills are 4-1 That’s a takeaway? Yes it is. Caught up in all the defensive turmoil and Cook fumbles, I think it’s an incredibly obvious yet important reminder. Of course, the defensive woes and Cook putting the ball on the ground isn’t sustainable. Those areas of the team must improve. At this stage, as the Bills are clearly far from a finished product, they’d much rather be 4-1 with clear flaws then 3-2, 2-3, or 1-4 while having played cleaner, more balanced football.

title: Buffalo Bills QB Josh Allen reaches 100 career NFL wins
summary: Josh Allen just won his 100th NFL football game.  The Buffalo Bills quarterback reached the milestone with a 37-34 overtime win over the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night football becoming just the fourth quarterback in NFL history to record at least 100 wins, including the postseason, in his first nine seasons.  Allen joins a pretty short list. Patrick Mahomes had […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 12: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills smiles prior to the game against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on October 12, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images Josh Allen just won his 100th NFL football game. The Buffalo Bills quarterback reached the milestone with a 37-34 overtime win over the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night football becoming just the fourth quarterback in NFL history to record at least 100 wins, including the postseason, in his first nine seasons. Allen joins a pretty short list. Patrick Mahomes had 112 wins through his first nine seasons, Russell Wilson had 107, and Tom Brady had 101. Allen, who took over as Buffalo’s starting quarterback in 2018, has now reached triple digits just 5 games into his ninth season in the league. The win also gave Allen his 92nd regular-season victory, tying him with Peyton Manning for the third-most by a starting quarterback in his first nine NFL seasons. Only Wilson, with 98, and Mahomes, with 95, have more. And with 12 games remaining in his ninth season, Allen has a chance to do more than just add to those totals. Six more regular-season wins would put him ahead of Wilson and Mahomes for the most in a quarterback’s first nine seasons. Taking over the top spot on the combined wins list will be a little tougher, particularly since there’s no guarantee how many postseason games Buffalo will play. But it’s certainly within reach. Both lists are a reminder of how much things have changed in Buffalo since Allen arrived in 2018.

title: Carolina Panthers 2027 NFL Draft Prospect Profile: Chris Cole
summary: The 2027 NFL Draft feels like forever away, and we’re all caught up in the start of the NFL season. Regardless, it’s never too early to look ahead to the Draft. This weekly series will take a closer look at some of the prospects the Carolina Panthers could select in the 2027 iteration of the […]
full_text: ATHENS, GEORGIA - SEPTEMBER 26: Chris Cole #9 of the Georgia Bulldogs runs a fumble recovery back for a touchdown during a game between the Georgia Bulldogs and the Oklahoma Sooners at Sanford Stadium on September 26, 2026 in Athens, Georgia. (Photo by Steve Limentani/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images The 2027 NFL Draft feels like forever away, and we’re all caught up in the start of the NFL season. Regardless, it’s never too early to look ahead to the Draft. This weekly series will take a closer look at some of the prospects the Carolina Panthers could select in the 2027 iteration of the Draft. In this series, we’ll only be looking at prospects the Panthers could seriously consider. This week our profile will focus on Georgia Bulldogs linebacker Chris Cole Bio Cole (6’3”, 235 lbs.) was the top rated player in the entire state of Virginia, choosing to attend Georgia instead of other offers like Miami, Penn State, and Tennessee. Despite going to Georgia, Cole managed to see the field as a true freshman, even earning a SEC All-Freshman nod. He saw the field even more as a sophomore, notching 59 tackles, seven for loss, 4.5 sacks, and a couple pass breakups. So far this season, he has grown even more and become an explosive game changer for the Bulldogs’ defense. He already has 22 tackles, five for loss, 1.5 sacks, and two fumble recoveries including an 85-yard scoop and score. Strengths/Weaknesses Cole is often considered one of the best cover linebackers in the Draft. He has elite speed for the position and the versatility to line up at off-ball linebacker, nickel, and even edge defender. His athleticism allows him to be a true sideline to sideline player against the pass and the run. His strong hands allow him to reroute receivers and tight ends while giving him the ability to finish tackles efficiently. While he has produced as a pass rusher, his technique leaves quite a bit to be desired if he’s truly going to be used as a blitzer at the next level. Cole also struggles against linemen who meet him at the second level on running plays. He’s not a thumper in the run game, leaving him to occasionally get washed out by the bigger, stronger blockers. Projection Chris Cole is a dynamic cover linebacker with the size and speed that NFL teams look for at the next level. His coverage ability and alignment versatility add to the pros side of the chart for Cole. He doesn’t have the bona fides against the run, especially against downhill plays where he needs to use his strength instead of his speed. Devin Lloyd has been an absolute steal for the Panthers (despite paying him gobs of money), and Bobby Okereke has been a solid find as well. After those two, however, the cupboards are pretty bare after injuries to depth players and the release of Trevin Wallace. Adding another quality cover linebacker would help the Panthers run their desired zone scheme under Ejiro Evero. Even if the defensive coordinator changes next season, Cole is a versatile piece that any DC would love to have on their team. What do you think, Panthers fans? If Chris Cole is available when the Panthers select in the 2027 NFL Draft, should they take him? Sound off in the comments!

title: Reviewing the Bears’ PFN grades from Week 5 vs. Packers
summary: Of the potential outcomes the Bears could’ve faced in their Week 5 matchup against the Packers, few likely anticipated that the game would result in a 31-7 Green Bay victory. Unfortunately for the beloved, that proved to be the case on Sunday. If you’ll go across any forum where Bears enthusiasts talk with each other, […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 04: Tyson Bagent #17 of the Chicago Bears throws a pass against the New York Jets at Soldier Field on October 04, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Of the potential outcomes the Bears could’ve faced in their Week 5 matchup against the Packers, few likely anticipated that the game would result in a 31-7 Green Bay victory. Unfortunately for the beloved, that proved to be the case on Sunday. If you’ll go across any forum where Bears enthusiasts talk with each other, a majority of them — fans and media alike — had Chicago winning the game. Online football betting sites generally had the Bears as the favorites, even with the game being played at Lambeau Field. In the end, though, the Packers’ smothering defense and high-powered offense made it too much for the Bears to overcome, regardless of whether it was Tyson Bagent or Case Keenum at quarterback. Each week, I’ll review how Chicago’s eligible performers graded by Pro Football Network’s Impact Scoring model. Here’s how Week 5 looked. Offense Tyson Bagent: 65.9 (24th of 30 QBs) D’Andre Swift: 80.0 (6th of 42 RBs) Roschon Johnson: 71.8 (26th of 42 RBs) Luther Burden III: 70.8 (42th of 66 WRs) Kalif Raymond: 67.7 (58th of 66 WRs) Rome Odunze: 65.2 (64th of 66 WRs) Colston Loveland: 67.9 (34th of 37 TEs) Theo Benedet: 74.8 (47th of 86 OTs) Joe Thuney: 77.7 (17th of 46 OGs) Garrett Bradbury: 68.6 (22nd of 26 Cs) Jonah Jackson: 78.3 (14th of 46 OGs) Darnell Wright: 71.9 (57th of 86 OTs) As one could anticipate, Bagent didn’t score all that well on Sunday. His -0.41 EPA per dropback ranked just No. 26 in the NFL in Week 5, and his -10.9 completion percentage over expected ranked only No. 28 among 30 quarterbacks. D’Andre Swift put together a solid outing, but he’s the only one of the Bears’ skill position players who had a respectable performance from an analytical perspective on Sunday. Chicago’s guard tandem fared well, but the game marked Darnell Wright’s worst game of his season in what’s otherwise been a stellar 2026 for him thus far. Defense Austin Booker: 86.5 (4th of 78 EDGEs) James Lynch: 66.7 (23rd of 78 EDGEs) Dayo Odeyingbo: 61.6 (47th of 78 EDGEs) Montez Sweat: 56.1 (59th of 78 EDGEs) Grady Jarrett: 76.9 (30th of 95 DTs) Neville Gallimore: 75.4 (35th of 95 DTs) Kentavius Street: 53.9 (94th of 95 DTs) Devin Bush: 86.3 (6th of 66 LBs) D’Marco Jackson: 73.6 (45th of 66 LBs) T.J. Edwards: 70.4 (57th of 66 LBs) Tyrique Stevenson: 78.1 (24th of 88 CBs) Malik Muhammad: 62.7 (81st of 88 CBs) Jaylon Johnson: 61.2 (85th of 88 CBs) Dillon Thieneman: 77.1 (21st of 64 SAFs) Cam Lewis: 74.2 (35th of 64 SAFs) Xavier Woods: 64.6 (62nd of 64 SAFs) The Bears saw encouraging defensive play out of a few individual players, but the lack of cohesion from the unit as a whole made it tough to stop the Packers, especially in the vertical passing game. As the grades would indicate, Malik Muhammad, Jaylon Johnson, and Xavier Woods got beat multiple times down the field on Sunday. Muhammad’s instances felt like more of a zone coverage processing issue, while Woods and Johnson admittedly just looked slower out there. All told, though, Austin Booker was one of just six edge rushers with at least two sacks in Week 5. Devin Bush also had a nice game, tallying eight tackles, two tackles for loss, two quarterback pressures, and a targeted passer rating of just 86.3. Special teams (for the sickos) Cairo Santos: 62.9 (27th of 29 Ks) Tory Taylor: 81.8 (12th of 30 Ps) With Cairo Santos missing a 43-yard field goal, it’s no wonder he graded out as one of the worst kickers in the NFL in Week 5. That said, Tory Taylor performed well against the Packers, ranking No. 8 in the NFL with an average of 46.3 net yards per punt on his four attempts. It’s not a great look when one of your best performers from a game is the punter, but Taylor at least looked solid for the Bears.

title: Hot Take Tuesday: Bears-Packers: A Brutal Beating and the End of a Brutal Discourse
summary: Well, that certainly wasn’t fun. The Chicago Bears probably played their worst game of the Ben Johnson era, and unfortunately, it came against the Green Bay Packers in a brutal 31-7 whipping up at Lambeau Field. I, like many Bears fans, felt damn good going into this one. It felt like two teams going in […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 11: Tyson Bagent #17 of the Chicago Bears is sacked by Brandon Cisse #2 of the Green Bay Packers during the second quarter at Lambeau Field on October 11, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Daniel Bartel/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, that certainly wasn’t fun. The Chicago Bears probably played their worst game of the Ben Johnson era, and unfortunately, it came against the Green Bay Packers in a brutal 31-7 whipping up at Lambeau Field. I, like many Bears fans, felt damn good going into this one. It felt like two teams going in different directions. It felt like the Bears had a chance to put the Packers in a spiral that they made not get out of for the rest of the season. The Bears had a chance to make a statement. But it was the Packers that made a statement, and they made it loudly and clearly. They are not ready to be an NFC North doormat, and they are far too talented a team to be dismissed. I’m not saying the Packers are a great team, but they definitely aren’t a bad team, which was a trap I certainly fell into heading into this game. And yes, if Caleb Williams was playing, things would have been different. The Bears may not have won, but the game would have been, at a minimum, significantly closer. But when you were as confident as I was with QB2 running the offense, I don’t get to say, “But Caleb Williams” after the fact. The Bears took it on the chin, and many of us fans did as well. What was the roughest thing about all of it was that a Ben Johnson team wasn’t ready to play the Green Bay Packers. That doesn’t make sense to me. Ben wanted this rivalry to matter. He called out Matt LeFleur in his opening press conference. He screamed “F*ck the Packers!” in his postgame speech. It matters to him. He wanted it to matter to the players. So how is that how they come out after a week of practice? Every aspect of the team failed. Who played well? Nobody. The Bears got flat-out whipped. They went home with their heads held low. I hate using the word embarrassing, but it certainly fits the display of football we saw on Sunday. But a big part of that whipping was the play of the quarterback. Bears fans have been on the wrong side of a lot of Bears-Packers games over the last 35 years, and what’s been the underlying factor? The team with the better QB almost always wins. It’s not rocket science. That’s how this league works, and it’s how this rivalry has certainly worked for many, many years. I didn’t come into this game thinking that Tyson Bagent was as good as Jordan Love- far from it. But I did think that Bagent, with Ben Johnson’s wizardry, would be able to put in a solid performance, and with the Packers spiraling in the wrong direction, I thought Chicago would cruise in this one. But Tyson Bagent was objectively awful. There’s no defending his performance. None. You can’t complain about the offensive line. Bagent had time. You can’t complain about the weapons; they were open. You can’t complain about the scheme; Bagent didn’t execute it. He was lost. He looked like he didn’t belong on an NFL field. That doesn’t mean I’m out on Bagent forever. He’s a QB2 for a reason. But the discourse that he might one day be a QB1 died on Sunday, and it’s never coming back. If the Bears were offered a 4 for Bagent this past offseason (as the rumor has been), they blew it by not making that trade. Bagent has tanked his trade value. He’s a QB2. Nothing more. He can beat a bad team; he can’t beat a good team. He has a weak arm, and to offset that, he needs to operate within structure and do it quickly. Bagent hesitated all game long, and he got destroyed because of it. For me, the discourse around Chicago about Bagent being some hidden gem has been annoying. Many fans have tried to make him be something more than he is. Had the city had more reasonable expectations, perhaps this performance wouldn’t have been as jarring. But Tyson Bagent has fully proven what he is, and there shouldn’t be any thought of him becoming something else because he doesn’t have the physical traits to do it. That doesn’t change the fact that he’s a great story. Jalon Daniels in Tampa is a great story, too. Bagent’s rise to QB2 in Chicago is a great story. Not every UDFA QB has to become Kurt Warner for it to be a great story. Bagent becoming a QB2 as an undrafted QB out of Division II Shepard College is the story, and it’s a fantastic one. But there is no Kurt Warner storybook ending here. The story has been written. Now, Bagent is a QB2. An acceptable QB2. Not a great QB2, but a functional one. The discourse trying to create him into something else is annoying and creates a divide in the fan base, but it’s also unfair to Bagent. Placing unreasonable expectations on a player only leaves that player unable to reach those. Tyson Bagent won a game while Caleb Williams was out. The Bears went 2-2 in games Williams didn’t finish or didn’t play in. That’s exactly what you hope for when your QB is out. Bagent and Case Keenum did the job. Now, it’s time to hope Caleb is ready to go against Atlanta. The Packers beat that ass. Unfortunately, that ass was Tyson Bagent and the Chicago Bears. This one stung, but it didn’t sting to me like the losses to Brett Favre and Aaron Rodgers did in the past. Those losses felt hopeless. This doesn’t feel hopeless. It feels like a rivalry. The Packers gave the Bears their best shot and slapped them in the mouth. The Bears have a chance for revenge on Christmas Day, and I expect them to have it. Bear down, and as always, F*ck the Packers.

title: Chicago Bears week 6 power rankings roundup
summary: Humble pie tastes awful. Especially when it’s served with extra cheese from that team. The Chicago Bears need to lick their wounds and prepare for another road game against a high-powered offense. But before we get there, we have to look at where the pundits and analysts have the Bears ranked. WCG – Aaron Leming […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 11: Case Keenum #11 of the Chicago Bears scrambles against the Green Bay Packers during the fourth quarter at Lambeau Field on October 11, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Humble pie tastes awful. Especially when it’s served with extra cheese from that team. The Chicago Bears need to lick their wounds and prepare for another road game against a high-powered offense. But before we get there, we have to look at where the pundits and analysts have the Bears ranked. WCG – Aaron Leming 13. Chicago Bears (3-2) Going 2-1 (so far) without Caleb Williams is something all Bears fans would have taken when he went down with what appeared to be a potential season-ending injury. That said, recency bias exists, and a 31-7 blowout loss to the Packers is still fresh in everyone’s mind. They’ve shown that they can dominate quality teams; now they must show more consistency. The Athletic – Chad Graff and Josh Kendall 11. Chicago Bears (3-2) Last week: 8 Sunday: Lost to Packers 31-7 Who have you beaten? Panthers, Eagles, Jets After raising the stakes in their rivalry with the Packers, the Bears got humbled in Green Bay. But good news is on the horizon with Caleb Williams nearing a return. It’s hard to knock the Bears too much for going 2-1 in his absence with Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent at the helm. CBS Sports – Pete Prisco 15. Chicago Bears (8) The run game struggled against the Packers, and because of that the backup quarterbacks did as well. But the worst part: The defense was awful. USAToday – Nate Davis 10. Chicago Bears (10): Just throw out Sunday’s Lambeau sleep. Injured QB Caleb Williams appears on the verge of returning for a team that generally held up well without him. PFT – Mike Florio Bears (No. 9; 3-2): Tyson Bagent’s expiration date seems to have arrived. ESPN NFL Nation – Courtney Cronin 13. Chicago Bears Week 5 result: Lost to the Packers 31-7 Week 5 ranking: 8 Biggest issue on defense: The secondary is more problematic than the pass rush The Bears’ preseason belief that their secondary would be the strength of the defense has gone out the window. That unit allowed Green Bay quarterback Jordan Love to complete six passes for 25-plus yards and has been trending down since a shootout with the Panthers in Week 1. Rookie defensive backs Dillon Thieneman and Malik Muhammad II will understandably experience growing pains, but the play of veteran cornerbacks Jaylon Johnson (77.3% of targets thrown into his coverage have been caught) and Tyrique Stevenson Sr. (allowing a 140.7 passer rating when targeted) is a major cause for concern. Yahoo Sports – Frank Schwab 8. Chicago Bears (3-2, LW: 6) It’s hard to rank the Bears. On one hand, they were horrendous in a 31-7 loss to the Packers. Also, they have scored 60 points in four games since scoring 59 in the opener. They’ve had two games scoring seven or fewer points. A defense that had been playing well gave up too many big plays against the Packers, who had 358 yards passing. Of course, everything will change soon when Caleb Williams comes back. It’s unfair to judge a team too harshly when it went 2-1 with two different backup quarterbacks. And Williams is close to returning from a hamstring injury. “He’s on track,” Bears head coach Ben Johnson said, via Bears Wire. “We’ll see if that’s Atlanta [for Week 6] or after. I think it’s going to be close.” Once Williams returns, it’ll be easier to get a clear read on the Bears.

title: Chicago Bears Rome Odunze needs to be better, but the drop narrative is unfair
summary: Let’s get this out of the way — Rome Odunze has not yet played like the #9 overall pick. He has played like a solid WR, but when you draft a WR in the top 10, you rightfully should expect him to become a top of the league player. Still, I think Rome is getting […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 11: Rome Odunze #15 of the Chicago Bears leaves the field after a loss against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on October 11, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s get this out of the way — Rome Odunze has not yet played like the #9 overall pick. He has played like a solid WR, but when you draft a WR in the top 10, you rightfully should expect him to become a top of the league player. Still, I think Rome is getting a bad deal by Chicago Bears fans. Sure, Rome has had some bad drops throughout his career, as well as contested catches that he should have come down with. However, I think that the narrative is clouding our judgement, and the “drops” decried by fans have not always been fairly characterized. Let’s acknowledge some of the egregious drops, as there have been a few. The first, and arguably worst was this drop against the Rams with a chance to go to the NFC Championship on the line. While the ball was thrown behind Rome, he needs to snatch this pass rather than let it travel to his body: There’ve been a lot of really bad Rome Odunze drops during his time with the Bears. The one right on his hands in the endzone against the Eagles is the freshest. This one against the Rams was the most costly. I don’t blame Ben Johnson for losing patience. pic.twitter.com/qnByY9eelK — All Things Chicago Sports (@things_sox) October 1, 2026 Another happened during the Week 3 game against the Philadelphia Eagles, where Odunze lost concentration in the end zone before he could secure the ball: Rome Odunze Was Wide Open, And He Drops It. Case Keenum Did Everything He Freaking Could On That Play, And It Should Have Been A Touchdown. 😭 pic.twitter.com/yF7cVX1a30 — SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) September 29, 2026 There have been a few other legitimate dropped passes to gripe about, including one against the Patriots his rookie year that slipped straight through his hands on a comeback route. But I am here to say: step out of the echo chamber and into reality. Rome needs to be better, yes, but the narrative around his drops is getting out of hand. This was no more clear than on Sunday when Tyson Bagent airmailed a pass to Rome, where he remarkably got two hands on the ball, just for the CB covering him to get his hands in to break it up (please ignore this Twitter user’s silly analysis): 9th overall pick rome odunze is a B U S T #dabears this is a B U M on your screen pic.twitter.com/3zZrzaE3kP — James (@DaaaSweener) October 11, 2026 Calling this anything more than a highly difficult play broken up by a great defensive effort is just parroting a narrative. There are several other instances where the narrative parrots a drop after Odunze doesn’t secure a diving sideline catch 6” off the ground. And it’s not just that the drop narrative has gotten out of hand; it’s that we seem to forget that he has made contested catches throughout his career. Here are some of my favorites: HIGHLIGHT REEL CATCH FROM ROME ODUNZE pic.twitter.com/HLAoyk82WI — Harrison Graham (@HGrahamNFL) September 13, 2026 Here’s the tight copy on Caleb Williams’ 4th down throw to Rome Odunze. It’s a middle of the field Hi-Lo concept — that stretches to the boundary. pic.twitter.com/q0wuPfIJ8A — Matt Bowen (@MattBowen41) January 11, 2026 3. Bears Vs. Commanders Rome Odunze TD wiped by an illegal motion flag. Even the announcers said there was NOTHING there. Took 7 off the board for no reason. pic.twitter.com/7BHUe17sma — Bears Facts (@DaBearsTakeOver) April 14, 2026 Some Caleb Williams to Rome Odunze highlights for your enjoyment on this Thanksgiving morning pic.twitter.com/T5gfd5hAju — Bearsszn (@bearszn) November 28, 2024 Coming into the league, Rome’s identity was a contested catch specialist who might not be able to separate enough at the next level. While Rome needs to find consistency in contested catches, he continues to be one of the best in the league at creating separation: WR Separation Score vs TPRR 📊 — Carnell Tate building chemistry with Ward — Downs, Doubs, Odunze, Pickens prime targets for positive regression — MHJ in a league of his own pic.twitter.com/kDtxG8H22T — JClyde (@JClyyde) October 8, 2026 This chart shows that Rome Odunze is consistently getting open, at a similar rate to Drake London, Garrett Wilson, and Romeo Doubs, but isn’t seeing the same target share as others. Through five games, Rome has 17 receptions for 273 yards, giving him pace for 58 receptions and 928 yards. While these aren’t #9 overall pick numbers, they are far from unproductive. I am still confident that Rome can turn into an even better pro with time. Mind you that he has only played with Caleb Williams four times since Week 13 of last season, while two of those came after a return from injury for Odunze. Let’s practice patience and give him time and consistency with Caleb to figure it out.

full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - JANUARY 26: Head Coach Mike Ditka of the Chicago Bears gets carried off the field after they defeated the New England Patriots in Super Bowl XX January 26, 1986 at the Louisiana Superdome in New Orleans, Louisiana. The Bears won the Super Bowl 46-10. (Photo by Focus on Sport/Getty Images) | Getty Images 1. Rest in peace to Bears legend Mike Ditka, who starred for Chicago as a revolutionary tight end and then delivered the city its only Super Bowl. Keep those sweater vests in rotation this whole year, especially for when the Bears return home in a few weeks. 2. Let’s keep it real: the Green Bay Packers whooped the Bears on Sunday. They earned their right to talk a little trash. This is a rivalry, after all, and they must’ve been wanting that lick back something awful after getting embarrassed twice at Soldier Field last season. I just want to say…you better be that brave when you’re not facing a backup quarterback at Soldier Field on Christmas. 3. That Washington franchise is just cursed. I’m not sure how else to say it. Every single time they get a sniff of hope—notably, in the form of No. 2 overall picks Robert Griffin III and Jayden Daniels—injuries and subsequent bumbling screw it all up. It all looked great for them after they forced a Cam Skattebo fumble with just under two minutes on the clock. (Seriously, what was it with both these teams and not wanting to just WIN THE GAME?) And it looked even better when they got the ball down to the New York 24-yard line with under a minute to go and the Giants having no ability to stop the clock. But, because a 41-yard field goal is too daunting a prospect, apparently, the Commanders decided to drop back and throw the ball with 14 seconds left, only for Jayden Daniels to scramble and get tackled inbounds with no timeouts. Please fire everyone involved. 4. You know who got this scenario right? The Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football, and you can beat the Commanders-Giants fiasco informed their decisions. Could things have gone wrong for them if Tyler Bass had missed that 45-yard field goal on 2nd-and-10 with two minutes left in the game? Sure. But they didn’t. Why? Because Joe Brady trusted Bass to do his job and go win the football game instead of half-heartedly trying to gain a few extra yards. Is that the difference between Brady being an offensive-minded coach and the likes of John Harbaugh and Dan Quinn not being so? I don’t know. But NFL coaches need to quit being scared of taking chances to win a game when it’s right in their grasp. Because if you keep playing around and waiting for someone else to screw up, a win can slip right through your fingers in the process. 5. Shoutout to Snoop Huntley for showing what a real professional backup quarterback can do in the Ravens’ overtime win over the Atlanta Falcons. The numbers weren’t super flashy (201 yards passing, two TDs), but the execution was just about flawless for the longtime Lamar Jackson understudy. That’s the difference between someone like a Huntley/Case Keenum type who’s been around the block and a young gun like Tyson Bagent with main-character energy. The old heads did all the little things right, and their teams won as a result. Take notes, youngblood. 6. My personal mantra when it comes to sports: never talk smack to opposing fans in the middle of a game. That approach served me well as I watched alongside a Packers fan friend of mine—no, seriously, great guy—as the Bears ripped the Packers’ hearts out twice last season. But I digress. This video of an Eagles fan hoping on the phone to trash-talk his Jacksonville Jaguars friend only to watch his team lose on a last-second field goal moments later is the definition of karma. Just sit and watch, y’all. Our teams will be better for it. 7. The Marvin Harrison Jr. saga is why you never pick the wide receiver, no matter how talented, over the potentially franchise-altering quarterback. While we won’t pretend that the Arizona Cardinals stand out as a beacon of organizational stability and development, the third-year pass-catcher out of Ohio State never came close to living up to the billing of a No. 4 overall pick. Can you imagine how fired Ryan Poles would’ve been if he’d passed on Williams to build around Fields and Harrison? I always pull for guys to rebound after tough starts to their career (see: Bryce Young), and maybe things can improve for him with his old buddy CJ Stroud, who needs a comeback of his own. But boy am I glad the Bears didn’t have to be the ones to trade him. 8. One week, Drake Maye looks completely cooked. The next, he’s putting up a 93.5 passing grade and lighting the Raiders up like that annoyingly early Christmas tree someone’s going to put out right after Halloween. Such is the maddening talent and instability of the ex-No. 3 pick from that aforementioned draft. The talent is undeniable. But the brain worms still exist. Here’s hoping he’s turning the corner toward figuring things out—just not so much it causes a problem for the Bears when they play the Pats two weekends from now. 9. Bring back excitable announcers! Charlotte Hornets play-by-play man Eric Collins went viral for his call of his Ja’Marr Chase touchdown grab on Sunday, which reminded me of when they used to let Gus Johnson do NFL games on occasion. I don’t care if it’s a little over the top. It’s at least different from every other guy sounding exactly like Kevin Burkhardt. (No offense.) 10. Question of the week: what happens when the NFL’s best offense over the last three weeks (which is playing at home next week) meets one of the worst road defenses in the league so far this season? A shootout? A bloodbath? An anticlimactic stalemate? Your answer is your prediction for the Bears’ visit to Atlanta to play the Falcons (hopefully with Williams back behind center).

title: Stock up, stock down: Bears-Packers review
summary: It’s getting tough to get a read on the Chicago Bears. They’ve been feast or famine through five games. Scoring 59 points, then three. Then 27, 23 and crashing back to seven points. The defense allowed 37, nine, seven, 12 and 31 points. Of course, it’s hard to find consistency with your backup quarterback(s). Ideally, […]
full_text: Chicago Bears cornerback Jaylon Johnson (1) pursues Green Bay Packers running back Marshawn Lloyd (32) on Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin. The Packers won the game, 31-7. Tork Mason/Green Bay Press-Gazette | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co It’s getting tough to get a read on the Chicago Bears . They’ve been feast or famine through five games. Scoring 59 points, then three. Then 27, 23 and crashing back to seven points. The defense allowed 37, nine, seven, 12 and 31 points. Of course, it’s hard to find consistency with your backup quarterback(s). Ideally, once Caleb Williams returns the volatility on the offensive side will level out. The defensive side, however, might continue to be tough to watch the rest of the year. Let’s get into this week’s list. Stock up Austin Booker, DE – Booker notched another two sacks on Sunday, three TFLs and two QB hits. He’s emerging as the No. 2 pass-rushing threat, something many have been hopeful of since he was drafted. Zavion Thomas, WR – Thomas finally popped off this week. He took a jet sweep for 11 yards, had another catch for 11 yards and finally hit a kick return for 61 yards. He averaged 32 yards per return. Hopefully, he can keep building on his snaps. Devin Bush, LB – Bush led the team in tackles and made a couple of the (very few) good plays for the defense, including two TFLs. Bush did get burned by Christian Watson on the latter’s first score. But it looked like he was expecting help over the top from Xavier Woods. Obviously if a linebacker, even one as fast as Bush, is expected to keep up with Watson, it’s just not going to happen. Stock down Tyson Bagent, QB – Bagent is a great story. Making the NFL alone as a D-II undrafted quarterback is a miracle itself. He’s earned every opportunity he’s gotten and he’s put in the work. Unfortunately, this is a results-based business and the results aren’t good. Bagent can be a decent backup in the league, but he’s not a starter. Roschon Johnson, RB – The promise that was brought up again and again when Roschon was drafted never materialized. Last season there were a lot of questions about why he was unable to earn a role in Ben Johnson’s offense. We’ve all seen the reasons, now. Five carries, six yards. Jaylon Johnson, CB – Johnson looks washed. I hate to say it, because it wasn’t long ago that he was a dynamic player and a huge part of the defense. Unfortunately, his injury looks like it’s robbed him of his speed. The Packers were deliberately targeting him every time they could and it worked seemingly every time. Honorable mention: Ben Johnson, coach – Johnson was outmatched Sunday. He stuck with Bagent when it clearly wasn’t working and his playcalls didn’t seem to have any easy answers for Bagent. Who is up and down in your world this week?

title: 3 Reasons Why the Chicago Bears Lost vs. the Packers
summary: We are on to the fifth installment of my new series for the 2026 season, where I recap what I believe were the three reasons the Chicago Bears won or lost the previous game. In week 5 at Lambeau Field, we all know what happened. The question is why? Here are my three reasons. 1. […]
full_text: NFL Football: Chicago Bears Tyson Bagent (17) scrambles in the pocket vs Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field.Green Bay, WI 10/11/2026 CREDIT: Erick W. Rasco (Photo by Erick W. Rasco/Sports Illustrated via Getty Images/Getty Images) (Set Number: X164960) We are on to the fifth installment of my new series for the 2026 season, where I recap what I believe were the three reasons the Chicago Bears won or lost the previous game. In week 5 at Lambeau Field, we all know what happened. The question is why? Here are my three reasons. 1. Pass Defense Not only did Packers QB Jordan Love have more time to throw in this game than he has in any game this season, but he also had a plethora of wide open options to choose from downfield. The pass rush had arguably their worst game of the season at the same time the secondary decided to have it’s worst game of the season. Not a good combination. Love completed 25 of 31 passes (81%) for 367 yards and 2 scores and was only sacked twice. Both at the end of the first half when GB was clearly trying to pass the ball to get some more points on the board before the break. This is the first game where the Bears secondary’s flaws were on full display for the world to see. Not having Coby Bryant alongside rookie Dillon Thieneman hurts. But with Jaylon Johnson looking washed and not one defensive back making plays in this one, GB carved up the Bears. Hopefully Kyler Gordon’s return will help boost the back end, but it is not looking good. 2. Turnovers Bagent simply looked out of his league in this one. Not sure if it was the nerves of the rivalry, a great defensive scheme or what, but he was slow to process the field and made poor decisions when it was time to pull the trigger. We knew coming into this season that the offense would have to carry the defense, despite some early season success from Dennis Allen’s unit. After all, Chicago has enough weapons to keep up with anyone on offense. If the QB can get them the ball and keep the chains moving enough to put points on the board. That said, I absolutely could have give Bagent his own section here, but it was the turnovers, on the road against a humming Packers Offense that really hurt Chicago’s chances. We have seen Ben Johnson lead us to 4th quarter comebacks often, but it is becoming increasingly clear that is truly a Caleb Williams stat – and his ball security is critical to any success the offense experiences. 3. Kyle Monangai, RB You have to wonder if Coach Johnson learned anything from last weeks contest when he fed the second year back a whopping 30 carries despite the teams RB1 healthy and on the sideline ready to play. Sure, Swift’s fumbles were back-breaking and Monangai had the hot hand, but 30 carries are a lot. Especially for a 5’8”, 207lb human. And Monangai ultimately got so banged up that he was held out of the first clash against Green Bay this season. Well, his absence was felt. Roschon Johnson, Monangai’s backup, is better served on special teams as he makes next to zero impact for the offense. And while Swift held his own, the one-two punch of him and Monangai was sorely missed as the latter provides the juice that the team needs with his rugged and assertive playstyle. Hopefully he is back on Christmas Day, along with Caleb Williams, because that offense simply doesn’t look the same without those two. What about you? Who or what stood out the most in the loss to the Cheese?

title: NFL analyst claims Joe Burrow is ‘the best quarterback in football’
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals have entered their 2026 bye week with a 3-2 record after a 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins this past weekend. The Bengals are in a better spot so far through 5 weeks than in the past few years, and that should excite Cincinnati fans. Another piece fans may not realize is […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals have entered their 2026 bye week with a 3-2 record after a 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins this past weekend. The Bengals are in a better spot so far through 5 weeks than in the past few years, and that should excite Cincinnati fans. Another piece fans may not realize is that Joe Burrow is playing the best football of his career in the early part of a season. Burrow had some frustrating turnovers against the Pittsburgh Steelers and Jacksonville Jaguars, but outside of those, he has played at an elite level. One football analyst turned on the 2026 Burrow tape and believes without a doubt that he is the best quarterback in football right now. Mark Schlereth of the OG Football Podcast shared his thoughts on Burrow and stated: “I can see why they never run it.” "He's Brady-esque" Mark just was on the call for the Bengals vs Dolphins in Hard Rock and what he saw out of Joe Burrow made him rethink how he would evaluate this offense 😳 pic.twitter.com/501rNvmG1k — The OG Football Show (@OGFootballShow) October 12, 2026 “He is in a complete cylinder. He is so ‘Brady-esque’ in that he is the best scrambler in football that never leaves the pocket… If he sees a profit, he takes it instantly… It is incredible to watch; he is just the best quarterback in football without question,” Schlereth said. Burrow is the most accurate quarterback in the NFL and can dice up any defense across the league when healthy. The Bengals QB currently has 1,361 passing yards, 11 touchdowns, and 3 interceptions through the first 5 games. Cincinnati will have their hands full out of the bye, visiting their AFC North rival in Baltimore, and Burrow will need to be at his best to leave with a win.

title: Bengals News: Is it Jack Endries time?
summary: With Tanner Hudson headed to IR and done for the season with a torn pec suffered in the Cincinnati Bengals’ win over the Dolphins, the offense is down one reliable tight end who has proven to be a trusted safety valve for Joe Burrow. While there’s no shortage of mouths to feed on the Bengals’ […]
full_text: With Tanner Hudson headed to IR and done for the season with a torn pec suffered in the Cincinnati Bengals’ win over the Dolphins, the offense is down one reliable tight end who has proven to be a trusted safety valve for Joe Burrow. While there’s no shortage of mouths to feed on the Bengals’ offense, they are down one tight end, and they just happen to have a tight end from this year’s draft on the roster. Former Texas tight end Jack Endries fell to the Bengals in the seventh round of this Spring’s draft and made the 53-man roster. He hasn’t taken any offensive snaps so far this season, only making a handful of appearances on special teams, but he caught six passes for 43 yards and a touchdown throughout the preseason. With Erick All not quite clicking, Endries has a real chance to shine now that Hudson is done for the year . Here’s what else is going on: Bengals RT Amarius Mims calls out major names after his unique problem pops up yet again in win over Dolphins “It’s crazy because that was the second I pair busted open, but that was my first time wearing the shoe,” Mims told WLWT’s Jaron May after the game. “Like I just got these in literally before we left for Miami, before we got on the plane, and I wore them. I looked down, man. My shoes are talking, man. My big toe. I see my big toe. I said, ‘Oh God, man, it’s not good.’ The Bengals fed the hot hand out of the backfield on Sunday in Miami, opting to give Samaje Perine 14 carries to Chase Brown’s 13. It’s close to being even, but Brown came into the season with a lock on RB1, and seemed to be the guy through the first couple games. Possibly not so much now, though, as Bengals’ offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher sees the situation as more fluid as they begin to run out of shotgun more, which suits Perine. Why the Bengals’ run game – and RB carry distribution – could be changing “I wouldn’t want to tackle (Perine),” Karras said. “When we get into our gun 11 (personnel) runs, Chase and Samaje both bring unique stuff where Chase can find a hole and hit it at 20 miles per hour. Samaje, even if you don’t get to the linebacker, he is running through it and going to take him 2, 3 yards to tackle him.” It wasn’t too terribly long ago when Jake Browning kept the Bengals’ playoff hopes alive while Burrow rehabbed from injury. Now Joe Flacco is the backup quarterback and Browning has a new home in Los Angeles. Browning has signed with the Chargers , who’ve started the 2026 season with an 0-5 record. title: Ja’Marr Chase’s fines for the people’s elbow celebration get rescinded by NFL
summary: Good news for fans of fun. Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja’Marr Chase had his fines from Week 2 rescinded by the NFL. Chase had two fines from that game, while Tee Higgins had four. There is still no word on Higgins’ fines being changed in any way, yet. The duo has claimed the celebration is […]
full_text: Good news for fans of fun. Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja’Marr Chase had his fines from Week 2 rescinded by the NFL. Chase had two fines from that game, while Tee Higgins had four. There is still no word on Higgins’ fines being changed in any way, yet. The duo has claimed the celebration is a combination of ‘the people’s elbow’ — a move performed by Dwayne ‘The Rock’ Johnson as a professional wrestler as well as the first down signal. I think it is clear what most people, and the league, saw when it was performed. The NFL came down hard with multiple fines for each player, but there was always a very good excuse for these two against how much they were fined, or for even being fined at all. Higgins did the celebration multiple times in Week 1, and yet he was not hit with a fine or a warning. Chase failed to pull off the celebration, but as far as they were concerned, it clearly was okay if the league didn’t do anything. This really stems from Chase making one of the most ridiculous catches you will ever see and then pulling out the celebration. That caught the attention of everyone and the league, and needless to say it was taken to mean something different than Higgins and Chase allege. For now, it seems the celebration will be shelved, but there is a sense of justice for at least Chase so far. Maybe the league will flop out a residency for Higgins soon as well. #Bengals WR Ja’Marr Chase won appeals of fines for his “people’s elbow” celebration, as two fines of $14,926 were rescinded from the #Texans game. title: Bengals Tuesday Trenches: 5 Bye Week Overreactions
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals did what they needed to do on Sunday to beat the lowly Miami Dolphins. In doing so, they head into their bye week with a winning record. At 3-2, they’re technically in last place in the AFC North, but they’re very much in the thick of things. That’s not to say things […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals did what they needed to do on Sunday to beat the lowly Miami Dolphins. In doing so, they head into their bye week with a winning record. At 3-2, they’re technically in last place in the AFC North, but they’re very much in the thick of things. That’s not to say things are perfect in Cincinnati, because they’re not. After the first two games showcasing a dominant defense, Al Golden’s crew has struggled over the last three weeks. The offense, despite all their star power, looks mediocre at times. Before we get into some overreactions heading into the bye week, here are some random thoughts on the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins : Congratulations to Evan McPherson, whose 22nd consecutive made field goal established a new franchise record, surpassing the previous mark held by Shayne Graham. Joe Burrow completed more than 70% of his passes and threw four touchdowns, but averaged just 5.1 yards per completion. Much of his afternoon was spent dinking and dunking underneath, taking what the defense gave him rather than pushing the ball downfield. On the rare occasions he did take a shot deep, though, he reminded everyone what he’s capable of: JA'MARR CHASE ARE YOU SERIOUS @CINvsMIA on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/k4RKY5bLbY — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 Jordan Battle took plenty of heat for his performances in Weeks 3 and 4, and deservedly so. He responded with two interceptions against Miami, but what impressed me most was his tackling. Battle was much more reliable in the open field on Sunday, and this tackle may very well have saved a touchdown: More than the interceptions, these are the plays I want to see more of from Jordan Battle. Make the sound tackle and keep a moderate gain a moderate gain on the play. pic.twitter.com/VTDWyJKmCH — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 12, 2026 The Bengals, largely thanks to their rebuilt defensive line, have been pretty successful at stopping the run between the tackles. When opposing running backs get to the outside, though, it’s a different story. After shutting down Houston’s rushing attack in Week 2, Cincinnati has struggled to contain the ground games of the Steelers, Jaguars, and Dolphins. It’s becoming a troubling trend. I know the Bengals only won by a touchdown, but the game wasn’t nearly as close as the final score suggests. Miami’s late touchdown was the very definition of garbage-time scoring. Still, I don’t love the fact that the Bengals are the only team the Dolphins have managed to score more than 13 points against this season. Bye Week Overreactions With the bye week upon us, here are a few overreactions based on what we’ve seen from the Bengals through the first five weeks of the season. Samaje Perine should be RB1 Zac Taylor decided to ride the hot hand on Sunday in Miami, giving Perine 13 carries compared to Chase Brown’s 11. Perine was the more effective runner against the Dolphins, just as he was in Week 4, although neither back had much success against Jacksonville. That doesn’t mean Brown should be relegated to the bench. Brown has been far more involved in the passing game, hauling in 24 receptions compared to Perine’s seven. Considering the Bengals have Joe Burrow under center and operate a pass-first offense, Brown isn’t going anywhere. Dexter Lawrence wasn’t worth the No. 10 pick After back-to-back losses in Weeks 3 and 4, followed by a game in which the Dolphins nearly doubled their combined scoring output from the previous four weeks, it’s clear the Bengals should have used their top-10 pick on someone who could actually transform their defense. Right? Wrong. Lawrence has earned the second-highest defensive grade among defensive linemen who have played at least 50% of their team’s snaps, according to PFF, with an 82.5 grade. He also ranks third among defensive tackles in quarterback hurries. And don’t overlook the improved play of linebackers Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight Jr. Much of their development can be attributed to Lawrence occupying blockers in front of them, allowing them to make plays they might not have made a year ago. Lawrence isn’t the problem. He’s a big part of the solution. Tee Higgins is WR1 Both Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have caught 27 passes through five games, but Higgins has racked up 423 receiving yards compared to Chase’s 289. And that doesn’t mean a damn thing. On almost any other team in the NFL, Higgins would unquestionably be WR1. Unfortunately for him, he shares the field with the best wide receiver in football. Chase can do things that almost no other receiver in the league can replicate. Higgins is a phenomenal player, and there’s no denying that, but Chase is on another level. Darrin Simmons is on the hot seat Special teams haven’t exactly been a bright spot for the Bengals this season. Outside of Evan McPherson and the kicking game, the unit has been responsible for several costly mistakes. In Week 3, a muffed punt and a roughing-the-kicker penalty cost Cincinnati 10 points. Against Miami, Lawrence was flagged for roughing the snapper on a field goal attempt, extending a drive that ultimately ended in a Dolphins touchdown. And that wasn’t the only special teams mistake on Sunday. Here’s the thing, though: Simmons has been Cincinnati’s special teams coordinator since 2003 and has held the title of assistant head coach since 2020. If there’s one thing Mike Brown and the Bengals’ front office are known for, it’s loyalty. Simmons has been with the organization for more than two decades, and despite the recent mistakes, it’s hard to imagine him going anywhere. He’ll probably be in Cincinnati until he decides to retire. Tanner Hudson > Erick All Erick All returned to the Bengals after an injury that kept him off the field for much of the last two seasons. Through the first four weeks, Cincinnati made a concerted effort to establish an offense that operated more frequently from under center. Unfortunately, the results were mixed at best. Against Miami, the Bengals moved away from that approach, potentially signaling a shift in offensive philosophy coming out of the bye. If that’s the case, Hudson could see his role expand at All’s expense. That doesn’t necessarily mean Hudson is the better tight end. He’s simply more familiar with the shotgun-heavy offense the Bengals have relied on over the last two seasons, while All spent much of that time recovering from injury. If Cincinnati continues to lean into what Burrow does best, Hudson could find himself playing a much bigger role moving forward. What are some of your Bengals overreactions as the team heads into their bye week? Relevant Song Lyrics? And we’re winning (winning), winning (winning) ugly And we’re winning (winning), winning (winning) ugly And we’re headed for the heartbreak Headed for the blues, yeah

title: Officials miss horrible late hit on Joe Burrow in win vs. Dolphins
summary: Late in the Cincinnati Bengals’ 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins, quarterback Joe Burrow was seen throwing his helmet when he came off the field after failing to score a touchdown in the red zone. Some thought the frustration came from failing to finish the drive, but it appears it was more related to officiating. […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 11: Joe Burrow #9 of the Cincinnati Bengals reacts against the Miami Dolphins during the third quarter at Hard Rock Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images Late in the Cincinnati Bengals ’ 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins, quarterback Joe Burrow was seen throwing his helmet when he came off the field after failing to score a touchdown in the red zone. Some thought the frustration came from failing to finish the drive, but it appears it was more related to officiating. Somehow, the officials missed a blatant roughing the passer call on Burrow’s third-down throw. This is the play that made Joe threw his helmet on the sidelines. That should have been a flag for a late hit so obvious. pic.twitter.com/6eySZ9NWKI — Depressed Cincy Fan (@depressedcincy) October 12, 2026 In the video, you can see two defenders hit Burrow well after he releases the ball. Furthermore, it appears both players land on top of Burrow with their full body weight, something the NFL has tried to take out of the game via roughing the passer penalties. This seems to be a problem Burrow has dealt with for his entire NFL career. We see flags for hits on quarterbacks much less obvious than this every week, but for some reason, Burrow doesn’t seem to get those calls. Burrow was surely frustrated to not get the call, as it would have extended the drive, but you have to wonder if this is also a result of all of the other missed calls that have built up over time. If the NFL really wants to protect quarterbacks, they could start by enforcing the rules when it comes to one of the more popular quarterbacks in the game.

title: Bengals News: Amarius Mims calls for help with his cleats problem

In a season where he’s faced Ruben Bain Jr., Will Anderson, Danielle Hunter and T.J. Watt, Mims has been stonewalling some of the best players in the league. One part of his game that needs some […]

The same happened in Week 5 in Miami, leading Mims to ask for help. Bengals News: Amarius Mims calls out major names after his unique problem pops up yet again in win over Dolphins “Mims is rightfully fed up with the situation. When he explained what happened to reporters after the game, he called on shoe manufacturers to step up and find him a solution.” Jack Kiser Acquired on Waivers, Swayze Bozeman Placed on Reserve/Injured List After losing a linebacker and special teams contributor, the Bengals quickly acted and acquired a replacement that Al Golden is very familiar with. Bengals embrace an early bye after a win in Miami “The Bengals go into the bye with a 3-2 record and one game behind the Ravens in the AFC North. The teams have their first meeting of the season in Baltimore on Oct. 25.” Bengals’ C+ Draft Class Is a Cashius Howell Show Until the Rest of the Seven Picks Arrive “Nobody expects a fourth- or sixth-rounder to turn into an All-Pro overnight. The Bengals are playing the long game with Lew and Parker, and that makes a lot of sense. But until somebody else from this group actually gets on the field and makes a play, this rookie class is riding on Howell’s back.” Joe Burrow calls Bengals’ Perine ‘Mr. Reliable’ after Dolphins win “For Perine, his quarterback’s evaluation highlighted the trust behind those opportunities. When Cincinnati needed to finish a lengthy drive, Burrow turned to a classic target.”

title: Browns: Is Minkah Fitzpatrick a dirty player? You make the call!
summary: The Cleveland Browns and their fans have an uneasy history with New York Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick. It was Fitzpatrick, after all, who, while with the Pittsburgh Steelers, effectively ended Cleveland running back Nick Chubb’s career with a direct hit to Chubb’s knee during a Monday night game in 2023. So it is understandable that […]
full_text: (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns and their fans have an uneasy history with New York Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick. It was Fitzpatrick, after all, who, while with the Pittsburgh Steelers, effectively ended Cleveland running back Nick Chubb’s career with a direct hit to Chubb’s knee during a Monday night game in 2023. So it is understandable that Cleveland fans may take a dim view of Fitzpatrick. That history resurfaced in the first quarter of Sunday’s game, when Fitzpatrick committed a facemask penalty so severe it tore the helmet from wide receiver KC Concepcion’s head. Then, just a few plays later, Fitzpatrick delivered a head shot to Concepcion on a pass play that knocked him out of the game with a concussion. On Monday, head coach Todd Monken was asked about the play and took the position that it was all just a part of the game : “It was a bang-bang play. He made a nice break on the ball. It is unfortunate what happened, but that is going to happen in games, and I’ve gone against, like I said last night, Minkah a bunch, and I’ve always had a ton of respect for him, and I’ve never understood him to be a player that’s trying to injure other players. I’ve never known him to be that. I know he’s a guy that plays the ball well in the air and is aggressive, and unfortunately it ended up being a bang-bang play, and it cost us a player.” Monken has certainly been around the game a long time. And while it is perhaps a bit odd that he chose not to back his player, Monken has seen a lot of football. Not everyone saw it that way, however, as Cleveland offensive tackle Dawand Jones had a very different opinion on the matter, one that he had no problem sharing with Fitzpatrick in the moment, according to cleveland.com : “I just told him that (expletive)’s (expletive) up. I was there on the field when he did that (expletive) to Chubb, and he just told me, ‘It’s football,’ and I’m not down with that (expletive). “That (expletive)’s not football at that point; you’re just out there trying to hurt people. I’m not cool with that. But I’m gonna tell you to your face, flat out how it is. You can like it or not and get down with it, or you could do something about it. And you see what he did.” On Monday, we took to social media to question why the NFL puts up with Fitzpatrick’s style of play. And to put it mildly, that did not go over very well with fans of the Jets and Steelers. Which got us to thinking: are we wrong about this? Was it really just a good, hard football play? Have we gone soft, as one person put it, from watching English Premier League football? Then it struck us! Our readers are bright people; they would know! Back in the 1970s, there was a weekly feature during televised NFL games where they would show a controversial play and challenge the viewers at home to “make the call!” So in that spirit, here is a poll about the hit so you can have your say – is Fitzpatrick a cheap-shot artist, or simply an aggressive but misunderstood player? Vote early, vote often! (Actually, don’t cheat the vote!) And be sure to have your say in the comments or by visiting The Feed post . Bring the Dawg Pound with you on the SB Nation app! summary: The ever-changing Cleveland Browns roster, especially with lingering injury concerns, had a number of moves on Tuesday as part of Week 6 preparations for the Baltimore Ravens. full_text: The ever-changing Cleveland Browns roster, especially with lingering injury concerns , had a number of moves on Tuesday as part of Week 6 preparations for the Baltimore Ravens . On Monday, multiple reports came out that RB Audric Estime would be added to the Browns roster , with many wondering who would be departing to make room for the former New Orleans Saints and Denver Broncos back. Instead of one of the rumored trades making room , Cleveland placed backup RB Raheim Sanders on injured reserve Tuesday, while making the Estime signing official. Sanders had three carries and one reception in 20 snaps in Week 5 , with no indication of when he may have injured his hip, the designation the team gave for his IR move. On top of those two 53-man roster changes, the Browns made four moves on the practice squad: Signed TE Devin Culp and G Vershon Lee to the practice squad Released CB Myles Bryant and WR James Proche II from the practice squad. Proche was signed last week, but was not elevated for the game. Bryant has been on and off Cleveland’s roster since signing this offseason but has not played in a game. The team shared the following about the two practice squad additions: Culp (6-4, 237) is in his third NFL season out of Washington. Originally drafted by Tampa Bay in the seventh round in 2024, Culp has appeared in 18 career games. He will wear No. 82. Lee (6-4, 318) is officially in his first NFL season out of South Carolina. Originally signed by Minnesota as an undrafted free agent in 2025, Lee has appeared in one career game. He will wear No. 65. title: Quinshon Judkins can’t get going, wide receiver reps change in Browns offense
summary: You hate to throw things out the window in terms of judgment of this game, but that’s sort of what I did with respect to the Browns’ offensive performance against the Jets. It was raining all game, and got heavier in the fourth quarter. When the rain was forecast, my expectations turned to a low-scoring […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NJ - OCTOBER 11: Quinshon Judkins #10 of the Cleveland Browns during the game against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on October 11, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images You hate to throw things out the window in terms of judgment of this game, but that’s sort of what I did with respect to the Browns’ offensive performance against the Jets. It was raining all game, and got heavier in the fourth quarter. When the rain was forecast, my expectations turned to a low-scoring game, with the potential for some turnovers. Why, then, would I get extra concerned about the offense because my expectations were met? Below, we analyze the snap counts and stats on offense for the Cleveland Browns ’ Week 5 game against the New York Jets. Quarterback Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats QB Deshaun Watson 68 100% 15-of-33 (45.5%) for 155 yards, 1 TD. 6 carries, 40 yards (6.7 YPC). The Jets were able to sack Deshaun Watson eight times. Between that, the running game not working, and a few penalties, we saw Watson try to push the ball downfield a few times in earlier downs to make up yards. It went against the formula of taking those short, open passes in previous weeks to help get easy, efficient yards. I also thought later in the game that Watson tried to take off a few times in situations where he probably should’ve tried to let something rip, even if it led to an interception. Granted, we didn’t see what the receiving opportunities looked like on those plays, but still. I’m thinking more about the 4th-and-11 sack he took to conclude the game. PFF graded Watson out to a 48.2 on offense. Running Back Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats RB Quinshon Judkins 36 53% 14 carries, 44 yards (3.1 YPC). 3 catches, 6 yards (4 targets). RB Raheim Sanders 20 29% 3 carries, 12 yards (4.0 YPC). 1 catch, 1 yard (1 target). RB Jaleel McLaughlin 14 21% 0 catches (1 target). FB Michael Burton 1 1% No stats registered. I remain down on Quinshon Judkins . I feel like I’m beating a dead horse each week, but when you see all of the team’s impressive rookies, Judkins has fallen to the back of the line. There is nothing about his running style or ability right now that looks special or even starter-worthy. He does not look like the same back from pre-injury a year ago. PFF graded him as the team’s worst offensive player (41.7). What really drove me crazy about Judkins is him going out of bounds to stop the clock with about four minutes to go, right after the defense got the turnover. I know there are other things that contributed to the loss, but I wonder if that created a trickle down effect of needing to throw the ball as opposed to running more clock, which led to the butterfly effect of the bad punt snap and go-ahead touchdown for the Jets. Jaleel McLaughlin received some more snaps this week. Unfortunately, he dropped the one open pass that came his way that could have been a pretty decent-looking gain in the first half. Wide Receiver Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats WR Denzel Boston 62 91% 3 catches, 46 yards (7 targets), 1 TD. WR Jerry Jeudy 55 81% 3 catches, 19 yards (7 targets). WR Isaiah Bond 49 72% 3 catches, 74 yards (7 targets). WR Malachi Corley 16 24% No stats registered. WR KC Concepcion 11 16% 1 catch, 5 yards (1 target). Once again, Denzel Boston came up with a big catch, using his speed and size to haul in a go-ahead touchdown catch mid-way through the fourth quarter. KC Concepcion got two early targets, but the second one didn’t count because he was knocked out (penalty negates the target). Even though you have the next-man up mentality, when you consider the timing Watson tries to build with the receivers, and the rain, that certainly could’ve impacted the game. For example, Isaiah Bond got a huge boost in reps this week. In fact, Boston, he, and Jerry Jeudy all had 70%+ of the snaps, so Cleveland went with more three-receiver looks. But Bond had more big-play opportunities come his way. Watson just barely missed a touchdown pass to him, throwing it beyond his reach. And trying to rally late, Watson hit him open over the middle and he dropped it. Despite that, PFF graded Bond out to a 63.7. Tight End Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats TE Harold Fannin 63 93% 1 catch, 4 yards (4 targets). TE Blake Whiteheart 13 19% No stats registered. Harold Fannin only had one catch late and was a non-factor in the rainy conditions. He was the Browns’ second-lowest graded player by PFF, grading out to a 43.9. Offensive Line Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats OL Spencer Fano 68 100% OL Elgton Jenkins 68 100% OL Austin Barber 68 100% OL Zion Johnson 68 100% OL Tytus Howard 35 51% OL Dawand Jones 33 49% Tytus Howard was dinged up early in the game, tried to return, and eventually seemed to give way to Dawand Jones . I know Howard hasn’t been the best this season, but Dawand Jones was the team’s lowest-graded lineman (46.9) by a wide margin this week, as Zion Johnson , Spencer Fano , and Elgton Jenkins all graded respectably despite all the sacks we saw.
