title: Anton Harrison To IR: Surgery Timeline Could Define Jaguars’ 2026
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars picked up the most exciting win of 2026 on Sunday in London, but may have lost the most important piece of their offensive line in the same afternoon. Starting left tackle Anton Harrison was carted off the field at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in the third quarter of the 19-17 victory over the […]
full_text: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 11: Anton Harrison of the Jacksonville Jaguars is carted off the field during the 2026 NFL London Games match between Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 11, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Ryan Pierse/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars picked up the most exciting win of 2026 on Sunday in London, but may have lost the most important piece of their offensive line in the same afternoon. Starting left tackle Anton Harrison was carted off the field at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in the third quarter of the 19-17 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles after suffering a knee injury. What the team learns in the operating room over the next week could go a long way toward determining just how much damage that moment inflicted on the rest of the season. Here’s the latest on what we know: Surgery Imminent (Reportedly) Harrison had missed just three games in his first three NFL seasons since being drafted 27th overall out of Oklahoma in 2023. The Jaguars recently picked up his fifth-year option in April, with a flip from right tackle to left. On the play in question, Harrison went down during a Bhayshul Tuten rush, appearing to grab his right knee after disengaging from his block against Eagles defensive lineman Moro Ojormo. On Monday, head coach Liam Coen confirmed the team was awaiting the results of further tests and imaging before drawing any conclusions on Harrison’s future availability. By Tuesday morning, the picture became considerably clearer with NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport and ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler both reporting that Harrison is expected to undergo arthroscopic knee surgery following the team’s return from London. While the reports confirmed the injury and procedure, the open question is what the surgeon finds once inside the knee. The team has not yet confirmed the injury specifics, whether Harrison will remain in London until the Jaguars conclude their Week 6 matchup against the Houston Texans, or whether Harrison could return to Jacksonville immediately to get the recovery clock started. Medical staff often prefer to allow swelling to subside before performing arthroscopic surgery, which may factor into the timing decision. The Two Timelines According to the reports from Rapoport and Fowler, the surgical findings will determine one of two very different outcomes: Harrison could be out as few as three to five weeks, placing him on the shorter end of the Injured Reserve window, or the procedure could reveal damage significant enough to cost him three to four months, effectively ending his 2026 regular season. The doctor will not know which outcome applies until the arthroscope is inside the knee. The difference between those two scenarios is enormous for a team with Super Bowl aspirations. A three-to-five-week absence puts Harrison back on the field before the end of November. A three-to-four-month timeline ends his year, with a hope for postseason availability. Jaguars Schedule Through November: Bye Week Indianapolis Colts (at home) Baltimore Ravens (road) Tennessee Titans (road) New York Giants (road) Tennessee Titans (at home) With this slate, Jacksonville may be able to weather the storm reasonably, should a three-to-five week return be the eventual prognosis. With the morning reporting of a three week minimum recovery, the team later, announced Harrison would be placed on Injured Reserve. We have signed S Kaevon Merriweather to the active roster and signed LS Jacob Bobenmoyer to the practice squad. We have also placed OL Anton Harrison on the Reserve/Injured list. @Shift4 | #DUUUVAL https://t.co/6DXsiErbyB — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) October 13, 2026 The roster move to IR was pretty much a given based on the timelines for recovery and the Jaguars bye week approaching. NFL Precedents for Linemen Los Angeles Rams defensive lineman Myles Garrett, who recently underwent arthroscopic knee surgery, could be the most relevant and recent NFL comparable to what Jacksonville is hoping for from Harrison. Garrett, the reigning Defensive Player of the Year, underwent arthroscopic knee surgery in mid-September and was placed on Injured Reserve. The expectation when Garrett went on IR was that he would be ready to return after completing the mandatory four-game minimum. In the Meantime: Options Walker Little seems to be the immediate answer at left tackle while Harrison is out, having already stepped into the role for the final quarter against Philadelphia, giving up zero quarterback pressures. Trent Williams stood his ground pic.twitter.com/Zt4TfvoKhe — PFF (@PFF) October 12, 2026 However, Little has experience on both the left and right sides, starting 2026 on the right during training camp, after losing the starting role on the left to Cole Van Lanen in 2025. With his flexibility and history, transition to either side is not unfamiliar territory. This places Jacksonville in a reasonably fine position, all things considered. Cole Van Lanen also provides organizational flexibility for the line, should the situation require additional options, as he could also flip back to the left side, where he played before his 2025 knee injury. Based on the team’s history of always prioritizing linemen with positional flexibility, the possibility of a post-bye week offensive line shuffle could be on the table to get the best five on the field. The possibility of a return from IR for Patrick Mekari adds an additional layer to this complex offensive line discussion. Jacksonville placed Mekari (back) on injured reserve with a designation to return during the August final roster cuts. General Manager James Gladstone hinted at the possibility of a shorter-window return for Mekari in early September, stating, “I think he’d be quickly thereafter the threshold for return to get in.” If Mekari’s 21-day practice window opens this week or during the bye, that provides additional swing tackle and guard depth, while providing more options for different line combinations. LT: Walker Little or Cole Van Lanen LG: Emmanuel Pregnon or Ezra Cleveland C: Robert Hainsey RG: Ezra Cleveland, Emmanuel Pregnon, or Patrick Mekari (TBD) RT: Walker Little or Cole Van Lanen Swing OT and Swing OG: Patrick Mekari (TBD) or Ezra Cleveland/Emmanuel Pregnon, if relegated to backup Coach Coen, on Monday, confirmed that outside help is unlikely and that a player would likely be elevated from the practice squad if Harrison were unavailable for Sunday. “I feel like we have pretty good depth right now, so I think we’ll be all right,” Coen stated. The Jaguars’ Week 6 game against the Houston Texans is scheduled for 9:30 (EST) Sunday at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, followed by the team’s Week 7 bye week.

The latest Kansas City Chiefs news Jury returns mixed verdict in Tyreek Hill civil battery case, awards $500,000 to ex-wife | Pro Football Talk The civil lawsuit brought by Tyreek Hill’s ex-wife alleging multiple counts of battery and related legal claims has resulted in a verdict. Via Diana Moskovitz of Defector Media , the jury found Hill responsible for two counts of battery. He was found not responsible on the remaining counts. The jury awarded Keeta Vaccaro $500,000 in compensatory damages. The jury did not enter an award of punitive damages. The jury’s decision not to award punitive damages is curious. Battery is an intentional tort. In Florida, however, the law requires “clear and convincing evidence” of intentional misconduct. It’s possible, in theory, that the jury found evidence of battery under the lower “preponderance of the evidence” standard but not “clear and convincing” proof, which is a higher bar. State shares boundaries for Kansas City Chiefs STAR Bonds District | KSHB 41 The district stretches across Wyandotte County and Johnson County, including KCK, Bonner Springs, Edwardsville, Shawnee, Lenexa and Olathe. The map excludes the University of Kansas Medical Center complex, a predominantly vacant portion of Shawnee and existing STAR bond districts. In a Kansas Department of Commerce press release, the state said the map was designed with “clear goals shared by the administration and the legislature.” Those goals include maximizing economic benefit and paying off bonds as quickly as possible. Long Time Ex-Chiefs’ 6-Year Veteran Re-Signs with Playoff Rivals 1 Day After Release | Heavy Sports “The Bills reversed the transaction they made to have CB Anthony Kendall on the 53-man roster for Monday’s game to help play slot CB in the absence of Dee Alford. Today they released Kendal & signed OLB Mike Danna back to the active roster.” Chris Brown, the team’s play-by-play radio broadcaster, posted on Tuesday. The day before, as Brown alluded to, the team made the opposite move and signed Kendall to the active roster and released Danna; a move that was designed to give the Bills more depth at nickel cornerback against the Rams on Monday night. The Jury Is Still Out on Chiefs’ Safety Room Following Bye Week | Sports Illustrated Starting with Gilman, the former Los Angeles Chargers and Baltimore Ravens standout isn’t exactly lacking statistically compared to his last couple of seasons. Across Pro Football Reference , Pro Football Focus and NFL Pro ‘s data, his coverage data averages out to 10 targets and six completions, 8.3 yards per target and a 120.6 passer rating. He’s being tried more often down the field (13.9-yard average depth of target) and performing at his recent — albeit underwhelming — standard, but it’s the lack of ball production that’s really hurting. One of Gilman’s main draws is his ability to make splash plays, evidenced by his 28 career pass breakups, six fumble recoveries, five forced fumbles and five interceptions. Four games in, he’s been quiet, which is a concern. Chiefs star Travis Kelce now embraces a practice drill he once loathed | The Kansas City Star “Even after the whistle is blown and the play is so-called dead, defensive players are still running up to you trying to punch the ball out,” Kelce said of the training-camp drills. “And I don’t know why … it’s very annoying, especially when you’re in your third day of pads or sixth day of pads in seven days or whatever there was (at training camp), and you’re just getting … haymakered by linebackers and DBs down the field as you’re trying to, like, finish the play. So I was just being a (jerk) one day. I was like, I better see (teammates) throwing haymakers in the game, or I’m … pissed. Around the NFL 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw’s 1-game suspension upheld on appeal | The Athletic San Francisco 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw’s one-game suspension has been upheld on appeal, the NFL announced Tuesday night. He will miss Monday night’s home game against the Washington Commanders and will be eligible to return Oct. 25 at the Atlanta Falcons. “Hearing officer James Thrash, jointly appointed by the NFL and the NFLPA, has upheld the one-game suspension of San Francisco 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw,” Michael Signora, the NFL senior vice president of football and international communications, posted on social media. NFL suspends Rams’ Alaric Jackson for two games after punch | ESPN The NFL on Tuesday suspended Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson for two games without pay after he punched Buffalo Bills outside linebacker Bradley Chubb following Monday night’s 37-34 overtime loss in Los Angeles. The league said Jackson violated Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, which applies to “any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship.” “Have to make better decisions than that,” Rams coach Sean McVay said. Rams release kicker Harrison Mevis after disastrous loss to Bills, sign Jets’ practice squad kicker | CBS Sports The Los Angeles Rams are making a special teams change on the heels of their 37-34 overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday night. NFL Media reports the team is releasing kicker Harrison Mevis and signing Blake Grupe off the New York Jets’ practice squad. Mevis, affably known as “the Thiccer Kicker,” made all four of his extra-point attempts on Monday, but missed his two field-goal attempts. His first miss came from 50 yards in the first quarter, and his final miss came in overtime on a 48-yard game-winning attempt — a kick that was tipped by Bills defensive end Greg Rousseau. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride How Chiefs’ receiver rotation could adjust without Tyquan Thornton Allen, on the other hand, could step into the big-play role that will be missing without Thornton. Last season at the University of Cincinnati, Allen caught 51 passes for 674 yards and an FBS-leading 13 touchdowns. Six of those scores came on throws of 20 or more yards downfield; 23% of Allen’s targets in 2025 were deep throws. During the preseason and training camp, Allen appeared to be developing chemistry with quarterback Patrick Mahomes on difficult throws, whether against tight coverage over the middle or on the sideline. Allen may not have Thornton’s linear speed, but his route running and ball skills could make up for it when the ball’s in the air. title: One wide receiver most fits the bill for a Chiefs midseason trade
summary: The latest addition to the Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver room — signing Justin Watson to the practice squad — may not have been the flashy signing Chiefs Kingdom expected, but it also may not be the only new face in the group this season. The season-long injury to wide receiver Tyquan Thornton (dislocated ankle) […]
full_text: (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The latest addition to the Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver room — signing Justin Watson to the practice squad — may not have been the flashy signing Chiefs Kingdom expected, but it also may not be the only new face in the group this season. The season-long injury to wide receiver Tyquan Thornton (dislocated ankle) puts the team in position to look at ways to improve the position. We expect the Cheetah, Tyreek Hill, to return to the Chiefs this season , but there are no guarantees. If a significant move is to be made, it could be a trade. It wouldn’t be the first time general manager Brett Veach has traded for a wide receiver midseason. 2022: Traded a compensatory third-round pick and a sixth-round pick for Kadarius Toney 2023: Traded a future sixth-round pick for Mecole Hardman 2024: Traded a fifth-round pick for DeAndre Hopkins So who could Kansas City get via trade? The NFL Trade Deadline is November 10th, less than a month from today. The rumors are starting to swirl, and according to NFL Insider Jordan Schultz , a receiver on the (3-2) Cleveland Browns could be available. “Jerry Jeudy… the Browns clearly like the young receiver group they have and are building… Jeudy made some big plays in Thursday night’s win over [the Pittsburgh Steelers ], but then only played 24 snaps on Sunday, even with (KC Concepcion) leaving early with a concussion.” “It’s pretty well-known around the league that Jeudy is available, but my understanding is that Cleveland would like something in that early-third-to-fourth range; I’m just not sure they’ll be able to get it.” Jerry Jeudy Six years ago, Jeudy was the 15th overall pick of the Denver Broncos in the 2020 NFL Draft, which is the first criterion that stands out about trading for him. Whether it was Toney or Hopkins, or even wide receiver Josh Gordon in 2021, Veach has targeted former high-end talents or former first-round picks when the organization has no prior history with them. However, there are some ties to the Chiefs: Wide receivers coach Chad O’Shea coached Jeudy for two seasons in Cleveland, including a Pro Bowl campaign in 2024 in which Jeudy racked up 1,229 yards on 90 receptions. It’s the only Pro Bowl season of Jeudy’s career. This season, Jeudy has been buried in the rotation and has only caught eight passes for 81 yards. However, he has shown he can make plays downfield in Cleveland. Over the 2024 and 2025 seasons, Jeudy caught 12 passes thrown 20 or more yards downfield, for 438 yards and four touchdowns, according to Pro Football Focus . Jeudy is a volatile playmaker; he had 19 drops between the 2024 and 2025 campaigns. If Cleveland is motivated to find draft compensation for Jeudy’s talents, the Chiefs are a strong fit based on Jeudy’s pedigree, the ties to O’Shea and what he brings to the offense. If Kansas City can send a Day 3 pick for the 27-year-old wideout, it could be a strong option to replenish the Chiefs’ playmaking for this season and the future without taking a huge risk. He is signed through the 2027 season, with a $13.4 million cap hit next year. Editor’s Note: Jeudy’s contract includes a nearly $23 million non-guaranteed option bonus next season. Financially, a team would likely be motivated to get out of that contract before using his services in 2027. Do you like the idea of Kansas City trading for Jeudy? Let us know in the comments.

full_text: (Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 NFL regular season’s Week 5 did not feature the Kansas City Chiefs , who sat on their 4-0 record through the bye week. Let’s see how the national media tweaked their opinion on the Chiefs over the weekend in this week’s sampling of power rankings: ESPN : 2 (No change) Biggest issue on defense: Not enough sacks The Chiefs can generate pressure on the quarterback, whether it’s via Chris Jones , George Karlaftis or rookie R Mason Thomas . But they have one of the biggest statistical anomalies of the 2026 season: zero sacks in the first month. Before their bye week , they couldn’t put Raiders QB Kirk Cousins on the turf despite a season-high 21 pressures. If the Chiefs can start collecting sacks, their defense could be a top unit in the second half of the season. — Nate Taylor The Athletic : 2 (No change) Who have you beaten? Broncos, Colts, Dolphins, Raiders It hasn’t been the most daunting slate for the Chiefs since the opener, but any critique of where they stand is nitpicking. Patrick Mahomes looks really good coming off an ACL tear, Kenneth Walker has been a revelation for their offense and the defense has played like a top-10 unit. The key question now is how they’ll replace Tyquan Thornton. — Chad Graff and Josh Kendall Pro Football Talk : 2 (No change) They’ve got a chance to deliver the death blow to the Chargers’ season. — Mike Florio CBSSports.com : 2 (No change) They come off their bye with a home game against the winless Chargers. They do so with injury concerns at receiver and the pass rush hasn’t had a sack in three games. — Pete Prisco Yahoo! Sports : 2 (Up from 3) Jets pass rusher David Bailey is the leading early contender to win NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year after his three sacks on Sunday, bringing him to five on the season. But Chiefs cornerback Mansoor Delane has a case too. Delane is off to a great start to his pro career. Entering Monday, he ranked fourth among all cornerbacks in Pro Football Focus’ grades. According to PFF he has allowed just nine catches for 80 yards in three games (he missed one because of injury). Quarterbacks have a 46.5 passer rating when throwing his way. Delane was a polarizing pick after the Chiefs traded a third- and fifth-round pick to move up three spots and take Mansoor sixth overall. It seemed like an overpay. But the Chiefs have to be thrilled with what they’ve seen so far. — Frank Schwab USA Today : 2 (No change) Coming out of their bye week, K.C. goes into its Chargers bye week before the schedule really picks up and tougher tests come. But there is help on the way at wideout … just not Tyreek Hill (yet). For now, steady hand(s) Justin Watson is returning to the practice squad. — Nate Davis Sports Illustrated : 3 (No change) I don’t recommend anyone do this, but if you simply search “Travis Kelce” on X, it is literally the most insane collection of scam AI slop meant to enrage Taylor Swift fans. Sometimes, I don’t think we give this guy enough credit for keeping his wits about him. — Conor Orr FOX Sports : 2 (No change) The most impressive part about this Chiefs resurgence is how RB Kenneth Walker has given them the steady, powerful running game they’ve often seemed to lack. That’s given QB Patrick Mahomes room to breathe and not have to carry the offense. That will really help with the injuries to WRs Tyquan Thornton and Rashee Rice . Those are two big ones to watch as they come out of their bye week and have a huge swing through Seattle and Denver beginning in Week 7. Next game: vs. Chargers (Sunday, 1:00 p.m. ET) Stat To Know : Since Patrick Mahomes became the full-time starter in 2018, the Chiefs have started 4-0 in four completed seasons (2018, 2019, 2020 and 2024), reaching the Super Bowl in three of those seasons. — Ralph Vacchiano

title: How Chiefs’ receiver rotation could adjust without Tyquan Thornton
summary: There should be a keen eye on the Kansas City Chiefs’ offense moving forward after the ankle dislocation suffered by wide receiver Tyquan Thornton, sidelining him for a 12-to-16-week timeline, according to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. Among the Chiefs wideouts, Thornton led in receiving yards (219), touchdowns (2) and first downs (10). He established himself […]
full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images There should be a keen eye on the Kansas City Chiefs ’ offense moving forward after the ankle dislocation suffered by wide receiver Tyquan Thornton, sidelining him for a 12-to-16-week timeline, according to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network . Among the Chiefs wideouts, Thornton led in receiving yards (219), touchdowns (2) and first downs (10). He established himself as the team’s big-play receiver until he crumpled to the ground after a clutch catch-and-run in the fourth quarter of the Week 4 win over the Las Vegas Raiders . So, courtesy of NFL Next Gen Stats and Pro Football Focus premium stats, let’s take an in-depth look at how the Chiefs’ receiver rotation could adjust based on what has happened so far: The three starting receivers The trio of players who have run the vast majority of the routes available to wide receivers 1. Xavier Worthy (119 routes) 2. Tyquan Thornton (90) 3. Rashee Rice (83) Rice leads all Chiefs players, including tight ends, in slot snaps (47), lining up there for 46% of his pass-play snaps. He has caught five passes for 68 yards from the slot. Rice’s average depth of target is seven yards, speaking to his role as a catch-and-run playmaker. Rice may be the volume player, but Kansas City will miss Thornton’s playmaking when he’s aligned in the slot (28 snaps). Despite aligning there on only 27% of his pass plays, he produced 154 yards and a touchdown on six catches from the slot. The average pass thrown Thornton’s way was 18 yards downfield. Meanwhile, Worthy has produced just 18 yards (and a fourth-and-goal touchdown) aligned as a slot receiver despite catching six passes from there. He’s primarily used as an outside receiver, leading the team in wideout snaps (93) and spending 69% of his pass plays on the perimeter. He has a standard average depth of target of 9.7 yards. With Thornton out for an extended period and Rice recovering from a hamstring injury, the Chiefs will clearly look for slot receivers to make an impact. To spell Rice, they need someone who can gain yards after the catch on quick throws; to replace Thornton, they need big-play ability. The next men up The backup receivers ready to rotate in 4. Jalen Royals (29) 5. Cyrus Allen (5) So far this season, Royals has aligned in the slot 10 times and on the outside 20 times for pass plays. None of his production — three catches for 17 yards and a score — has come when he ran a route from the slot. Since his time at Utah State, Royals has primarily aligned on the outside, but he fits Rice’s play style: he’s hard to tackle once he gets upfield after the catch. This season, the average throw to Royals is 7.2 yards downfield, nearly matching Rice’s mark. If Rice misses time, Royals feels like a direct substitute. Allen, on the other hand, could step into the big-play role that will be missing without Thornton. Last season at the University of Cincinnati, Allen caught 51 passes for 674 yards and an FBS-leading 13 touchdowns. Six of those scores came on throws of 20 or more yards downfield; 23% of Allen’s targets in 2025 were deep throws. During the preseason and training camp, Allen appeared to be developing chemistry with quarterback Patrick Mahomes on difficult throws, whether against tight coverage over the middle or on the sideline. Allen may not have Thornton’s linear speed, but his route running and ball skills could make up for it when the ball’s in the air. The reserves Potential practice-squad elevations 6. Justin Watson 7. Andrew Armstrong If one of these players gets called up, it’s a sign the Chiefs feel they need more size than Worthy, Royals, and Allen provide. Both are 6 feet 2 inches or taller and have plenty of high-effort blocking reps. If Watson is called up, it likely means Kansas City feels it is missing a downfield route runner. The bottom line The Chiefs likely don’t need to change much about the offense regarding Rice, who could return as soon as this week from a hamstring injury; if he misses time, Royals will likely see more playing time in a similar role. The key adjustment will be in response to Thornton’s injury, and Allen — based on his college production and preseason playmaking with Mahomes — could be the secret sauce to filling Thornton’s shoes.

title: Kimani Vidal, Akheem Mesidor headline Week 5’s Chargers Winners/Losers
summary: With the Chargers still winless through five weeks, it’s getting more and more difficult to find players to stick in the winners column. Surprisingly, this week was arguably the easiest week to find such players. Interested to see who stood out despite another loss? Let’s go ahead and check out this week’s winners and losers. […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 11: Los Angeles Chargers running back Kimani Vidal (29) celebrates after running in a touchdown against the Denver Broncos during the first half at SoFi Stadium on Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Eric Thayer / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images) With the Chargers still winless through five weeks, it’s getting more and more difficult to find players to stick in the winners column. Surprisingly, this week was arguably the easiest week to find such players. Interested to see who stood out despite another loss? Let’s go ahead and check out this week’s winners and losers. Winners RB Kimani Vidal Vidal authored the longest run of the season for the Chargers when he broke off a 42-yard touchdown at the end of the third quarter to give the Chargers a seven-point lead in a game where points were at a premium. On the play, Vidal broke multiple tackles within the first 10 yards, then bounced to the outside and hit the sideline. Thanks to massive efforts by wide receiver Theo Wease and fullback Scot Matlock who provided a caravan down the field, Vidal was able to dance his way into the end zone for his team-leading second score on the year. With two consecutive weeks of seeing an increased snap share, Vidal’s latest performance should earn him even more looks if he’s going to prove to be the most explosive back on the team. FB Scott Matlock Matlock was activated off of IR this week and he returned a whole new player. After a preseason where he looked completely out of place at tight end, he looked slimmed down and much more confident in his abilities this week. When used as an extra blocker in max protection looks, he earned the highest pass block grade on the team (82.5), per Pro Football Focus. After a month of underwhelming play from Alec Ingold at fullback, Matlock has a chance to come right in and earn a massive snap share after just one performance. OT Travis Burke Burke and the rest of the Chargers offensive line struggled to bottle up the pass rush of the Broncos, but it was the ground game where the rookie tackle looked phenomenal. The 6’7 Burke earned an 84.2 in run blocking by PFF, the highest grade on the team by an offensive lineman by 37.4 grade points. That’s a huge gap and shows just how lackluster the rest of the line was when the Chargers tried to get the ground game going. I don’t know if Burke has been good enough to warrant any changes up front, but I think it may be tough to argue that Burke isn’t already one of the Chargers’ best five offensive linemen. EDGE Akheem Mesidor The Chargers’ 2026 first-round pick may have had his best game as a pro against the Broncos. Per Pro Football Focus, Mesidor earned a career-high fives “stops” against Denver, which is a play that constitutes a failure by the Broncos offense. That also led to a single-game high of five tackles, as well. Mesidor’s overall game grade was an 89.6, just 0.04 away from earning an “elite” mark by the grading service. It didn’t matter if he was rushing the passer or defending the run, Mesidor was impactful in all phases of the game, even when he was in coverage (76.9). Losers S Genesis Smith Those two interceptions against Josh Allen and the Bills seem like ages ago. Smith posted a team-low 35.5 game grade by Pro Football Focus in Week 5, including a coverage grade of 36.7. That’s his second-lowest mark of the year, behind only the 29.8 he posted against the Raiders in Week 2. The fourth-round rookie continues to be extremely boom-or-bust for the Chargers defense. Some weeks he looks like the game speed as caught up to him, while in others he looks utterly lost on the back end. In the fourth quarter after yet another sudden change turnover by the offense, Smith found himself lined head-up over Broncos wideout Courtland Sutton in the slot. At the snap, quarterback Bo Nix faked a handoff to his running back while the receiver outside Sutton moved laterally on a bubble screen. Smith immediately took a hard jab towards the receiver as if he was his responsibility, allowing Sutton to run right past him and catch the wide open touchdown. Smith had cornerback Cam Hart to his outside. Hart would have been responsible for the bubble. When a 6’4 receiver runs towards you within the 10-yard line, it’s probably smart to acknowledge him before he’s just about past you. With everyone manned up, Smith was truly about to let Sutton go untouched into the end zone just to have a shot at tackling the receiver running horizontal to the line of scrimmage. One was much more of a threat than the other. Smith picked wrong and was unfortunately the author of another head-scratching lowlight. HC Jim Harbaugh Good on Harbaugh for truly taking the blame and acknowledging just how bad his fourth-down decision was. The whole thing was made so much worse due to him torching his two challenges for the game all in the first half. Justin Herbert was spotted nearly an entire yard back from the chains despite what the review showed of his third-down scramble. Even with a blatant shot of it on camera, the Chargers were helpless to do anything about it. That was tough, but the choice to roll with a quarterback sneak with a hobbled quarterback and a front five that featured four rookies? I cannot express how little sense that made. And for the cherry on top, it wasn’t even a good sneak! No one pushed Herbert from behind. Guys just stood around instead of contributing to the potential success of the pivotal play. Top to bottom, one of the ugliest debacles under Harbaugh in his 2+ seasons.
author: Michael Peterson

They had a real and legitimate chance to win this game, but a botched fourth-down call and weak ball security gave Denver the ball four consecutive drives from the Los Angeles 41-yard line or closer. When you only have a seven-point […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 11: Head coach Jim Harbaugh of the Los Angeles Chargers looks on during the third quarter of the game against the Denver Broncos at SoFi Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chargers dropped to 0-5 after crumbling in the fourth quarter against the Broncos. They had a real and legitimate chance to win this game, but a botched fourth-down call and weak ball security gave Denver the ball four consecutive drives from the Los Angeles 41-yard line or closer. When you only have a seven-point lead, that’s a quick and easy way to throw out your chances of leaving victorious. Now, they enter the week prior to their bye still looking for the answers. Will they manage to find them while facing the undefeated Chiefs? Your guess is as good as mine. Let’s check out where the Bolts landed in this week’s power rankings. Sports Illustrated – #28 “ Justin Herbert’s turnovers doomed the Chargers again, as they fell to 0-5 in 2026 with a loss to Denver. ” “ L.A. led 17-10 in the second half, but it wasn’t enough to get a win. The schedule doesn’t lighten up for the Chargers, and they’re an extreme long shot to make the playoffs. They fell from +10000 to +20000 to win the Super Bowl. ” – Conor Orr The Athletic – #30 “It’s jarring how bad things have gotten for the Chargers. Justin Herbert managed just 121 passing yards Sunday with one touchdown, one interception and two fumbles. L.A. can’t run the ball either. And the strength of schedule isn’t letting up anytime soon.” – Josh Kendall and Chad Graff NFL.com – #30 “If I could eject myself from the Chargers experience, I would. The banged-up offensive line can’t protect Justin Herbert, who can’t keep himself from continuing to make mistakes. He’s loose with the ball under pressure (leading to the costly fumble we saw in the fourth quarter), his processing seems to be damaged by the weekly struggles (seen in the late interception he threw directly to Brandon Jones), and there’s no clear path out of this mess. The Bolts gave away a winnable game Sunday, one in which they appeared poised to prevail before self-destructing in spectacular fashion. This isn’t your typical Chargering; it’s much, much worse.” – Nick Shook Pro Football Talk – #30 “The price for a potential Justin Herbert trade is dropping by the week.” – Mike Florio CBS Sports – #30 ‘‘At 0-5, their season is over. The Chargers doing Chargers things to lose to the Broncos Sunday is so on point. Jim Harbaugh needs to look in the mirror.” – Pete Pricso ESPN – #30 ‘‘According to defensive coordinator Chris O’Leary, a key emphasis for the Chargers during practice last week was the defense needing to rise up against a “sudden change opportunity.” But they gave up points three times in four post-turnover possessions Sunday (a touchdown and two field goals) and the fourth was a missed field goal attempt. It’s not an easy task; with the offense giving away a league-high 13 turnovers, short fields are becoming common.” – Anthony Gharib Sporting News – #31 “The Chargers are losing everyone again to injuries and also losing a lot of close games because of little mistakes. The ultimate “Chargering” continues to plague Jim Harbaugh. They are now up to a league-high 13 giveaways in 5 games.” – Vinnie Ieyer

title: Los Angeles Chargers news: Are you worried about Omarion Hampton’s usage?
summary: As someone who owns a share of Hampton in one of his two dynasties, this is something I’ve tossed around in my head over the last two weeks. Against the Seahawks, Hampton looked like the best back out there. Against Denver, he did not and Vidal’s 42-yard touchdown where he broke and evaded numerous tackles […]
full_text: Inglewood, CA - October 11: Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert (10) hands off to running back Omarion Hampton (8) during the first quarter of an NFL football game against the Denver Broncos at Sofi Stadium on Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026 in Inglewood, CA. (Eric Thayer / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images) As someone who owns a share of Hampton in one of his two dynasties, this is something I’ve tossed around in my head over the last two weeks. Against the Seahawks, Hampton looked like the best back out there. Against Denver, he did not and Vidal’s 42-yard touchdown where he broke and evaded numerous tackles was spectacular. That’s not going to help Hampton’s case to be the workhorse we all expected him to be this year. But how much of a net-negative is that, if at all? If Vidal is the better back (let’s just say this for the sake of the hypothetical), then should we be more okay with Hampton losing out on opportunities and overall snap share? Would you be okay watching the team’s 2025 first round pick fall back towards obscurity if Vidal was performing in the manner we would have expected Hampton to this year? I really, REALLY expected great things from Hampton. I still see the level of talent he has through the lack of production, but it’s fairly apparent he is not as well-versed running behind a bad line like Vidal is. I mean, the latter essentially did it for the entire 2025 season. He had multiple 100-yard games, including two with over 120. Vidal has done it before. He has proven success under his belt. But what does history say about first-round running backs who don’t outright own the starting job by the end of their second season? I don’t personally have that information right now, but something tells me it doesn’t bode well for that player. Maybe I’m wrong, but I’m going to keep digging into it. Are you all worried about Hampton in the same way I am? Less so? More so? Let me know how you’re all feeling below. And now for today’s links. title: Rams PFF grades: Jaylen Watson & Puka Nacua earn top marks vs Bills
summary: The sting of the Los Angeles Rams’ overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills still has not faded. LA fell to 2-3. They are currently third in the NFC West and outside of the playoff picture. Sure, the schedule lightens up over the next two months. The Rams have not been who we thought they’d be […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 12: Puka Nacua #12 of the Los Angeles Rams completes a catch against Christian Benford #47 of the Buffalo Bills during the third quarter of an NFL football game at SoFi Stadium on October 12, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The sting of the Los Angeles Rams’ overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills still has not faded. LA fell to 2-3. They are currently third in the NFC West and outside of the playoff picture. Sure, the schedule lightens up over the next two months. The Rams have not been who we thought they’d be through five games. Let’s dive into the Pro Football Focus (PFF) grades and advanced metrics. Who can the Rams rely on to get back on track? Top five grades on offense 1 – Puka Nacua, WR: 85.3 It was clear the Rams intended to get the ball to Nacua often. He was targeted a whopping 24 times and caught 17 passes for 138 yards and a touchdown. Buffalo stuck with their soft zones. Nacua took advantage. He was often targeted on screen plays as well. Nacua did most of his damage against Davison Igbinosun. He caught six of eight targets for 52 yards with the score. Nacua caught a pass against seven different defenders. Puka Nacua just had the second-most targets in a game (24) in the 21st century. Only 2009 Brandon Marshall (28) had more — Ian Hartitz (@Ihartitz) October 13, 2026 2 – Blake Corum, RB: 74.9 Blake Corum also did his best damage as a receiver. He caught three of four targets for 53 yards. 49 yards came after the catch point. Corum’s opportunities were limited as a runner, although he did find the end zone as did Kyren Williams. Corum rushed five times for 19 yards and broke one off for more than 10 yards. 3 – Alaric Jackson, LT: 73.2 Jackson earned a good/great run blocking grade of 83.0. The Rams still made it their third-straight game with over 50 pass attempts. On a per average basis the rushing attack was less effective on Monday night. The bigger concern with Jackson is his two-game suspension following a post-game altercation with EDGE defender Bradley Chubb. 4 – Steve Avila, LG: 71.8 Coleman Shelton earned LA’s top pass blocking grade at 87.1. Avila wasn’t far behind at 83.2. Neither allowed a pressure in pass protection. 5 – Matthew Stafford: 69.0 The box score was more kind to Stafford than the PFF grading. The veteran signal caller completed 40 of 54 passes (74.1%) for 383 yards and three touchdowns. PFF credited him for one big-time throw and dinged him for one turnover-worthy play. Stafford got rid of the ball quickly at 2.55 seconds on average. This helped mitigate pressure as he was pressured only 13 times on 56 drop backs. His average depth of target (ADOT) suffered as a result at 6.9 yards. Applying a 50% drop back threshold, Stafford is currently PFF’s 17th ranked quarterback by passing grade at 67.4. He has more turnover-worthy plays (nine) than big-time throws (eight). Cam Ward ranks 24th, and he’s in jeopardy of getting benched by the Tennessee Titans. The Bills defense was an opportunity for the Rams offense to get back on track. Instead, it was more of the same. Don’t let the box score fool you. This was not a tremendous game by Stafford. Other notes on offense Tutu Atwell played 32 snaps on offense and seems to have a hold on the WR#3 role within the offense. We will see how long it lasts. This was a larger workload than he saw in any game last season and tied the 2024 regular season finale against the Seattle Seahawks where the Rams rested key players. If we are only counting games where LA tried to win, we’d have to go back to his 43-snap effort in Week 5 of 2024. Top five grades on defense Players with at least five snaps only 1 – Jaylen Watson, CB: 89.9 The Rams limited Buffalo’s receivers to just 30 yards on three receptions. Coverage was sticky and Josh Allen was forced to turn to either his legs or his running backs and tight ends. It worked until Allen inevitably caught the defense on their heels with a backbreaking scramble. That isn’t Watson’s fault. He did his part. Watson’s first game back validates just how important he is for the defense. He and Trent McDuffie have been as advertised so far. 2 – Nate Landman, MLB: 79.0 Landman earned a rough PFF coverage grade of 29.7 despite not being targeted. His run defense of 94.5 is stellar. Landman forced two fumbles on running back James Cook. The second punch out ended a Bills overtime offensive possession in Rams territory and probably should have swayed the outcome in favor of LA. It has been a long while since Landman has made this list. His return is welcome. NATE LANDMAN PEANUT PUNCH!!! 📺 @ESPNNFL | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/2S1rKhnRp8 — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) October 13, 2026 3 – Tyler Davis, DT: 68.0 It’s telling that the rest of the Rams defense graded in the 60’s or worse. Buffalo was effective in the traditional run game as well as Allen making them pay with his legs. The pass defense limited the damage enough to keep things close. Davis earned the second-highest run grade behind Landman at 69.4. Poona Ford, who usually excels in this role, was far down the list at 54.1. At least the Rams were able to depend on Davis against the Bills. 4 – Trent McDuffie, CB: 60.3 Lowest passer rating allowed by CB this season (min 150 snaps) Trent McDuffie 21.1 Josh Wallace 29.2 Isaiah Rodgers 43.8 Christian Gonzalez 44.0 Nehemiah Pritchett 44.0 pic.twitter.com/LvSJhBEvRT — PFF (@PFF) October 14, 2026 5 – Omar Speights, MLB: 58.4 Other notes on defense Credit to Quentin Lake for fighting through an injury to be available on Monday night. It still wasn’t his best performance. He was the lowest graded player on defense despite playing all 63 defensive snaps. He finished with a mark of just 28.4 and allowed three receptions for 81 yards on five targets.

title: Change for change’s sake won’t fix Rams special teams
summary: The Los Angeles Rams keep treating special teams like a rundown car. Swap a part. Expect it to run better. It never does. It took years of decay for the car to arrive in its current state. There is no quick fix. Overhauling it to a vintage antique takes significant investment in terms of time […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 04: Head coach Sean McVay of the Los Angeles Rams runs onto the field prior to the game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on October 04, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams keep treating special teams like a rundown car. Swap a part. Expect it to run better. It never does. It took years of decay for the car to arrive in its current state. There is no quick fix. Overhauling it to a vintage antique takes significant investment in terms of time and resources. LA’s decline in special teams did not happen overnight. It took years and years of neglect by Sean McVay and the Rams front office. Which NFL teams have the best special teams units? pic.twitter.com/MX5j1eLt0o — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) October 13, 2026 Swapping out minor parts—like special teams coordinators, returners, kickers, long snappers, and others—won’t fix a systemic problem within the organization. The Rams used to prioritize special teams. They utilized late-round draft picks and undrafted free agency with contributions in the third phase in mind. Players like Daren Bates, Nick Scott, and Cory Littleton all were onboarded with little regard for offensive or defensive roles. But, of course, that was mostly when John Fassel was calling the shots. Special teams were a value add back then. Johnny Hekker, Greg Zuerlein, Jake McQuaide, Littleton, Scott, Bates, Pharoh Cooper, Bates, and JoJo Natson all played major roles in LA’s heyday. Fassel left the Rams after the 2019 season. Special teams performance has been on a steady decline since. It doesn’t matter how many times you make superficial changes. You can cut Xavier Smith and trot out a new punt returner . Firing Chase Blackburn midseason 2025 made fans feel better until they learned his full-time replacement Bubba Ventrone isn’t any better. Now, the team is moving on from kicker Harrison Mevis and expecting better results from a player who already failed elsewhere in Blake Grupe . Vintage cars aren’t built in a day. Awful football units aren’t drastically improved with minor swaps, especially during the regular season when resources are scarce and available player pools are limited. The Rams cannot truly course correct on special teams until the upcoming offseason, but even then it may take years of incremental improvements before the unit returns to the level of adding value. The entire team must buy into the approach. Les Snead and the scouting department must acquire talent for the sole purpose of the third phase. Coaches must develop those players and find room for them on the backend of the roster. It may require keeping less depth at certain positions and moving on from situational contributors on offense or defense. But the cost is almost certainly worth paying. Special teams is routinely costing the Rams wins, even when the other two units are performing at a high level. The third phase could single-handedly derail Super Bowl hopes for a roster built to win a championship. Change for the sake of change is getting old. It’s a sleight of hand trick meant to distract you short term. Nothing will truly be fixed until the Rams dedicate significant resources and time to special teams.

title: NFL suspends A.J. Jackson 2 games after post-game punch
summary: The NFL has suspended L.A. Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson for two games after he was shown throwing a punch at Buffalo Bills edge rusher Bradley Chubb following Monday night’s overtime loss, according to multiple reports. The Rams have listed David Quessenberry as Jackson’s backup, which puts him in line to start against the Arizona […]
full_text: The NFL has suspended L.A. Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson for two games after he was shown throwing a punch at Buffalo Bills edge rusher Bradley Chubb following Monday night’s overtime loss, according to multiple reports . The Rams have listed David Quessenberry as Jackson’s backup, which puts him in line to start against the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders. Jackson would be eligible to be reinstated in Week 8 against the L.A. Chargers. Just in: #Rams LT Alaric Jackson has been suspended 2 games for punching Bradley Chubb after their game on Monday night. LA won’t have Jackson in Week 6 vs. Arizona and Week 7 vs Las Vegas. pic.twitter.com/lwUiVWvghO — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) October 13, 2026 The NFL did not suspend Jackson prior to the season after he was accused and arrested for a domestic violence incident, reportedly the third such accusation during his career . An undrafted free agent out of Iowa in 2021, Jackson has been a pleasant surprise for the Rams on the field during games. PFF ranks him as the 12th-best tackle this season . He earned a three-year contract extension with the team but his personal life has been controversial to say the least, and now his temper has been caught on camera. The 36-year-old Quessenberry has not started a game since 2023 with the Vikings. The Rams did re-sign him after last season and kept him on the roster, so they feel comfortable with him as an option. Rookie third round pick Keagen Trost had his 21-day window to be activated opened last week , meaning he could return at any time. However, it would be surprising if he was activated and then starting at left tackle for the Rams. But stranger things have happened.

title: Rams vs. Bills snap counts: Tutu Atwell takes over WR3 role
summary: Tutu Atwell played 32 snaps against the Buffalo Bills on Monday, the most he’s had in a game since Week 5 of last season and a clear indication of who Sean McVay likes the most right now as the Rams’ third receiver. Atwell was only targeted one time and caught a pass for four yards, […]
full_text: Tutu Atwell played 32 snaps against the Buffalo Bills on Monday, the most he’s had in a game since Week 5 of last season and a clear indication of who Sean McVay likes the most right now as the Rams’ third receiver. Atwell was only targeted one time and caught a pass for four yards, but obviously McVay thinks L.A. has a chance to do some things differently with him in the lineup instead of Jordan Whittington or Konata Mumpfield. Those two receivers played a combined 17 snaps. And it was explosive plays that mattered. Rams-Bills explosive plays After another of what seems like countless special teams gaffes, the Los Angeles Rams let the Buffalo Bills gallop right past them for a 37-34 win on Monday Night Football at L.A.’s SoFi Stadium. The game proved to be an advertisement for today’s NFL, how explosive plays can either set or change the tone of the outcome. Although the Rams used a grinding offensive attack to methodically move down the field, accumulating 78 offensive plays and 33 first downs, they had only five explosives. They all came on pass plays, all in the the last half and overtime. Overall in 2026, L.A. sits 17th in explosive offensive plays. Conversely, the Bills played to form, 1st in NFL Explosive Play Rate. They had 10 offensive explosives on 57 offensive plays, mixed evenly between run and pass with an 11th coming in the return game. Th Bills didn’t drop any bombs on the L.A. defense, their big plays arose from identifying lanes and and open field running. Whether it’s patient quarterbacks when the Rams pass rush doesn’t get home or backs/receivers that get the ball in space, all can apply pressure to the limited athleticism of L.A.’s linebacker and safety units. The Rams defense is 25th in explosives allowed. Offensive and defensive explosive play rates: The Bills offense is very good pic.twitter.com/Dr7YFUrYSn — Sam Hoppen (@SamHoppen) October 13, 2026 Here the snap count review from Sunday, players their snap counts and percentage of play time in bold. Quarterback Matthew Stafford (82, 100%) Played well enough for the Rams to win, too bad the outcome wasn’t put in his hands completely on the overtime drive. Staff had been lights out in the fourth quarter, 11 of 13 for 119 yards, as the Rams posted 20 points. Last week vs. Philly, it was 13 of 17 for 149 yards and two scores. Running back Kyren Williams (60, 70%) The Rams offensive braintrust decided again, that 50+ passes was the path to victory, so Williams never got into a groove as a run threat. He was pointed out for a couple on nice pass blocking reps and made an amazing catch late. On the Rams final scoring drive with 30 seconds left in the game, L.A. had third and seven from the buffalo 10. Stafford threw behind Williams, who had circled out of the backfield and the running back reached a hand back and snatched it in. Blake Corum (22, 27%) Actually did some damage as a receiver, hauled in three of four targets and had very nice 34-yard catch and run at the end of third quarter that led to a score in the fourth. On the Rams first drive coming out of the half, he was wide open in the flat with an open field to the end zone, but Staff, under pressure, overthrew him. Wide receiver Puka Nacua (70, 85%) Hard to predict how bad this offense would be, if Nacua went out for a long term. His physicality at the catch point and ability to plow forward with yards after the catch is quite amazing. Week in, week out, just a stud. Davante Adams (60, 70%) This strikes me as the exact role that you can envision the older version of Adams in, as a complimentary WR#2. Adams route-running savvy is still top notch and can create separation, particularly near the goal line. There are times though, that he can mail it in running routes when not the primary target. Tutu Atwell (32, 39%) Second highest snap count going back to October of 2024. It’s not just fans, even the national broadcasters spoke of the need to get Atwell’s speed into the game and cited McVay as saying he wanted him as a bigger part of the offensive plan. He caught a single short out and ran a lot deep clear out routes, but was never targeted deep. Jordan Whittington (11, 13%) Basically invisible, subbing in for Atwell in running situations. Did tote five kickoffs for an average of just under 28 yards per, over the Rams season average of 25. Konata Mumpfield (6, 7%) Came into the game nicked up and was in and out, likely the same shoulder problem.. I guess the Rams figured that an injured Mumpfield was a better fit into the game plan than rookie CJ Daniels. Tight end Tyler Higbee (55, 67%) Sipping from the Fountain of Youth, Higbee’s playing his best football in years. The Rams are lining him up in the slot or outside at 44 percent clip and he’s responded with a catch rate of 80 percent, 14 of 20 receptions for first down and the highest depth of target for his whole career. Colby Parkinson (53, 65%) Obviously gutting through his injury, just two short targets in a Rams game plan where the passing offense was all underneath. Is going with a player of Parkinson’s talent level and limited by injuries, a better choice than giving your Round 2 draft pick some needed time on the field? This is one of the questions that needs to be asked when you start 2-3. Davis Allen (41, 50%) Made two outstanding clutch catches to go along with his usual blocking duties. Offensive line Alaric Jackson, Steve Avila, Coleman Shelton, Kevin Dotson, Warren McClendon (82, 100%) The run game was primarily between the tackles. Even though it wasn’t particularly effective, the big guys have generally done well run blocking, allowing the least amount of stuff/loss plays (34.8%) in the league. Throwing 50+ passes is exorbitant even for the pass-happy Rams, the line was pretty good pass blocking against an aggressive Buffalo blitz program, only allowing a 22 percent pressure rate. Next Gen Stats recorded the Rams with 4 of 12 passes completed under pressure. Special teams Sniff, sniff. That’s the tell tale odor of a dead animal in the wood pile. Placekicker Harrison Meevis is the first to go, but the smell lingers. Now, more importantly, what’s the plan to clean up the rest? same last year, i think, https://t.co/oPNL9lUpcH — Jim Youngblood 53 (@53_jim70721) October 13, 2026 Defensive line Kobie Turner (43, 67%) Aaron Donald (43, 67%) Braden Fiske (26, 41%) Poona Ford (29, 45%) Tyler Davis (21, 33%) Ty Hamilton (7, 11%) Not the best showing for this unit, Buffalo also uses a lot of three tight end formations and came in to run the football. They did, to the tune of 234 yards. The Bills never went away from what worked, even into overtime. Against a running QB, lane discipline is paramount and too often the Rams interior left huge gaps for Josh Allen to traverse. Edge Byron Young (55, 86%) Josaiah Stewart (53, 83%) Wesley Bailey (16, 25%) Desjuan Johnson (4, 6%) Quiet getting after the passer. For the game, Bills’ QB Josh Allen had nearly three seconds in time to pressure percentage on passes, even though he couldn’t get deep and had to take the underneath stuff. Stewart seemed to get locked up regularly by the opposing tackle and lost contain. Young was close to making a couple more sacks with backside pursuit, but couldn’t close the deal. Off-ball linebacker Nate Landman (57, 89%) Good on him to know that Bills RB James Cook has been a fumbler ( most in the NFL from last year on), the punch outs were big time plays. Landman has an old school, tough guy game between the tackles. However in space, he lacks move skills and is exploitable. In over his head in pursuit of more agile offensive players and certainly to spy active quarterbacks. Omar Speights (23, 36%) Trending down. Although his play time was up a few from last week, his total was the second lowest since early in his rookie year. 1st play of the game. He was hunting… https://t.co/YJXqUufd19 pic.twitter.com/HqYvgOOEqe — Cody Alexander (@The_Coach_A) October 13, 2026 Safety Quentin Lake (64, 100%)…

title: Rams’ odds to win NFC West drop under 20%
summary: The worst case scenario for the Los Angeles Rams in Week 5 actually happened. The San Francisco 49ers improved to 5-0, including a win against the Rams, and L.A. fell to 2-3 after their Monday night loss to the Buffalo Bills. The Rams have 19% odds to win the NFC West now, according to Kalshi. […]
full_text: The worst case scenario for the Los Angeles Rams in Week 5 actually happened . The San Francisco 49ers improved to 5-0, including a win against the Rams, and L.A. fell to 2-3 after their Monday night loss to the Buffalo Bills. The Rams have 19% odds to win the NFC West now, according to Kalshi . That’s surprisingly high given how perfect L.A. needs to be for the rest of the season to have any hope of catching the 49ers. If San Francisco even goes 8-4 the rest of the season, the Rams would need to go 12-0 to beat them straight up, or 11-1 with a win over the 49ers. That’s assuming the Seahawks don’t have a better record than them also. In the NFC West, the Rams are in third place. In the NFC, they are in ninth place. In Sean McVay’s history as Rams coach, the team has won the division four times: 2017: Lost WC 2018: Lost SB 2021: Won SB 2024: Lost DIV In 2024, the Rams won the division but had to go on the road to face the Eagles in round two, where they were eliminated in freezing temps. How differently could that game have gone if L.A. wasn’t 10-7 and had homefield advantage? The Rams have been a wild card three times under McVay: 2020: Won WC, lost on road in round 2 2023: Lost WC 2025: Reached NFC Championship, lost on the road Yes, there is time for the Rams to rebound to make the playoffs, but McVay’s teams have not been good on the road in the playoffs. Nor are most teams. The decision to rest everybody in the preseason? It’s a problem. The lack of investment in special teams? It’s a problem. Overlooking the draft every year? It’s a problem. I wrote about this last month as a concern and these are all problems that consistently lead the Rams to losing at least two games every year to start the season. That may as well be the same as losing a playoff game. You set yourself up for January with how you play in September and October. Once again, the Rams didn’t set themselves up for anything but disappointment.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Rams sign Blake Grupe to replace Harrison Mevis
summary: The Los Angeles Rams signed kicker Blake Grupe off of the New York Jets practice squad on Tuesday, a corresponding move to the release of Harrison Mevis. Grupe has not attempted any kicks in 2026, but has played 50 career games between the New Orleans Saints and Indianapolis Colts. Grupe was claimed by the Jets […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams signed kicker Blake Grupe off of the New York Jets practice squad on Tuesday, a corresponding move to the release of Harrison Mevis . Grupe has not attempted any kicks in 2026, but has played 50 career games between the New Orleans Saints and Indianapolis Colts. Grupe was claimed by the Jets after he was cut by the Colts at the end of training camp, but moved to the practice squad on October 1. The former Notre Dame kicker is in line to be in a Rams uniform this week against the Arizona Cardinals. New #Rams K Blake Grupe was claimed off waivers by the #Jets after rosters were pared to 53. He never kicked for them and was moved to the practice squad. Grupe heads to LA under ST coordinator Bubba Ventrone. Both previously with the #Colts , though not at the same time. pic.twitter.com/LGoUKPf5yb — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) October 13, 2026 Mevis was never that good for the Rams. He was accurate within 45 or so yards, but didn’t have the leg for longer kicks. That was always apparent, but more so on Monday night as L.A. lost to the Bills in overtime after Mevis had his 48-yard blocked by Gregory Rosseau. He also missed a 50-yard attempt in the first quarter. Sean McVay would at times avoid kicking field goals in 2025 just because Mevis was so bad at it beyond 50. But Grupe is 19-of-27 from 50+ in his career. Grupe went 11-of-11 on kicks for the Colts last season over four games, including 4-of-4 from 50+. He has made 96 extra points in his career on 98 attempts. However, the Saints released him during the 2025 season because he led the NFL in missed kicks with 12. It is not like the Rams can act surprised that they’re scraping the bottom of their options in October because L.A. has consistently ignored the value of special teams under Sean McVay. This is the third time the team has made a midseason change in the last five years. Grupe is the Rams’ eighth different kicker since 2020.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Rams release kicker Harrison Mevis after Bills loss
summary: The Los Angeles Rams released kicker Harrison Mevis on Tuesday, less than 24 hours after his blocked kick against the Bills in overtime led to a loss at home against Buffalo. Sean McVay was visibly upset with Mevis and special teams after the game when talking to reporters, and he said that the Rams would […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams released kicker Harrison Mevis on Tuesday, less than 24 hours after his blocked kick against the Bills in overtime led to a loss at home against Buffalo . Sean McVay was visibly upset with Mevis and special teams after the game when talking to reporters , and he said that the Rams would evaluate all positions immediately. He was not joking around. With special teams continuing to cost Los Angeles valuable opportunities, the Rams decided to move on from the second-year kicker rather than wait for him to rediscover his rookie-year form. The team has already replaced him by signing Blake Grupe off of the Jets practice squad . Mevis missed a 50-yard field goal in the first quarter, when that distance is usually automatic for most kickers in today’s NFL. Then Gregory Rosseau blocked a 48-yard kick in overtime that would have won the game, but it may not have gone in anyway. don't love this!!!! https://t.co/NFh94q2VYd pic.twitter.com/QlJKfxV2Ev — Benjamin Solak (@BenjaminSolak) October 13, 2026 Mevis entered the NFL with plenty of promise after converting 12 of 13 field goal attempts during his rookie regular season, an impressive 92.3% success rate. His early production suggested the Rams had found a dependable option at a position where consistency can make the difference between winning and losing close games. Unfortunately, that reliability has disappeared in 2026. Through five games, Mevis converted just five of nine field goal attempts, finishing with a disappointing 55.6% success rate. Those struggles represented a significant decline from his rookie campaign and raised serious questions about whether he could be trusted in critical situations. The breaking point came during Monday night’s overtime thriller against the Buffalo Bills. Mevis missed a field goal before having a potential game-winning attempt blocked in overtime, contributing to a heartbreaking 37-34 defeat. For a Rams team with legitimate Super Bowl aspirations, those missed opportunities proved too costly to overlook. With his 2026 struggles dragging down his overall numbers, Mevis leaves Los Angeles with a 17-for-22 regular-season field goal record, good for a 77.3% career conversion rate. Rams release K Harrison Mevis. (via @RapSheet , @MikeGarafolo ) pic.twitter.com/2VDFYFo0Ht — NFL (@NFL) October 13, 2026 JB Scott listed several kickers who the Rams could consider as replacements and now L.A. is immediately back on the hunt. The next kicker will be the team’s eighth different starter since 2020. The decision to release Mevis underscores the urgency surrounding the Rams’ special teams problems. Los Angeles has struggled to find consistency in that phase of the game, and the kicking position has become an increasingly obvious liability. Now, the Rams must identify a more reliable replacement capable of delivering when the pressure rises. With Matthew Stafford and the offense providing championship-caliber production, Los Angeles cannot afford to keep losing games because of preventable special teams mistakes. Mevis had an opportunity to establish himself as the Rams’ long-term answer at kicker. Instead, his struggles in 2026 have brought his time in Los Angeles to an abrupt end.
author: Steven Ridings

title: Extreme “Special Teams” Makeover: Rams edition
summary: The Los Angeles Rams are -31.8 in Special Teams EPA through five weeks, making their third phase a catastrophic liability that threatens to undermine an otherwise competitive football team. If Sean McVay and Les Snead want to maximize this roster’s Super Bowl potential, an extreme special teams makeover needs to be on the table, starting […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Matt Gay #14 of the Las Vegas Raiders kicks a field goal during the third quarter of an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams are -31.8 in Special Teams EPA through five weeks, making their third phase a catastrophic liability that threatens to undermine an otherwise competitive football team. If Sean McVay and Les Snead want to maximize this roster’s Super Bowl potential, an extreme special teams makeover needs to be on the table, starting with a reliable kicker who can consistently turn scoring opportunities into points. The Rams have two outside options worth considering if they want to fix their special teams problems before they cost them another game: trading for a familiar face or signing one of the most accurate kickers in NFL history. This is about as upset as I’ve seen Sean McVay after a game. He blames himself for the conservative third and five call in OT and kicking the long field goal. There will likely be special teams changes this week. pic.twitter.com/Y06H3vLON1 — Arash Markazi (@ArashMarkazi) October 13, 2026 Option 1: Trade for Matt Gay A reunion with Matt Gay could be exactly what the Rams need to stabilize their kicking game. Gay is currently with the Las Vegas Raiders on a one-year contract that expires after the 2026 season, making him a potential trade target if the Raiders are willing to negotiate. Gay already knows what it takes to succeed in Los Angeles. During his two-and-a-half seasons with the Rams from 2020 through 2022, he converted 74 of 80 field goal attempts, good for an impressive 92.5% success rate. His best season came in 2021, when he made 94.1% of his field goals and helped the Rams capture Super Bowl LVI. Although Gay’s career field goal percentage sits at approximately 84.6%, his previous success in Los Angeles gives the Rams reason to believe he could rediscover his best form. He has also demonstrated the ability to make long kicks, including a 59-yarder for Las Vegas in 2026. A trade would give the Rams a proven option who understands the organization and has experience performing under championship expectations. With Gay’s contract expiring after this season, Los Angeles could potentially acquire him without committing to a long-term deal. Option 2: Sign Justin Tucker If the Rams prefer to pursue a different route, Justin Tucker represents another intriguing possibility. Tucker has a career field goal percentage of 89.1%, making him one of the most accurate kickers the NFL has seen. From 49 yards or less, his 94.8% success rate is nearly automatic. The biggest question is whether Tucker can return to his previous level of consistency. His track record is difficult to ignore, but the Rams would need to evaluate his current form and availability before making a commitment. If he can still deliver that kind of accuracy, he would give Los Angeles a dependable option whenever the offense stalls outside the red zone. Just gonna leave this here… 👀🤔 Does @SuaKCravens have a point?! Should the Rams consider pursuing Justin Tucker after the special teams struggles? 🐏🏈 pic.twitter.com/YVuhVJueti — ESPN Los Angeles (@ESPNLosAngeles) October 13, 2026 Verdict: Either The Rams cannot afford to keep surrendering valuable points and field position because of special teams mistakes. Trading for Gay offers familiarity, proven success in Los Angeles and a relatively short contractual commitment. Tucker provides a potentially high-upside alternative if the Rams believe he can recapture his elite form. Either move would represent a meaningful step toward fixing a unit that has become a glaring weakness. With championship aspirations, the Rams need to stop treating special teams as an afterthought and start investing in solutions. An extreme makeover might be exactly what this team needs to turn a major liability into a legitimate strength.

title: On Monday night, Rams failed to close out for second time in 2026
summary: The Los Angeles Rams failed to close out a game against the Buffalo Bills in Week 5 on Monday Night Football, and it’s easily at least the second time that has happened this year with the Rams losing a 16-point lead and eventually the game to the Denver Broncos in Week 3. The Rams had […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 12: Head coach Sean McVay of the Los Angeles Rams reacts to a play during the first quarter of the game against the Buffalo Bills at SoFi Stadium on October 12, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams failed to close out a game against the Buffalo Bills in Week 5 on Monday Night Football, and it’s easily at least the second time that has happened this year with the Rams losing a 16-point lead and eventually the game to the Denver Broncos in Week 3. The Rams had that game, and for other reasons, the Rams could’ve had the win against the Bills. The Rams didn’t lead by 16, but they had chances to put the Bills away. The special teams may deserve the brunt of the blame, but a team loses as a team. The takeaway is that just like in 2025, the Rams are showing an inability to close out the games. The Rams are showing weak spots on special teams. Special teams and a failure to close the game can go hand in hand when the margins for winning and losing are so small. But the offense and defense are part of the equation too. After a loss like this, the entire team needs to be examined. That’s how it works when you fall to 2-3 with Super Bowl dreams. For the Rams, it’s concerning. For other NFL teams, it’s exactly what they want to see. The Rams faltering, and the Rams are delivering in the worst way. Rams’ Sean McVay fuming over special teams errors: ‘It cost us the game tonight’ (nfl.com) ““It’s been a while since I’ve been this pissed after a game,” McVay said via the Associated Press . McVay had every right to be upset. He should first direct his ire at the man in the mirror. The coach’s decision to take his foot off the gas after the Rams pushed past the 35-yard line on the final drive was an unexcusable gaffe. His kicker, Harrison Mevis , already missed one kick on the night and doesn’t have the strongest leg. Settling for a 48-yard kick was asking for trouble. The Rams’ special teams have long been an issue. The team didn’t fix it this offseason, and the problems reared their head Monday night. From the opening kickoff, the unit was wobbly, allowing Ray Davis to return a kickoff 70 yards. On the Rams’ first drive, Mevis missed a 50-yard field goal. Then came the block. McVay said he plans to “evaluate everything” about his kicking unit. “In the kicking game, especially with our PAT, field goal, not even close to good enough,” he said. “It cost us the game tonight.” Bills get a massive blocked field goal in overtime, then Josh Allen leads Buffalo to dramatic win over Rams (sports.yahoo) “It looked on Monday night like Josh Allen had played well enough to win, only for the rest of the Buffalo Bills to let him down. But the Bills, and James Cook in particular, got a reprieve. The Los Angeles Rams were in position to win a thrilling game in overtime on a field goal, after Cook had lost his second fumble of the game to start overtime. But linebacker Greg Rousseau, who is off to a great start this season, blocked a potential game-winning Rams field goal.“ Rams vs. Bills score: Buffalo hits game-winning field goal in OT after Greg Rousseau’s block gives new life (cbssports) “Overtime was a near disaster for the Bills as they took possession to begin the extra period and seemed destined to put points on the board, particularly after Khalil Shakir ripped off a 57-yard gain to get them on the doorstep of the red zone. However, on the very next play, James Cook fumbled for the second time on the night. The loose ball forced by Rams linebacker Nate Landman was scooped up by Aaron Donald, and it appeared as if that was the final nail in the Bills’ coffin. That was until Rousseau’s clutch block.” Rams lose in overtime heartbreaker to Buffalo Bills and fall to 2-3 (latimes.com) “Tyler Bass kicks a 45-yard field goal in overtime shortly after the Bills block a Harrison Mevis field-goal attempt in the Rams’ 37-34 loss.” Rams’ Matthew Stafford shows off Davante Adams connection with MNF touchdown (sports.yahoo) “Stafford and Adams had just the one connection as of the two-minute warning of the first half, but Stafford was crisp and on target as he attempted to keep up with Josh Allen and the Bills in a 13-7 game. He found eight different players with his passes as the game continued toward halftime. Donald looked more like the dominant pass rusher and run stuffer fans were accustomed to seeing after McVay shared a glowingly positive update about his injury status before the matchup. The Rams’ defense gave up 6.4 yards per play to Allen and the Bills, showing they still had plenty of work to do as the game headed toward halftime.“ HIGHLIGHTS: Rams WR Davante Adams catches a pass from QB Matthew Stafford for a 4-yard touchdown vs. the Bills (therams.com) “Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Davante Adams catches a pass from quarterback Matthew Stafford for a 4-yard touchdown against the Buffalo Bills at SoFi Stadium.” HIGHLIGHTS: Matthew Stafford’s best throws from 3-TD game vs. Bills in Week 5 (therams.com) “Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford’s best throws from his three-touchdown game vs. the Buffalo Bills during Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season.” Rams wasted a statistically exceptional offensive performance in loss to Bills (ramswire) “The Los Angeles Rams ‘ offense had a night to remember against the Buffalo Bills , even though the result will make everyone forget their 34-point, 454-yard performance. The loss was such an unbelievable letdown; no team in the NFL this season has come close to collapsing the way the team did on Monday night. The Ringer’s Sheil Kapadia shared that the Rams are the first team in two years to perform so well on offense and still lose the game. According to Kapadia, the Rams’ offensive output was in the 99th percentile in terms of EPA per drive.“ Watch Rams’ Alaric Jackson punch Bills’ Bradley Chubb in wild MNF scene (sports.yahoo) “After the incident, Chubb commented on the exchange, saying: “They always catch the second guy, so I let him swing and my teammates held me back and I just chilled.” We will now have to wait and see whether the NFL hands down any punishment to Jackson, who was already in hot water over a June arrest for suspicion of felony domestic violence. He previously served a two-game suspension in 2024 for violating the NFL personal conduct policy.“ Comment of the Day: “You need to block the opposing team too so they don’t block the kick. Comedy of errors McVay grows a yellow streak up his back at 3rd and 6 and tried a run to the right. Mevis comes out during a timeout to look at the goalposts like he never seen them before the kick was blocked by someone who wasn’t blocked. What a joke and And Malibu McVay is home at his hacienda Looking at the waves of the pacific and thinking he wants Romos old analyst job.” -LaRams&NyMets Feed post of the day:
