title: Coaching matters, Klint Kubiak’s bad day at the office
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders went into Gillette Stadium for their Week 5 game against the New England Patriots and got the crap kicked out of them 45-17. Up until now, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak has looked like a prodigy and a whiz kid. However, Sunday in New England was an abject failure in all […]
full_text: (Photo by Edward Monigan IV/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders went into Gillette Stadium for their Week 5 game against the New England Patriots and got the crap kicked out of them 45-17. Up until now, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak has looked like a prodigy and a whiz kid. However, Sunday in New England was an abject failure in all three phases and for the first time all season, they looked completely unprepared. Since blame starts at the top and rolls downhill, that’s exactly where we are going to start. Coach Kubiak’s bad day at the office “Very disappointing performance from players and coaches” – Klint Kubiak From the start, the Raiders offense looked lethargic and utterly predictable. Going three-and-out on the first possession, getting out-hustled and straight-up manhandled. A 10 am start time seemed to have an unforeseen effect on Kubiak, who pissed down his leg with bad coaching decisions. The Raiders’ offense is dysfunctional outside of Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer, being exposed week after week. Before our very eyes. Somehow, Kubiak couldn’t find a way to scheme wide receivers open against fourth- and fifth-string defensive backs. To make matters worse, the Raiders have every intention of standing pat with the group of receivers they have now who aren’t making an impact. “We did not get it done as a staff as an offense today.” – Klint Kubiak When the Patriots started blitzing on nearly every play, the offense made no adjustments while the game was still manageable. No blitz beaters and it seemed as though he was content for his offense to roll over and die. Calling run play after run play despite the obvious mismatch of having all 5-8 of Marcus Jones covering 6-4 Bowers one-on-one nearly all game long. “I abandoned the running game too early and didn’t give it a chance to get going.” – Klint Kubiak Continuing to trot out an injured Ashton Jeanty and making him the workhorse was stupid. Mike Washington Jr. is averaging 5.0 yards per carry to Jeanty’s 3.4 yards per carry this season. Washington didn’t enter the game until there were three minutes left in the third quarter and the team was down 28 points. Even then, it was for a measly swing pass that went for five yards and he was promptly removed from the game. Return man Dylan Laube got four times (4) more carries than Washington. Laube, a local kid from New Hampshire, was awarded the opportunity to get a 2-yd touchdown run after a timeout in which Washington was taken off the field. Was it because he was a better pass blocker? Or was it because he was at home in front of family and friends? Mendoza first action The highlight of the game for Kubiak came when he finally decided to let his #1 overall draft pick get into the final drive of a blowout loss and get his feet wet a little bit. With 6:06 left in the fourth quarter, Fernando Mendoza entered the game and conducted a no-huddle offense straight down the field. Doing so with poise and command all the way down to the red zone. A beautiful sideline pass to Malik Benson was ruled incomplete as Benson’s toe-drag swag was not on fleek. He was unable to get his second foot down in bounds. Ultimately, Mendoza came up a yard short on 4th and four on a quarterback scramble. Ending the drive and the game for the Raiders’ offense. When asked about getting Mendoza in for a series, Kubiak had this to say. “I just wanted to get him some exposure…every rep is valuable for him.”

title: Las Vegas Raiders sliding down Week 6 NFL Power Rankings after blowout loss
summary: The media was singing the Las Vegas Raiders’ praises last week. However, it’s a much different tune in the Week 6 NFL Power Rankings roundup after a 45-17 blowout loss to the New England Patriots. Sports Illustrated 16. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 10 While I’m not overreacting at all to the Fernando Mendoza appearance […]
full_text: (Photo by Winslow Townson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The media was singing the Las Vegas Raiders’ praises last week . However, it’s a much different tune in the Week 6 NFL Power Rankings roundup after a 45-17 blowout loss to the New England Patriots . Sports Illustrated 16. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 10 While I’m not overreacting at all to the Fernando Mendoza appearance at the end of the Patriots blowout, I do wonder if three straight losses at least generates some conversation. Something tells me the Raiders are dug in on this, but .500 after six weeks will change a lot of minds. — Conor Orr Klint Kubiak called Kirk Cousins the Raiders’ starter during the head coach’s press conference on Monday, putting a brief halt to the questions about when Mendoza will take over under center. However, Orr is correct that if the Silver and Black lose to the 4-1 Buffalo Bills this Sunday, those conversations are really going to heat up. Does that mean the rookie’s first start will be behind a shaky offensive line against a Los Angeles Rams defensive line that features two future first-ballot Hall of Famers in Week 7? Granted, Myles Garrett may not return from injured reserve by the end of the month, which could change the situation. But the following week against the New York Jets feels like the sweet spot, unless Las Vegas pulls off an upset or two before the trip to the Big Apple. Bleacher Report 18. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 10 Even after consecutive losses, the Las Vegas Raiders are sitting at 3-2. Most Raiders fans would have taken that sort of start to the season, given the option to do so in August. However, things feel a lot different after a blowout loss to the New England Patriots than they felt following last week’s close loss to the rival Chiefs. Playing across the country with a less-than-100-percent Ashton Jeanty certainly didn’t help Las Vegas. However, the Raiders’ defense looked legitimately bad for the first time this season, and the lack of wide-receiver depth was glaring as Las Vegas tried to keep pace with Drake Maye and Co. Fernando Mendoza made his 2026 debut after the game got out of hand on Sunday. While Kirk Cousins wasn’t benched for performance reasons, calls for Mendoza will intensify if Las Vegas has many more team performances like the one it had in Week 5. — Kristopher Knox Knox has pretty much the same take as Orr and me on the Mendoza-Cousins situation. The hot start to the season might have temporarily altered the timeline for the No. 1 pick’s first start. However, if the postseason goes back to being an afterthought, it’s probably time to see what the kid is made of. ESPN 17. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 11 Biggest issue on defense: Growing pains in the secondary are showing Rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses had a strong start, being named the AFC’s Defensive Player of the Week after the Raiders’ Week 2 win over the Chargers. But Masses has allowed nine catches, 155 yards, two touchdowns and a 60% completion rate the past three games. Against the Patriots, the Raiders’ young trio of defensive backs — Masses, rookie safety Treydan Stukes and second-year cornerback Darien Porter — all struggled. Porter gave up a 49-yard reception to wide receiver Kyle Williams. Stukes gave up three catches for 59 yards, including a 35-yard touchdown in the first quarter. — Ryan McFadden It’s interesting to me that the young defensive backs are getting called out here. Don’t get me wrong, Masses has struggled over the last three weeks, and Stukes had a bad game in New England. But whether you use Pro Football Focus or Next Gen Stats , Eric Stokes has given up the most yards in coverage (209 or 205) and the second-highest completion percentage (62.5% or 56.0%) of the corners who have at least 10 coverage snaps. Also, Taron Johnson is third in yards (132 or 168) and is first in completion percentage (68.4% or 68.2%). Yes, Porter gave up a 49-yard catch to the Patriots. However, he’s yielded three completions on nine targets (33.3%) for 61 yards, per PFF, or four receptions on 11 targets (36.4%) for 86 yards, per NGS. So, that one play accounts for about 80% or 57.0% of the production he’s allowed so far this season. Also, the play the second-year pro was beaten on in New England was a Cover 0 call where he had to cover a deep over route while the Patriots had max protection to give Drake Maye all day to throw. On top of that, he had two PBUs last Sunday. Sure, Stokes and Johnson have been on the field more than any of the young guys mentioned, which leads to the higher volume stats. But the point here is that the entire secondary is struggling right now, not just the first- and second-year defensive backs. Additionally, Rob Leonard has to shoulder a good portion of the blame since his play-calling has become predictable and put the defense in bad spots over the last three weeks. The Athletic 17. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 13 Who have you beaten? Dolphins, Chargers, Saints The Raiders were exposed Sunday after a strong start to the season, largely on the back of wins over bad teams. But this trip to New England revealed a lot of flaws for Klint Kubiak and company. The defense was a total mess, allowing six touchdowns on 10 real drives. — Chad Graff, Josh Kendall I stand by what I said at the beginning of the season: the Raiders shouldn’t apologize for beating bad teams a year after being the worst team in the league. However, when it comes to them being legitimate playoff contenders in 2026, this is where the 3-2 record gets misleading. Vegas’ best win right now is against a 1-4 New Orleans Saints team that has lost its last two games by multiple possessions and a combined 31 points. That takes the air out of the “Saints are better than their record indicates” argument, and the 0-5 Miami Dolphins and 0-5 Los Angeles Chargers aren’t doing the Raiders any favors with how they’ve played over the last five weeks. NFL.com 19. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 12 The Raiders finally became the overmatched team we expected to see in 2026. Las Vegas’ defense couldn’t stop a nosebleed on Sunday, surrendering over 500 yards of offense to a unit that seemed lost just two weeks prior. An inability to protect Kirk Cousins (plus a continued lack of production from the ground game) prevented the offense from keeping up in a blowout loss. It’s certainly not time to consider benching Cousins for Fernando Mendoza, but the Raiders have officially encountered their first pothole and will need to divert accordingly in order to sustain the momentum built by a strong start. — Nick Shook Shook kind of alludes to this: a two-game skid is the first significant adversity Kubiak has faced as a head coach. How will he get his team to respond? We’ll find out on Sunday. It may be doom and gloom right now, but if the Silver and Black can pull off an upset against the Bills, I’ll turn to my friend Michael Corleone for the appropriate response.

title: Zeke Masses loses playing time, will he rebound in Week 6?
summary: Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 draft class (eight of the 10 picks are on the 53-man roster) fared in a 45-17 loss at the New England Patriots on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at home against the Buffalo Bills. Fernando Mendoza:The No. 1 overall pick made his […]
full_text: (Photo by Winslow Townson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 draft class (eight of the 10 picks are on the 53-man roster) fared in a 45-17 loss at the New England Patriots on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at home against the Buffalo Bills. Fernando Mendoza: The No. 1 overall pick made his NFL regular-season debut and he played the Raiders’ final 10 offensive snaps in a mop-up role in a lopsided loss. Coach Klint Kubiak praised Mendoza for the speed of his play. He completed six of eight passes for 48 yards and showed solid mobility. Treydan Stukes: The Raiders’ second-round pick played all 75 defensive snaps. The Raiders’ entire secondary struggled and Stukes was no exemption. At times, it looked like the Patriots were picking on the rookie. It will be interesting to see if Josh Allen and the Bills try to target Stukes as well. Trey Zuhn: The third-round pick was inactive with a knee issue. It’s unknown if he will be ready to play Sunday. Jermod McCoy: The fourth-round pick played 12 snaps on defense, his second defensive action this season. Perhaps that trend will continue in the coming weeks against the pass-happy Bills and Rams. He also played 13 snaps on special teams. Mike Washington: The fourth-round pick played a season-low 5 offensive snaps a week after playing a season-high 18 snaps. he had one carry and get less playing time than third-string running back Dylan Laube. Kubiak said he needs to do a better job of getting Washington involved. Let’s see if that’s the case Sunday. Dalton Johnson: The fifth-round pick safety was inactive for the fourth team in five games after he was active in Week 4. Zeke Masses: The fifth-round pick played just 33 percent of the defensive snaps and appeared to lose his starting role to Darien Porter, who masses beat out earlier in the season. Masses has been experiiencing growing pains the past three games after winning the AFC Defensive Player of the Week award in Week 2. We’ll see if he can earn more playing time againdt the Bills. Malik Benson: The sixth-round pick played a season high 16 offensive snaps because of injuries at wide receiver. He had one catch for six yards on four targets. The training camp star has two catches for 12 yards on eight targets this season.

title: Miami Dolphins Fans: Your Game 5 Takeaways
summary: Following Sunday’s loss by our Miami Dolphins to the Cincinnati Bengals, I asked the following question: What are your overall takeaways from this afternoon’s fourth game of the season between our Miami Dolphins and the Cincinnati Bengals? What are the positive and negative takeaways from this afternoon’s game, as they apply to the team overall […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 11: Jordan Phillips #94 of the Miami Dolphins celebrates with teammates against the Cincinnati Bengals during the second quarter at Hard Rock Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images Following Sunday’s loss by our Miami Dolphins to the Cincinnati Bengals, I asked the following question: What are your overall takeaways from this afternoon’s fourth game of the season between our Miami Dolphins and the Cincinnati Bengals? What are the positive and negative takeaways from this afternoon’s game, as they apply to the team overall and to individual units or players? Below are some of your answers and thoughts on the game- Finsane1 is ready to see what a backup QB has. McCord Pleeeeez FinsUp!!! jmworacle says this is going to take a big given Grier and all of his missteps. Also, trade down from that #1 overall if we get it. Thanks to Chris Grier’s incompetence it’s going to take a few more years to clean up. If the ‘Fins get the number one overall pick my advice would be to trade down. StanleyDoyle1 has some short-term issues and one big long-term issue at QB. The short-term issues are obvious and not a problem for someone like me who picked them to finish 2-15. Youth & inexperience. Lack of talent at certain positions (QB, Edge, WR, maybe DT) I’m encouraged by the OL. Go out and sign the top RT in free agency, draft a G, and you’re set. A few rookie stars in the making at LB and maybe WR with Bell. But long-term, the issue is the management and coaches: Picking Willis has proven to be a major error in judgment. He’s not the answer, he’s not even enough to form the question. But they picked him, and invested a ton of cap-space in a guy who would fight to be a number 2 on another team. They went with the safe and familiar, and it has blown up as a disaster. What does this tell you about their ability to identify and build talent? Draybch77 would like to talk to the person responsible. Who payed Malik to slide when he broke free for what could only be described as a possible touchdown? Phoenix6 wants to know if anyone knows where the big guy is. Did Kenneth Grant even play? Haven’t heard his name in any post or comment… Zen4Phins says there are positives and negative but that we could still run over the division. Positives: Rookies played well again today. Sounds like I’m making excuses but Burrow (with limited pressure), Chase and Higgens are a tough ask overall for this defense and they contained those 2 for the most part. 1td 99yds, 8 rec, 14 tgts and 1 was for 45 to Chase. Ollie was awesome again. Scored 24 pts and rushed over 200yds. Oline has been healthy in the early part of the season finally. Negatives: Rough day, in the rear view, for Willis. I gotta believe he’ll see it, work hard to fix it, and succeed. Not a qb on our roster all year so far that would fair much better in my opinion. Take the underneath all day if he sees or wants it and we move smoothly. Special teams opening kickoff coverage teleported us to the griddy dance early. 3rd down and redzone defense struggled and Burrow looked comfortable. Some time off and a chance to go undefeated in Division play! MiamiItaliano is out on Willis but hey, well still have that rodriguez kid. Negatives: Malik Willis is definitely not the guy. Probably gets benched after another poor performance against the Jets. Then they have to keep the guy on the books next year because his dead cap hit is $39.3 million. They still have Tua’s dead cap hit at $31.8 million next year lol. Also, J-Rod is not good at coverages yet. Burrow threw around him like he was a kid at recess. And the offense tried to pad stats in garbage time, barf. Positives: J-Rod did have 11 tackles. I Hate Sports , is, I think, trying to tell us something about the starting QB. biggest issues during today’s game Willis Interception Willis Interception Willis Fumble Willis Accuracy/Timing Willis Decision Making gertdoggy sees the road to the Super Bowl getting that much more difficult. Well we probably lost the first round bye in the playoffs with this loss. FinsUp88 sees a qb that needs to get back to what he showed last season in a limited sample. Overall, I continue to love the effort and fight this young team continues to show and build upon. I thought our secondary fought hard and faired very well against top tier wideouts today, liked seeing that. The defense continues to improve and communicate better, the stops will come eventually, they seem to be building the D the right way. Willis is killing the offense. He is pushing on nearly every pass play, when I am sure the coaching staff had continued stressing taking what the defense gives you. He has opportunities to use his legs and seems so reluctant to (this is what I was most excited about with him, using his legs to extend plays and drives). He is passing in available options continuously for the big shot and is killing drives and momentum, while keeping our defense the field for too long. I understand the talent in our skill positions isn’t elite and separation is limited, but he needs to take the open play when it’s there and use his legs to keep the defense honest when nothing is there. If Willis can even touch what he looked like last year in GB, we should be close enough for a win here soon, this team fights too hard to not get it done soon. Well another disapointing outing for at least some of the team with many of you sounding like you are over the whole Malik Willis experiment. I suspect that we will be looking at that experiment for the rest of the season barring an injury. Luckily many of the rookies continue to look good and show growth from game to game which should give us all some hope going forward, beyond this current season. As always thank you to each of you who took the time to join in on our Phinsider Question Of The Day.

title: Dolphins add Brady Cook to practice squad in bye week move
summary: The Miami Dolphins have signed quarterback Brady Cook to their practice squad, days after releasing their third-string passer from the active roster. The move comes following the team’s loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, dropping them to 0-5 on the year. The Dolphins released Cook from their 53-man roster on Saturday to make space for defensive […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 27: Brady Cook #15 of the Miami Dolphins exits the field after warmups prior to an NFL football game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Hard Rock Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins have signed quarterback Brady Cook to their practice squad, days after releasing their third-string passer from the active roster. The move comes following the team’s loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, dropping them to 0-5 on the year. The Dolphins released Cook from their 53-man roster on Saturday to make space for defensive tackle Kenneth Grant, who was activated off the injured reserve list. To make space on the practice squad for Cook, the Dolphins released running back Jarquez Hunter. The Dolphins traded for Hunter this summer, sending the Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Tutu Atwell in compensation. Hunter landed on the practice squad after the preseason and never made an appearance with Miami. A 2025 undrafted free agent out of Missouri, Cook spent his rookie season with the New York Jets. He appeared in five games, starting four of them, and threw for 739 yards on a 57.5 completion rate. He had two touchdown passes and seven passes intercepted. He recorded a 55.4 passer rating. Cook was cut by the Jets as part of the team’s roster cuts at the end of the preseason this year. He has not made an appearance since signing with the Dolphins. Miami’s quarterback room includes starter Malik Willis and backup Kyle McCord. Cook slides back in as the team’s third option at the position.

title: Miami Dolphins – Stream of Consciousness…no good patterns to be found…YET!
summary: Say it with me: Jeremiah Smith, Jeremiah Smith, Jeremiah Smith OR trade down! That’s it! Say it with me: The Saints actually covered TJ Hockenson and when they tackled him, he got hurt. He didn’t catch all 15 targets thrown to him this week! What a concept! Ok, there was a game on Sunday. I […]
full_text: OAKLAND, CA - DECEMBER 21: Clarence Davis #28 of the Oakland Raiders scores the winning touchdown on a pass reception against the Miami Dolphins during the 1974 AFC Divisional Playoff game at Oakland Alameda Coliseum on December 21, 1974 in Oakland, California. The Raiders defeated the Dolphins 28-26. The Sea of Hands Play. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/Getty Images) | Getty Images Say it with me: Jeremiah Smith, Jeremiah Smith, Jeremiah Smith OR trade down! That’s it! Say it with me: The Saints actually covered TJ Hockenson and when they tackled him, he got hurt. He didn’t catch all 15 targets thrown to him this week! What a concept! Ok, there was a game on Sunday. I watched it. You watched it. I saw a game that should have been played in the preseason. I am thinking of buying a “Wheel of Disfortune” to spin and see what pathetic mistake the Miami Dolphins will make. Spin one: Oooh, an 81-yard opening kickoff return***. Spin two: Generate zero pass rush and let the rookie “J.R. Badass” take the blame for not blanking Bengals tight end Mike Giesecki when the quarterback had 5.9 seconds to throw (not his fault). Spin three: Have Chop “Chump” Robinson imitate the “Invisible Man.” Spin four: Have Malik complete more passes to the other team than to his team. Spin five: “Raise the white flag!” That said, the Phins did not quit; at least some of them didn’t. Some of them are simply outclassed and no amount of coaching will fix their individual flaws. Don Shula went to a Super Bowl with David Woodley at QB and some very fine players (looking at you with love Don McNeal and Jimmy Cefalo). That is coaching. I will repeat myself from another column: Don Shula took a run-dominated offense to the Super Bowl and within 3 years took a pass-dominated offense to the Super Bowl. The best metaphor for this team is Dr. Jekyll and Mister Hyde. One play Ollie Gordon runs for 12 and then the next play Malik runs for his life (takes off too soon IMHO) and then…he throws God-awful INTs like Doug Williams’ Tampa Bay INTs. For those of you too young to have experienced it, Doug Williams was a gigantic QB with an absolute CANNON (maybe one of the strongest arms in NFL QB history) but he struggled to throws medium to short routes. These tendencies created a plethora of Doug Williams bad QB jokes. Yes, this man went on to win the Super Bowl about seven years later (after a stint in the USFL). I will tell you a cool story about that on another article. I don’t think OC Bobby Slowik understands the concept of a rhythmic flowing offense. In the one preseason game that Malik played in, he threw some beautiful timing patterns to the TE et al and I was impressed. It was flowing like Pompeii. This has not happened during the real season. Mark Schlereth (who is doing a great job on the color analysis – IMHO) pointed out numerous plays where didn’t see or didn’t throw the check down. Why? Taking the check downs augments the flow! I saw the news today that Hafley says Malik has to be better, I say you must save Malik from himself. Some QBs cannot be allowed to think: this was true of Vinny Testaverde. Jimmy Johnson allowed him to throw 5 INTs in the national championship game against Penn State. One of JJ’s many, many, many game coaching blunders. In another column, I pointed out that the deep shots can help the running game but we have to hit them. Back to Slowik’s ineptness: Chris Bell. This rookie is special but we target him once or twice? Hello! We did a reverse with Chris Bell and BANG! It worked! Maybe some of Chump’s invisibility powder rubbed off on Chris. Maybe Malik could literally not SEE Chris Bell. I did notice the Bengals paying attention to Chop on some plays but he simply doesn’t have the elite pass-rushing skills like Jason Taylor or Superman-like strength like Cameron Wake (simply wow to the 7 th power for that man!) to create his own “get-throughs.” Props to the Bengals: they knew what they had to do to win. Short passes, precise passes and one of my mantras that I heard from someone (can’t remember who) ……”on-time on-target.” Schlereth astutely pointed out “there is no defense for the perfect pass.” Burrow (on virtually any other organization) would be in the “On the way to Canton talk” already in his career. He is THAT dude! The Bengals are the Jets of the AFC central and we are rapidly taking the Jets place as the laughing stock of the AFC East. Let that sink in. I was in attendance at the last Phins playoff win in Joe Robbie Stadium. Methinks Burrow will end up like Marino, taking a team to the Super Bowl (that game was FIXED from the kickoff for the Rams) and losing and then never going again. I thought Burrow was a terrible QB his first year at LSU(after transferring from Ohio State) and then something changed in him. And boy did it change. The year BEFORE he won the natty and the Heisman, he was in a bowl game against UCF when one of their players cheap shotted him in his face. I thought he was permanently crippled at the time but not only was he not crippled, he came back in the game and surgically dissected UCF. Again, simply wow. Anyone can win when things are going their way but what impresses me in getting hit in the face and then getting back up like Neo did against Agent Smith! I hope something could transmogrify (Calvin & Hobbes anyone?) Malik into Super-Malik!!!! *** I knew we would lose after the opening kickoff because of this weird fact (I didn’t AI check it because “I am a tad lazy and if AI checks everything for me, me pea-brain will atrophy”): The team scoring on the opening kickoff return loses a lot. Just like in baseball, if the leadoff hitter homers in the first inning, his team loses. Probably a Russian wives’ tale. But I am not Russian. : In 1974, the Phins lost to the gosh darned Raiders (the Ken Stabler days). The opening kickoff Nat Moore (rookie season from the Gators, methinks) took the opening kickoff to the house. We lost. I was ten and at Disney World, serenated by Rock Hudson, who sang from Cinderella’s castle. When we arrived home, my dad told me we lost. I cried. I cried even more when I saw the play in the photo. In the 2007 season, the national championship and Super Bowl games both started with a kick return touchdown. Ted Ginn and Jacob Hester. Ohio State and the Chicago Bears both lost. Ouch. Sunday, the Bengals didn’t score on the KO return but their offense finished the job. The football Gods didn’t strike down the Bengals for almost scoring. We have to appease the football Gods and upgrade our NFL Shingle before we can even think of winning!

It was a close contest, but Miami still came out on the losing end of the clash. One major reason why the Dolphins were able to keep it close against an explosive Bengals squad was the play of former backup, now starter at the running back position, second-year back Ollie Gordon II. Miami Dolphins Week Five MVP – RB Ollie Gordon II Ollie Gordon II took over the starting running job following a devastating ACL tear for Miami’s electric runner, De’Von Achane. Since assuming the role, Gordon has already surpassed his rushing yardage total from his rookie season, while equaling his touchdowns as well. On Sunday against the Bengals, Gordon rushed for 88 yards on 18 attempts while finding paydirt for a third time this season. His bruising, powerful style wore down Cincinnati in the hot, South Florida heat. The Dolphins and offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik would be smart to continue to lean on Gordon as the season unfurls — especially considering the struggles of starting quarterback Malik Willis. title: Miami Dolphins reactions: Tuesday thoughts with The Earl
summary: The Miami Dolphins dropped yet another heartbreaker this week to the Cincinnati Bengals.  The good news?  They are guaranteed not to lose in week 6.  They enter their bye week with plenty of issues to clean up before the deep partof the season.  Here are my takeaways from the game. I’M NOT.  I’M JUST NOT. […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 11: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins looks on before a game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Hard Rock Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins dropped yet another heartbreaker this week to the Cincinnati Bengals. The good news? They are guaranteed not to lose in week 6. They enter their bye week with plenty of issues to clean up before the deep partof the season. Here are my takeaways from the game. I’M NOT. I’M JUST NOT. The biggest, most glaring issue in this game was quarterback Malik Willis’s play. Everyone will discuss this ad nauseam this week and into next week. I refuse to do so. Not because I am scared to discuss it or because I refuse to recant my position on him; I was a vocal advocate for the Dolphins signing him, and I stand by that, which I’ll explain in a moment. I refuse to discuss it because, well… I plain just don’t want to. You’uns can have fun with that. TON 618 is one of the largest black holes ever discovered , with a mass estimated to be about 66 billion times that of the Sun and a diameter of roughly 66,000 light-years. For reference, the diameter of the Milky Way galaxy is about 150,000 light-years. This thing is nearly half the size of our home galaxy. A colossal stellar object whose size we truly cannot fathom. The QB talk black hole amongst Dolphins fans dwarfs TON 618. Like anything that passes the event horizon, it is on a collision course with the singularity and will never be seen again. I would like to avoid the intense spaghettification due to its gravitational pull and stay on this side of sanity. What I WILL talk about is the financial ramifications. I had this discussion in a chat last week that I wanted to bring to light. GM Jon-Eric Sullivan said that he is going to add competition for the QB position every year by drafting one; if not every year, then every other year. So far, he has done most of what he said he would do. In the 2026 draft, however, that didn’t really materialize. Only 2 QBs were selected in round 1, and one was gone long before Miami got on the clock. Their only option was Ty Simpson at 12. The next QB selected was Carson Beck at pick 65, the first pick of the 3rd round. Again, he was gone before Miami had a pick, unless they took him at 43. I think they are pretty happy with the pick they made there. They could have selected Drew Allar at 75 instead of Caleb Douglas. Allar looked good in preseason, but Douglas also looks like a good pick. That was all for the Day 1 or Day 2 picks. The next QB was drafted at 110 in round 4, and if we are being realistic, that’s not true competition. There weren’t many options in the free-agent market, at least not anyone you’d want to consider. Sure, they could have gone with Tyrod Taylor or Kirk Cousins, but those are old vets with no future. They want someone with promise and potential. That’s why Malik Willis made sense. They knew him from his time in Green Bay, so they had some background information. The issue was the price tag. Pre-FA estimates were getting ridiculous, with figures over $40M per year. That was never going to happen, and Miami got Willis for a market-inflated deal very similar to what the Jets got for Justin Fields the season before. This is the biggest sore spot for fans. They have stated that Miami has wasted money and have hurt their cap position. That is not true whatsoever – more on that in a moment. They have stated that Miami could have stayed with Quinn Ewers and saved that money. The forgotten part of that discussion is they saw Ewers all camp long. As bad as Willis has been, Ewers was WORSE. They had him there in the room, in meetings, on the field. And he was worse. Camp reports from trusted opinions said that Ewers was considerably worse. Now, maybe he’s a Matt Moore gamer that sucks in practice, but shows up for games. But they saw enough and said “no thanks”. Anyone that thinks Ewers would have been a BETTER option is fooling themselves. Cheaper… but not better. Thus the crux of the argument: the money that could have been saved. First, let’s discuss CASH vs. CAP. In NFL contracts, there is a difference between what teams actually pay to players (CASH) and what they right down in their ledgers for accounting (CAP). Malik Willis signed a 3 year, $67,500,000 contract with $45,000,000 guaranteed . In terms of AAV (average annual value), he is getting $22,500,000 per year. But that is all half-truths and gorilla dust . You have to look at the CASH flow for his contract. The Dolphins gave a $22,285,000 signing bonus. That is $22.25M that Willis got in a check on the day he signed the contract. That’s CASH the Dolphins paid out of payroll. For CAP purposes, they have prorated this over a 5-year period which includes 2 void years on the deal, which are just dummy placeholder years for cap purposes. That means Willis has an automatic cap hit of $4,457,000 for the next five seasons. In 2026, he has a guaranteed salary of $1,215,000. This is CASH the Dolphins pay out in weekly game checks (he also has a $10,200 workout bonus). That means for the CAP, the Dolphins are “paying” Willis $5,682,200 in 2026. Willis will get SIGNIFICANTLY more than that in actual dollars, but the number they have to keep on the books is much lower. That’s a big need in a season where they don’t have the cap room to maneuver. In 2027, the Dolphins guaranteed Willis the salary portion of his contract, which is $21,500,000. That again will be game checks he receives and actual CASH he receives. For the CAP, the Dolphins will be forced to report $25,957,000 for their books. That’s a significant hit overall. But the thing is, the Dolphins are set to have the 3rd highest amount of cap space at $110,315,175 . With CAP inflation, that amount will likely be higher. This includes dead money for Tua and Bradley Chubb, a void year hit for Austin Jackson, who will not return, AND Willis’ CAP hit. The Dolphins will be flush with both CAP and CASH in 2027. Now, could they have saved $25+M in 2027 and likely just over $13M in dead cap for 2028 if they hadn’t signed Willis in the first place? Sure. But they will not need anywhere close to that amount of those things WITH Willis in the mix, let alone without him. Sully said he’s not going to be a big player in FA. Why should we doubt him at this point? This was a long-winded way of saying that Sully did the CORRECT thing by swinging the bat on Willis. I don’t think it’s time to give up on him yet, although a few more performances like Sunday and they may start. That window for hope is closing exceedingly fast. Regardless, the FO made the proper move by signing a QB they were familiar with, that was both reasonably cost effective AND still young enough to be a piece for the future, and still didn’t get so attached they won’t look at other options. Back in the day, ct and I discussed the move to acquire Rosen. We both agreed (shocking) that trading for him was the right move. He was a young QB with upside that maybe needed a change of scenery. Ct’s biggest contention was signing Fitzpatrick because if the goal was to tank, then Rosen was the best option. Fitz would win too many games and looking back, he was right. The Willis situation is almost exactly the same, just more costly in terms of CASH and CAP. At least he didn’t cost a draft pick like Rosen did, which in my opinion, is more valuable than the contract stuff. Willis is on pace right now to give the Dolphins the 1st overall pick. His upside was worth the chance, even if it is failing. Ewers lacks that upside, so I’m fine with the cost of the transaction. Who knows… maybe McCord is the guy we’ve all hoped for all these years and at this rate, he could get a chance sooner rather than later. THE DEFENSE WAS BETTER THAN I EXPECTED When I saw that Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins were playing, I expected the absolute worst. Miami’s secondary has…

title: Is There a Trade Market for Jauan Jennings?
summary: With the Minnesota Vikings bringing in a bunch of wide receivers recently, some folks. . .yours truly included. . .have been wondering exactly why. The Vikings already, seemingly, have a lot of talent at wide receiver, but it appears that one of those players could be on the way out after being quite underwhelming in […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 4: Jauan Jennings #14 of the Minnesota Vikings warms up before the game against the Miami Dolphins at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images With the Minnesota Vikings bringing in a bunch of wide receivers recently, some folks. . .yours truly included. . .have been wondering exactly why. The Vikings already, seemingly, have a lot of talent at wide receiver, but it appears that one of those players could be on the way out after being quite underwhelming in the early portions of this season. From @PatMcAfeeShow : In the wake of the Marvin Harrison Jr trade, another WR whose trade market is expected to heat up is #Vikings WR Jauan Jennings. Would a #49ers reunion make sense? pic.twitter.com/DR6mY1OvYb — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 13, 2026 Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network is reporting that the trade market for Vikings’ wide receiver Jauan Jennings is expected to “heat up” ahead of the league’s trade deadline, which is 10 November. The Vikings signed Jennings to a one-year contract worth up to $13 million back in May, and it’s hard to imagine how the deal could be more of a disappointment thus far. In his first four games (he missed the game against Chicago to deal with a family issue), he’s been targeted just nine times and has only two receptions for nine yards. That gives him less productivity than players like Tai Felton, Myles Price, DeeJay Dallas, and Gavin Bartholomew. I don’t have the math in front of me, but I’d be surprised of those four players combined were slated to make as much this season as Jennings is. According to a tweet made by the folks from Spotrac , trading Jennings away would incur a $5.4 million cap hit for the Vikings this season and a $4.4 million cap hit for whichever team would acquire him. Not crippling, by any stretch, but it’s not a pittance or anything like that, either. I’m not sure how much Jennings would fetch in a trade at this point, either, but the signs certainly seem to be pointing towards him not being a member of the Vikings for too much longer. What do you think, folks? Is Jauan Jennings still going to be a member of this team by the trade deadline? Is he even going to be a member of the Vikings when they come back from the bye week? Let us know what you think in the comments section.

title: O’Connell’s Adjustments and the Quick-Game Balance for Murray
summary: The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0 and looking like legitimate Super Bowl contenders, with Kyler Murray’s offense evolving under Kevin O’Connell and Brian Flores’ defense playing at a historic level. On the latest episode of The Real Forno Show, host Tyler Forness and producer Dave Stefano broke down the complementary football powering Minnesota’s undefeated start, the […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - OCTOBER 11: Kevin O'Connell head coach of the Minnesota Vikings watches from the sideline during the first half of a game at Caesars Superdome on October 11, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0 and looking like legitimate Super Bowl contenders, with Kyler Murray’s offense evolving under Kevin O’Connell and Brian Flores’ defense playing at a historic level. On the latest episode of The Real Forno Show , host Tyler Forness and producer Dave Stefano broke down the complementary football powering Minnesota’s undefeated start, the growth of Kyler Murray in O’Connell’s system, and what the trade deadline could bring. Forness didn’t mince words about the defense: “142 yards for the New Orleans Saints, barely over 20 minutes of time of possession.” He pointed out the Vikings have had their defense on the field for just 84 plays over the last two games — 18 fewer per game than last year’s average. “The offense has a lot to do with that. They are controlling the ball.” Stefano agreed: “The defense is absolutely rocking. They are elite and they could be historic.” On O’Connell’s adaptability, Forness pushed back hard against critics: “It is absolutely insane to me that it keeps being perpetuated around the media and the fan base, because it’s simply not true.” He detailed how O’Connell has adjusted for every quarterback from Kirk Cousins to Sam Darnold to J.J. McCarthy, and is now tailoring the system to Murray. The data backs it up: under 2.5 seconds, the quick game posted a 61.5% success rate but negative EPA; over 2.5 seconds, the EPA jumped to 0.24. “How much are you going to continue valuing ball control versus trying to get explosive plays?” Forness asked. Key Points: The Vikings’ defense has allowed just 109 points through five games — fewest in the NFL since 2010 Kyler Murray posted his first positive EPA game of the season against the Saints O’Connell’s flea flicker to Gavin Bartholomew nearly connected — the miss blamed on lack of chemistry with T.J. Hockenson injured The failed double pass drew criticism, but Forness argued “the real story is behind the why they called it in the first place” Will Reichard continues to impress — Stefano: “He wants to be basically a scientist at it. Getting a PhD in kicking” Forness predicts the Vikings will target defensive line depth at the trade deadline, not perceived needs like guard or running back Jauan Jennings’ lack of targets raised concerns — Forness: “maybe we’re starting to reach a point… where it’s just an oil and water situation” WR workouts (Juju Smith-Schuster, Dwayne Eskridge) signal the Vikings aren’t satisfied with receiver depth Listen: Or on your favorite podcast aggregator. Watch: Stefano summed up the feeling among Vikings fans: “This could be that special season that we all have hoped for.” With a brutal stretch looming — Colts, Packers, Lions, Bills, 49ers — the coming weeks will reveal whether this 5-0 start is built to last. As Forness put it: “Five and oh, baby. Literally cannot get better.” Catch The Real Forno Show with Tyler Forness and Dave Stefano — your go-to Minnesota Vikings podcast on the Vikings 1st & SKOL network from Bleav. New episodes drop regularly, and Thursday’s show promises a deep dive into the first five weeks. Fan with Us!!! Tyler Forness @TheRealForno of Vikings 1st & SKOL @Vikings1stSKOL and A to Z Sports @AtoZSportsNFL , with Dave Stefano @Luft_Krigare producing this Vikings 1st & SKOL production, the @RealFornoShow found at the @BleavNetwork . So here’s a question for you: Which Vikings matchup are you most worried about — the Lions, Bills, or 49ers?

(Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images With TreVeyon Henderson expected to miss multiple weeks due to a high ankle sprain, a familiar face has returned to the ground game in Foxborough. The New England Patriots announced the addition of running back Hassan Haskins to the practice squad on Tuesday along with cornerback D’Shawn Jamison. Haskins, 26, had worked out and signed at Gillette Stadium ahead of the 2026 preseason opener. The 6-foot-2, 228-pound running back went on to be released as a vested veteran at the NFL’s 53-man roster deadline. He spent two weeks on the practice squad in September and has remained a free agent since then. Originally entering the NFL in the fourth round of the 2022 draft at No. 131 overall, Haskins made previous stops with the Tennessee Titans and Los Angeles Chargers. Through 44 career games, the former first-team All-Big Ten selection via the Michigan Wolverines stands with 76 carries for 229 yards, 18 catches for 119 yards, three touchdowns and one start. He has handled 371 snaps on offense, 683 snaps on special teams and now checks in as the fourth healthy back in the fold behind starter Rhamondre Stevenson, trade acquisition Corey Kiner and scout-teamer Lan Larison. Jamison, 27, joins Al’zillion Hamilton as the second cornerback on New England’s practice squad midway through October after the promotion of veteran Kindle Vildor. The 5-foot-9, 185-pound Texas Longhorns product went undrafted in 2023 and made his initial NFL tours with the San Francisco 49ers, Carolina Panthers and Pittsburgh Steelers. He spent the first month of the 2026 campaign on the practice squad of the Arizona Cardinals before working out in Foxborough along with rookie corner Jeremiah McClendon. Notching 10 tackles and one pass deflection, Jamison has appeared in 18 games while seeing 107 snaps on defense and 166 snaps on special teams. His career includes one start as well as three kickoff returns. The Patriots released outside linebacker Jose Ramirez to make room among the 17-man group. Ramirez, 27, had re-signed to New England’s practice squad last week after going through the wire unclaimed. The 6-foot-2, 252-pound edge rusher first arrived as the calendar turned to September and was called up to the 53-man roster three weeks later. In two games, he recorded one solo tackle across 30 snaps between defense and special teams before being waived . Entering the NFL in the sixth round of the 2023 draft at No. 196 overall, Ramirez made four appearances while a member of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The former MAC Defensive Player of the Year out of Arizona, Riverside City College and Eastern Michigan spent last year with the CFL’s Hamilton Tiger-Cats on the way to reaching a futures agreement with the Philadelphia Eagles. Head coach Mike Vrabel’s 3-2 club moves forward with an open spot on the active roster and a full practice squad. The New York Jets visit Gillette Stadium on Sunday. The AFC East kickoff is set for 1 p.m. ET.

summary: With two Yuge wins, the Patriots are officially on an upward streak. The experts have noticed. Nick Shook from NFL.com ridiculously had the Pats ranked 31st two weeks ago ahead of the Bills game, but has since acknowledged the Pats rising from the ashes. The rest of the other experts have as well. Nice to […]
full_text: Oct 11, 2026; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; New England Patriots fans pose for a photo during the second half in a game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Bob DeChiara-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect With two Yuge wins, the Patriots are officially on an upward streak. The experts have noticed. Nick Shook from NFL.com ridiculously had the Pats ranked 31st two weeks ago ahead of the Bills game, but has since acknowledged the Pats rising from the ashes. The rest of the other experts have as well. Nice to see New England back in the top 10 where it feels they belong. Coming to town this coming Sunday are the 2-3 New York Jets. Pats fans may take them lightly, but the organization can’t afford to. A loss puts both teams at 3-3, with the Jets moving to second place in the AFC East. No one wants that. Everyone knows how much extra weight division and conference games carry in the standings, precisely why this matchup matters. The Pats are operating on an over-stuffed injury report and depleted roster. Mike Vrabel, Josh McDaniels and Zak Kuhr made it work effectively last week. Wednesday the initial Week 6 injury report comes out, giving us a better idea of which players are available but I think the coaching staff can keep it duct-taped together for another week. Pats head into the new week favored by 7.5. Geno Smith has thrown zero interceptions so far this season, but I believe New England’s defense will find a way to disrupt his passing game. I see the Patriots winning and padding their divisional lead over New York. GO PATS!! AFC East: Buffalo Bills (4-1) at Las Vegas Raiders (3-2) New England Patriots (3-2) vs. New York Jets (2-3) Miami Dolphins (0-5) – Bye Week AFC Matchups: Kansas City Chiefs (4-0) vs. Los Angeles Chargers (0-5) Baltimore Ravens (4-1) at Cleveland Browns (3-2) Jacksonville Jaguars (4-1) vs. Houston Texans (1-4) Denver Broncos (3-2) vs. Seattle Seahawks (3-2) Pittsburgh Steelers (3-2) at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1-4) Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) -Bye Week Indianapolis Colts (2-3) vs. Tennessee Titans (0-5) 6th – Nate Davis (USA Today): QB Drake Maye has seemingly captured his MVP-caliber form the past two weeks after a very rough September. Might he even go to another level given WR A.J. Brown could be back as soon as Sunday against the Jets? [+1] 7th – Vinnie Iyer (Sporting News): Drake Maye’s first three games: average of 195 passing yards per game, 1 touchdown to six interceptions, 72 total rushing yards. Maye’s past two games: average of 322 passing yards per game, 7 TDs to 1 INT, 79 total rushing yards. What’s the difference? Might just be playing easier pass defenses of Buffalo and Las Vegas . [+2] 7th – Ian Glendon (Full Press Coverage): The Patriots have completely changed their season in two weeks. Beating Buffalo was the attention-grabber, but crushing Las Vegas 45-17 was the confirmation. Drake Maye and the offense looked explosive, and New England suddenly has a real argument as one of the AFC’s most dangerous teams. The Jacksonville loss still exists, but it feels a lot farther away now . [+2] 9th – NFL Nation (ESPN): Biggest issue on defense: Cornerback depth. They played with only three healthy CBs on Sunday, as starters Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) and Carlton Davis III (neck) were inactive, and rookie backups Karon Prunty and Channing Canada were unavailable because of hamstring injuries. When fill-in starter Charles Woods left the game in the second half because of a shoulder injury, it further thinned a perilous CB situation, leaving just Marcus Jones and Kindle Vildor as available options. New England has allowed a 66% completion percentage this season, which ranks 25th in the NFL. — Mike Reiss [+5] 9th – Mike Florio (ProFootballTalk): The patriotic pigeons had a field day on Tom Brady’s statue . [+4] 10th – Conor Orr (SI): I don’t really care whether it was a designed play or not, but Efton Chism’s in-game backwards pass, which followed an unbelievable end zone grab the week prior against the Bills, ensures that the story of the NFL in 2026 cannot be written without Josh McDaniels and a white Patriots wide receiver shorter than six feet tall. Time is truly a flat circle . [+2] 10th – Nick Shook (NFL): It took one wild win over the Bills to return the Patriots to excellence. They detonated the Raiders on Sunday, with fantastic offensive performances by Drake Maye, Efton Chism III, Kyle Williams, DeMario Douglas — heck, just throw in every skill-position player. They all feasted in a game that saw New England finish with 536 yards of offense, pairing perfectly with a defense that put the clamps on Las Vegas early . [+8] 11th – Pete Prisco (CBS Sports): Drake Maye has righted things in a big way. He’s been on fire the past two weeks as the Pats have turned their season around . [+4] 11th – Frank Schwab (Yahoo! Sports): Drake Maye isn’t a bad QB. Go figure. After naysayers got their licks in during Maye’s three-game slump to start the season, which was an extension of his postseason issues, Maye has 643 passing yards, seven passing touchdowns, 79 rushing yards and a rushing score in his last two games. Those games came against the Bills and Raiders, who had one combined loss before facing New England. Stunning, but a 24-year-old QB who was one vote from winning MVP last season might still be good . [+2] 13th – Ralph Vacchiano (FOX Sports): The Patriots are such a different team when Drake Maye is playing like Drake Maye. In the first three games of the season, Maye threw just one touchdown pass with six interceptions and averaged 195 passing yards per contest. But in the last two games — both wins — he’s had seven touchdown passes, one interception with an impressive 321.5 passing yards per game. And with him rolling, their running game was suddenly working, too. It’s no wonder that they made quick work of the upstart Raiders. And with the Jets and Dolphins coming up in their next three games, they’ve got a shot to get on a little bit of a roll now, too. Stat To Know : The Patriots averaged 12 points per game in Weeks 1-3, ranking 31st in the NFL. In Weeks 4-5, they averaged a league-best 37 points per game . [+2] AVG RANK: 9.3 [+3.6]

Campbell left the game against the Raiders in the second quarter after running back Rhamondre Stevenson was tackled […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - OCTOBER 11: Will Campbell #66 of the New England Patriots reacts as he takes the field against the Las Vegas Raiders prior to an NFL football game at Gillette Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots received positive news in the injury department. Starting left tackle Will Campbell avoided a major injury in his right knee on Sunday. According to The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero, Campbell is now considered week-to-week. Campbell left the game against the Raiders in the second quarter after running back Rhamondre Stevenson was tackled into his right leg. The tackle departed for the locker room but returned to the sideline to go through pass sets and ride the stationary bike. After joining the team in the locker room for halftime, Campbell did not return to the sidelines and was ruled out. “We’ll see how the week goes. He’ll get looked at and continue to rehab,” head coach Mike Vrabel said Monday. “He wasn’t able to finish the game, so I don’t know how much time he’ll miss. I don’t know if he’ll be back towards the end of the week or be back Wednesday. We’ll take it day by day, see how he feels tomorrow, see what he does Wednesday and keep you updated on the injury report.” In Campbell’s place, rookie first-round pick Caleb Lomu played a season-high 49 offensive snaps. At his natural left tackle position, Lomu held up well allowing just one hurry. “I don’t think it was too big for him. I think he was able to settle down. You didn’t really notice him a lot, so I think that’s probably a good thing,” Vrabel said of Lomu’s performance. “He was able to anchor at times on some power and allowed Drake [Maye] to be able transfer up into the pocket. I thought it worked together well with AVT [Alijah Vera-Tucker] when he got in there.” Lomu should be expected to start at left tackle moving forward, while the Patriots also have fellow rookie Dametrious Crownover on the active roster. Offensive tackle Marcus Bryant is also eligible to return from injured reserve. The Patriots will host the New York Jets at Gillette Stadium this Sunday for a 1 p.m. ET kickoff.

title: Patriots injury analysis after Raiders win in Week 5
summary: The New England Patriots have plenty to feel good about coming out of their win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. Their offense had its best day of the season, quarterback Drake Maye returned to his MVP form, and the defense had Kirk Cousins and the Raiders offense in a blender throughout the day. […]
full_text: The New England Patriots have plenty to feel good about coming out of their win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. Their offense had its best day of the season, quarterback Drake Maye returned to his MVP form, and the defense had Kirk Cousins and the Raiders offense in a blender throughout the day. However, the Patriots did not have perfect day either. Once again, after all, the injury bug bit them pretty hard. With that said, here is our weekly injury analysis after rewatching the game. Patriots injury analysis: NFL Week 5 RB TreVeyon Henderson: On the very next snap after catching a lateral from teammate Efton Chism in the second quarter, Henderson was tackled from behind on an 11-yard jet sweep. In the process, he suffered an ankle injury that forced him to leave the game and gingerly walk to the locker room. The second-year running back was originally announced as questionable to return and ultimately ruled out. LT Will Campbell: Just two players after losing Henderson, the Patriots also saw Will Campbell go down. The starting left tackle was rolled up on from behind on a short run, staying down and grabbing his right knee — the same one he hurt last season when he tore his MCL and had to be placed on temporary injured reserve. He exited for the blue medical tent and later the locker room, but reappeared later in the second quarter. Campbell spent time on the sideline and riding a stationary bike. Despite the positive signs, however, he never returned to the game and did not reemerge after halftime. CB Charles Woods: The Patriots were already down four cornerbacks entering Sunday, and another one got banged up midway through the third quarter. Charles Woods, who had started the game with Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis both absent, remained down on one knee after a tackle for loss. He was labeled as questionable to return with a shoulder injury — he already dealt with a shoulder issue coming into the game — but did eventually make his way back onto the field. ED Dre’Mont Jones: Jones stayed down after rushing the passer in the fourth quarter. He did not appear to have absorbed any non-standard form of contact, but nonetheless required medical assistance on the field. He eventually got up and walked off the field into the blue medical tent, fist-bumping teammates along the way. The Patriots announced him as questionable to return with a shoulder injury and he was kept out for the remainder of the game. DT Cory Durden: Durden had his feet tangled up after Raiders running back Dylan Laube’s touchdown in the fourth quarter, but he managed to walk to the bench under his own power. He did miss the ensuing extra point kick, but was back on the field at the next possibility thereafter: blocking on Andy Borregales’ point-after try to cap the Patriots’ next offensive possession. What this means for the Patriots Out of the five Patriots to get banged up on Sunday, three are question marks heading into Week 6: Will Campbell, TreVeyon Henderson, and Dre’Mont Jones. Let’s start with Henderson, whose status was updated on Tuesday morning: he reportedly suffered a high ankle sprain that will keep him out for “multiple weeks” even though the Patriots are optimistic about a reasonably quick return. Still, Henderson being out will put pressure on a New England skill position group already without wideouts A.J. Brown and Mack Hollins. Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner are the top two running backs with Henderson out, with Lan Larison providing extra depth on the practice squad. As for Campbell and Jones, they are in the TBD category for now. Jones’ injury didn’t appear overly serious when it happened, but that also does not mean his return to the field this week is guaranteed, particularly as far as full capacity is concerned. If he is limited our out versus the New York Jets, Elijah Ponder and Gabe Jacas will likely see an uptick of snaps again. Campbell, meanwhile, is also expected to miss time after spraining his knee. First-round rookie Caleb Lomu took over and is set to continue lining up at left tackle until the nominal starter is cleared to return. When that happens remains to be seen, especially considering that Mike Vrabel sounded somewhat optimistic when talking about the second-year man on Monday. Beyond the losses, the Patriots also might be getting some talent back soon: A.J. Brown, who suffered his own high ankle sprain in Week 1 and was subsequently placed on injured reserve, is eligible to return to practice this week. All signs point toward such a return happening sooner rather than later. The Patriots will be back on the practice fields on Wednesday, starting their on-field preparation for the upcoming game against the Jets.

full_text: The New England Patriots offense has taken another hit. Running back TreVeyon Henderson, who was unable to finish Sunday’s win over the Las Vegas Raiders, has been diagnosed with a high ankle sprain. The injury will sideline him for “multiple weeks,” according to a report by Adam Schefter of ESPN. The Patriots are, however, hoping for a return “sooner rather than later.” Henderson, 23, left the game against the Raiders in the second quarter. He was tackled from behind on an 11-yard jet sweep and remained on the ground injured. After gingerly departing for the locker room, he was initially announced as questionable to return to the contest but never actually reemerged. In his absence, the Patriots turned to starting running back Rhamondre Stevenson and third-stringer Corey Kiner. Stevenson and Kiner combined to gain 116 rushing yards on just 19 carries against the Raiders, averaging 6.1 yards per carry and scoring a touchdown. Kiner also lost a fumble on his first touch of the game, New England’s only turnover in a 45-17 victory . Henderson originally joined the Patriots as a second-round draft pick in 2025. The Ohio State product finished his rookie campaign with a combined 1,241 scrimmage yards and 10 touchdowns in 21 games. In 2026 so far, he has carried the ball 42 times for 163 yards and a score. He also caught two passes for an extra 22 yards. The Patriots will host the New York Jets at Gillette Stadium this Sunday for a 1 p.m. ET kickoff.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Eli Raridon shows immense potential in win over Raiders
summary: The New England Patriots saw untapped potential in Eli Raridon when they selected the tight end in the third round of this year’s NFL Draft. On Sunday, the rookie began to show why. Raridon set career highs with five catches for 57 yards in the Patriots’ 45-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, offering an […]
full_text: The New England Patriots saw untapped potential in Eli Raridon when they selected the tight end in the third round of this year’s NFL Draft. On Sunday, the rookie began to show why. Raridon set career highs with five catches for 57 yards in the Patriots’ 45-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, offering an encouraging glimpse of what he can bring to Josh McDaniels’ offense. “I think he’s talented,” head coach Mike Vrabel said. “I think he’s continuing to get more comfortable each and every day, that he sees what this league is about, maybe starts to have more confidence in himself that he can do this at this level and he can do it fairly well.” The Patriots have wasted little time getting Raridon involved as a rookie. Despite missing time early with a thigh injury, he has played 50% of the team’s offensive snaps and found the end zone in his NFL debut. And while the coaching staff has been pleasantly surprised by Raridon’s early work as a blocker, Sunday’s performance against Las Vegas truly showcased how he can make an impact as a pass catcher. McDaniels got the rookie, who ran a 4.62-second 40-yard dash, on the move and into space, allowing him to showcase his explosiveness in the open field. Raridon gained seven yards on a crossing route, picked up 13 yards on a slide concept and hauled in a 31-yard reception on a perfectly placed wheel route down the sideline from Drake Maye. “I think it was good to see Eli work at the line of scrimmage, block a little bit, but then also be able to get out and do some things in the pass game and things that he’ll have to improve on. If you’re targeted five times as a tight end, you want five catches,” Vrabel said. Raridon’s early involvement and fit in the offense have been encouraging signs to begin his rookie season. And it would be no surprise if the tight end slowly becomes more-and-more involved in the offense as the season progresses. “I think when he knows what to do, and there’s a lot of different looks that he hasn’t seen, defenses and defensive fronts, but I think just continuing to improve and continuing to invest in these young players,” Vrabel said.

title: Patriots playoff picture after Week 5 win over Raiders
summary: The New England Patriots’ second straight victory came in dominant fashion. The team of head coach Mike Vrabel defeated the visiting Las Vegas Raiders 45-17 at Gillette Stadium, improving to 3-2 on the year and decisively closing the book on its early-season struggles. The win also has another effect: it moves the Patriots up in […]
full_text: The New England Patriots’ second straight victory came in dominant fashion. The team of head coach Mike Vrabel defeated the visiting Las Vegas Raiders 45-17 at Gillette Stadium , improving to 3-2 on the year and decisively closing the book on its early-season struggles. The win also has another effect: it moves the Patriots up in the AFC playoff standings and keeps them within striking range in the division. AFC East standings Buffalo Bills (4-1) New England Patriots (3-2) New York Jets (2-3) Miami Dolphins (0-5) The Patriots came close to taking over the AFC East lead on Monday night, but the Bills beating the Rams 37-34 in overtime prevented that scenario from unfolding. They therefore remain one game behind their rivals, holding the ever-important head-to-head advantage following their win in Buffalo last week. The Jets’ victory over the Browns means that they are also not too far off either at this point in the season. However, the upcoming game in Foxborough will be crucial for both teams: for the Jets to prove their legitimacy, and for the Patriots not to lose any further ground in the division. As for the Dolphins, they continue to look like one of the worst teams in the NFL. AFC playoff standings Kansas City Chiefs (4-0) Baltimore Ravens (4-1) Jacksonville Jaguars (4-1) Buffalo Bills (4-1) New England Patriots (3-2) Denver Broncos (3-2) Las Vegas Raiders (3-2) On the bubble: 8. Cleveland Browns (3-2), 9. Pittsburgh Steelers (3-2), 10. Cincinnati Bengals (3-2), 11. New York Jets (2-3), 12. Indianapolis Colts (2-3), 13. Houston Texans (1-4 ), 14. Miami Dolphins (0-5) , 15. Los Angeles Chargers (0-5) , 16. Tennessee Titans (0-5) The Patriots’ win over the Raiders allowed them to leap-frog Las Vegas in the standings and move from the seventh to the fifth playoff seed. That is also possible due to their 3-1 conference record, and their strength of victory and strength of schedule being the highest and second-highest, respectively, among all AFC teams at the moment. Still, the race for the playoff seeds remains very competitive at this early a stage in the season. Realistically, though, the cream will rise to the top over the next few weeks and some clubs prove themselves pretenders rather than being able to fight for one of the seven available spots in the postseason picture.

title: Saints vs. Vikings Game MVP
summary: After being embarrassed now for two consecutive weeks, it is very difficult to find MVPs after games like these. full_text: After being embarrassed now for two consecutive weeks, it is very difficult to find MVPs after games like these. However, one player did show up this week, and while his efforts were not matched it was definitely good to see him back on the field and have somewhat of a pulse on this team. Carl Granderson is the MVP for the game against the Vikings. There was not a lot to be proud about on either side of the ball. But with Granderson making his return to the lineup, it was refreshing to see someone on the defensive front compliment Chase Young. Granderson finished the game with 5 total tackles 2 solos 1.5 sacks 2 TFLs and 2 QB hits. He was very disruptive and showcased something that this Saints defense has sorely been lacking opposite Chase Young for nearly the entire season. Saints will travel to New York/New Jersey to take on the Giants on Sunday. Hopefully, things will turn around sooner than later.

title: State of the NFC South: Week 5
summary: Tampa Bay Buccaneers This division makes no sense. The one team that has looked like the worst team in the NFL each week ends up winning against the Dallas Cowboys, a team trying to make the playoffs. It was a game that was more about the Cowboys giving the game away rather than the Bucs […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 11: Justin Jefferson #18 of the Minnesota Vikings runs the ball during the second quarter of a game against the New Orleans Saints at Caesars Superdome on October 11, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) | Getty Images Tampa Bay Buccaneers This division makes no sense. The one team that has looked like the worst team in the NFL each week ends up winning against the Dallas Cowboys, a team trying to make the playoffs. It was a game that was more about the Cowboys giving the game away rather than the Bucs winning it, but nonetheless, Tampa Bay is on the board. Rookie QB Jalon Daniels had a decent game, but the real star was Bucky Irving, who finished with 165 rushing yards. The Buccaneers’ success is dependent on Irving having good games. This is the first time Irving has gone over 100 yards this season. Carolina Panthers The Panthers were on their bye week. Next, they face the Philadelphia Eagles, and with their tough start to the season, the Panthers have a chance to widen their first-place lead. Atlanta Falcons After beating the division rival Saints on Monday Night Football, Atlanta had a tougher opponent in Week 5. The Baltimore Ravens have been one of the best teams in the NFL, but they were going to be without Lamar Jackson. Still, with how well the Ravens are coached, especially on offense, Baltimore was going to be a challenge, and in the end, the Falcons couldn’t get it done. This was still a good game for the Falcons, and the game even went to overtime, nut near the end of the fourth quarter, Michael Penix was injured. After the Ravens drained nearly the entire overtime clock and scored a touchdown, the Falcons got the ball, but Tua Tagovailoa threw an interception on the second snap. New Orleans Saints And now the Saints, we have a new team in last place. After their embarrassing loss to the Falcons, the Saints followed it up with another bad game. It’s clear that the team is angry with the results; Tyler Shough is playing through injuries, and the Saints are risking his health even more by playing him, and Kellen Moore’s time as head coach is starting to slip away. When everyone knows the Vikings are going to blitz, the Saints are unprepared for the blitz. Being unprepared is a common occurrence for the team, and as of now, there is no sign the Saints are going to turn this thing around. NFC South standings: Carolina Panthers (2-2) Atlanta Falcons (2-3) Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1-4) New Orleans Saints (1-4)

With the Saints searching for answers after another disappointing result, performances from young players like Sanker are worth watching as the season continues.

full_text: Malik Harrison | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New York Giants on Tuesday added veteran linebacker Malik Harrison to their 53-man roster, filling the spot opened on Saturday when defensive lineman Chauncey Golston was placed on injured reserve. Harrison, 28, is in his seventh NFL season. He spent the first five seasons of his career with the Baltimore Ravens after being a third-round pick by the Ravens in the 2020 NFL Draft. Harrison spent the 2025 season with the Pittsburgh Steelers. In 90 regular-season games, he has made 43 starts. Harrison has signficant experience playing both inside and outside linebacker, so he provides the Giants depth at that level of their defense. He has also been a valuable special teams contributor throughout his career. Harrison was elevated from the practice squad for the first three games this season, the maximum allowed by NFL rules. He played 56 snaps, all on special teams, with two solo tackles. To take Harrison’s spot on the practice squad, the Giants made the signing of defensive end Dawuane Smoot official.
