title: NY Giants news: Changing the offense, Jameis Winston, Isaiah Likely, more
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories as the Giants get set to host the New Orleans Saints. Let Jameis Winston cook? Why Giants should ditch run-heavy approach and let QB air it out | The Athletic The Giants may have stumbled into the world Winston is most comfortable in during the […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories as the Giants get set to host the New Orleans Saints. Let Jameis Winston cook? Why Giants should ditch run-heavy approach and let QB air it out | The Athletic The Giants may have stumbled into the world Winston is most comfortable in during the second half of Sunday’s 27-27 tie with the Commanders. Partly due to the game flow — the Giants were trailing by two scores for most of the second half — and partly due to a need to shake things up after a woeful first half, the coaches opened up the passing game and went up-tempo with a no-huddle offense. The Giants’ best playmakers are wide receiver Malik Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely. It makes more sense to run the offense through that duo rather than the underwhelming running backs corps of Cam Skattebo, Najee Harris and Tyrone Tracy Jr. Now, 33 combined targets like Nabers and Likely had Sunday may be excessive. But it’s not a coincidence that the offense took off when Winston started feeding that duo in the second half. John Harbaugh defends surprising Giants call to play for OT instead of a win | New York Post Kicking the extra point to pull within seven points seemed to make the most sense, but the analytic assessment is to go for the 2-point conversion to boost the chances to win the game in regulation. The thinking is the trailing team will need 15 points to win the game, so go for two after the first touchdown and if you do not get it, go for two after the second touchdown. “I think generally speaking, theoretically, you go for two,” Harbaugh said Monday. “Then you see if you have to go for two twice, give yourself a chance to win the game in regulation. But the way the game was going, I just decided I wanted to put it into overtime. I didn’t want to take the chance on the 2-point conversion. I thought overtime would give us the best chance. Plus, it’s a road division game, so the tie isn’t the worst thing for the road team. So, I just feel like all in all, I made that decision to go for one and put it in overtime if it came down to two scores.” Isaiah Likely: Halftime dialogue, Jameis Winston’s open ears fueled Giants’ OT push | USAToday.com Likely said the feedback loop with Winston centered on trust in leverage and winning individual plays. He added that Winston responded by placing the ball in their hands and expecting them to produce. “Great feedback at halftime. Player dialogue, coaches’ dialogue, and really just getting behind your brother,” said Likely. “You know, Jameis was open ears. He understood that the job in the second half was to get us back in the game and that’s exactly what he did…Jameis is one of those, when he’s clicking, he’s clicking. I feel like he showed that fire in his eyes coming into the huddle every time, knowing that when there’s plays to be made, he can make a play.” Top 10 best NFL free agent acquisitions through Week 5 | CBSSports.com 7. Giants TE Isaiah Likely. Contract: Three years, $40 million with $26 million guaranteed. Despite losing starting quarterback Jaxson Dart with a season-ending knee injury in Week 2, the New York Giants remain in first place in the NFC East division through five weeks with a 3-1-1 record. Free agency acquisition tight end Isaiah Likely is a big reason why New York has been able to maintain any semblance of a coherent passing game despite fill-in quarterback Jameis Winston ranking second-to-last in the league in completion percentage at 57.6%. Likely’s four receiving touchdowns are tied for the fourth-most in the NFL and rank as tied for the most among tight ends leaguewide. His 19 receiving first downs are the most among all tight ends through five weeks this season. With No. 1 wide receiver Malik Nabers still finding his footing in 2026 after returning from a torn ACL, Likely has been a godsend for the Giants’ passing game. Jameis on building chemistry in the pass game . @Jaboowins is enjoying the chemistry being built with @whyguard13 & @DaGorilla4 🙌🏽 pic.twitter.com/HSLMbfJSIF — Where’s Jameis (@WheresJameis) October 13, 2026 Can John Harbaugh’s Giants sustain winning while walking NFL tightrope? | New York Daily News Harbaugh noted that he and his coaching staff have been able to pivot week-to-week so far to find new ways of concealing weaknesses and highlighting strengths of their shorthanded and evolving roster. They are without Dart, edge rusher Brian Burns, wide receiver Calvin Austin and defensive tackle Roy Robertson-Harris already, among others, after all. “We as a coaching staff do a great job of kind of finding our identity in some of these different areas, and we will,” Harbaugh said. As Giants’ pass rush pressure improves, Jayden Daniels’ showing raises concerns | NJ.com Still, it’ll be fascinating to see how Carter and the Giants’ defense handle Daniels the next time they see him, in Week 10 at MetLife Stadium. Daniels on Sunday ran nine times for 103 yards, with touchdowns of 26 and 38 yards. Carter knows this is something the Giants must fix. “We’ve just got to be more disciplined in our rush lanes,” he said. “We talked about it all week. So honestly, if that happens in the game, it’s on us as a front. We really got to be better at caging him and stopping our rush [to not over pursue]. We’ve got to be better at that next time we see them for sure.” Radio call of Nabers touchdown last weekend "Big time play by a big time player!" 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/NYSmd5P7tv — New York Giants (@Giants) October 12, 2026 NFL Insider Explains Why Giants Really Traded for J.J. McCarthy | SI.com “They do wanna see whether or not someone drafted that high and that young is capable of being a backup or even a starter at some point,” Schultz said, adding that there could be more sightings of McCarthy on the field “in certain situations.” But not as a starter, at least not for the immediate future.“That would really surprise me,” Schultz said. “If Jameis were to play really badly in a couple of weeks in a row and they lost two in a row, I think it’s a different conversation. I don’t really expect that to happen. Not only did they sign Jameis, but they extended him, and they gave him real money in a two-year extension. title: 4 takeaways from NY Giants OL Jon Runyan Jr.: An optimistic progress report
summary: The New York Giants are chugging along after five weeks of the regular season, most of which has not gone to plan. The Giants lost Jaxson Dart in Week 2 and have made it work with backup quarterback Jameis Winston, who has not lost in three starts with the team. Giants offensive lineman Jon Runyan […]
full_text: Jon Runyan (76) | Getty Images The New York Giants are chugging along after five weeks of the regular season, most of which has not gone to plan. The Giants lost Jaxson Dart in Week 2 and have made it work with backup quarterback Jameis Winston, who has not lost in three starts with the team. Giants offensive lineman Jon Runyan Jr. explained what it’s like to play with Winston. “This kind of outgoing personality, you see it all over social media. Especially how well he was documented throughout the summertime with the FIFA World Cup,” Runyan Jr. said. “That is one part of the kind of person he is, but he’s not like that all the time. In meetings, out in the field, he is serious, all about business. I don’t really ever see him cracking any jokes. I don’t see him cracking a smile. He is locked in, focused. He understands that he has the keys to this offense. And I think he knows how good of a team we can be, and I think he understands that.” Giants responding well to adversity The Giants have lost Dart outside linebacker Brian Burns and wide receiver Jack Braxton Barrios, among others, to season-ending injuries. Still, the Giants remain in first place in the NFC East. Runyan credited the coaching staff for keeping this team on track. “Yeah, I think it says a lot about not only our coaching staff, what they’ve kind of tried to build throughout the whole offseason program and into training camp. It says a lot about them, the foundation that they’ve built, and a lot of us as players, we’re sitting 3-1-1 right now,” Runyan Jr. said. ”A couple plays here and there, I feel like we could also be 1-4. I still feel like we have a long way to go on this team. Luckily, we are 3-1-1 at the moment. And like I said, we still have a long way to go. This whole division stacks up how it does, as long as we take care of what we got, like we got the Saints coming in this week. (Head) Coach (John) Harbaugh has been saying go 1-0 every week, and that’s kind of been our mindset, and it’s been working so far this year.“ Andrew Thomas anchoring the o-line Andrew Thomas is playing through a groin injury that is obviously making things difficult for him. His teammates have noticed, and appreciate the big man. “He’s just a warrior out there. I do see him looking like he’s laboring here and there, but he won’t show it on his face. He’s just going to keep working, keep his mouth shut, and keep playing,” Runyan Jr. said. “And that’s just the kind of person and player he is. And it’s really awesome to watch. He’s definitely the lead by example guy of our entire, I could say entire offense, but definitely the offensive line. And he’s definitely the glue that holds us all together, having such a good, dominant player that he is for a very long time.” Open communication with coaches Bringing in head coach John Harbaugh and his staff have done wonders for the Giants. They may be winning these games ugly, but the process in which they are coming together week in and week out is a much-needed change for the team. “There’s a pretty open line of communication there that guys in the group setting get to see that accountability in real time. And then coaches holding the players, and the players holding the coaches accountable to mistakes that they both feel that could be fixed, that would help the team going down the road,” Runyan Jr. said. “So, there’s been a, I feel like in my opinion, really good communication back and forth between players and coaches that is only going to help us when we get further down the road in the season. And especially going to be helpful when we face a little bit more adversity, knowing that we have that solid foundation with everybody around us.” Runyan and the Giants are taking on the New Orleans Saints in their Week 6 matchup. Kickoff is scheduled for Sunday at 1 p.m. ET inside MetLife Stadium. Fans can watch the game on FOX or stream it on the FOX One app.

summary: No. 1 — San Francisco 49ers (5-0) | SAME The 49ers keep rolling after an impressive road win in Seattle. full_text: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan. | Getty Images No. 1 — San Francisco 49ers (5-0) | SAME The 49ers keep rolling after an impressive road win in Seattle. Mike Evans went OFF, catching seven passes for 113 yards and a touchdown while battling through rib injuries. His addition has provided the Kyle Shanahan offense with a much-needed outside threat who is playing unreal late in his career. The defense forced four turnovers, as the 49ers continue to dominate. No. 2 —Buffalo Bills (4-1) | SAME The New England Patriots came to play! The Bills’ defense surrendered 405 yards in the game, but a late Josh Allen interception, followed by a 12-yard Hunter Henry catch on third-and-10, secured the victory for New England. The 49ers jump the Bills here, but Buffalo is still a top-three team in the NFL. No. 3 — Kansas City Chiefs (4-0) | 📉 1 spot The Chiefs were on their BYE, but still have persistent questions about their weapons on offense after the injury to Tyquon Thornton last week. Still, they’re finding ways to win, have Patrick Mahomes, and Steve Spagnuolo’s defense is playing well. No. 4 — Minnesota Vikings (5-0) | (6th) 📈 1 spot The Vikings defense continues to be elite. They held the Saints to 142 yards and Tyler Shough to 96 passing yards. Aaron Jones rushed for 113 yards and a touchdown on 25 carries, while Kyler Murray threw for 211 yards with a dime to Justin Jefferson. The Vikings offense is getting by, but the defense has carried them to an undefeated record through five weeks. No. 5 — Los Angeles Rams (2-3) | SAME The Rams lost a heartbreaker in overtime, 37-34. Josh Allen did Josh Allen things at the end of the game. Both Allen and James Cook rushed for over 100 yards in the game. Matt Stafford threw for 383 yards and three touchdowns, while Puka Nacua caught 17 balls for 138 yards. Rams have three losses, but they’re still a top team in the NFL. No. 6 — Seattle Seahawks (3-2) | (3rd) 📉 3 spots Seattle turned the football over four times against the 49ers, who were all over Sam Darnold. Seattle could not stop Mike Evans. Sure, Seattle has two losses, but they’re still a top team in the league. No. 7 — Jacksonville Jaguars (4-1) | (8th) 📈 1 spots Cam Little’s last-second field goal let Jacksonville steal a win in London, where they’ll play the Texans next week. Parker Washington played very well in the win and was the solution for Liam Coen’s offense against an Eagles offense that has no identity. No. 8 —Baltimore Ravens (4-1) | (9th) 📈 1 spot Baltimore closed out a tight game with a nice comeback win over the Atlanta Falcons. Tyler Huntley did what he had to in the 30-23 victory. Baltimore should be receiving Lamar Jackson back either this week or the next. No. 9 — New England Patriots (3-2) | (14th) 📈 5 spots New England is back?! The Patriots destroyed the Las Vegas Raiders at home, 45-17, which likely made Josh McDaniels smile. Drake Maye threw for 374 yards in the win. The Patriots defense SHUT down the Raiders’ rushing attack and has stabilized over the past two weeks. No. 10 — Chicago Bears (3-2) | (7th) 📉 3 spots The Bears were embarrassed by the Green Bay Packers, 31-7. It was bad; Tyson Bagent couldn’t do much offensively, but it was the Chicago defense that could NOT stop Jordan Love and the Packers’ passing offense. Case Keenum moved the offense a bit, but it wasn’t enough. A game to forget for the Bears, but it sets up well for the rematch between Matt LaFleur and Ben Johnson in Week 16. No. 11 — Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) | (12th) 📈 1 spot The Bengals escaped Miami with a 31-24 win. Miami scored two fourth-quarter touchdowns, which made the game look more respectable, but it was Joe Burrow who threw four touchdowns, despite just 190 total yards on 23 completions. Miami did, however, gain 331 total yards and turned the football over three times, while rushing for 217 total yards, 74 of which were by quarterback Malik Willis. No. 12— Detroit Lions (3-2) | (16th) 📈4 spots Detroit dropped 45 on the Cardinals in the desert, beating Arizona 45-21. Jahmyr Gibbs rushed for 151 yards on 25 carries and two touchdowns, and the Lions offense looked like what we’re used to seeing. Jared Goff added three passing touchdowns. No. 13 — Carolina Panthers (2-2) | (15th) 📈 1 spot Carolina was on a BYE, but moved up one spot in the rankings! No. 14 — Pittsburgh Steelers (3-2) | (20th) 📈 6 spots The Pittsburgh Steelers established the run well with Jaylen Warren, who had 101 yards on 15 carries with a touchdown. Aaron Rodgers threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns in the Steelers’ 34-22 win against the Colts. No. 15 — Denver Broncos (3-2) | (13th ) 📉 2 spots The Broncos won a divisional matchup on the road against the Los Angeles Chargers, but their offense still doesn’t look right under Sean Payton. Their defense is a top unit in the league, but Bo Nix and the offense have struggled. Denver had 224 total yards, with Nix throwing for just 123 yards. Still, a win is a win. No. 16 — Las Vegas Raiders (3-2) | (11th) 📉 5 spots The Raiders were embarrassed by the Patriots and not much went right for Kirk Cousins and Klint Kubiak. We did see, however, Fernando Mendoza, who went 6 of 8 for 48 yards in garbage time. Las Vegas did nothing on the ground against this Patriots front; Asthon Jeanty had 27 yards on 10 carries. No. 17 — Green Bay Packers (3-2) | (26th) 📈 9 spots The Packers have three wins despite this season going TERRIBLY so far. But, WOW, did the Packers’ offense turn on against the Bears’ defense: a 31-7 win where Jordan Love threw for 367 yards and two touchdowns. MarShawn Lynch rushed for a pair of touchdowns as well, while only averaging 3.1 yards per carry. No. 18 — New York Giants (3-1-1) | 📈 1 spot The Giants tied the Washington Commanders, 27-27, and they had the win in their hands but missed a field goal and fumbled it away; but the Commanders also did not want to win the football game, which led to one of the wilder endings I’ve ever covered. The Giants may look to spread things out and operate out of the shotgun with Jameis Winston, for it’s obvious he’s more comfortable letting it sling, rather than operating a heavy play action passing attack that can’t run the ball anyway. No. 19 — Atlanta Falcons (2-3) | (17th) 📉 2 spots Atlanta lost in overtime at home to a backup quarterback — not ideal! Still, the Ravens are a well-coached team, and perhaps the game ends differently if Tua Tagovailoa wasn’t forced into action. Michael Penix Jr. perhaps doesn’t throw the game-sealing interception. Still, Atlanta lost the game, but they’re better than their 2-3 record would suggest. No. 20 — Dallas Cowboys (2-3) | (10th) 📉 10 spots Dallas was beaten by a backup quarterback on Thursday Night Football. The Buccaneers dominated for much of the game, despite a late push by Dak Prescott. The final score was 24-16; Christian Parker’s defense has been an abject disaster, as Bucky Irving rumbled for 165 yards and a touchdown on the ground. No. 21 — Houston Texans (1-4) | (23rd) 📈 2 spots The Texans beat up on the Tennessee Titans, 26-3. C.J. Stroud threw for 261 yards and a touchdown, but the Texans lost David Montgomery to an injury in the game. I don’t like having the Texans this high, but, like the Falcons, they’ve underperformed and failed to finish close games against solid opponents earlier in the season. No. 22 — Cleveland Browns (3-2) | (18th) 📉 4 spots The Cleveland Browns fell to the Jets, 17-12, at MetLife Stadium. Braelon Allen ran for 116 yards and a touchdown in the game, as Garrett Wilson caught seven passes for 104 yards with a score against the Browns, who could not get much going on offense. No. 23 — Philadelphia Eagles (2-3) | (22nd) 📉 1 spot The Eagles are a mess offensively, as they lost in a last-second field goal against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Even though the Eagles are beat up on the offensive line, they’re trading Pro Bowl offensive linemen. Still, their defense is a solid unit, but the team is lost right now. No. 24 — Indianapolis…

title: The NY Giants may need to change how they think about offense
summary: The New York Giants are 3-1-1 despite the Week 2 season-ending injury to starting quarterback Jaxson Dart. That injury brought veteran Jameis Winston onto the field and he became the Giants’ full-time starting quarterback the next week against the Tennessee Titans. Since then, the Giants are 2-0-1, but each time have secured those outcomes by […]
full_text: New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston throws a pass. | Getty Images The New York Giants are 3-1-1 despite the Week 2 season-ending injury to starting quarterback Jaxson Dart. That injury brought veteran Jameis Winston onto the field and he became the Giants’ full-time starting quarterback the next week against the Tennessee Titans. Since then, the Giants are 2-0-1, but each time have secured those outcomes by the skin of their teeth. Big Blue might be more aptly nicknamed “Code Blue” this season, as they’re waiting until a critical moment to steal a favorable outcome from the jaws of defeat. Part of the problem seems to be an identity crisis on offense. Before I continue, I do want to extend some grace to the Giants’ offense. They’re going through the process of tailoring the offense to Jameis Winston’s preferences and skill set, much as they did with Dart over the summer. To remind those who forgot, all reports had the Giants’ offense as being just bad those early weeks at Greenbrier. At the time, they were going through the process of installing the entire playbook, then paring it back to what Dart executed the best. While I can’t say definitively, I do suspect that the coaching staff is going through that process again, but doing so in full view of the world and while also preparing for a new opponent each week. Likewise, the weather conditions have been difficult in each of the last three weeks. So I want to be as patient and understanding as possible. Recognizing the problem The Giants need to be realistic about the world in which they now live. They desperately want a power running game to be the foundation of their offense. The problem is that the Giants’ running game has just been bad since the loss of Dart. The Giants’ running backs have averaged just 3.49 yards per carry over the last three games, with zero touchdowns and three fumbles. That is simply not winning football, to the point where the failure to produce combined with the philosophic focus on the run game is actively harming the team. Against the Tennessee Titans, the Giants’ had a success rate of just 55% on series that started with a run. That is, the percent of series that picked up a first down or ended in a touchdown. Starting series with passes were much more effective and generally led to favorable outcomes. All rushing plays averaged -0.15 EPA per play (in other words, each run made it less likely that the Giants would score on the next play), with their early runs (on first and second down) had a -0.17 EPA per play. Late runs were actually useful at 0.26 EPA per play, however. The next week against the Cardinals, the rush continued to hurt the Giants. They didn’t have any good options for starting drives, but the run was still the worse option. Early runs in that game averaged a putrid -0.37 EPA per play with a 19 percent success rate, while runs on third and fourth down also hurt the offense with a -0.54 EPA per play. The split was particularly lopsided this past week against the Commanders. The Giants averaged -0.40 EPA per play on all running plays, while their 1st and 2nd down runs had a -0.52 EPA per play and a 19 percent success rate. Their late runs did have a 0.14 EPA per play, but that doesn’t really outweight negatives of early down runs. All passing plays had a 0.29 EPA per play, with a modest 0.04 EPA per play on early passes and a great 0.99 EPA per play on late passes. It is worth noting that the Giants threw far more against Washington than they did against Tennessee and Arizona. The Giants ran 36 times to 27 passing plays against Tennessee and had 30 runs with 37 passing plays against Arizona. Compare that to 65 passing plays and just 25 running plays against the Commanders. The weather likely impacted how the Giants called the games, as well as their need to mount a furious comeback against the Commanders. That said, we also know how John Harbaugh wants an offense to operate. He wants his teams to be tough, physical, and run-first with an emphasis on the power run game. That much is absolutely plain to see when we look at how often the Giants throw the ball on neutral downs. Their 48.7% pass rate on neutral downs (first and second downs, prior to the two-minute warning, and outside of garbage time) is the fourth-lowest rate in the NFL. The problem is that despite having the fourth-highest run rate on neutral downs, the Giants’ -0.2.18 EPA per play on neutral-down runs is among the worst in the NFL. The Giants’ EPA on dropbacks, meanwhile, is 12th in the NFL at 0.141 per play — just between the Bengals and Packers. But why, though? There have been plenty of theories tossed out as to why the Giants’ running game has struggled since Dart went down. Is it based too much on the threat of the quarterback run? Is the offensive line just regressing and blocking poorly? Are the running backs too slow? I would posit that each of those plays a role, but also that the Giants’ coaching staff isn’t doing the players any favors. As noted above, the Giants’ tendencies are pretty apparent from both tape and charting. They want to run the ball, and if they line up on a neutral down, odds are that it’s going to be a running play. And if the defense has a good idea of what’s coming, the offense needs excellent play design, excellent execution, or both to be successful. For instance, fullback Patrick Ricard was on the field for 22 plays against the Commanders, two of which were penalties. Of the remaining 20 plays, 12 of them were runs and 10 of those were between the tackles. The Giants had a strong tendency to play out of condensed sets, and then run between the tackles into the teeth of the defense. The Giants bring both Ricard and Aaron Stinnie onto the field for a first down run at the start of a drive, as well as tight end Chris Manhertz and wide receiver Malachi Fields. This is a clear signal to the defense that the Giants intend to run the ball and they respond with a true “Base” personnel package. Furthermore, the Giants align Stinnie on the play-side to start, which pulls the bulk of the Commanders’ defense to the strong side of the offense. At the time of the handoff, the Giants had seven blockers with on the play-side to eight defenders. That automatically puts the Giants at a numbers disadvantage at the point of attack. The Giants do try to manipulate the Commanders’ defense by putting Ricard in motion and pulling Sisi Mauigoa. Unfortunately, that simply causes the defense to shift back to their original alignment while Jon Runyan Jr. gets tripped up in the trash trying to work to the second level. That delays his block and effectively leads to Sisi having to block three defenders at the point of attack. Using motion and pulling blockers is almost always a good idea and something the Giants did to great effect in Week 1. However, here — and far too often over the last three weeks — their play selection and design made it too easy for the Commanders’ defense and too hard on the Giants’ offense. Overall, Cam Skattebo ran the ball 13 times and Najee Harris carried the ball 5 times. In each case, most of their carries came in heavy, condensed formations. However, their best carries came when the Giants spread their formation out. In fact, Skattebo’s 19-yard run and 9-yard run both came when the Giants used 11-personnel and wider formations to lighten the box an force Washington to defend more field. What to do now? Quite simply, the Giants need to open their offense up, they need to lean into the pass, and they need to help their players. I want to make it clear that I don’t think the Giants need to turn into the Cowboys and throw 40 times per game. However, it’s clear that despite Jameis Winston’s history of turnovers and the Giants having a razor-thin depth chart at wide receiver, passing is their better option right now. Even with the interceptions (the first of which I’d chalk up to a great defensive play more than “Jameis gonna Jameis”), Winston was…

title: NY Giants news: Giants open as underdogs, Jameis Winston should be the quarterback, more
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know for the NFC East- leading New York Football Giants. Why the Giants’ tie with the Commanders proved they’re finally different | SNY.tv For the Giants, though, it’s hard not to err more on the side of optimism. They are not Super […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know for the NFC East- leading New York Football Giants. Why the Giants’ tie with the Commanders proved they’re finally different | SNY.tv For the Giants, though, it’s hard not to err more on the side of optimism. They are not Super Bowl contenders. They are not ready to run away with the wide-open NFC East. They have their flaws. But it’s very clear, through the first five weeks, they aren’t the team they’ve been the past few years. That’s truly all that matters. Compare these Giants to the ones run by Brian Daboll … or Joe Judge … or Pat Shurmur … or Ben McAdoo and there are so many ways this game never reaches its tied conclusion. The Giants were not a team built to handle adversity — it suffocated them in painstaking fashion like a plague. Time and time and time again. But these Giants are different. A month-plus of football is enough a sample size to state that. Abdul Carter continues to be a difference-maker Abdul Carter highlights from the WEEK 5 TIE pic.twitter.com/hrdMtm4eb6 — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) October 12, 2026 How grit and mental toughness of John Harbaugh’s Giants showed up again | The Record Given the circumstances, the New York Giants will take their 27-27 overtime tie with the Washington Commanders from a wet and wacky Sunday afternoon in Maryland with appreciation for the big picture impact on the season. Week 5 was a disaster for the NFC East. Which team is down the worst? | The Athletic The good news? It’s over. What’s one other reason to be optimistic coming out of the Week 5 fiasco? Carroll: That the Giants even got to the point that this game could become a fiasco is impressive. As we’ve seen over the last few weeks, this is a team that will not quit and has pulled off late-game defensive stands to seal victories. Sunday, it was Winston who turned up the heat and mounted a 14-point comeback to tie the game. Winston’s play can be erratic, but he put on a show and became the only Giant since 1950 to amass 300-plus passing yards, three-plus passing touchdowns and 25-plus rushing yards in the same game. The other big plus coming out of Sunday’s game was the play of New York’s top pass catchers: tight end Isaiah Likely (11 catches, 94 yards, two touchdowns) and receiver Malik Nabers (11 catches, 121 yards, one TD). The two are huge focal points of the offense, so to see them get more involved, especially in big moments, will be crucial for this offense going forward. Seismic defensive pivot on full display | New York Post It is perfectly understandable to not know how to feel if you were pulling for the Giants coming out of the bizarre 27-27 tie with the Commanders. There is no doubt the Giants, after staging a strong, resilient comeback from down 14 points in the fourth quarter, wasted an opportunity to gain their first road victory of the season. QB Report Cards for 2026 NFL Week 5 | Bleacher Report Everyone understands that Jameis Winston can sling the ball all over the yard. Everyone also understands he could implode at any moment and make a gut-wrenching mistake. Instead of eating a second-quarter sack, Winston tried to make something happen against the Washington Commanders and fumbled the ball. From that point forward, he led the New York Giants on seven drives that should have ended in points (not including a kneel-down at end of regulation). However, two missed field goals and a Cam Skattebo fumble prevented that from happening. “It’s just a whole bunch of stuff that people want to talk about as bad, but like, bro, the good outweighs the bad,” said running back Tyrone Tracy Jr..”It overwhelms the bad. So, you have to continue just to keep talking Jameis up, man. Keep talking Jameis up because like, people want to bench him, people want to talk bad about him. But like, at the end of the day, man, that boy is a hooper. He goes out there and plays ball.” Grade: B Tiki on advice he gave to Skattebo Tiki says Cam Skattebo's mindset has to change if he wants to fix his fumbling issues: pic.twitter.com/H2mccpsMPE — WFAN Sports Radio (@WFAN660) October 12, 2026 New York Giants have a ball security problem and that’s, well… A problem | USAToday.com The fumble fit a broader pattern the coaching staff has emphasized. Harbaugh acknowledged that ball security has not yet reached an unacceptable threshold, but the group must continue pursuing improvement rather than accepting current results. “Gotta keep chasing it. I mean, that’s the thing. You just can’t throw your hands up and say, ‘Well, we’re just not good at it.’ We have to believe in our players,” Harbaugh said. “We understand that at some point in time, it becomes unacceptable, but we’re not there yet. We’ve got guys that want to do the right thing, and we have to, as a team, as an offense, we have to get to the point where we protect the football.” NFL Week 5: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday’s games | ESPN.com Trend to watch: After posting less than 100 rushing yards against the Cardinals last week, Cam Skattebo, Najee Harris and Tyrone Tracy Jr. combined for 21 yards on 11 carries in the first half vs. Washington. The RBs also combined for 1.9 yards per catch in first half. Skattebo then had a crucial fumble with less than two minutes remaining in overtime when the Giants were in field-goal range. title: The Jets need to rethink their tight end approach
summary: Kenyon Sadiq was placed in the concussion protocol during the third quarter of the Jets’ Week 5 win over the Cleveland Browns. The rookie tight end finished the game with only 13 snaps, 8 of which came on passing plays. Naturally you might look at that playing time and assume it was the result of […]
full_text: New York Jets tight end Kenyon Sadiq (16) tries to get past Tennessee Titans linebacker Anthony Hill Jr. (53) and linebacker Cody Barton (50) during the third quarter at Nissan Stadium in Nashville, Tenn., Sunday, Sept. 13, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Kenyon Sadiq was placed in the concussion protocol during the third quarter of the Jets’ Week 5 win over the Cleveland Browns. The rookie tight end finished the game with only 13 snaps, 8 of which came on passing plays. Naturally you might look at that playing time and assume it was the result of leaving the game early with an injury. I went back, though, and looked at how the Jets allocated playing time at the position prior to Sadiq exiting the game with just under 6:00 to go in the third quarter. These are the snap totals up to that point. Mason Taylor 21 Jeremy Ruckert 13 Kenyon Sadiq 13 And the number of snaps on passing plays prior to Sadiq’s exit go as follows. Mason Taylor 15 Kenyon Sadiq 8 Jeremy Ruckert 6 I like to think that I am capable of offering detailed analysis on this site, but some things are pretty obvious. Kenyon Sadiq is far and away the Jets’ biggest threat at the tight end position. Two weeks ago against the Detroit Lions he went over 100 receiving yards. It’s difficult to comprehend the Jets giving more snaps total and in the passing game to Mason Taylor. It’s just as difficult to comprehend giving Jeremy Ruckert an equal share. I don’t know how to dive deeper into this other than to say Sadiq’s total snap share and share of snaps on passing plays should be appreciably higher than the other two under normal circumstances. In a situation where this team is playing without two of its three starting wide receivers, using Sadiq so little at the expense of the other two is baffling.

title: NFL Power Rankings: Week 6 Edition
summary: Now that Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season is in the books, it’s time for an incredibly meaningful and serious exercise: NFL Power Rankings! What differentiates these rankings from all others is that they’re THE only truly accurate ones in the entire universe. Hard to believe, I know. But it’s true. Let’s take a […]
full_text: London, United Kingdom - October 11: Jordan Mailata of Philadelphia Eagles looks on during the NFL match between Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 11, 2026 in London, United Kingdom. (Photo by Vince Mignott/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images Now that Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season is in the books, it’s time for an incredibly meaningful and serious exercise: NFL Power Rankings ! What differentiates these rankings from all others is that they’re THE only truly accurate ones in the entire universe. Hard to believe, I know. But it’s true. Let’s take a look at how all 32 teams stack up. BLG’S WEEK 6 NFL POWER RANKINGS 1 – Kansas City Chiefs (Last Week: 1) – The Chiefs return from their bye to host the winless Chargers on Sunday. Andy Reid is 22-5 directly after the bye. 2 – San Francisco 49ers (LW: 2) – Brock Purdy (+300) has moved slightly behind Josh Allen (+250) in MVP odds with the Niners picking up a big win over an NFC West rival. They’re the top dog in the conference in addition to their division. 3 – Seattle Seahawks (LW: 3) – There’s no major shame in narrowly losing to this 49ers team. Especially if they can quickly bounce back with a win over Denver on Thursday night. 4 – Baltimore Ravens (LW: 4) – The Ravens entered Week 5 as 3.5-point road underdogs with Lamar Jackson out … and beat Atlanta in overtime. Gutsy effort to keep them alive for the top spot in the AFC. 5 – Buffalo Bills (LW: 5) – Josh Allen finished 15 yards shy of setting a new single-game rushing total as he ran over the Rams’ defense for a big overtime win. 6 – Minnesota Vikings (LW: 6) – Despite the fact that their offense isn’t very good, the Vikings keep winning. Of course, it helps that they’ve faced one of the easier schedules in the league. Moving forward, Minnesota has the NFL’s toughest remaining strength of schedule. 7 – Chicago Bears (LW: 7) – The Bears got blown out … but it was their first loss since Caleb Williams hasn’t been able to start. And it sounds like he could return in Week 6. So, I think the Bears will be just fine. 8 – Los Angeles Rams (LW: 8) – People like to clown on the Rams for starting 2-3 because they were the preseason favorite. They’re surely frauds, right? Unfortunately, that’s not the case. If it was, they wouldn’t still be favored to win the Super Bowl. Comparing the Eagles and Rams because they're both 2-3 is pretty wild to me. Rams have faced the 2nd-toughest schedule so far and have the 4th-easiest remaining schedule. Eagles have faced the 10th-easiest schedule and have the 16th-easiest remaining schedule. Moreover: pic.twitter.com/LdHwmZ7MP4 — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) October 13, 2026 9 – Jacksonville Jaguars (LW: 10) – The Jags narrowly pulled out a win over the Eagles in London. They’re sitting pretty at 4-1 in the AFC South with the next closest team being the 2-3 Colts. Jacksonville has the NFL’s easiest remaining strength of schedule in no small part due to their division being pretty bad. 10 – Detroit Lions (LW: 12) – The Lions’ defense continues to be suspect but that offense sure can cook. 11 – Cincinnati Bengals (LW: 13) – The Bengals picked up a free win by beating the worst team in the NFL. 12 – New England Patriots (LW: 14) – Burying Drake Maye after the Pats’ blowout loss to the Jags was premature; he has seven touchdown passes to one interception over the past two weeks. And it sounds like A.J. Brown will be back soon. 13 – Las Vegas Raiders (LW: 11) – The Raiders have lost two in a row following their 3-0 start. And now they have the Bills and Rams next. They’re clearly in danger of dropping below .500. 14 – Dallas Cowboys (LW: 9) – Dallas entered Week 5 as 9.5-point home favorites against an undrafted rookie quarterback making his first career road start … on a short week. The Cowboys lost by eight points. One way to describe that performance? Embarrassing . 15 – Denver Broncos (LW: 16) – The Broncos beat a winless Bolts team. 16 – Carolina Panthers (LW: 18) – The Panthers return from their bye to play the Eagles, who’ve lost three straight, in Philly. They’ll have a significant rest advantage in this matchup with their opponent coming off international travel from London. 17 – New York Giants (LW: 17) – If you told Giants fans before the season that they’d only lose one of their first five games … while Jaxson Dart suffers a season-ending injury … I’m pretty sure they would’ve signed up for that! While they’re not a threat to contend for a Super Bowl this season, they’re at least giving their fans some excitement, which they’ve been starved of for a long time now. 18 – Green Bay Packers (LW: 23) – It looked like the Packers were in pretty rough shape after losing that Thursday night game to Atlanta while at home. Since then, they’ve bounced back with two wins, including a blowout over the Bears. Maybe they’re righting the ship. 19 – Philadelphia Eagles (LW: 15) – I feel like I’m lower on the 2026 Eagles than my ranking would suggest here. They’re benefiting from the benefit of the doubt I was giving them earlier in the season. While I do think there’s hope for defensive improvement, the offense stinks so bad. Overall, it’s a weird team. They’re not far off from being 4-1 but they’re also pretty close to being 0-5. 20 – Atlanta Falcons (LW: 19) – The Falcons with Michael Penix? Intriguing. The Falcons with Tua Tagovailoa? No thanks! 21 – New Orleans Saints (LW: 20) – Remember when it seemed like the Saints might be on the rise? Well, now they’re at the bottom of the NFC South. And only above Arizona in the NFC playoff picture. 22 – Pittsburgh Steelers (LW: 24) – The Steelers are going to keep their non-losing season streak going, aren’t they? 23 – Indianapolis Colts (LW: 21) – No one is taking the Colts seriously. 24 – Houston Texans (LW: 26) – The Texans are finally on the board with a win! Helped that they got to play the winless Titans. I’m not expecting the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade to work out for them. The precedent for high draft picks getting traded early into their careers isn’t encouraging. 25 – Tampa Bay Buccaneers (LW: 27) – Seems like Jalon Daniels can play a little bit? 26 – New York Jets (LW: 28) – It wasn’t pretty but the Jets beat a Browns team that had won three games in a row. That’s not nothing. 27 – Cleveland Browns (LW: 22) – Deshaun Watson turned in his worst game of the season. That’s a shame. 28 – Washington Commanders (LW: 25) – It’s rare that a single play should warrant a head coach getting fired. But Dan Quinn (and Jayden Daniels) botching that end of game scenario was unconscionable. The Commanders really ran the clock out on themselves in a spot where a win could’ve revived their season. Instead, they’re 1-3-1 overall and 0-2-1 in the division. Looking like a lost year. 29 – Arizona Cardinals (LW: 29) – 0-4 since Week 1 and three of those four losses were decided by more than one possession. They are who we thought they were. 30 – Los Angeles Chargers (LW: 30) – Turns out that Justin Herbert is not The Prince Who Was Promised. The Bolts are real bad and the losing will only continue. Next up for them: the Chiefs and the Rams. 31 – Tennessee Titans (LW: 31) – Cam Ward isn’t doing anything to prevent the Titans from taking a quarterback high in the 2027 NFL Draft. 32 – Miami Dolphins (LW: 32) – I’m beginning to think the Dolphins might not win the Super Bowl this season.

title: Eagles practice squad news: 2 players signed, 2 players cut
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced four practice squad transactions on Tuesday afternoon. Here’s an overview: Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. XAVIER TRUSS The 25-year-old Truss is a newcomer to the Eagles. He played college football at Georgia before going unpicked in the 2025 NFL Draft. Truss originally signed with the Denver […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - AUGUST 16: Xavier Truss #71 of the Denver Broncos looks to block against the Arizona Cardinals in the second half during the NFL Preseason 2025 game at Empower Field at Mile High on August 16, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced four practice squad transactions on Tuesday afternoon. Here’s an overview: OT Xavier Truss and DT Zion Wilson were signed to the practice squad. TE Josiah Deguara and CB Shaun Wade were released from the practice squad. Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. XAVIER TRUSS The 25-year-old Truss is a newcomer to the Eagles. He played college football at Georgia before going unpicked in the 2025 NFL Draft. Truss originally signed with the Denver Broncos before landing with the New Orleans Saints, where he logged zero offensive snaps and 30 special teams snaps last season. After being waived by the Saints during roster cuts, Truss joined the Cleveland Browns’ practice squad in mid-September. He was then cut last week. Here’s a look at Truss’ snap counts by position: 2026 (NFL preseason) — LG 48, RG 41 2025 (NFL preseason) — RT 65 2024 (college) — RT 656, RG 87, LG 2 2023 (college) — RT 424, LG 117, RG 61, LT 32 2022 (college) — LG 599, LT 1 2021 (college) — RG 185 2020 (college) — LT 60 2019 (college) — LT 44 As you can seen, Truss has experience at four of the five offensive line positions. That probably makes him a useful player to have for filling reps in practice settings. And should the Eagles’ offensive line situation get even more desperate, they could look to call him up a depth option. Pre-draft scouting report via NFL.com’s Lance Zierlein : Sixth-year senior who saw more reps at tackle but will need to play guard on the next level. Truss is tough but inconsistent. He’s adequate as a base blocker but lacks the core strength and body control to stay centered and connected over the rep. He moves well enough to play in space but only at an average level. Truss does a nice job of keeping rushers at the end of his punch and he scans for potential trouble in both of his gaps. Athletic limitations and a lack of bend could create anchor and recovery issues inside. Truss is a likely Day 3 selection with backup potential as a guard. ZION WILSON BGN’s Alexis Chassen previously wrote about Wilson’s return on Monday. I’ll just add that it’s nice to see him back in Philly after he showed some potential in the preseason. Curious that the Eagles didn’t look to add him back to the practice squad sooner. Or maybe they did and Wilson wanted to keep his options open. Also, not sure why the Eagles are looking to add more DT depth when they already have five on the roster and Gabe Hall on the practice squad. But, again, I like Wilson’s developmental potential. JOSIAH DEGUARA The Eagles signed Deguara back in mid-September after Eli Stowers was placed on injured reserve. The team temporarily elevated him for their Week 3 game against the Chicago Bears, where he logged zero offensive snaps and 21 special teams snaps. Now he’s gone. I wonder if the Eagles might opt to open Stowers’ 21-day practice window soon? He became eligible to return from injured reserve after Week 4. SHAUN WADE After spending training camp with the Eagles, Wade was released in late August. He returned to Philly on the practice squad in late September. But now the 28-year-old cornerback is gone again. title: NFL Trade Rumors: Howie Roseman shopping for starting caliber offensive lineman
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are in the market for a starting-caliber offensive lineman. This much should already be apparent from the team’s offensive line situation. This was the configuration they had to use in Week 5 due to Lane Johnson retiring and the Eagles trading Cam Jurgens away: Mailata and Steen (who got banged up on […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - DECEMBER 8: Philadelphia Eagles general manager Howie Roseman walks the field prior to the game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on December 8, 2025 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are in the market for a starting-caliber offensive lineman. This much should already be apparent from the team’s offensive line situation. This was the configuration they had to use in Week 5 due to Lane Johnson retiring and the Eagles trading Cam Jurgens away: Left tackle — Jordan Mailata Left guard — Willie Lampkin Center — Jake Majors Right guard — Tyler Steen Right tackle — Markel Bell Mailata and Steen (who got banged up on Sunday but returned to the game) are firmly entrenched as starters this season. Lampkin and Majors (who was called up from the practice squad) made their first NFL starters. The Eagles seem to like Bell’s long-term potential but growing pains are expected in the short-term. The extent Drew Kendall’s knee injury isn’t clear but the Eagles didn’t put him on injured reserve, so, he should be back sooner than later. He could return at center to replace Majors. But the Eagles might not just sit on their on hands when it comes to their offensive line. Speaking on his unCovering the Birds podcast last week, the Inquirer’s Jeff McLane saw Roseman has been making calls about blockers that might be available via trade, even after sending Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens: “I also think Roseman could reload at the position. A couple NFL sources told me he was shopping for a starting caliber offensive lineman as of Wednesday.” The Eagles lost a game since then, so, maybe Roseman is less inclined to buy if it’s a short-term rental. But perhaps that’s not the vision anyway. Maybe the Eagles’ general manager is looking to acquire a player with long-term starting capability. It’s not perfectly clear who might fit that description. It’s not like there’s an abundance of quality offensive linemen in the NFL. Something to monitor ahead of next month’s NFL trade deadline, though.

title: Eagles-Jaguars Film Review: This team isn’t going anywhere unless they fix the run game
summary: Ugh. Another week, another game where the Eagles’ offense found a way to make everything feel painfully difficult. There were some signs of life on the rewatch. I promise. But it was rough in places. Before getting into all of that, I was at the game, and it was freaking awesome. It was so loud, […]
full_text: Philadelphia Eagles' Dameon Pierce is tackled by Jacksonville Jaguars' Foyesade Oluokun during the NFL London Games match at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, London. Picture date: Sunday October 11, 2026. (Photo by Ben Whitley/PA Images via Getty Images) | PA Images via Getty Images Ugh. Another week, another game where the Eagles’ offense found a way to make everything feel painfully difficult. There were some signs of life on the rewatch. I promise. But it was rough in places. Before getting into all of that, I was at the game, and it was freaking awesome. It was so loud, and I had an absolute blast. Watching the Eagles in person is special, even when the football itself leaves you wanting to scream. I loved being there. Eagles fans are the absolute best, and the atmosphere was unbelievable. The Eagles finished with 22 rushing yards on 18 attempts. That is not a typo. Before the final drive, their second-half offense had produced 10 yards on 15 plays across four punts. You cannot keep asking the defense to survive that. The offensive line is dealing with a lot of change, but some of the assignments and calls made an already difficult situation even harder. The passing game was a little more interesting. Empty formations gave Jalen Hurts some clearer answers against pressure, and there were a couple of successful under-center play-action throws. Hurts also left opportunities on the field, particularly over the middle, so this wasn’t another game where I thought the quarterback had almost no chance. There was enough here to see a way forward. Offense Let’s start with the run game, because it kept dragging everything else down. I wrote in the preview that DaVon Hamilton is a very good nose tackle who is tough to move. With that in mind, why are you asking Willie Lampkin, a very small left guard making his first start, to block him on fourth-and-1? From shotgun? With your third-string running back? What part of that matchup makes you feel good about the call? Lampkin has to execute his assignment, of course, but the staff has to consider who it is asking him to move. This is a difficult matchup on any down. The Eagles were already short of their usual personnel. They needed to make life easier for the players available, and this did the opposite. The rushing numbers in this game are as bad as it gets. It was a total disaster. 12) There were moments in this game when I felt a tiny bit more confident about the pass game. However, there were still far too many bad calls. This drive included this call that I just don't get. What are they trying to get here? The spacing looks so awkward. Cooper might come… pic.twitter.com/Ye9joNnSAF — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 13, 2026 The under-center passing game still has its own recurring problem. The Eagles go into a condensed formation, try to get Hurts moving, and an unblocked defensive back appears in his face. Again. It is hard to develop a functioning play-action game when the quarterback faces a free rusher before the concept has a chance to develop. They need an answer for the cornerback blitz. Keep a tight end in to protect the edge. Give Hurts a quick throw into the space behind the blitzer. Widen the receivers so the cornerback has farther to travel and his intentions are easier to see. The best answer depends on the play and the defensive look, but something has to be built into the plan. This cannot keep happening every single week. I am not against getting Hurts outside the pocket. I am against repeatedly asking him to do it without accounting for the defender who keeps ruining the play. We did see some good under-center throws later, but that doesn’t make this recurring issue disappear. 2) The Eagles had a couple of nice plays from under center in this game, which we will get to later, but this was another failure. They still don't have an answer for the CB blitz. They can't successfully get Hurts on the move because they can't stop unblocked defenders appearing… pic.twitter.com/FwqRGboXzw — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 13, 2026 The shotgun running game has a different version of the same frustration. The Eagles keep leaving an edge defender unblocked and relying on the read to take him out of the play. That can work when the defender has to commit, and the quarterback keeps threatening him. But this is 2020. Modern-day edge defenders are so good at playing read-option runs. Josh Hines-Allen is far too good to simply assume that leaving him unblocked will remove him from the run fit. Modern edge defenders can play this slowly and still close on the back. Hurts barely keeps the ball anymore anyway, which makes it even easier for the defender to avoid committing too early. Whatever the reason for the lack of keeps, the staff has to account for how the play is actually being defended. The read is supposed to give the offense an advantage. The QB run game should give you +1 extra in the run game. But the Eagles are not using it. On a day when the team literally cannot run at all, and you don’t have ANY of your top 3 running backs, why wouldn’t you at least try to get the QB run game going?! I do not understand it! 3) The Eagles still seem to believe they can leave an edge defender unblocked. Modern edge defenders are very good at not overcommitting to the run early, so they can force the QB to hand it off and still make the tackle. Hurts barely keeps it anymore anyway, so these plays are… pic.twitter.com/n40e6Se7Aq — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 13, 2026 Thankfully, there were some plays where the Eagles actually had a plan for pressure this week! They used empty formations a lot, and I liked it. Spreading everyone out helped Hurts identify what the defense was doing and gave him an immediate place to go with the football. Here, Hurts gets the cornerback to show his hand before the snap and throws straight to Dontayvion Wicks, who turns around immediately. The receiver and quarterback are working together, the answer is available, and the ball comes out. Sometimes it really can be that simple. After watching so many plays where pressure seems to surprise the entire offense, it was good to see a coordinated response. Empty does not solve every protection issue, but this is the kind of straightforward answer the Eagles have been missing. 4) Hey, we did see the Eagles have a plan for some pressure in this game! That's a start! They went to Empty formations a lot to make it easier for Hurts and the offense, and it worked! Hurts gets the CB to show his hand pre-snap, then throws it right to Wicks, who turns around… pic.twitter.com/XCd35BNqsa — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 13, 2026 I have been very critical of the passing-game design since Week 2, but Hurts missed opportunities in this game. This is one of them. I counted 2 other plays where he should have thrown it. Wicks is available over the middle, and the ball needs to come out when Hurts hits his back foot. He can make this throw. We have seen him make it In fact, a couple of plays after this, he made a tougher throw to Wicks over the middle of the field. The difference? That one was on 3rd down. Which is why I think Hurts turns down these throws at times. He’s too risk-averse, and we know that Nick Sirianni preaches winning the turnover battle, too. Hurts did not play badly overall, but he left a few plays out there. I thought there were two or three opportunities over the middle where he needed to be more willing to pull the trigger. It is fair to criticize the structure around him and still expect him to capitalize when that structure gives him an open receiver. This offense is too risk-averse at times, and Hurts is part of that. You cannot afford to pass up these opportunities when your run game is giving you almost nothing. The good news is that the opportunity existed. The frustrating part is that they did not take it. 5) I've been critical of the design of the passing game since Week 2, but there were opportunities for Hurts to pull the…

title: Jalyx Hunt injury update: Eagles pass rusher not expected to play in Week 6
summary: While the Philadelphia Eagles are potentially expecting some key players to return from injury this week, it sounds like they’ll be without at least one of their regular defensive starters against the Carolina Panthers. Jalyx Hunt is not expected to suit up against in Week 6 after suffering ankle/knee injuries on the final play of […]
full_text: London, United Kingdom - October 11: Jalyx Hunt of Philadelphia Eagles injured during the NFL match between Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 11, 2026 in London, United Kingdom. (Photo by Vince Mignott/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images While the Philadelphia Eagles are potentially expecting some key players to return from injury this week, it sounds like they’ll be without at least one of their regular defensive starters against the Carolina Panthers. Jalyx Hunt is not expected to suit up against in Week 6 after suffering ankle/knee injuries on the final play of the second quarter during the Eagles’ loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Vic Fangio had the following to say about Hunt on Tuesday morning: “I think it’ll be pretty miraculous for Jalyx to play this week.” “But he’s the kinda guy who will be pushing the envelope and making the medical people clear him. He’s not going to be one of those guys who’s hesitant to come back.” Sounds like he’ll avoid going on injured reserve, at least? Hunt, an offseason standout who’s yet to log a sack in 2026, leads the Eagles in quarterback hits with four. The Eagles’ pass rush as a whole has been lacking; Philadelphia ranks tied for the fourth-fewest sacks per game (1.2) this season. With Hunt expected not to play, the Eagles have four edge rushers who might suit up on Sunday: Jonathan Greenard, Nolan Smith, Arnold Ebiketie, and A.J. Epenesa. (The team also has Keyshawn James-Newby, Mason Reiger, and Joshua Weru on the practice squad.) It’s not yet clear if Greenard will be able to play after suffering an ankle injury in Week 4 that caused him to miss Week 5. He didn’t practice last week but he was ruled questionable and seemed to be a game-time decision before the team held him out. Fangio expressed hope that Greenard could be available but said the team will have to see how the veteran handles practice this week. Getting Greenard back would be ideal. If he’s not able to suit up, the Eagles are looking thin with Smith, Ebiketie, and Epenesa as their top trio. All of those players have game experience and it’s not like Fangio hasn’t used a three-man rotation before. But this team could really afford a spark on the edge that Greenard might be able to provide.

title: Vic Fangio confirms Eagles will rotate Jeremiah Trotter Jr. and Jihaad Campbell moving forward
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles entered Week 5 planning to make a change at off-ball linebacker. That plan went out of the window after Jeremiah Trotter Jr. was questionably ejected for an on-field fracas that took place during the game’s opening kickoff. As revealed by Zack Baun (via the Inquirer), the plan was to have Jihaad Campbell […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - OCTOBER 04: Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr. #54 reacts during the game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Los Angeles Rams on October 4th, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles entered Week 5 planning to make a change at off-ball linebacker. That plan went out of the window after Jeremiah Trotter Jr. was questionably ejected for an on-field fracas that took place during the game’s opening kickoff. As revealed by Zack Baun ( via the Inquirer ), the plan was to have Jihaad Campbell and Jeremiah Trotter Jr. rotate at the linebacker spot next to the Eagles’ All-Pro starter. There was also a curious mention on the game’s broadcast about Trot Jr. potentially starting the game. Speaking during his Tuesday morning press conference, Eagles defensive coordinator denied that was the case: “That is an out-and-out lie. Never said that.” Fangio did, however, confirm the Eagles’ plan to get Trotter more involved: “Yeah, we were going to play Trotter some.” There have been calls ( including here at Bleeding Green Nation ) for Trot Jr. to see more snaps with Campbell struggling this season as he also plays through a knee injury. Asked for his evaluation of Campbell’s most recent performance, Fangio replied: “Played OK. Played OK.” Fangio was asked about the impetus for the change. His answer: “Well, Trot played good in the start that he had when Zack [Baun] was out. It was a close. I just think he deserves playing time.” Fangio said the rotation will go “by series” as opposed to specific game situations. Fangio is typically not shy to put what he feels are his best players on the field, regardless of their status. He clearly didn’t want to play Bryce Huff, the Eagles’ first and most expensive offseason signing in 2024, despite the front office’s investment in him. Now Fangio is putting the Eagles’ first-round pick from the 2025 NFL Draft in a situation where he’s going to lose playing time to his backup. One can only wonder if it’s a matter of time before Trot Jr. fully takes over. Or perhaps it’ll truly be a time-share the rest of the way. We’ll see. I don’t disagree that Trot Jr. deserves more playing time; he’s good and he often knows where to be. But he does have some athletic limitations that have prevented him from earning a start job sooner. He also notably missed a key tackle on Kyren Williams that allowed the Los Angeles Rams to score the game-winning touchdown in Week 4. He’s not perfect. But there is intrigue to be had with his upside. And now we’ll be able to see how he fares with more playing time.

title: Christian Parker seems to be getting Sean Desai’d by the Cowboys
summary: You may have noticed that former Philadelphia Eagles passing game coordinator/defensive backs coach Christian Parker is off to a rough start as the Dallas Cowboys’ defensive coordinator. Here’s how the Cowboys’ defense ranks in a number of metrics exiting Week 5: Yikes. Given these struggles, the Cowboys are reportedly hiring a more experienced assistant to […]
full_text: Jul 29, 2026; Oxnard, CA, USA; Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker at training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect You may have noticed that former Philadelphia Eagles passing game coordinator/defensive backs coach Christian Parker is off to a rough start as the Dallas Cowboys’ defensive coordinator. Here’s how the Cowboys’ defense ranks in a number of metrics exiting Week 5: 31st in yards allowed per game (395.4) 26th in offensive points allowed per game (27.2) 32nd in EPA per play 32nd in success rate Yikes. Given these struggles, the Cowboys are reportedly hiring a more experienced assistant to pair with Parker as a first-time play-caller: Mike Pettine . And not only are they bringing the Bucks County, Pennsylvania native into the fold. But the Cowboys are also moving Parker from his normal role on the sideline to the booth . It’s hard to look at this setup and not think back to when the Eagles bizarrely decided to put Matt Patricia in charge of their defense mid-stream during the 2023 season, effectively demoting Sean Desai in the process without actually formally doing so. That setup ended up being an abject disaster for the Eagles, who historically collapsed at the end of that season. Maybe this approach will go better for the Cowboys given that Parker and Pettine actually have experience working together. Ed Werder offered some more insight on this move: The Cowboys are carefully representing the hiring of Pettine as someone who is here to support Christian Parker and offer advice based on his experience. But NFL coaches I’ve spoken to who know Pettine and the dynamics of the situation with the Cowboys believe the more influence and responsibility Pettine has, the better for the team. One HC who had Pettine on his staff: “They finally hired a real coach. Pettine is legit. Dallas will walk away with that division now.” But maybe not and we can all laugh at the Cowboys for being such a mess. If Parker does eventually end up getting canned by the Cowboys, which is the fate that Desai met after the 2023 season, it’ll be interesting to see what’s next for him. He had a lot of success in Philly as an assistant coach, which is what landed him his current job. There was some thought the Eagles viewed him as a potential Vic Fangio successor. But that may no longer be the case. Something to monitor!

title: Eagles News: The case for punting on the 2026 season
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! I happen to agree with BGN alumnus Jimmy Kempski’s assessment of the 2026 Eagles. This team is probably cooked. Sure, they’re not far off from being 4-1. And maybe they even win a bad NFC East. But they just haven’t played […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: (L-R) Head coach Nick Sirianni and executive vice president Howie Roseman of the Philadelphia Eagles talk prior to the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! I happen to agree with BGN alumnus Jimmy Kempski’s assessment of the 2026 Eagles. This team is probably cooked. Sure, they’re not far off from being 4-1. And maybe they even win a bad NFC East. But they just haven’t played very well on the whole, especially relative to other teams. This isn’t their year. And that’s OK! They’ve been on one of the most successful runs, if not THE most, in franchise history. Although it’s certainly disappointing, they’re allowed to have a bad year without it meaning doom and gloom for the franchise moving forward. I’m still pretty optimistic about the Eagles’ long-term future with Jeffrey Lurie and Howie Roseman at the helm. Expecting the Eagles to flat out tank isn’t realistic but the front office should absolutely be making decisions with more than the team’s 2026 outlook in mind. Taking a step back this year could position the Eagles very well in future seasons. It is indeed time for a reset. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … The Eagles should punt on the 2026 season, trade still-valuable players for future assets – PhillyVoice We’re only five weeks into the 2026 NFL season, but it is already crystal clear that it is not going to be a special one for the Philadelphia Eagles. More bluntly, if you’re a Birds fan, this season sucks. And, spoiler, it is only going to continue to suck. However, Howie Roseman and the Eagles are in a position to choose their suckage path the rest of the season. One is to try to compete for a division title in the craptastic NFC East, and if successful pretend that anything can happen in the playoffs. The other is to maximize the value on likely soon-to-be outgoing players, and reset the roster for another long-term run. One is to try to compete for a division title in the craptastic NFC East, and if successful pretend that anything can happen in the playoffs. The decision really shouldn’t be all that hard. They should choose the reset. Seven things Solak thinks entering NFL Week 6: Time for Mendoza? Cowboys issues? – ESPN I think … neither coach whose team committed end-of-game errors on Sunday will survive the season. […] Sirianni said after the game when asked about the touchback decision: “I didn’t make the right decision, and I lost us that game, and that’s what I said to our guys.” It echoes what he has said about the Eagles’ errant fourth-down decision-making over the past few games — passing on go-worthy fourth downs only to attempt more difficult ones later. The buck stops with him. He’s right, of course. And if the Eagles cannot hang the laurels of playcalling or coach development on Sirianni’s chest; if they can’t call him an elite mediator of disgruntled players; if they can’t expect him to maximize winning chances with fourth-down decisions or clock management … what do they ask of him? What does he bring to a team in transition — a team that’s wondering if it’s finally time to take its medicine and rebuild for a new era of contention? Eagles vs. Jaguars: 8 winners, 8 losers, 6 IDKs – BGN Sirianni is hardly the only coach who doesn’t ace game management. Look at Liam Coen! The Jags didn’t have a great day in that regard. But Coen provided value for his team with his contributions as an offensive mind. Sirianni isn’t bringing that to the table. Outside of player motivation, I’m not really sure what edge Sirianni is giving his team. Rather, he’s been a liability. And, make no mistake, he WILL be held accountable for the Eagles’ struggles if they continue. Especially as it relates to their offensive woes: NFC East Mixtape Vol. 197: The NFC Least is back! – NFC East Mixtape It only took five weeks into this NFL season, but the NFC Least is officially BACK! Despite two of the teams playing one another, not a single NFC East team won in Week 5. What’s more is that there were some particularly embarrassing moments. The Dallas Cowboys got destroyed by a winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers team while the Philadelphia Eagles blew a lead with 8 seconds in London against the Jacksonville Jaguars. The New York Giants might feel okay to have salvaged a tie, but they owe Jayden Daniels and Dan Quinn a huge thanks as that duo really let down the Washington Commanders. RJ Ochoa and Brandon Lee Gowton discuss it all! You can see that we have a BRAND NEW NFC East Mixtape YouTube Channel so make sure to subscribe as the show will live here exclusively in video format. AND you can also listen to the show! On Blogging The Boys and/or Bleeding Green Nation podcast feeds as well as the SB Nation NFL Show feed! NFL winners and losers: The NFC East has become football’s saddest division – SB Nation As a whole, the NFC East is a combined 8-10-2. Not the worst division on paper but it owns some of the most embarrassing losses in the NFL so far. Their collective schedules are only getting more difficult from here, and we could easily see three coaches get axed from the East before the season finishes — unless there’s some demonstrable improvement. This shouldn’t happen in the NFC East. Routinely, it’s one of the league’s better conferences, home to some of the richest rivalries, and with more trash talking than most of football combined. Instead of talking trash to each other, these teams can only point to how trash they have become. That would actually see the Panthers favored by less than a safety on a neutral field. It is clear that FanDuel doesn’t trust Bryce Young yet. Honestly, that’s kind of fair, but this still feels like a betting line weighted more on performance from past seasons for both teams than it is on the last four to five games of the 2026 season. 3 Numbers to Know From the Jaguars’ Win Over the Eagles – Big Cat Country 6%. That was Jacksonville’s win probability with eight seconds left in the game, per NFL Pro. Jake Elliot had just knocked through a 48-yard field goal to put the Eagles up by one point. If the Jaguars had any timeouts remaining, they might’ve been able to pick up a chunk completion before stopping the clock and attempting a lengthy walk-off field goal. But the Jaguars didn’t have any timeouts, and the Eagles made sure they’d have even less time by kicking off short of the endzone to prevent a touchback. Then Ameer Abdullah happened. title: Mike McCarthy explains why Steelers re-signed Elandon Roberts
summary: It was the surprise of roster cutdown day when the Pittsburgh Steelers parted ways with veteran inside linebacker Elandon Roberts. After signing late in camp and returning to the team following a season in Las Vegas, Roberts seemed like a sure bet to make the team. He didn’t.  The Steelers opted to keep seven defensive linemen […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) It was the surprise of roster cutdown day when the Pittsburgh Steelers parted ways with veteran inside linebacker Elandon Roberts. After signing late in camp and returning to the team following a season in Las Vegas, Roberts seemed like a sure bet to make the team. He didn’t. The Steelers opted to keep seven defensive linemen and four middle linebackers. Roberts was the odd man out, until now. Mike McCarthy confirmed during his weekly press conference on Monday that Roberts is rejoining the Steelers on the practice squad. “I enjoyed him in training camp. I thought he did a nice job,” McCarthy said . “I think the timing was a little bit to do with his opportunity… We’re trying to get better. He’s a veteran who has done great things throughout his career. This man just wants to win. Can’t have enough people like that.” Roberts, 32, played in the Steelers’ final two preseason games against the Jets and Bills, making four tackles in each. He spent the 2023 and 2024 seasons in Pittsburgh before playing in Patrick Graham’s defense during Graham’s final year as the defensive coordinator in Vegas. Roberts recorded 90 tackles, six tackles for loss, one pass defended, and one fumble recovery in 17 games (16 starts) with the Raiders. He registered 147 tackles, 15 tackles for loss, 10 quarterback hits, and 3.5 sacks in 33 games with the Steelers. The Steelers don’t have much depth behind Patrick Queen and Payton Wilson, especially with Carson Bruener’s primary role on special teams. “The tooth chipper” is a solid run defender, especially at the goal line, that can help a run defense that ranks tied for 13th in the league (103.4).
