title: Steelers Week 5 grades: Offense has most complete performance of the year
summary: Don’t look now, but the Pittsburgh Steelers’ offense is getting hot. They scored a season-high 34 points against the Indianapolis Colts, and are averaging just under 30 points over their last three games. As we do each week, Joey Bray and I will hand out grades for the previous game’s performances, so let’s get into […]
full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Don’t look now, but the Pittsburgh Steelers’ offense is getting hot. They scored a season-high 34 points against the Indianapolis Colts, and are averaging just under 30 points over their last three games. As we do each week, Joey Bray and I will hand out grades for the previous game’s performances, so let’s get into it. QB Aaron Rodgers Jarrett Bailey: Rodgers put up another solid performance against the Colts, finishing the day going 22-of-31 for 235 yards and three touchdowns. This marked his third straight game with three or more touchdown passes, tying a franchise record held by Terry Bradshaw and Ben Roethlisberger. He was decisive, he used the entire field, and he protected the ball – you can’t ask for much more than that. Grade: A- Joey Bray: Rodgers started this game with 11 consecutive completions. This game also marked the first time since December of 2021 that Rodgers has thrown for three or more touchdown passes in three consecutive contests. I was most impressed by how Rodgers moved around the pocket. The Colts’ pass rush is not very good, but Rodgers deserves some credit for the way he was able to maneuver the pocket in this one. You have to be impressed with the way Rodgers performed in this one. Grade: A RB Jaylen Warren Jarrett Bailey: Do you know who leads all running backs with at least 25 touches in total EPA over the last three weeks? Did you guess Jaylen Warren because the heading says Jaylen Warren and this is a Steelers site? Great job, you’re correct. Yes, Warren has been the most efficient running back with the ball in his hands for the last three weeks, and he had another career day against the Colts with 188 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns. He’s turning into a superstar in real time. Grade: A+ Joey Bray: The Steelers running back is third in the NFL in scrimmage yards at his position, behind only Bijan Robinson and Jahmyr Gibbs. This was the third consecutive game of over 100 scrimmage yards for Warren, who has been the Steelers’ best player this season. As we head into Week 6, Warren is averaging a whopping 5.9 yards per carry, behind only James Cook and Kenneth Walker. Warren’s efficiency this season has simply been out of this world. Grade: A+ Skill group Jarrett Bailey: It wasn’t the best day for DK Metcalf numbers wise (three catches, 12 yards) but he did have a key block on Jaylen Warren’s long touchdown reception. Germie Bernard also stepped in and caught six passes for 80 yards, while Pat Freiermuth added a pair of touchdowns. Overall, a strong day from the other skill players around Warren. Grade: B Joey Bray: Jaylen Warren was the best player on the field yesterday. Pat Freiermuth had a great game in which he scored a pair of touchdowns, moving him into a tie for the most receiving touchdowns by a tight end this season. Those performances alone carry this grade. The receiver room was lackluster, but was without Michael Pittman Jr., as well as Roman Wilson and Ben Skrownek who left with injuries in the first half. Germie Bernard led all receivers in yards and catches. Despite two early drops, the young receiver looked the part in his first real opportunity in the Steelers offense. With how Warren and Freiermuth played, it’s hard to be that upset with the lackluster receiver room. The Bernard performance was also encouraging, which certainly helps their case. Grade: A Offensive line Jarrett Bailey : Aaron Rodgers was the least pressured quarterback in the league in Week 5. After being sacked five times against the Browns, that’s a complete 180 from the unit. Warren’s big day on the ground was also sprung from huge run lanes opened up. Easily the best day the offensive line has had all year, and the best Steelers’ offensive line single week in recent memory. Grade: A+ Joey Bray: This young Steelers offensive line is bound to have some growing pains, as we saw against Cleveland. However, performances like the one they had yesterday against Indianapolis make you confident in the future of their group. Rodgers was only sacked once, and the offensive line gave Rodgers enough time to slowly maneuver through the pocket even when there was pressure. We already discussed just how efficient Warren was with his 6.7 yards per carry in the contest. It was an overall clean game from an offensive line that is starting to trend up. Grade: A+ Secondary Jarrett Bailey: The secondary still has a good bit to clean up. Jaquan Brisker got beat a couple times, and there still appears to be too many miscommunications that lead to chunk plays. That said, Asante Samuel Jr. had a pair of really nice pass breakups to prevent touchdowns, and it was a much better performance than the one we saw in Week 5. Grade: C+ Joey Bray: You know what? The secondary ended up doing better than I thought given how limited they were this week, although I’m not certain how much credit to give them considering Colts Daniel Jones was incredibly inaccurate throwing the ball down the field. Asante Samuel Jr. posted one of the better games of his Steelers career with four passes defended. This group certainly could use a boost, but looked the part against what was an overall mediocre Colts passing attack. Grade: C Run defense Jarrett Bailey: The biggest surprise of the week for me was how good the Steeler’s run defense was without Derrick Harmon. Credit to Yahya Black, Sebastian Joseph-Day, and Gabriel Rubio for stepping up in their increased roles on Sunday, as well as Cam Heyward and Keeanu Benton, of course. Jonathan Taylor totaled just 45 yards – that’s a good day at the office. Grade: A Joey Bray: No Derrick Harmon? No problem. The Steelers seem to have Jonathan Taylor’s number. The star running back amassed just 45 yards on the ground with his 15 carries. The Colts only rushed for 66 yards as a team. After giving up several rushes of over 20 yards last week against Cleveland, this was a resounding response from the run defense. Grade: A+ Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Steelers Week 6 power rankings roundup: Is Pittsburgh gaining respect?
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers got back on track with a huge win over the Indianapolis Colts, 34-22 in Week 5. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers tossed three touchdowns for the third consecutive game. Running back Jaylen Warren had a touchdown reception of 80 yards and a touchdown run of 50 yards in the contest. It was the third […]
full_text: (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers got back on track with a huge win over the Indianapolis Colts, 34-22 in Week 5. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers tossed three touchdowns for the third consecutive game. Running back Jaylen Warren had a touchdown reception of 80 yards and a touchdown run of 50 yards in the contest. It was the third straight game in which the star back had recorded over 100 scrimmage yards. Without further ado, it’s time for our weekly look around the internet to see where various media outlets place the Steelers among the rest of the NFL in this week’s power rankings roundup. FOX Sports: No.17 (No. 22 Last Week) “The Steelers are the most Jekyll and Hyde team in the NFL, which is why I have been all over the Power Rankings map with them. They are on a win-one, lose-one pace. But more than that, they seem to alternate between looking awful and looking terrific. They were back to mostly terrific against the Colts on Sunday. Aaron Rodgers had the offense humming, and he got a big-time performance from underrated RB Jaylen Warren, too.” – Ralph Vacchiano The Athletic: No.16 (No.20 last week) “Even if this season hasn’t gone exactly as Aaron Rodgers imagined (at least based on the moments of frustration between him and Mike McCarthy), Rodgers continues to climb the record books. In an impressive win over the Colts, Rodgers surpassed Peyton Manning for the third-most all-time touchdown passes, including the playoffs (582).” – Chad Graff and Josh Kendall CBS Sports: No.13 (No. 21 last week) “At 3-2, the offense showed some life against the Colts. The running game with Jaylen Warren really led them to victory.” – Pete Prisco Pro Football Talk: No.12 (No. 14 last week) The Steelers are in a three way tie for 12th on the PFT NFL power rankings with the Browns and Bengals. “They’re second in the list because they beat the Bengals.” – Mike Florio NFL.com: No.22 (No.25 last week) “Pittsburgh is becoming an every-other-week team, producing offensive explosions in odd-numbered weeks and struggling in even weeks. While that’s a path destined for a near-.500 record, perhaps Sunday’s output vs. Indianapolis was an example of a group recovering from a tough loss and applying the lessons learned. It was certainly encouraging to see the Steelers finally lean on Jaylen Warren. That’s a method that will produce consistent success, regardless of week number.” – Nick Shook Yahoo! Sports: No.17 (No. 21 last week) “Aaron Rodgers’ stat line isn’t perfect. His 59.8 completion percentage is the worst of his career as a starter. So is his 88.9 passer rating. But what he’s doing at his age has been approached only by Tom Brady.” “Not counting Brady, whose production in his 40s is an extreme outlier, no quarterback in his age-43 season (Rodgers turns 43 in December) has ever had more than 952 passing yards or six touchdowns in a season. Their teams combined for two wins in their starts, and both were from Vinny Testaverde in 2007. Testaverde had a bad 65.8 passer rating that season. Rodgers already has 1,234 yards, 10 touchdowns and the Steelers have won three of his starts, more than every other quarterback at his age combined, other than Brady.” “Whatever happens the rest of this season, Rodgers’ season is already historic for his age.” – Frank Schwab USA Today: No.17 (No.19 last week) “Maybe they need to rethink the timeshare approach with RB Jaylen Warren, who’s produced 490 yards from scrimmage on 61 touches over the past three weeks as the primary backfield option.” – Nate Davis ESPN: No.20 (No. 20 last week) “The Steelers’ secondary has been in flux since Joey Porter Jr. began the hold-in during training camp that ultimately ended with his trade to the Cowboys. As a result, the Steelers’ secondary has been plagued with inconsistent play and busted coverages. Porter’s absence and departure, coupled with Jamel Dean’s ankle injury, forced rookie Daylen Everette into more action. And Asante Samuel Jr. hasn’t replicated his training camp performance. At safety, starter DeShon Elliott unexpectedly began the season on IR while still recovering from his 2025 knee injury, and free agent acquisition Jaquan Brisker has underperformed. Rookie Robert Spears-Jennings has shown promise, but he’s still young” – Brooke Pryor Most media outlets seem to be catching on to what many Steelers fans already know, that being they’re a very week-to-week team. It truly is anyone’s guess what version of the Steelers shows up on any given Sunday. Although the Colts clearly have issues, Pittsburgh was able to comfortably beat them while their offense continued to show signs of growth. Perhaps the Steelers can earn more trust from us and the rest of the internet with a road win over undrafted free agent quarterback Jalon Daniels and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers this weekend. full_text: (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers are coming off an impressive victory over the Indianapolis Colts, despite the injuries to their wide receiver group. Jaylen Warren is performing as a top-five running back in the NFL, and the workhorse role should continue, even with the return of Rico Dowdle. Germie Bernard stepped into an expanded role and delivered for the offense. The AFC North is shaping up to be a dogfight until the bitter end, with all four teams above .500. The Ravens sit on top at 4-1, and the other three teams are right behind them at 3-2. The Browns are technically in second place with their win over Pittsburgh, but their point differential of -19 isn’t sustainable for a full season. Meanwhile, the Steelers have a point differential of 2, and that needs to change. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , the Steelers open as 2.5-point favorites despite being the road team on Sunday. The game has an over/under of 40.5, and the Steelers’ moneyline odds are -144. The line will certainly move if Baker Mayfield returns for Tampa Bay, but for now, this line and Vegas believe it will be rookie Jadon Daniels again for the Bucs. Yes, the Bucs are coming off a big win in Dallas, but the Steelers need to take care of business in Tampa Bay. No matter if Mayfield or Daniels starts, the defense can ill-afford a slip-up on Sunday. Anything is possible in the NFL, but with the way the North is shaping up, every game is important, and while the division isn’t being run away with, keeping pace and controlling your own destiny needs to be the goal. Keep an eye on the line movement with the announcement of the starting quarterback, but the bottom line is Pittsburgh needs this win, and the defense has to put their stamp on the game. Todd Bowles’ defense is going to blitz a ton, which will play into Aaron Rodgers’ hands as he looks to get the ball out quickly. Expect more receiving work for Warren on screens and checkdowns. Specifically, the wide receiver room has been hit big time with the short-term IR trip for Michael Pittman Jr. and the news of a potential multi-week absence for Roman Wilson, who was primed to take on a bigger role with Pittman Jr.’s injury. The Steelers pivoted to feeding Jaylen Warren, and that will continue, according to Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy. The big opportunity is in place for rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard. title: 5 takeaways from the Steelers’ 34-22 win over the Indianapolis Colts
summary: The Steelers rebounded well from a Week 4 loss, defeating the Colts in Pittsburgh 34-22 to advance to 3-2 on the 2026 season. As always, there are plenty of takeaways to be had: 1. The Steelers needed a star on offense — and they finally found one When discussing the shortcomings of the Steelers’ offense […]
full_text: Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images | Getty Images The Steelers rebounded well from a Week 4 loss, defeating the Colts in Pittsburgh 34-22 to advance to 3-2 on the 2026 season. As always, there are plenty of takeaways to be had: 1. The Steelers needed a star on offense — and they finally found one When discussing the shortcomings of the Steelers’ offense in recent years, the biggest emphasis has usually been the team’s lack of franchise quarterback. In a league that’s still heavily passer-driven, that’s an accurate takeaway. But recently, I’ve thought that the Steelers have also lacked a true “star” on offense at a skill position over the years — a running back or pass-catcher who could elevate whoever else is on the offense, and single-handedly win a game from time to time. Since the Steelers’ “Killer B” era, there have been some failed attempts to find that player: JuJu Smith-Schuster couldn’t handle the WR1 role, Najee Harris didn’t live up to first-round expectations, and George Pickens didn’t find consistency — something the Steelers’ latest attempt at a star, D.K. Metcalf, has arguably struggled with even more. Some of the team’s struggles on offense over the years have not only been due to a rotating door of quarterbacks and offensive linemen, but also a supporting cast of skill position players who couldn’t be relied upon to consistently provide a spark. And while he’s just had a handful games in a leading role so far this season, Warren has looked the part of that missing star in each one. Despite starting the year in a timeshare with Rico Dowdle, Warren still ranks third in the entire league this season in yards from scrimmage, with gains of at least 20 yards in each of his last four outings. Against the Colts, Warren managed his best game of the season thus far, taking a short pass 80 yards for a score in the second quarter, and later breaking off a 50-yard run for another touchdown in the third. He finished Sunday with 15 carries for 101 yards rushing along with 87 yards and a touchdown as a receiver. With Dowdle due for a return soon, Warren’s workload should decrease in coming weeks. But if the Steelers play their cards right, that could also be a boon for the offense. Warren has earned a clear RB1 workload going forward, but some more rest down the stretch might help his big-play ability stay fresh. 2. Keeanu Benton earns his paycheck The Steelers signed defensive tackle Keeanu Benton to a four-year, $72 million extension this offseason after a breakout 5.5-sack season in 2025. And although Benton certainly hasn’t been bad in 2026, he’s yet to record a single sack through five games in a middle-of-the-pack Steelers defense — failing to make the kind of impact you’d ideally like to see from an $18 million per year defensive tackle. But against the Colts — facing a superstar runner in Jonathan Taylor and without Derrick Harmon on the defensive line — Benton had his best performance of the year. His stat line versus Indianapolis was good, with three tackles, one stuff, and one pass defensed, but the eye test showed a much larger impact. And Taylor was held to just 45 yards on 15 carries. Benton was constantly involved in clogging up Taylor’s running lanes, being one of the biggest reasons why a second-quarter goal-line stand from the Pittsburgh defense nearly succeeded. Benton also recorded a quarterback hit and contributed to several other pressures of Colts quarterback Daniel Jones. Benton gets double-teamed a lot more than most realize, but when he isn’t getting a heavy dose of defensive attention, he remains an above-average pass rusher for his position. How often DTs are double teamed and their grading on those plays pic.twitter.com/OSV04TyAl4 — Jrfortgang (@throwthedamball) October 8, 2026 With Harmon on injured reserve and Cameron Heyward not getting any younger, Benton’s performance against the Colts was a promising one as his importance to the Steelers defense continues to increase. 3. Cornerback duo shows some fight It’s fair to say this was not the 2026 the Steelers expected when it came to the secondary. Joey Porter Jr. is in Dallas. DeShon Elliott is up to five games missed on injured reserve. And Jamel Dean has struggled with an ankle injury that kept him out against the Colts. But on Sunday, the remaining defensive backs did just enough to secure the win. It wasn’t always pretty. Daniel Jones completed 24 passes for 267 yards, with tight end Tyler Warren having a productive day with seven catches for 83 yards. Four Colts pass-catchers logged 20-plus yard gains. Still, Pittsburgh’s starting duo of boundary cornerbacks in Daylen Everette and Asante Samuel Jr. — neither were supposed to start this year, for what it’s worth — combined for a whopping six passes defensed in a game where they were tested by Jones’ 44 passing attempts. One of those pass deflections, a deep pass where the rookie Everette appeared to get beat badly but did an excellent job of recovering on a clearly underthrown pass, was a microcosm of the group’s performance on Sunday: An imperfect but promising group that won’t always get the Alec Pierce-less Colts as an opponent. “Uh oh… UH OH- ah thank god” -me watching this live pic.twitter.com/QNs1YXUH93 — Chris Ferland 🐝 (@chris_ferland) October 11, 2026 Samuel had a few more highlights, creating a whopping four pass breakups. He’s always been a playmaker at defensive back, with six interceptions and 35 passes defensed through his first three full NFL seasons with the Chargers. He can be a bit of feast or famine player at times, notably struggling with the Bengals’ Tee Higgins in Week 3, but continues to come more into his own after spinal fusion surgery and the resulting rehabilitation kept him off the field for much of 2024 and 2025. Pittsburgh has been a zone-heavy team this season as a result of how shorthanded it is in the secondary — a style of coverage where chemistry and communication can make up for some shortcomings in athleticism and ability. But with Everette’s inexperience and the number of personnel changes so far this season, there have been some expected rough points. Rookie mistake here by Daylen Everette as he trails the post when play the deep third responsibility in the Cover 3, opening up Warren on the out & up route down the sideline. Everette needs to trust that his post safety is gonna take that post and pass this off. #HereWeGo pic.twitter.com/WZw8JPd1rC — Jack Sperry (@jack_sperry) October 12, 2026 With far more high-powered passing offenses looming on the Steelers’ later-season schedule, Pittsburgh certainly has some holes to fix. But Sunday’s performance showed some promise with the usual issues, and Elliott and Dean should return at some point. 4. The Steelers pulled away when it mattered Entering the Steelers-Colts game, I wrote that both teams were fairly evenly-matched. The rosters have some similarities with both franchises straddling the line between flirting with contender status and rebuilding in recent seasons. And as expected, the two teams served up an entertaining game with a number of back and forths despite the two-possession margin at the end. However, the Steelers were able to pull away in the fourth quarter. Pittsburgh outscored Indianapolis 10-3 in the final frame, with the defense forcing a red zone field goal and two turnovers on downs on the Colts’ final three drives. We’ve been writing about how the Steelers need to embrace their “ bully ball ” potential to thrive this season, and to do so, they need to be able to bully teams at the end of games. And on Pittsburgh’s final drive, starting with 2:35 left in the game, Warren was able to log six- and five-yard runs to get the team to victory formation and run out the clock. It might not be a performance that falls in the “clutch” category, but Pittsburgh consistently performed the best on Sunday when it mattered the most — including holding the Colts to four-of-15 on third downs. That’s a good sign with plenty of…

title: Seahawks activate special teams ace Irv Charles onto 53-man roster
summary: The Seattle Seahawks will have some reinforcements coming on special teams starting with this Thursday’s critical road game at the Denver Broncos. On Tuesday, the team announced that wide receiver Irv Charles has been activated onto the 53-man roster. Charles was placed on injured reserve prior to the start of the regular season as he […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks will have some reinforcements coming on special teams starting with this Thursday’s critical road game at the Denver Broncos. On Tuesday, the team announced that wide receiver Irv Charles has been activated onto the 53-man roster. Charles was placed on injured reserve prior to the start of the regular season as he continued to recover from an ACL tear suffered at the end of the 2024 season. Charles may be listed as a wide receiver but he’s never been targeted since entering the NFL in 2022, instead making a name for himself as a special teams gunner during his time with the New York Jets. Seattle’s special teams unit has been a mixed bag, with Jason Myers performing strongly throughout the regular season afer a sub-par preseason. The punt coverage unit has recovered two fumbles and otherwise hasn’t given up a punt return yard yet, but they have been one of the league’s worst units at defending kick returns. Charles figures to be a help on that front in addition to gunner duties. Seattle traded for Charles in May, giving up a conditional 2028 draft pick . Seattle released running back Velus Jones Jr in a corresponding move. As a vested veteran, Jones doesn’t have to clear waivers and is already back on the practice squad .
author: Mookie Alexander

title: The second-year leap from Seahawks 2025 draft class hasn’t happened yet
summary: When the Seattle Seahawks won the Super Bowl last season, their remarkable run to the Lombardi Trophy was boosted by tremendous contributions from their rookie class. Grey Zabel started every game at left guard, Nick Emmanwori finished second in Defensive Rookie of the Year voting, Robbie Ouzts got plenty of snaps as a big fullback, […]
full_text: When the Seattle Seahawks won the Super Bowl last season, their remarkable run to the Lombardi Trophy was boosted by tremendous contributions from their rookie class. Grey Zabel started every game at left guard, Nick Emmanwori finished second in Defensive Rookie of the Year voting, Robbie Ouzts got plenty of snaps as a big fullback, while Tory Horton scored five touchdowns before going on season-ending injured reserve. Oh yes, and Rylie Mills’ quasi-redshirt year ended with him sacking Drake Maye in the Super Bowl. It looked like the perfect culmination of an absolute heater of drafts for John Schneider. With Seattle retaining most of its free agents and otherwise sitting out even the mid-tier of free agency, it was reasonable to think that the Seahawks would be relying on their 2025 class to shoulder more responsibility and be bigger factors in 2026. It hasn’t happened. At least not yet. Grey Zabel continues to be a solid starting guard (although I don’t believe he’s been as good as last season), whereas Nick Emmanwori has come back from his ankle surgery and looks to be his usual stalwart self as a SINO (Safety In Name Only). That’s about where the good times end. Elijah Arroyo isn’t much of a factor Elijah Arroyo has one catch, one personal foul penalty on an interception in which he was the target, and that’s pretty much it for his 2026 contributions. Dating back to last year, Sam Darnold has thrown four interceptions targeting Arroyo, compared to just one touchdown. He didn’t have a particularly eye-popping 2025 and was injured in the back-stretch of last season, but a very good preseason has not translated into the regular season. If nothing else, it now looks very curious as to why Arroyo played so much in the final preseason game against the Kansas City Chiefs, when most would-be starters and main depth either didn’t play or maxed out at one series. There have been rightful questions as to why Arroyo is listed as TE3 on the depth chart and otherwise does not outsnap Eric Saubert, a journeyman blocking TE who’s not known for his receiving abilities. A cursory look at the All-22 this season suggests that Arroyo is generally not trusted in the run game. When he’s asked to “block” it’s really just being on the opposite side of the concept, almost to the point where he’s not relevant to the play even if he botches any backside responsibilities. For whatever reason, Brian Fleury completely flipped the tendencies against the San Francisco 49ers, to mixed results. As for his route-running? While there are opportunities that I believe were left on the table by Sam Darnold, the Los Angeles Chargers game alone is a microcosm of how Arroyo is being used: run very far. Every Elijah Arroyo route from the Chargers game. pic.twitter.com/VxixJqHA3f — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) October 10, 2026 If Arroyo isn’t trusted as a run blocker and is primarily used on vertical concepts, you’ve got a predictability problem. Sam was definitely targeting Arroyo here before (wisely, I think) pulling it down. pic.twitter.com/4bdry5ezHp — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) October 12, 2026 Arroyo’s blocking was a known weakness entering the draft, but the idea was that they would work on that part of his game in the NFL and he’d otherwise be a mismatch hunter in space. We’ve yet to see that materialize consistently (honestly, if at all). At the moment, I think Arroyo is not a schematic match for an offense that goes so heavy on 12 and 13 personnel but requires its tight ends to be credible blockers. The mysterious lack of Tory Horton I cannot explain why Tory Horton was nearer to a healthy scratch than a rotational player on offense and special teams on Sunday. Horton playing 11 snaps against the San Francisco 49ers is about in line with his normal count this season, but only three of those snaps were on pass plays. One of those pass plays was a screen to Emanuel Wilson, so in effect Horton ran two routes all game. But what shocked me was Horton losing kickoff return duties to Velus Jones Jr. Horton played zero special teams snaps, while Velus was the other returner alongside Rashid Shaheed. Jones does have a history as a kick returner dating back to college. You know what he also has a history of? Fumbling. Velus Jones Jr. with ANOTHER fumble on a punt return. This time, inside his own 10 yard line, as he was attempting to field the ball from his knees. #Bears — Aaron Leming (@AaronLemingNFL) October 14, 2022 The Chicago Bears are STILL pushing Velus Jones to be an RB & the primary return specialist His career numbers at those positions? Total Touches: 63 Total Fumbles: 4 That’s a turnover every 16 touches That’s about once every 2 games if he continues these roles END THIS NOW pic.twitter.com/NaZjllWvay — Chicago Jay (@Chicago_Jay1) September 9, 2024 Your guess is as good as mine as far as Horton not getting more playing time, especially as Rashid Shaheed continues to be a minimal factor on offense. The one thing I’d caution regarding Horton is that half of his career productivity in terms of receptions is just from two games against the Washington Commanders. The two games prior to last year’s Commanders game saw him shut out completely. He wasn’t a high target guy before the Rashid Shaheed trade and is even less so afterward. But when the ball is thrown his way, it tends to be an efficient outcome, as evidenced by six touchdowns on just 17 catches. Rylie Mills is a rotational player who’s struggling against the run I admit I peddled the Rylie Mills hype after watching him in training camp and preseason. Much of what I liked was as a pass rusher and not as a run defender. He was giving the starting offensive line a consistently hard time and his teammates praised his strength and effort. I don’t like what I’m seeing out of Mills as a run defender, which is going to keep him from getting snaps until that changes. I think Rylie Mills' season-low snap count against the 49ers was, in part, an acknowledgement that he really can't play too many snaps against quality rushing offenses. The Chargers are a bad, banged up offense and he was just getting displaced. pic.twitter.com/ugczd9zNHn — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) October 13, 2026 Mills’ pressure rate is also sub-10% and the worst of Seattle’s defensive line rotation, so he’s not providing a whole lot right now other than rest for one of Jarran Reed, Byron Murphy II, or Leonard Williams. No Jalen Milroe package this season Actually, I don’t really care about this. Year 3 will tell us a lot more about Milroe. I think he’s made enough of a leap from this preseason to the last preseason, though. Injuries end Robbie Ouzts, Mason Richman’s seasons early Then there’s just bad luck. Ouzts’ neck injury ended last season prematurely and continued to be an issue this training camp. It’s apparently not career ending, which is good news. Richman’s ACL tear in preseason mattered a ton, as he could’ve just as easily functioned as a backup guard over both Christian Haynes and Beau Stephens. Admittedly, Richman was Grey Zabel’s backup, but he has the versatility to play across the line and might have been a better option while Anthony Bradford remains out. This is NOT to say the 2025 draft class outside of Emmanwori and Zabel is a write-off, but the promise from 2025 as a whole has yet to translate in 2026. Compounding Seattle’s issue is the awful luck of having their top three picks from this year’s class all on injured reserve, with Bud Clark not coming back until 2027. If the start of Seattle’s season has felt a little “blah” despite the same 3-2 mark as last year, I think this is a major reason. Seattle is not getting enough (or anything) out of its last two draft classes—on the plus side, Nehemiah Pritchett is really stepping up for the 2024 class—which in turn is making the Seahawks look like a more top-heavy roster than last season.

title: 49ers News: We’re on to Washington
summary: The Commanders are a fascinating team. The same guys that beat Seattle also just tied the New York Giants. At 1-3-1, they’ll be desperate to save their spiraling season. A win on national TV against the hottest team in the league would be exactly what the doctor ordered for them.  With Sonny Styles leading the […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MD - OCTOBER 20: San Francisco 49ers defenders Arik Armstead (91) (front) , DeForest Buckner (99) and Nick Bosa (97) slide on the wet turf to celebrate sacking Washington Redskins quarterback Case Keenum (8) to end the game at FedEx Field. (Photo by Jonathan Newton / The Washington Post via Getty Images) The Commanders are a fascinating team. The same guys that beat Seattle also just tied the New York Giants. At 1-3-1, they’ll be desperate to save their spiraling season. A win on national TV against the hottest team in the league would be exactly what the doctor ordered for them. With Sonny Styles leading the way, their front seven will be a problem. He’s been really really good… maybe one of the few linebackers that can keep up with George Kittle or Christian McCaffrey. Their secondary looks much more exploitable. On the other side of the ball, their interior offensive line seemed like their biggest vulnerability before the season started. They’ve stabilized by signing Lucas Patrick to play center and getting starting guard Sam Cosmi back from injury. The x-factor, which I’m sure will be talked about ad nauseam, is none other than Jayden Daniels. Niners LB Dre Greenlaw’s appeal of suspension rejected, will sit vs. Commanders “Rookie Jaden Dugger, who filled in for Greenlaw against the Seahawks, is likely to start in Greenlaw’s place Monday night.” NFL Week 5 film review: How Mike Evans, Kyler Murray, Jordan Love provided answers (paywall) “ The Seahawks’ two-deep shells discourage deep passing and can make the picture cloudy for quarterbacks. However, they play a fair amount of one-on-one outside when they rotate their safeties or when one of their safeties is “poaching.” Matthew Stafford has made a living finding those one-on-ones, and Puka Nacua and Davante Adams win in those situations. This week, Brock Purdy found those matchups, and Evans made the Seahawks pay. Here, the Seahawks lined up with two deep safeties, as they usually do. This could dissuade quarterbacks from looking deep because there could potentially be deep help on both sides of the formation. However, after the snap, the weak-side safety turned his hips and looked to the three-receiver side. They were playing a form of quarters that left the backside corner Josh Jobe one-on-one with Evans. Some quarterbacks might still see the safety’s presence on that half of the field and decide not to throw deep, but Purdy knew the safety couldn’t help Jobe on the outside with his technique.” 49ers report card, grades: The defensive line saved their best game in years for the Seahawks “Let’s talk about that intentional grounding play. On the left side, Luke Farrell is the in-line tight end; Brayden Willis is lined up next to him, but off the line of scrimmage. The wide receiver split out left is Jordan Watkins, who motions that he’s off the line, but lines up on the line of scrimmage. That covers Farrell up, making him ineligible. And those are the types of plays that are why we see Watkins only run nine routes. On one of those routes, Watkins was bullied and couldn’t shake free from press. Cooks made himself available on the touchdown, but was called for a penalty, had another declined, and looks disinterested as a blocker. There is a weird amount of hate for Jacob Cowing that I do not understand. The coaching staff is starting to figure out how and where to use Cowing. Against Seattle, Cowing ran 41% of his routes in the slot and leaned more on underneath routes where he could find soft spots in the zone. He will still run clear out routes, but in my opinion, Cowing could be Purdy’s best friend. Without Deebo, I see Jacob taking over that role….Any time a defensive lineman reads a screen, it’s a sign their IQ is through the roof. Guess what Mykel Williams did? Keion owes Mykel a steak dinner for the sack, since Williams forced Sam Darnold to move off his spot….Dugger was a difference-maker. He got caught peeking on a play-action pass and allowed a first down. Honestly, that may have been his lone mistake. His discipline was incredible. He stayed in windows where Darnold wanted to throw to JSN, instead of taking the bait on a shorter throw. Those are the plays that don’t go in the stat sheet. Dugger was in the stat sheet plenty. He ran through the right tackle’s block to stop a screen that could’ve resulted in a first down. Dugger set the edge, made multiple stops, and played with starter-level physicality.” 49ers game review: How Gracen Halton and defense’s recent draft picks saved the day in Seattle (paywall) “Mustapha channeled the best of his promising 2024 rookie season by also breaking up would-be completions to wideouts Cooper Kupp and Jaxon Smith-Njigba with shot-from-a-cannon blows before he sealed the win by belting Kupp out of bounds on a 9-yard reception on 4th-and-10 from midfield with just under a minute left. Three plays earlier, Mustapha’s shot on Smith-Njigba was vital. After Mustapha whacked him to break up a first-down pass, the reigning NFL Offensive Player of the Year rose slowly and went to the sideline for a snap with the game on the line. When he returned, Smith-Njigba dropped a deep third-down pass before Mustapha punctuated his violent performance with his fourth-down tackle. 49ers overreactions: Was Mike Evans missing piece to finally winning Super Bowl? “Now, we can’t confidently say that Corliss Waitman is the best punter in the NFL this season. But the point is . . . he has been very good for the 49ers this season. On Sunday, none of his five punts were returned. As a result, the Seahawks began those five drives at the 11, 18, 8, 9 and 4. And, yes, Gracen Halton’s touchdown was a direct result of that last Waitman punt right before the end of the first half. Waitman’s net punting average is 43.6 yards, and that is nearly a 7-yard improvement over Thomas Morstead from last season.”

title: 3 trade targets at WR for the 49ers: A realistic, best-fit, and pipe dream
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are hurting at the wide receiver position. Being down to Mike Evans and Brandin Cooks as your top two targets sounds better in 2018, but the 49ers found a way to survive in Seattle with the two veterans. Evans is still a top-end receiver. However, Jacob Cowing and Jordan Watkins will […]
full_text: The San Francisco 49ers are hurting at the wide receiver position. Being down to Mike Evans and Brandin Cooks as your top two targets sounds better in 2018, but the 49ers found a way to survive in Seattle with the two veterans. Evans is still a top-end receiver. However, Jacob Cowing and Jordan Watkins will have to take significant snaps at receiver, and that feels very uncomfortable. The injuries to Demarcus Robinson, Deebo Samuel, and De’Zhaun Stribling aren’t season-ending, and the trio will be back sometime in the near future. Still, the 49ers should look to add more firepower at the position. In the grand scheme, having too many weapons is never a bad idea. Seattle will have revenge on their minds when the two teams meet again, and the 49ers will still need more options to go downfield against their secondary. Let’s have some fun with three targets, which I will list as most realistic, the best fit, and a home run/pipe dream swing from the 49ers front office. Realistic: Jauan Jennings Has anyone in recent memory overvalued their market more than Jennings and his agent? Turning down a multi-year deal with big bucks turned into a one-year deal with the Minnesota Vikings for $6,130,000 in guaranteed money. The Vikings’ offense is a mess, and Jennings is clearly frustrated with his role. Minnesota is on bye this week, and Jennings has a total of two receptions for nine yards on five targets in five games. Mind you, Justin Jefferson missed a week, as did Jordan Addison. Financially, the 49ers will be on the hook for his guaranteed money of just over a million dollars. It can be viewed as a step backwards given the need for speed, but his reliability, connection with Purdy, familiarity with the playbook, and nose for run blocking would be welcome. His mean streak is needed, and he can hit the ground running and step in immediately for the 49ers. It would take a seventh-round pick to bring Jennings back. A six-man receiver group of Evans, Deebo, Robinson, Jennings, Stribling, and Cowing (a special teams member, but that role is in jeopardy) feels better heading into January than any other group. Best fit: Demario Douglas This one is tough considering the New England Patriots still believe they can compete for a Super Bowl berth in the AFC. A.J. Brown is returning soon, the Patriots paid Romeo Doubs (that hasn’t gone well), and the team has a bit of a logjam for the receiver spot behind the two top targets, with Douglas and Kyle Williams in the mix. Why is Douglas the best fit? He is a natural separator from the slot and can shake tight coverages in small spaces. Pop can be anything from a short area target to someone who can create explosives down the field. The issue is the Patriots may not be in the business of moving targets from their offense, even if Douglas is unlikely to get an extension from the team. Would they want to move Pop for picks? That would be the question. A three-receiver set of Evans and Stribling outside with Pop in the slot could be deadly for Purdy and the 49ers offense. Home run/pipe dream: Terry McLaurin/Josh Downs Now, let’s start dreaming big. The Washington Commanders are a sinking ship, and the 49ers have a chance to continue that with a win over the Commanders on Monday night. The NFC East is yucky and wide open, but Washington has the worst chance of winning that division, and you have to wonder if the team would look to unload McLaurin’s contract for picks after a contentious negotiation period. The 49ers could write their wrongs of passing on Terry for Jalen Hurd in the 2019 NFL Draft. That’s a big swing. Indianapolis paid Alec Pierce. The receiver hasn’t returned anything on his huge contract, and the Colts aren’t likely to pay Downs either. The Colts need to keep losing, but Downs would be a huge addition given his route-running acumen and versatility at all three receiver positions. Downs can attack all three levels of the field and can shake free independently of Kyle Shanahan’s scheme. Still, this feels like a pipe dream, but his fit with the offense would make this offense a nightmare to game plan for.

title: 49ers report card, grades: The defensive line saved their best game in years for the Seahawks
summary: The San Francisco 49ers took an early lead over the Seattle Seahawks, then the teams traded the lead for the next three and a half quarters before the Seahawks failed to score on the final drive. It was the best defensive shootout we’ll see this season. Here are the grades from the 49ers’ Week 5 […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 11: Sam Darnold #14 of the Seattle Seahawks is sacked by Keion White #56 of the San Francisco 49ers during the fourth quarter at Lumen Field on October 11, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers took an early lead over the Seattle Seahawks, then the teams traded the lead for the next three and a half quarters before the Seahawks failed to score on the final drive. It was the best defensive shootout we’ll see this season. Here are the grades from the 49ers’ Week 5 win. Quarterback: B- Brock Purdy airmailed a few throws. He had some flat-out misfires. And then there’s the interception. Ironically, Seattle pressure saved Purdy from throwing into double coverage on one play. He also had a couple of dropbacks where he was sped up and missed a wideout because he thought he was under duress. Purdy was this close to throwing another interception after staring down a target that the linebacker dropped. But there was a drop on the first drive where there was a chunk play. Purdy escaped a sack and used his legs to extend the drive. He was constantly moving and manipulating space in the pocket. He showed a ton of guts hanging in there when he knew a big hit was coming. I thought Purdy exhibited the kind of toughness you need to beat a defense like Seattle’s. Running backs: B+ Christian McCaffrey didn’t have a carry on third or fourth down in this game. He only touched the ball 32% of the time on early downs. It was almost as if CMC was a decoy for four quarters. It makes you wonder if the coaching staff came into this game thinking they’d struggle to run the ball. McCaffrey had 68 rush yards on 11 attempts, with 32 after contact — 17 of those through the A-gap. McCaffrey caught all three of his targets for 15 yards. Kaelon Black had six carries for 16 yards. Fifteen of those came after contact, but he was stuffed three times, compared to zero by McCaffrey. McCaffrey earned this grade by forcing a pair of missed tackles and maintaining an 81% success rate. It didn’t feel like one of those “less is more” performances. I think that’ll show the next time these teams play, with McCaffrey getting 20 touches. Offensive line: B- A big reason for McCaffrey’s success was his 3.27 yards-per-carry average before contact. The line made it clear from the first play that they’d compete differently than they did against the Seahawks last year. Let’s get the bad out of the way: Connor Colby in pass protection. He had five blown blocks. Four of those were in pass pro. He also had a false start. A player who could’ve been drafted in the top 5 (Byron Murphy) against a seventh-rounder looked how you’d envision it. Dominick Puni and Colton McKivitz were beaten twice in pass protection. Jake Brendel and Trent Williams had clean sheets. Williams was excellent. On one of McCaffrey’s double-digit carries, he flat-lined a defensive back. The holding penalty on him doesn’t count, in my eyes. Williams did nothing wrong. Puni’s hold on the screen had zero impact on the play. Dom also didn’t need to do that, as the ball carrier was past him. McKivitz showed impressive awareness on one play, peeling off his block to pick up a blitzer. On the same play, Seattle’s defender had his hands all in Trent’s facemask (no call). The line as a whole has been quite good on the ground this year. As the game goes on, they seem to get better. Late in the game, Colby blocked two players to spring McCaffrey. Colby was so good against the run that, to me, it offset the pass-protection losses. Pass catchers: B- It may not have been the best game statistically, but it was the best game from an impact perspective for Mike Evans. He was flawless, which might make you scratch your head when you see the grade. Evans generated 12.21 in total EPA. That was more than 27 quarterbacks in Week 5. Everything about him was poetry in motion. You can be as physical as you want with Evans, but the way he shrugs off contact is unlike any wideout we’ve seen under Kyle Shanahan. Let’s talk about that intentional grounding play. On the left side, Luke Farrell is the in-line tight end; Brayden Willis is lined up next to him, but off the line of scrimmage. The wide receiver split out left is Jordan Watkins, who motions that he’s off the line, but lines up on the line of scrimmage. That covers Farrell up, making him ineligible. And those are the types of plays that are why we see Watkins only run nine routes. On one of those routes, Watkins was bullied and couldn’t shake free from press. Cooks made himself available on the touchdown, but was called for a penalty, had another declined, and looks disinterested as a blocker. There is a weird amount of hate for Jacob Cowing that I do not understand. The coaching staff is starting to figure out how and where to use Cowing. Against Seattle, Cowing ran 41% of his routes in the slot and leaned more on underneath routes where he could find soft spots in the zone. He will still run clear out routes, but in my opinion, Cowing could be Purdy’s best friend. Without Deebo, I see Jacob taking over that role. He looked the most comfortable, which is saying something, considering the competition. Brayden Willis found out what big-boy football is like on one play against Leonard Williams. He only played 11 snaps for a reason. Luke Farrell continues to impress and hold his own. Most of George Kittle’s work came underneath and as a blocker. However, he had one route where he almost made Nick Emmanwori fall. Kittle is still Kittle. Defensive line: A+ The Seahawks finished with the lowest EPA per play of any offense in Week 5. They were 28th in success rate. The scoreboard is a blatant lie. The defensive line finally turned pressure into sacks. There was no shortage of pressure in this game. Since 2022, Week 5 was the Niners’ 8th-highest pressure rate in a game. The list is full of 2022 and 2023 games. But against the Seahawks, San Francisco managed a 48.6 pressure rate. They had nine quick pressures. In back-to-back weeks, they’ve generated a pressure rate over 40%. That’s the first time they’ve done that without Nick Bosa. Ever. It’s also the third time they’ve been above 40% without Bosa. I called Keion White a supercharged version of Charles Omenihu. He was a maniac. Six pressures, two tackles for loss, two run stops, and a sack. Per Sumer Sports, he had the most impact plays of any edge rusher in Week 5. It felt that way. Even on the plays he didn’t finish, White still impacted the play. Any time a defensive lineman reads a screen, it’s a sign their IQ is through the roof. Guess what Mykel Williams did? Keion owes Mykel a steak dinner for the sack, since Williams forced Sam Darnold to move off his spot. Khalid Kareem, Ogbo Okoronkwo, and Romello Height each had two pressures. Kareem has been everything the 49ers could have hoped for as a run defender. The same is true for Sebastian Valdez. Valdez stood out on four plays. I was intrigued by Raheem Morris starting the third quarter with Valdez and Gracen Halton at defensive tackle. It’s a sign he’s going to play his best players. That’s no slight to Osa Odighizuwa. He was brought in to disrupt the quarterback. He’s done that. Osa had three pressures and a sack. Odighizuwa got a clean win on a screen pass, highlighting his pass-rushing ability. He’s an ideal fit for Morris’s scheme, given how much ground he covers on stunts. But when you generate a turnover and score off it, you’re not coming off the field. I had Halton down for five impact plays. He made the Seahawks first-rounder from a year ago look like a Day 3 pick. Halton’s sack came against Charles Cross, the left tackle who just received a $100 million extension. This kid is special. As a collective unit, the defensive line hasn’t looked like this in years. Keep in mind it was Mykel’s first game back, and they weren’t benefiting from Nick Bosa getting double-teamed. Linebackers: B+ Things could’ve…

title: 3 final observations from 49ers win over Seahawks: We’re seeing major improvements from a pair of defenders
summary: The San Francisco 49ers beat the Seattle Seahawks 32-29 in a thriller over the weekend, only further accentuating their case as Super Bowl contenders in 2026. The game involved seven turnovers, 13 penalties, and two inefficient passing offenses against strong defenses. And yet, it came down to the wire, with the 49ers edging it out, […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 11: Renardo Green #0 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates with teammates after an interception against the Seattle Seahawks during the third quarter at Lumen Field on October 11, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers beat the Seattle Seahawks 32-29 in a thriller over the weekend, only further accentuating their case as Super Bowl contenders in 2026. The game involved seven turnovers, 13 penalties, and two inefficient passing offenses against strong defenses. And yet, it came down to the wire, with the 49ers edging it out, thanks to a couple of clutch scoring drives and a major defensive stand at the end. Looking back at the game, here are my five final observations from Sunday’s win over the Seahawks. OL has one of its best run-blocking games The Seahawks have one of the best defensive lines in the league. Byron Murphy and Leonard Williams are such disruptors on the interior, which is why the trench battle between San Francisco’s offensive line and Seattle’s defensive line was going to be such a battle. The 49ers offensive line has played extremely well to start the year, especially in pass protection, but we were waiting to see the run game fully develop. And against arguably the toughest matchup its faced so far, I thought San Francisco’s offensive line did a great job creating lanes in the run game on Sunday. Christian McCaffrey rushed for 68 yards on 11 carries, averaging more than six yards per rush. McCaffrey got 3.55 yards after contact per carry, a great figure, but he also got 2.63 yards before contact, which is a very impressive figure against Seattle’s defense. As a result, we saw a couple of 10+ yard runs from McCaffrey, while Kaelon Black added one as well. There’s still things to continue figuring out in the run game, and the 49ers are an elite passing offense. But against an opponent, it was a very good sign to see the offensive line have one of its best run blocking games. Early returns on rookie class are quite strong The 49ers still have a lot to figure out from their rookie class. But the early returns on a few players have been quite strong so far. De’Zhaun Stribling had put together an impressive preseason and was already the starter in two-receiver sets to start the year before his ankle injury. Romello Height had one of his better games on Sunday, recording two pressures as the 49ers got a whopping 23 overall. It’s now back-to-back games for Height with multiple pressures, and he’s taken on the responsibility of a pretty big role so far with the injuries. Kaelon Black has had his ups and downs, but the trust is there in him, unlike a couple of running backs the 49ers have drafted the last few years. And Jaden Dugger filled in admirably for Dre Greenlaw on Sunday, racking up nine tackles, two pressures, a sack, and a tackle for loss in a huge game. We saw Dugger’s potential in the preseason as the ultimate chess piece, moving around as a linebacker and around the line of scrimmage. Now, in his biggest action yet, Dugger did his part, while also adding four defensive stops and not missing a single tackle. Then, on the defensive line, there’s Gracen Halton, who has been a big factor early in the season. Halton had another three pressures and three defensive stops on Sunday, marking his best performance of the season against a very tough opponent. I’ve said this before but Super Bowl winning teams usually always need some production from their rookie classes. The 49ers are getting it early on from this 2026 group. Two players in the secondary are coming back into their own The 49ers have looked to draft a number of younger players in the secondary over the past few years, and for the most part, they’ve seen some good results. But there were two players with high hopes in particular that were inconsistent last year: Malik Mustapha and Renardo Green. Mustapha had been working back from a torn ACL, and had a good number of ups and downs alongside the similarly inconsistent Ji’Ayir Brown that left some wondering whether the 49ers could look for an upgrade this offseason. But the team stuck with their young safety duo, and it’s starting to come together for the third-year pro. Man, Malik Mustapha was all over the place on Sunday. The heat-seeking missile had seven tackles, and made a number of impact plays. He broke up a pair of passes with big hits, including one on Jaxon Smith-Njigba on the final drive. He was flying through rushing lanes to try to make plays. It was one of his better performances of the season. Then, there’s Renardo Green, the embattled third-year cornerback who was benched a few times last year. San Francisco brought in Jack Jones, who has seen the field some times this year, but Green has really looked more confident on the field and is starting to come together. The young cornerback had two interceptions, while allowing just two completions on five targets for five yards. The other target? A pass breakup. Green allowed just an 8.3 passer rating on Sunday. He was the most-targeted cornerback, with three of those targets coming against Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Green broke up one, intercepted another, and gave up a four-yard catch on the third. The 49ers defense has been really good this year despite some injuries and a reliance on younger players. Credit goes to Raheem Morris and this defensive staff because the players look to be playing with a ton of confidence right now, especially these two young defensive backs.

title: Kyle Shanahan praises Raheem Morris for providing critical confidence boost
summary: With the 49ers coming off their best defensive performance of the season in their biggest game of the year so far, it’s no surprise there is a lot of praise coming the way of coordinator Raheem Morris. The 49ers’ outstanding defensive showing in the thrilling win over the Seattle Seahawks — which saw San Francisco […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 08: Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris speaks to the media ahead of the 49ers practice session at AAMI Park on September 08, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Robert Cianflone/Robert Cianflone/Getty Images) | Robert Cianflone/Getty Images With the 49ers coming off their best defensive performance of the season in their biggest game of the year so far, it’s no surprise there is a lot of praise coming the way of coordinator Raheem Morris. The 49ers’ outstanding defensive showing in the thrilling win over the Seattle Seahawks — which saw San Francisco force four turnovers, sack Sam Darnold five times and restrict Seattle to a 30 percent success rate — was one in which every area of the defense excelled. San Francisco’s front consistently won when defending both the run and the pass, the linebacker play was typically excellent, and the secondary’s ascension continued as the defensive backs thrived in coverage, albeit against a Seahawks receiving group light on difference-makers outside of the not fully healthy Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Through five games, the 49er defense has taken huge strides after what could at best be described as a below-par year with Robert Saleh as coordinator in 2025, though Saleh was hamstrung by a huge amount of injury adversity. Following the display in Seattle, that improvement is reflected by the numbers, with the San Francisco defense third in the NFL by Expected Points Added per play and eighth in the NFL by success rate . Morris’ fingerprints are all over the progress made by the 49er defense, but, speaking in his Monday conference call, head coach Kyle Shanahan identified where the former Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Atlanta Falcons head coach has arguably made the biggest difference. Shanahan said: “It doesn’t surprise me with Raheem. I’ve just been around him for too long. He’s one of the best people and best coaches I’ve ever been around. I tried to bring him here originally when I left Atlanta. They wouldn’t let him out. So, it’s been a long time coming to get him here. He’s done an unbelievable job this year, especially with the injuries, but just overall everything he’s mixed up schematically. I love the confidence he’s given our DBs and the way they’ve been playing since training camp. He’s had a real huge effect on this team and we’re very lucky to have him.” With an extensive background of coaching defensive backs in his career, the 49ers will have entered the year hoping Morris could have a transformative influence on their secondary. To this point, those hopes have been realized and then some. Renardo Green is enjoying a breakout year at cornerback. His three interceptions in five games mark a career-high following his pair in Seattle and his passer rating when targeted of 45.0 is seventh among all corners. Deommodore Lenoir’s numbers aren’t as impressive, but his lockdown performance against Courtland Sutton was key to the 49ers’ Week 4 win over the Denver Broncos. In addition, the play at safety through five weeks has served to allay concerns about San Francisco’s options at that spot, with Marques Sigle, Ji’Ayir Brown and Malik Mustapha all producing impressive play in varying amounts of time on the field. The challenge for the secondary and the defense overall will be to maintain this tremendous start. Given the difficulty of playing cornerback and secondary, there will clearly be ups and downs. However, if the defensive backfield can maintain a relative level of consistency, Morris’ unit should be in good shape to stay in the upper echelons of the league. For this young defense to regularly play at the level they produced in Week 5 will be a big ask, but in Morris, they look to have exactly the right mentor.
author: Nicholas McGee

title: What is the 49ers plan at receiver without Deebo Samuel?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers lost another piece of their offensive core when Deebo Samuel went down with a hamstring injury against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 5. Samuel, 30, had been looking to hit the edge before pulling up and fumbling on a non-contact play. He’ll now miss a few weeks, only adding to the […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers lost another piece of their offensive core when Deebo Samuel went down with a hamstring injury against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 5. Samuel, 30, had been looking to hit the edge before pulling up and fumbling on a non-contact play. He’ll now miss a few weeks, only adding to the injury bug that San Francisco is facing at receiver. The 49ers have now lost Ricky Pearsall, De’Zhaun Stribling, Christian Kirk, Demarcus Robinson, Samuel, and Khadarel Hodge all to injuries for some period of time. The 49ers trotted out Brandin Cooks for the first time, while Jacob Cowing played a heavy number of snaps behind Mike Evans. Additionally, we saw Jordan Watkins get 22 snaps as well. Right now, those three are the team’s top depth after Evans, who is still recovering in his own right from a painful rib injury. What is the 49ers plan at receiver without Samuel? “Well, yeah, with Deebo out, we have five guys on the roster and Deebo being out, that would be four,“ head coach Kyle Shanahan said about his receivers. So the next guys up to get activated would be one of the three guys on practice squad. Because also in that game Jake went down with an ankle. He ended up being all right, but the numbers got low real quick. That’s why we always like to get five up for game day. We’ve got four guys on our roster, so we’ll most likely decide on one of those guys throughout the week.” Currently, the 49ers have three receivers on their practice squad: Wesley Grimes, Will Pauling, and Xavier Smith. So will they look for more reinforcements during the week? Shanahan doesn’t believe so, at least for now. “I think we have enough,” Shanahan added. “We’ve got three guys on practice squad also who can help. Anytime you lose this number of guys, four guys or five guys whatever it is, it’s a huge challenge. But, we do have guys in this building who can do it and we’ll always look.” The 49ers, and other teams in the NFL, usually have five or six receivers, with one potentially being inactive on game day. San Francisco doesn’t even have the five healthy bodies on their 53-man roster, let alone a sixth. So, until players come back, it could be a significant dose of Mike Evans, as it was on Sunday when he had seven catches for 113 yards and a touchdown. The 49ers face the Washington Commanders and Atlanta Falcons over the next two weeks before their bye, giving them a chance to start 7-0 as the league’s best team. But for that to happen, they’ll have to figure something more out at receiver, as they’ve really struggled to get much production out of the position the last few weeks.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: NFC West Recap: 49ers take two-game lead; Seahawks, Cardinals, and Rams lose
summary: 5-0 Always the best way to start these. The San Francisco 49ers are undefeated and have now collected three wins in the NFC West, two of which are away games. If you told me they were going to be 5-0, but they’d have the injuries they have, I’d have a hard time believing it. But […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 11: Head coach Mike MacDonald of the Seattle Seahawks and head coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers greet each other after the game at Lumen Field on October 11, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Olivia Vanni/Getty Images) | Getty Images 5-0 Always the best way to start these. The San Francisco 49ers are undefeated and have now collected three wins in the NFC West, two of which are away games. If you told me they were going to be 5-0, but they’d have the injuries they have, I’d have a hard time believing it. But now that I see this 5-0, I’m getting giddier thinking about what this team will be like when they get some of those pieces back. As for the rest of the division? Well, they all lost. So it’s another wonderful week of football for 49ers fans. Brock Purdy remains in the MVP conversation; however, he’s now with second-best odds o n FanDuel Sportsbook , below Josh Allen after the latter’s legs secured a win for the Buffalo Bills Monday night. Allen’s odds are only +50 better, so it’s nothing huge, and Purdy still deserves to be in the MVP conversation. If you disagree, watch that fourth-quarter drive that Purdy put together that should have ended after ridiculous penalties were called. Instead, Purdy took care of things, put the 49ers in the lead, and set things up for the back-and-forth left to play out. Speaking of that game… San Francisco 49ers (5-0)/Seattle Seahawks (3-2) Two days removed, what can I say about this game that hasn’t been said? The 49ers are 5-0 and have beaten the Denver Broncos, Los Angeles Rams, and Seattle Seahawks to get there. If there’s any question about how “good” they are, that can be put to rest. In fact, they’ll get better once their pieces recover and return. But that game. W atch the recaps if you can . It will definitely be one of the year’s best when the season ends. While the 49ers had 29 points scored on them, that defense was beyond filthy, and they weren’t even at full strength. Just think what happens when Nick Bosa gets back to a defensive line that had five sacks without him against the Seahawks. The Seahawks now have two losses in three weeks. Things don’t get easier on their schedule. First, they have to go Mile High on a short week to face the Denver Broncos. Then they host the Kansas City Chiefs, followed by the Chicago Bears. That’s not a good three-game stretch. As a 49ers fan, rooting for the Chiefs isn’t exactly an ideal rooting situation, but we’ve all done worse. The Seahawks aren’t in trouble—yet. But after that stretch, they may have an issue, depending on the win/loss total They don’t face the 49ers again until Week 12, which means we can get that game out of the way before the final season stretch. Right now, the Seahawks are two games behind the 49ers. That’s huge. Arizona Cardinals (1-4) After forcing a three-and-out on the Detroit Lions’ opening drive, the Cardinals drove down the field. With five minutes left in the first quarter, a touchdown was secured and a 7-0 lead established. And then the Lions proceeded to beat the ever-loving snot out of the Cardinals. By half, that 7-0 Cardinals lead turned into a 24-7 Lions lead. And it kept growing, and growing, and going, and going . The Cardinals wouldn’t score again until the third quarter was winding down; by then it was over anyway. 45-21, Lions. Jacoby Brissett took five sacks and threw an interception while Lions quarterback Jared Goff went 19 for 30, 271 yards passing, three touchdowns, and zero interceptions. The Lions fumbled the ball three times but recovered all of them. It’s safe to say nothing went the Cardinals’ way today. Well, on the field. Off the field, they made a little trade to make up for that fourth overall pick they burned a few years back. Wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. and a seventh-round pick were traded to the Houston Texans in exchange for a second and sixth-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. Harrison’s time in Arizona was underwhelming to say the least, and the Cardinals got something back for their fourth overall selection in 2024. Some may write Harrison off as a bust, but given how good he was in college (not to mention being the son of a Hall of Famer), a change of scenery may be what he needs. The Cardinals will be worse for it in 2026, even if Harrison wasn’t lighting the field on fire. In any case, the Cardinals not only lose to the Lions, but they also lose Harrison, as he is now playing with DeMeco Ryans. Los Angeles Rams (2-3) The greatest football team ever assembled (according to, well, someone) is now 2-3. Their only wins come against the New York Giants, who had to switch to their backup quarterback in the first quarter, and the Philadelphia Eagles, who have some serious dysfunction. Of course, in their losing effort against the Buffalo Bills, it looked like the opposite might happen. With little time left in regulation, the Rams went down the field with ease to tie things at 34-34, just before the clock struck 00:00. The Bills, getting the ball first, moved down the field with a chance to set the score up. It was shaping up to be another touchdown. Then this happened: FUMBLE 🚨Nate Landman punches it out and Aaron Donald recovers! @BUFvsLAR on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/oUWPBMxS6h — NFL (@NFL) October 13, 2026 Thanks, James Cook. Thanks for nothing. The Rams then made quick work of the Bills’ wet paper bag of a defense and set things up for the game-winning field goal. No one wants to switch places with James Cook after that fumble, but I think the NFL got it right by saying we all shared his reaction to the kick: James Cook is everyone after this blocked kick 😅 @BUFvsLAR on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/OObWcSVHBQ — NFL (@NFL) October 13, 2026 My hypothesis for Josh Allen getting a small gap over Brock Purdy in the MVP odds is what happened when the Bills took over following that botch. It no longer was 11 on 11; it was Allen vs. the other 11 Rams defenders—and they couldn’t do anything about it. Allen just ran around the field to get the Bills in field goal range and call it a day. The Bills have done 49ers fans a solid by handing the Rams another loss. Their 2-3 record increases the incline of that uphill battle they’ll need to get a playoff spot, let alone into the Super Bowl. As for the game itself? It was fun, if not a bit sloppy. If that’s our Super Bowl preview, then I’m shivering. Onto Week 6 The 49ers will be hosting the Washington Commanders. Those of you in certain areas were treated to the end of the Commanders’ game against the New York Giants. I say that loosely because the overtime from that game bled into the 49ers/Seahawks game for about 10 minutes in some markets. That’s a discussion of its own. The Commanders ended their game with a tie due to some poor clock management in the final seconds of the game. The 49ers are favored by a touchdown, so hopefully we can relax after what we endured Sunday. The Seahawks have a short week and travel to face the Denver Broncos on Thursday Night Football. The Broncos are 3-2 and need to keep pace with the Kansas City Chiefs. With this being in Mile High, I expect this one to be interesting. A Broncos win would do the 49ers a huge favor. The Rams and Cardinals will square off in Los Angeles. Even though it’s the Rams, the Cardinals aren’t a draw, so the Rams will have to play in the afternoon on Sunday. Hopefully the Cardinals can keep that fight in them and hand the Rams another loss. 1st: San Francisco 49ers Next vs. Washington Commanders (Monday Night Football) 2nd: Seattle Seahawks; Next: at Denver Broncos (Thursday Night Football) 3rd: Los Angeles Rams; Next: vs. Arizona Cardinals 4th: Arizona Cardinals; Next: at Los Angeles Rams

title: Titans offensive line comes back down to earth in Week 5
summary: Everyone knew this Tennessee Titans offensive line was going to be tested versus the Houston Texans in Week 5. Prior to this matchup, they had been a surprising strength of a bad offense. The Texans’ defensive line definitely won the matchup. Titans quarterback Cam Ward was sacked on a season-high four occasions. We’ve seen worse […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - OCTOBER 04: Peter Skoronski #77, Dan Moore Jr. #75, and Gunnar Helm #84 of the Tennessee Titans line up against the Baltimore Ravens during the first half at M&T Bank Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images Everyone knew this Tennessee Titans offensive line was going to be tested versus the Houston Texans in Week 5 . Prior to this matchup, they had been a surprising strength of a bad offense. The Texans’ defensive line definitely won the matchup. Titans quarterback Cam Ward was sacked on a season-high four occasions. We’ve seen worse efforts from offensive lines in Tennessee, but this one was particularly bad throughout the second half. Ward was under constant duress and his escapability kept him from taking 7+ sacks. Ward was 23-of-36 passing for 170 yards, zero touchdowns, and one interception. On his interception, his arm was impacted by left tackle Dan Moore Jr., who was bull-rushed into the pocket. Speaking of Moore, he was downright bad. Pro Football Focus credited him with allowing a team-high seven pressures and one sack. Peter Skoronski, Austin Schlottmann, and JC Latham were also assigned blame for sacks. Atonio Mafi wasn’t blamed for a sack, but had the Titans’ worst pass-blocking grade (PFF) at 28.2 in true pass sets. The offensive line was also collectively whistled for four penalties. Two of them wiped out explosive passing plays. The Titans aren’t good enough on offense (duh) to have the offensive line eliminate explosive passing gains because they got avoidable penalties. The run-blocking effort was also terrible. Tony Pollard was limited to 3.7 yards per carry, rushing for 52 yards via 14 attempts. Tyjae Spears gained zero yards on two carries and lost a fumble. Kalel Mullings ran once for three yards. From Ward to Brian Daboll and the playmakers, the Titans have massive issues all over the offense. That’s why they’re currently scoring a league-low 11.6 points per contest. But the offensive line was another unit that totally let the offense down on Sunday. It was an all-around embarrassing effort.
