title: Power Rankings Week 6: Ties that bind the Washington Commanders to NFL’s basement
summary: The Washington Commanders are 1-3-1 and everyone is still talking about the embarrassing finish to their game against the Giants that ended in a 27-27 tie. We’ve gone over what went down, and everyone’s been trying to piece together who gets some, or all, of the blame for why the Commanders didn’t kick a field […]
full_text: Oct 11, 2026; Landover, Maryland, USA; Washington Commanders head coach Dan Quinn reacts after the game against the New York Giants at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Amber Searls-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Washington Commanders are 1-3-1 and everyone is still talking about the embarrassing finish to their game against the Giants that ended in a 27-27 tie. We’ve gone over what went down, and everyone’s been trying to piece together who gets some, or all, of the blame for why the Commanders didn’t kick a field goal before time ran out on their chance at a critical division victory. The bigger picture is the Commanders are sitting firmly in the bottom group of NFL teams after Week 5. They are 0-2-1 in the NFC East, and had the opportunity to get within one game of the Giants, who still sit atop the division at 3-1-1. The calls to fire Dan Quinn continue to grow, and the goodwill he got from an upset win over the reigning Super Bowl-champion Seattle Seahawks has long faded from most fans’ memories. They are ready for a change in coaches and a change in direction for Washington. Jayden Daniels made his return after missing 2 1/2 games due to another elbow dislocation. He made the Giants pay with his legs, and had the Commanders up by 14 points in the 4th quarter. The end-of-regulation gaffe has brought negative attention on the coaching staff, but Daniels is also catching blame for his role as the player with the ball in his hands on the final play. The Power Rankers have dropped the Commanders to the nether realms of the league, never to be heard from again unless Jayden makes a highlight play. The Commanders head to California this week to take on the #1 team on a lot of power rankings lists, the San Francisco 49ers. Washington opened as big underdogs (+7.5), and there isn’t much faith out there for a Seahawks-type upset after Sunday’s demoralizing ending. Will the Commanders be able to pull it together after the Week 7 bye or could another bad outcome lead to big changes on their off week? High: 20 Low: 30 Average: 26.6 #20 Walter Football I think we’ve seen enough from Dan Quinn as a head coach. There’s no reason the Redskins should have run a play when they could have just kicked the field goal. Quinn is a brilliant defensive coordinator, but he has now failed twice as a head coach, and the Redskins need to go in a different direction next year. Last week: 20 #25 Yahoo Sports (Schwab) Let’s wait a moment to pile on Dan Quinn, Jayden Daniels and whoever else was responsible for the fiasco at the end of Sunday’s tie. There were other issues. The Commanders allowed a field goal and three touchdowns on the Giants’ first four possessions of the second half. They had a 27-13 lead with just over 11 minutes left and couldn’t win. The Commanders couldn’t make a play against Jameis Winston to clinch a victory. And with a chance to ice the game with a 27-20 lead or win the game in the final 1:43 of regulation or after a missed Giants field goal in overtime, the Commanders punted three times. Those were failures too and can’t be forgotten. And obviously the end of the game was inexcusable. The Commanders were rudderless as the clock ran out, and that’s alarming. Quinn doesn’t call offensive or defensive plays so a stupefying failure in clock management at the end is a really bad look for him. Daniels has to be more aware as well. It’s not impossible for the Commanders to rebound from blowing a shot at a win Sunday, but it was embarrassing and will affect them all season in the NFC East race, if they ever get back in it. Last week: 25 Fox Sports (Vacchiano) What the hell was that? There’s really not much more to say than that after the way the Commanders lost (OK, tied) the Giants on Sunday. It was bad enough that they wasted a triumphant return performance by QB Jayden Daniels that was giving them hope for the rest of their season. It was worse that head coach Dan Quinn ’s defense forgot how to play in the second half and let the Giants shove them down the field and almost win the game. Letting the clock run out in overtime when you’re staring at a short, game-winning field goal? It’s inexcusable. And it’s on the coach — or more accurately, their soon-to-be-former coach. Stat To Know : The Commanders had an 89% chance to win immediately before the final play of overtime against the Giants. Last week: 25 Sporting News (Iyer) The good news is Jayden Daniels is healthy and doing his running thing. The Commanders are now 12-4-1 when he gets 8 or more rushing attempts in a game. He dropped 103 yards for 9 carries on the Giants, the second time he’s hit a century. Although the tie with the Giants stinks, his team should be thrilled to see Daniels back doing his thing. Last week: 24 NBC Sports (Wirth) Jayden Daniels had a monster game on the ground in his return, but cost his team an overtime win by not throwing the ball out of bounds on the final play. What a frustrating ending. Last week: 26 NFL Spin Zone (Bedinger) Jayden Daniels was back for the Washington Commanders in Week 5, and he was back to doing Jayden Daniels things. Unfortunately, so was the Commanders’ defense… With a… commanding …27-13 lead at the start of the 4th quarter, the Washington defense promptly gave up back-to-back touchdown drives. One of nine plays, the next of 10 plays. It was absolutely atrocious. Then, as both the Commanders and Giants traded the football in overtime, it came down to an obvious field goal attempt for Washington, but as they were trying to set up the field goal for their kicker, they ended up accidentally running out the clock. You simply can’t make this stuff up. What should have been a clear win for the Commanders – multiple times over – accidentally became a tie . And nobody likes those. Yikes. Sportsnaut (Johnson) An embarrassing end-of-game sequence for Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders . It’s a shame, too, because the second-year quarterback returned to the field with a bang (103 rushing yards and 2 touchdowns) on a Sunday when the Commanders’ rushing attack looked better than it has in more than a year. Unfortunately, it’s all going to be difficult to remember because Daniels’ handling of the clock in the final seconds resulted in a tie. Last week: 25 The Score It was supposed to be a great day for the Commanders, who saw Jayden Daniels return from injury and were really close to a divisional victory Sunday over the Giants. The chaotic tie feels like a loss for Washington, but at least Daniels is back, and the NFC East is a complete disaster right now. Last week: 25 Big Blue View (Falato) Washington was a disaster in that end-of-game situation. Getting Jayden Daniels back is huge for Washington, but the Giants’ defense shut down the offense —for the most part. Daniels, though, has to do a better job at the end of the game to secure that victory. Last week: 24 Team Rankings Last week: 26 #27 The Athletic (Graff/Kendall) Who have you beaten? Seahawks Has a tie ever felt like more of a loss? There are so many questions coming out of this one. How did Jayden Daniels not understand the situation? How did Dan Quinn not have his team better prepared for that late-game moment? In a way, that sums up where the Commanders sit after a promising 2024 season: just a lot of questions with no great results. Last week: 26 Bleacher Report This writer isn’t going to say the Commanders should fire head coach Dan Quinn now. That isn’t going to save what appears to be another lost season in the nation’s capital. But this year should be his last. Despite Quinn’s defensive background, Washington continues to struggle on that side of the ball. The Commanders were 26th in the league in pass defense entering Week 5, and that number isn’t getting any better after Jameis Winston carved them up. There’s also the poor clock management in overtime. Jayden Daniels deserves some blame, but the coaching staff must ensure its quarterback understands the…

Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Commanders fans and fans across the country. title: Commanders: Josh Harris “faces a near-revolt among the team’s fans”
summary: The Daily Slop – 13 October 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Bullock’s Film Room […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MD - AUGUST 14: Head coach Dan Quinn and managing partner Josh Harris of the Washington Commanders interact before the preseason game against the Miami Dolphins at Northwest Stadium on August 14, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Daily Slop – 13 October 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Bullock’s Film Room (subscription) Commanders offense struggles vs Giants Cover-0 blitzes On that three-and-out, the Giants found something that worked. On third and eight with just under six minutes remaining in the game, the Giants called a Cover-0 blitz. For those that don’t know, Cover-0 is an all-out blitz where the defense assigns a single defender for each eligible receiver, and the rest of the defenders rush. It’s risky because it’s pure man coverage without any safety help, but it also guarantees the defense can rush one more defender than the offense can block. Most teams that run Cover-0 in today’s NFL will line up almost every defender on the line of scrimmage and let the offense know it’s coming. Instead, the Giants try to show their normal base defense, but there are hints that a blitz is coming. The slot defender gives it away a bit, as do the safeties. The safeties are showing two-high, but also they’re shifted. One is in the middle of the field while the other is more over Dyami Brown in the slot. The Giants are a man coverage team, so it’s unusual to matchup a safety against a receiver in the slot. The biggest hint comes just before the snap, as the linebackers and slot corner all step forward to join the rush. But at that point it’s too late in the playclock for Jayden Daniels to change anything, so he snaps the ball. He looks to his left off the snap and appears to see the slot corner blitzing. He knows he doesn’t have anyone available to pick up that blitz, so his instinct is to take off running. Unfortunately, there’s not really anywhere for him to go and he ends up sacked. The embarrasing end to the game has overshadowed a pretty significant issue for the Commanders offense. The Giants spammed Cover-0 and the Commanders took far too long to find even the most basic of answer. I broke it all down: https://t.co/tNaWsMXxYR pic.twitter.com/NoRDlTg1OQ — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) October 12, 2026 ESPN Making sense of the Giants-Commanders tie If you want to know how much of a disaster the end of this game was for the Commanders, ask the Giants. After coming back from 14 points down in the fourth quarter, the Giants were in position to win this game in overtime, only for running back Cam Skattebo to fumble in field goal range. A stunned Giants team then allowed 51 yards on the next four plays, pushing the Commanders into position for their own game-winning field goal with 55 seconds to go. After those seconds came off the clock and the tie was confirmed, Giants defenders celebrated like they had just won the Super Bowl. John Harbaugh, who actually has won a Lombardi Trophy, might not have been any less ecstatic. “I wanted to get off the field before they could take it away from us,” said Harbaugh, describing the tie like it was free money he found on the ground. If the Giants could have fit the stadium’s goalposts on the plane back to New Jersey, you get the feeling that they might have torn them down before leaving. With 55 seconds to go, the Commanders were facing a first-and-10 on the Giants’ 26-yard line. The Commanders were obviously already in field goal range for rookie Drew Stevens, but amid rainy conditions, this had been an adventurous game for kickers. Stevens missed the opening extra point of the game wide left, while Giants kicker Dominic Zvada had missed field goal attempts from 46, 50 and 57. You would hope that Stevens would be able to make a 44-yard attempt if the Commanders didn’t get any additional yardage, and given that Skattebo had just fumbled while the Giants were in position to kick a 42-yard field goal, there had to be some trepidation on the part of coach Dan Quinn and first-year offensive coordinator David Blough. The Commanders could have essentially kneeled twice and brought Stevens on for a field goal here while draining the clock and preventing the Giants from getting the ball in case of a missed kick. Instead, they elected to try to pick up additional yardage. Rachaad White runs for 2 yards Nothing wild here, as the Commanders run a simple shotgun handoff to White for 2 yards. With 50 seconds on the clock as White’s tackled, the Commanders don’t need to be in any sort of rush. If they want to run the clock down as much as possible, they can line up, kneel inside of 40 seconds on second down on Stevens’ preferred hashmark, spike the ball again with several seconds left on third down and then kick on fourth down to win the game. By the time Daniels gets back to the line of scrimmage, there are 17 seconds left on the game clock. Blough’s playcall includes motion from the tight end, which takes another four seconds. By the time the Commanders snap the ball, the game clock is down to 12 seconds. There’s no way they can run the ball with enough time to reliably spike it on the next snap. The operation leading to this final play was a disaster. There’s no reason the Commanders even needed to run another offensive play, let alone a pass play. It’s absolutely the wrong time to be changing personnel and calling a play that requires pre-snap motion. Passing the ball in this situation isn’t in itself a disaster, although it wouldn’t be my first choice. The Giants had been zero blitzing Daniels throughout the game to try to force sacks or quick throws. With the proper instruction, this play isn’t a disaster. Daniels takes the snap and looks toward tight end Ben Sinnott in the flat, but Kayvon Thibodeaux has dropped into coverage and takes away his throwing lane. That’s not the end of the world. Throw the ball away over Sinnott’s head, stop the clock and kick the field goal. Very clearly, the information that needed to be conveyed to Daniels was not passed along before communication cut off with 15 seconds to go on the play clock. Daniels does not play out this sequence like someone who knows time is at all of the essence, likely because he believes the Commanders still have a timeout. After the throw to the flat is taken away, Daniels doesn’t throw the ball away or look toward any of his other receivers. He goes to tuck and run with the ball to pick up an extra yard or two, making it back to the line of scrimmage . There’s a reason Daniels took responsibility after the game. He’s partially to blame. Of course, there’s also a reason Quinn took responsibility after the game, too. It’s his job to make sure that the big-picture game management decisions are communicated appropriately To read more of this article, CLICK HERE “If I were a Commanders fan, I would never look at Jayden Daniels the same way… I do not think this defines him, but I am telling you for me, it would take a Magic Johnson-like rest of 80s for me to fully trust him in situational game management.” @getnickwright explains: pic.twitter.com/w3Bo6H2Wpo — First Things First (@FTFonFS1) October 12, 2026 As any head coach should do, DQ is shielding big time. — COMMANDERS FOOTBALL (@HogsHaven) October 12, 2026 Front Office Sports Dan Quinn’s Job Security in Doubt After Commanders Clock Fiasco It seemed unlikely as of Monday morning that the Commanders will fire Quinn this week. One source familiar with the team’s inner workings told Front Office Sports that was not the Commanders’ plan at this point. Even so, Quinn’s exit also seemed increasingly inevitable, perhaps a matter of when more so than if. The Commanders are 1-3-1 and in last place in the NFC East in the third season…

summary: Down went #1 in Week 6 of college football. The Red River Rivalry between #1 Texas and Oklahoma went to the Sooners. Although Arch Manning threw for three touchdowns, he also threw a pick-six and a late interception to set up the game-winning field goal. In the matchup between #2 Georgia and #6 Alabama, a […]
full_text: BLOOMINGTON, IN - SEPTEMBER 12: Indiana Hoosiers WR Nick Marsh (11) warms up prior to a college football game between the Howard Bison and Indiana Hoosiers on September 12, 2026 at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, IN. (Photo by James Black/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Down went #1 in Week 6 of college football. The Red River Rivalry between #1 Texas and Oklahoma went to the Sooners. Although Arch Manning threw for three touchdowns, he also threw a pick-six and a late interception to set up the game-winning field goal. In the matchup between #2 Georgia and #6 Alabama, a controversial no-call on what appeared to be pass interference by the Bulldogs helped them hold on to the lead in Tuscaloosa. With their starting quarterback Dante Moore recovering from a concussion, Oregon’s playoff chances all but faded away against a UCLA team that looks for real but lost it’s starting quarterback for the remainder of the season. Elsewhere in the Big Ten, #7 Indiana needed two fourth quarter touchdowns to survive the Nebraska Cornhuskers. Things will only get tougher for Indiana as they go to Columbus and take on Jeremiah Smith and #4 Ohio State. Texas, now ranked #7, will try to rebound against Florida, while #1 Georgia will take on Auburn. In what is likely their toughest test of the season, #2 Notre Dame will go to Utah to face off against #8 BYU. The SEC will feature a number of ranked-on-ranked matchups: #16 Mississippi State vs. #22 LSU, #13 Missouri vs. #9 Ole Miss, and #6 Alabama vs. #14 Tennessee. Finally, #18 Oklahoma State and their QB Drew Mestemaker, who’s looking more and more like the top quarterback in the draft, will play #20 Houston. Here are a few players who had a good week and might be able to help out the Commanders. Let me know what you think about these prospects and feel free to post players that stood out to you. LaNorris Sellers | QB | RS Junior | South Carolina LaNorris Sellers is a frustrating NFL prospect. He looks the part of an NFL quarterback. He’s 6’3”, 238 pounds, has a big arm, and he’s mobile. When Sellers plays his best, there are the slightest glimpses of Cam Newton. Those glimpses were on full display when the Gamecocks played Florida. Sellers found open receivers and threw the ball with accuracy. He even made some tight window throws downfield. The problem is Sellers is very inconsistent. As an example, he only completed 44% of his passes against Towson earlier this season. He also needs to read defenses more quickly and be more decisive as a playmaker. In the right place, Sellers might develop into a starter, but I think he would be a quality backup at the next level. The Gamecocks beat the Gators, and Sellers went 23 of 35, a completion percentage of 66%, four touchdowns through the air and one on the ground. lanorris sellers vs florida. pic.twitter.com/nv1fpGiIoC — . (@wrldofjordan_) October 12, 2026 Isaac Brown | RB | Junior | Louisville Isaac Brown is a home-run hitter. At 5’9”, 190 lbs, Brown is smaller, but he’s stout. Brown does many of the things an NFL running back must do. He’ll run between the tackles for positive yards and catch the ball out of the backfield. But Brown’s super power is his speed. If he can get in space, it is unlikely anyone will be able to catch him. Where Brown is lacking is that he’s not a particularly creative runner that will make defenders miss in space, and he’s not powerful enough to consistently break tackles and churn out tough yardage. Brown had a career-high 235 yards and two touchdowns on 17 carries in a win over Florida State. Top 10 Fastest Max Speed | Week 6 1 | 21.8 MPH Isaac Brown @isaac6brown_ RB Louisville IGA Score™ : 94.5 #ReelSpeed pic.twitter.com/wRVcC7Wgl3 — Reel Analytics (@RAanalytics) October 12, 2026 Nick Marsh | WR | Junior | Indiana The Commanders need a number one receiver and Indiana looks like they have two prospects that can be just that. I discussed Charlie Becker earlier this year, now it’s Nick Marsh’s turn. A transfer from Michigan State, Marsh is every bit of 6’3”, 210 pounds, and he uses that size to bully defensive backs. Yet at that size, he moves like a smaller receiver through the stems of his routes. He looks like he has plenty of speed to run away from defenders after catch. Another thing about Marsh is he will block his behind off. In the discussion for the second receiver to be drafted after Jeremiah Smith, Marsh made a strong case against Nebraska. He made six catches for 187 yards and two touchdowns as the Hoosiers handed the Cornhuskers their first loss. Nick Marsh is playing like a top-20 pick pic.twitter.com/fvyB1yieAJ — James Foster (@NoFlagsFilm) October 10, 2026 Top 10 Fastest Max Speed | Week 6 10 | 20.6 MPH Nick Marsh @TheSticks_11 WR @IndianaFootball IGA Score™ : 86.6 #ReelSpeed pic.twitter.com/nhcOZOJnDR — Reel Analytics (@RAanalytics) October 12, 2026 Patrick Overmyer | TE | Senior | Houston One bright spot of the Commanders’ game against the Giants was Chig Okonkwo showing a little of what made him a coveted free agent. Patrick Overmyer is another prospect that is a receiving threat as a tight end. Overmyer stands 6’5” and weighs 240 pounds. Houston mostly uses Overmyer flexed off the line as a big slot receiver. From that spot, he is a mismatch for many defenders: too fast for linebackers and too big for defensive backs. They often line him up in the backfield where he either lead blocks or sneaks out for a pass. If the Commanders want to be creative with their use of a tight end, Overmeyer should be on their list of draft prospects. He had eight receptions for 83 yards and four touchdowns in a win over Kansas State. UTTERLY UNREAL 😱 Patrick Overmyer rakes in 4⃣ TDs in #22 Houston's dominate win Overmyer Highlights vs. K-State 🎬 @UHCougarFB pic.twitter.com/VR4YSyldNN — Big 12 Studios (@big12studios) October 10, 2026 Matt Craycraft | C | Senior | Duke It wasn’t all bad for Lucas Patrick against the Giants, but I saw multiple plays where he was knocked into the backfield by defensive tackles. Matt Craycraft has started at center for the Blue Devils since 2023. He’s a smart player, not because he goes to Duke, but because he’s been named All-ACC Academic 2023-2025. On the field, Craycraft is simply a solid player in the middle of the line. At 6’3”, 305 pounds, Craycraft is athletic enough to play in a zone-blocking scheme and strong enough for a gap-blocking scheme. His awareness in pass protection allows him to identify incoming blitzers, recognize twisting rushers, and block defenders in space. It’d be nice to see him play a little nastier and finish his blocks with authority. Although the Blue Devils did not get the win against Georgia Tech, he helped their running back Nate Sheppard gain almost 100 yards both rushing and receiving. Craycraft is #72. Xavier Gilliam | DT | Junior | Tennessee The Commanders run defense has been one of the best in the NFL. But, it needs more players who can win one-on-one matchups in the pass game. Xavier Gilliam has terrorized offenses this season. He’s a local product that played at Quince Orchard before two seasons at Penn State. The volunteers have unleashed the 6’2”, 305 pound transfer. He is explosive off the line of scrimmage and relentless forcing the issue into the backfield. Gilliam combines his initial quickness with various moves to maneuver past defenders. He is strong enough to bench press blockers and disengage to make a play. Gilliam lines up as a nose for Tennessee, but he’d likely play defensive end for the Commanders, kicking inside in four-man fronts. Gilliam helped Tennessee defeat Arkansas with four tackles, a sack, and a forced fumble that he recovered. #Tennessee DT Xavier Gilliam (2) has been lights out for the Volunteers. He's played like a R1 pick He's up to 22 pressures, six sacks, and 21 run-stop tackles for the season Violence, quickness, and power are the three words I'd use to describe his game pic.twitter.com/mwtXRKcuml — Daniel…

title: NFL Week 6 latest intel, buzz questions, news, fantasy tips: What we're hearing
summary: What is going on with the Eagles?! We have intel on Philly's three-game slide, three remaining unbeaten teams, QBs at risk of being benched, potential WR trades and more.
full_text:
Somehow, we have already made it to Week 6 of the  2026 NFL season . And insiders Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano have been making calls to sources around the league for the latest news and notable buzz.

 On the positive side, there is still a trio of undefeated teams. (The Chiefs had a Week 5 bye, so they are 4-0, while the 49ers and the Vikings are both 5-0.) Which of the three has earned the most confidence from people around the league? But on the other side of things, some teams are really struggling as we hit Week 6. The Eagles have lost three straight games and have fallen apart in the fourth quarter in the past two. Is the panic meter rising in Philadelphia? Could we see changes?

 Speaking of changes, are any quarterbacks in danger of getting benched? Could we see more wide receivers on the move before the trade deadline as some offenses try to find a spark? It's all here, as Jeremy and Dan answer big questions, hand out useful fantasy football nuggets and empty their reporting notebooks heading into Week 6.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Eagles concern | Top undefeated 
 WR trades | Possible QB benchings 
 Fantasy football advice 

 
 

 How concerned are the Eagles amid three straight losses? 
 Graziano: Pretty concerned. This is a team that just saw a nearly complete overhaul of its offensive line last week , and not all of it was intentional. Lane Johnson 's retirement leaves a significant hole on the line and in the locker room. The Eagles are also still awaiting Landon Dickerson 's return from injury , and they're counting on significant contributions from the likes of Drew Kendall , Willie Lampkin and third-round rookie Markel Bell . This comes while still breaking in rookie wide receiver Makai Lemon , playing the past two games without top wideout DeVonta Smith and missing the top three running backs from their depth chart.

 The defense has looked better the past couple of weeks -- but it wasn't able to carry the Eagles through the early part of the season as they had hoped it would while the offense found itself under first-year coordinator Sean Mannion. That offense is dealing with a lot more than just growing pains right now, and after consecutive losses in which the Eagles' win probability exceeded 96% , there's reason to wonder where they'll find the leadership to get them through a tough part of their season.

 Fowler: Yeah, my sense is the concern is quite high. The Eagles sought to implement an offense that, in part, utilizes play-action passes over the middle to match a potent running game. But that's not working as intended. The offense ranks in the bottom third in play-action usage. It ranks 31st in total offense. Jalen Hurts struggles at times throwing inside the numbers, which was apparent Sunday in London. The impending return of Saquon Barkley and Smith will help, but I'm not sure that will solve the problems that run deeper than one or two players.

 

 The hiring of Mannion signaled a shift in thinking, an implementation of more under-center and play-action work for Hurts. A transitional period was expected, if not inevitable. But the Eagles now have to rebuild the offensive line at the same time, which is a huge challenge. It can't be ignored that the Eagles needed a last-minute drive in Week 2 against still-winless Tennessee to avoid a 1-4 start, a reality no one in Philadelphia will tolerate very long.

 Graziano: That becomes the question, right? If they aren't going to tolerate it, then what are they going to do about it? We know general manager Howie Roseman is always on the lookout for trades to improve the roster, and the NFC East is certainly there for the taking . But the way the Eagles conduct themselves at this year's trade deadline will tell us a lot about how they view themselves. The Cam Jurgens trade wasn't a sign of a roster-wide sell-off; they were done with Jurgens, and the return was good . But if they lose a couple of more games in the next three to four weeks, things could get very interesting in Philly.

 Fowler: Very interesting. The schedule is manageable, even favorable. On deck is a two-game home slate against Carolina and Dallas, then at Washington, followed by the Giants at home and a perfectly placed Week 10 bye. After that comes Pittsburgh, Dallas, Arizona and Indianapolis.

 The good news is all of those games are winnable. But if the Eagles don't capitalize on that stretch, it feels as if there will be change at some level. Because while the defensive formula is sustainable, Philadelphia is going on two seasons of bad offense. So, Roseman might not be done making moves, and the offense seems like a potential spot to watch in that regard.

 

 
 Which of the three undefeated teams is getting the most confidence around the league? 
 Fowler: Kansas City was mentioned most when I asked league evaluators this week. The Chiefs' running game has been a revelation with Kenneth Walker III . Patrick Mahomes looks more comfortable by the week on his surgically repaired knee . Steve Spagnuolo's defense is as stingy as usual. The Chiefs are light at receiver, but a pass-catching trio of Travis Kelce , Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy is plenty viable. (Rice is out with a hamstring issue but will be back.) Basically, the Chiefs are the team with the fewest concerns out of the group.

 San Francisco has been tremendous thus far -- you could argue no team is playing better -- but the looming question is whether the 49ers can stay healthy. That has been the question with them. And Minnesota rolls out a championship defense that has been enough to offset the team's 27th-ranked total offense -- so far. Whether Minnesota can win in January with this offensive attack is a real question unless it can prove otherwise in the coming weeks.

 Graziano: Agreed on all accounts. The Chiefs seem to be impressing people the most in terms of the sustainability of their success. But people are taking note of what Kyle Shanahan is doing in San Francisco amid its annual cascade of injuries . After last season -- when the 49ers lost Brock Purdy , Fred Warner , Nick Bosa and others for extended periods and still managed to win 12 games and make it to the second round of the playoffs -- Shanahan's message to his locker room was that San Francisco could overcome just about anything. The Niners are continuing to play with that mentality, and they're in pretty good shape at 5-0, with head-to-head victories over each of the other three teams in the NFC West.

 

 Fowler: San Francisco defensive coordinator Raheem Morris is pushing the right buttons. He has extensive knowledge of the NFC West from his time with the Rams and has a formula to combat the divisional gauntlet. The edge rusher position is still worrisome, as 2025 first-round pick Mykel Williams is working his way back and Bosa can't stay healthy . Perhaps GM John Lynch will look for a short-term fix at the trade deadline. But the 49ers' offense can score against anyone, and Purdy has proved that he stands with the best in the league's quarterback hierarchy.

 What do you make of Minnesota's offense, Dan? This is a timely bye week for coach Kevin O'Connell, a proven playcaller, to identify what works and accentuate the strengths of the passing game. O'Connell has smartly leaned into the running game while navigating the Kyler Murray transition, calling roughly 30 rushes per game. Aaron Jones Sr.  has been up to the task with 410 rushing yards, and Jordan Mason ( injured reserve, thumb ) should be back soon.

 Graziano: The Vikings are a fascinating case because they have largely been carried by Brian Flores' stifling defensive game plans. But they felt the offense showed improvement during the Week 4 victory over Miami and continued that progress in the Week 5 triumph in New Orleans. The Vikings felt Murray was distributing the ball better and using his legs more effectively than he had in previous outings. Murray missed most of the Week 1 game and the entire Week 2 contest…

title: Seven things Solak thinks entering NFL Week 6: Time for Mendoza? Cowboys issues?
summary: Get ready for Week 6 with takes on two QB situations, two teams with defensive issues, two coaches on the hot seat and more.
full_text:
Are you excited for NFL Week 6 ? Sure, Bills-Rams just ended like eight hours ago. But the Seahawks and Broncos are playing in another iteration of the Russell Wilson bowl on Thursday ! The Texans' season hangs on the brink against the Jaguars in London on Sunday morning . Caleb Williams should be back for the Bears against the Falcons Sunday afternoon ! And Micah Parsons ... apparently won't play in his revenge game against the Cowboys on Sunday night . Whatever.

 Every Tuesday of the NFL season , I'll turn the page from the previous week to the upcoming one with seven things I think. These aren't full-scale predictions. They aren't concrete takeaways from the past week of NFL action, either; those are fired off Sunday or Monday. Instead, these are the uncertain topics. They are things that might be true, but it'll probably take the next few games to find out. And at the bottom, you'll find a few extra half-thoughts ... just those little inklings I'm unable to shake.

 
 Subscribe: 'ESPN's Leaguewide' 

 
 This week, I'll start with a quarterback change I'm expecting to see soon, touch on a couple of defenses in need of big talent lifts, and anticipate an improvement for an undefeated team. Here are seven things I think ahead of Week 6.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 One more start for Cousins? 
 Seahawks need more than Charbonnet? 
 Two head coaches in trouble? 
 Murray, Vikings rounding into form? 
 Cowboys need to sit some vets? 
 Time for the Cards to look at Beck? 
 Massive issues in the Bears' secondary? 
 Some extra inklings 

 
 

 

 I think ... Kirk Cousins  will get one more start before Fernando Mendoza time 
 Cousins has been totally solid for the Raiders this season. Relative to expectation and contract, there has been nothing disappointing about his play.

 That said, the Patriots went after him Sunday . New England defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr blitzed Cousins on 41.2% of his first-half dropbacks, per NFL Next Gen Stats, and got a 53% pressure rate and two sacks for his trouble. Although Cousins is a wily veteran capable of identifying blitzes and carving them up with hot routes, he's also 38 years old and was not particularly mobile even a decade ago, let alone now.

 The Patriots' game plan was apparent and smart. With starting cornerbacks  Christian Gonzalez  and Carlton Davis III  both unavailable due to injuries and a couple of depth corners also laid up, Kuhr tried to break the Raiders' passing game at the pocket before Cousins could attack his inexperienced cover men. On paper, it didn't work too great -- Cousins was 10-for-15 with 123 yards and a score through two quarters. But it got the Patriots off the field when they needed it.

 Here's a Cover 0 snap on third-and-5 . Cousins can't backpedal fast enough to buy time on the pressure and can't get enough arm into the throw to drive it before the cornerback arrives. Charles Woods , the third-year corner making his first career start, has plenty of time to arrive for the pass breakup.

 

 Here's an extremely similar look on third-and-14 -- already a tough down to handle. Cousins hangs a vertical ball up for Tre Tucker against Kindle Vildor , who was called up from the Pats' practice squad. It's the right read and an open throw, but the ball is uncatchable.

 

 Now, a guy should not be benched for an uncatchable third-and-14 heave against Cover 0. But Kuhr was able to deploy this approach because he knew Cousins couldn't burn him with escapability and play extension. Once Kuhr manufactured the free rusher, he could tell his young corners with total confidence that the ball would come out fast. Drive on the first break. Play aggressively, attack the catch point. Don't worry about eyes in the backfield or long-developing routes -- those won't happen.

 Cousins has 10 dropbacks on the season in which he, at any point, starts to scramble. Only  Michael Penix Jr ., Matthew Stafford and Jordan Love have fewer. He has just three actual scrambles (dropbacks on which he crosses the line of scrimmage to run). Only 7.6% of his throws have come with him on the move (only Stafford and Jared Goff have lower percentages), and his average speed at release of 2.85 mph, per Next Gen Stats, is the lowest of all passers this season.

 Cousins simply does not move. Quarterbacks such as Stafford, Goff and Penix have much bigger arms to get away with this play style, while quarterbacks such as  Aaron Rodgers and Joe Burrow have their elite processing and accuracy to get away with it. At his age, Cousins doesn't have those cardinal traits. He has enough arm, and he certainly has plus accuracy and processing. But it's not enough to tip the scales back in his favor.

 This has not been a death knell for the Raiders through five weeks, as Cousins is 10th in the league in EPA per pressured dropback and 11th in success rate on pressured dropbacks. He's making do with what he has. But the limitation is apparent, and future opponents will attack it. The Raiders have the Bills in Week 6 , the Rams in Week 7 and the Jets in Week 8 . The Rams and Jets are above average in blitz rate on the season, and the Bills are right around average. They're going to come after Cousins and make the bet Kuhr did -- that eventually the Raiders' lack of a running game will stick them in third-and-long, and those blitzes will create early and errant throws.

 The Raiders might have a solution to this problem: the spry legs of Mendoza that have done little but warm a bench through five weeks.

 I have no doubt that the Raiders will initially be worse against pressures and blitzes when they first deploy Mendoza. He is a rookie and lacks the Spidey-sense that Cousins has honed over a decade-plus of NFL football. Mendoza will take bad sacks and throw the ball into coverage traps because that's what rookies do.

 

 But he'll also move. He will create second-reaction throws that have yet to exist in this offense. He'll allow head coach Klint Kubiak to dust off the rollout sections of his playbook, which were so integral for Sam Darnold in Seattle but have been shelved for Cousins in Vegas. Mendoza is not known as an elite mover, but he's totally functional -- and most importantly, leagues ahead of Cousins.

 To quickly pivot from Cousins to Mendoza might feel like an early abandonment of a well-laid developmental plan. But I would argue that the pivot is justified. The Raiders are currently 3-2 in a suddenly much-more-winnable AFC West than previously believed. Yes, the Chiefs are 4-0 -- but the Raiders went neck-and-neck with them in Week 4, and both the Broncos (3-2) and Chargers (0-5) have been clearly worse than Las Vegas through five weeks. The 1.5 games back should not deter the Raiders from pushing for the division -- and in that effort, potentially landing a wild-card berth regardless.

 I won't be too upset if they keep riding the Cousins train. Like I said, the lack of mobility is a problem but not one that has totally hamstrung an otherwise solid passing attack. The Raiders could defensibly stick with Cousins for another month or two and still prioritize Mendoza's development over anything else. After all, benching Cousins after Week 6 would give Mendoza to the Rams and (presumably)  Myles Garrett in Week 7 -- that's a stiff ask.

 But it's hard to win those first three games ... then lose two ... and not wonder if the team is closer to contention than expected. And then not wonder whether Mendoza's timeline should be accelerated to match.

 

 
 

 I think ... the Seahawks have too many eggs in the Zach Charbonnet basket 
 Last season, Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba had 15.1% of the team's total touches. That was the fourth-highest number for a non-running back leaguewide. His 36% target share was the highest for a single player since 2012 Brandon Marshall. It was incredible to see how successfully the Seahawks built the entire plane, especially in the passing game, out of JSN.

 Because we all thought the…

title: 2026 NFL Power Rankings: How all 32 teams stack up for Week 6
summary: How does every NFL team stack up heading into Week 6? We made our 1-32 list and picked the biggest defensive problem for every team.
full_text:
NFL teams are averaging 23.3 points in the 2026 season . Though some of those points have come from defensive touchdowns and one punt return TD from the Vikings, it's mostly an indicator that offenses are getting into scoring territory  a lot .

 So why are defenses struggling so much? In addition to our updated 1-32 rankings, we asked our NFL Nation reporters to pick out the biggest defensive issue for each team. From secondary depth to third-down defense, what is causing each team to falter?

 To form the list, our power panel of more than a dozen NFL analysts evaluates how all 32 teams stack up against one another. Here are a few highlights from this week's rankings:

 
 The Patriots have returned to the top 10 after back-to-back wins over the Bills and Raiders. Sunday's win was catalyzed by another strong performance from quarterback  Drake Maye , who led the team to its most points (45) and yards (536) in a game since 2021. The Patriots could continue their hot streak with matchups against the Jets and Dolphins in two of the next three weeks. 
 The Packers are also climbing back up our list after two losses in their first three games. Green Bay entered Sunday's matchup  against Chicago as 1.5-point underdogs, but it completely dominated the Bears to avenge  its wild-card loss last season. Quarterback Jordan Love 's 367 passing yards were the second most by any QB in Bears-Packers series history, per ESPN Research. 
 The bottom three teams in our rankings (Chargers, Titans and Dolphins) are all 0-5. It's the fifth time since the 1970 merger that three teams from the same conference have started a season with that record, per ESPN Research. Los Angeles had the most excruciating loss of the bunch this past weekend, blowing a seven-point lead with nine minutes left against the Broncos . 
 
 Let's get into the full list, starting with the same No. 1 team from last week.

 Previous rankings: Week 2 | Week 3  | Week 4  | Week 5 

 

 
 Jump to a team: 
 ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN 
 CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND 
 JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN 
 NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF 
 SEA | TB | TEN | WSH 

 
 

 

 1. San Francisco 49ers (5-0) 
 Week 5 result: Beat the Seahawks 32-29 
 Week 5 ranking: 1 

 Biggest issue on defense: Third-down efficiency

 

 Under new coordinator Raheem Morris , the Niners rank fifth in yards per play allowed (4.7) and have limited big plays as well as any team in the league. But they have struggled to get off the field consistently. The Niners rank 20th in third-down defense, giving up a first down on 40.8% of their opportunities. As a result, their defense has been on the field for 31 minutes, 12 seconds per game, which ranks 23rd in the NFL. -- Nick Wagoner 

 
 

 

 2. Kansas City Chiefs (4-0) 
 Week 5 result: Bye 
 Week 5 ranking: 2 

 Biggest issue on defense: Not enough sacks

 

 The Chiefs can generate pressure on the quarterback, whether it's via Chris Jones , George Karlaftis or rookie R Mason Thomas . But they have one of the biggest statistical anomalies of the 2026 season: zero sacks in the first month. Before their bye week , they couldn't put Raiders QB Kirk Cousins on the turf despite a season-high 21 pressures. If the Chiefs can start collecting sacks, their defense could be a top unit in the second half of the season. -- Nate Taylor 

 
 

 3. Buffalo Bills (4-1) 
 Week 5 result: Beat the Rams 37-34 (OT) 
 Week 5 ranking: 4 

 Biggest issue on defense: Letting offenses off the hook

 

 The Bills haven't had much issue pushing offenses backward on first down. But opponents have had far too much success extending drives in second-and-long and third-and-long situations. Plenty of this has to do with the Bills' dwindling cornerback depth, but that's hardly an excuse for how C.J. Stroud , Jared Goff ,  Drake Maye  and  Matthew Stafford  completed 74.6% of their passes for 558 yards and five touchdowns (posting a 80.8 QBR) on second downs against the Bills. -- Nick Suss 

 
 

 4. Seattle Seahawks (3-2) 
 Week 5 result: Lost to the 49ers 32-29 
 Week 5 ranking: 3 

 Biggest issue on defense: Not enough stops in the red zone

 

 The biggest problem for the Seahawks' defense might actually be their offense; the 44 points they've given up off turnovers is tied for most in the NFL. You have to look hard to find a true weakness with a unit that ranks second in both defensive EPA and ESPN's defensive efficiency metric, but the Seahawks are 27th in opponent red zone efficiency (75%) and tied for last in opponent goal-to-go efficiency (100%). Granted, they haven't allowed offenses to get that far down the field often -- only 12 times inside their 20 (tied for fifth fewest) and seven times inside their 10 (tied for seventh fewest). -- Brady Henderson 

 
 

 5. Jacksonville Jaguars (4-1) 
 Week 5 result: Beat the Eagles 19-17 
 Week 5 ranking: 5 

 Biggest issue on defense:  Getting sacks from the edge

 

 It's nitpicky, considering the Jaguars are No. 1 in run defense and second in scoring defense, but they could do a better job of getting sacks from their edge rushers. Their 80 QB pressures are tied for sixth and 11 sacks rank ninth, but edge rushers  Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker  have only 3.5 sacks combined. They each had 1.5 sacks in the season opener against the Browns  but a combined half sack since (Walker on Sunday). Both are a large part of the run defense (63.8 yards per game) by setting the edge, but their sack production needs to increase. -- Michael DiRocco 

 
 

 6. Minnesota Vikings (5-0) 
 Week 5 result: Beat the Saints 23-13 
 Week 5 ranking: 9 

 Biggest issue on defense: Depth not tested yet

 

 It's not easy to find a negative indicator from a defense that has been the league's best this season, based on NFL Next Gen Stats' expected point average. But because the Vikings have been almost entirely healthy, their depth at multiple positions is untested. In fact, eight defensive players have been on the field for at least 80% of the snaps. That doesn't mean the backups would falter in more prominent roles. It's just hard to judge based on game reps. -- Kevin Seifert 

 
 
 

 7. Baltimore Ravens (4-1) 
 Week 5 result: Beat the Falcons 30-23 (OT) 
 Week 5 ranking: 6 

 Biggest issue on defense: Getting stops on third down

 

 The Ravens are allowing teams to convert 41.5% of their third downs, which ranks 20th in the NFL. It's frustrating because Baltimore seems to be winning on the early downs before giving up a big play on third down. Opposing quarterbacks are averaging 8.7 yards per attempt on third down, the fifth highest in the league. The Ravens gave up nine third-down conversions Sunday, which are the most they've given up in a game in two seasons.  The Rams' defense has been inconsistent at times, and it has only eight sacks this season (tied for sixth fewest in the NFL). But Los Angeles should get more sack production once the reigning Defensive Player of the Year is back on the field. Garrett, who had knee surgery in mid-September , is eligible to return to practice this week. title: 2027 NFL draft order projections for Round 1, chances for top pick, more
summary: ESPN's Football Power Index projects the 2027 NFL draft order for Round 1, complete with each team's chances to pick in the top five, in the top 10 and at No. 1.
full_text:
The 2027 NFL draft is still months away, but with the 2026 season underway, we're starting to track pick order in Round 1. Which teams are in position to add elite prospects in the top 10 next April? What about the top five ... or even at No. 1?

 What follows is not the current draft order based on records. It is a projection of what ESPN's Football Power Index thinks the order ultimately will be by the end of the season. Each week during the season, the FPI projects the draft order by simulating the remainder of the season 10,000 times. Game probabilities are based primarily on the model's team ratings and game locations. The draft order is determined by the records the model projects for each team after 17 games, as well as each team's average draft position across the simulations.

 So where do things stand? Here are the full sortable projections, complete with each team's chances to pick in the top five, in the top 10 and at No. 1.

 
 See more on the NFL draft 

 
 

 First-round picks that have been traded: 

 
 The Green Bay Packers ' selection was dealt to the Dallas Cowboys in the Micah Parsons trade . 
 The Indianapolis Colts ' selection was dealt to the New York Jets in the Sauce Gardner trade . 
 The Los Angeles Rams ' selection was dealt to the Cleveland Browns in the Myles Garrett trade . 
 The better of Dallas' two selections (either its own pick or the Packers' original pick) was dealt to the Jets in the Quinnen Williams trade .

title: Revisiting 2026 preseason bold predictions for 32 NFL teams: Which are on track?
summary: In the preseason, we made bold predictions for every NFL team, from Jordan Love's MVP case to Isaiah Likely's catch total. Which ones are on track? Which seem unlikely?
full_text:
Part of making preseason predictions is seeing how those forecasts actually fare. It's easy to predict something, but we also need to check on our predictions and hold ourselves accountable.

 Before Week 1, I made one bold prediction for every NFL team as part of our lookahead to the 2026 season . These were big swings -- things I thought could happen but would be upsets if they did. And five weeks into the season, we've learned a lot.

 That makes this a great time to dive back into those preview predictions and find out how things are going. Which ones are on track? Which might still happen? And which were so far off that we might as well scrap them for a completely new one? In some cases, five weeks means everything has changed. In others, not so much.

 Let's take a look and see where we stand for all 32 teams.

 

 
 Jump to a team: 
 ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN 
 CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND 
 JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN 
 NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF 
 SEA | TB | TEN | WSH 

 
 

 On target 
 

 Buffalo Bills 
 Original prediction: Wide receiver Keon Coleman will record 750 or more receiving yards and at least five touchdowns -- both career highs.
 

 Why it's on target: Coleman had been on a bit of a production tear on plays when DJ Moore was off the field until Monday night, when he managed only 7 receiving yards in a game that Moore missed. Still, Coleman's 224 receiving yards so far put him on pace for 761 yards over a full season. If Moore -- who did not play Monday due to a shoulder injury -- misses more time, that will help Coleman's cause. Not playing the Rams every week should, too.

 
 

 Jacksonville Jaguars 
 Original prediction: Cornerback Montaric Brown will record a worse-than-average yards allowed per coverage snap (1.1 per NFL Next Gen Stats).

 

 Why it's on target: Considering Brown is at 3.8 yards allowed per coverage snap, we're well on our way. The idea for this prediction was that Brown's strong 2025 campaign was fueled by on-ball results that tend not to be stable from year to year and that he would regress in 2026. So far, that looks right. Brown has missed all but six snaps in the past two games due to a hamstring injury.

 
 

 

 New York Giants 
 Original prediction: Tight end Isaiah Likely will lead the team in receptions.
 

 Why it's on target: Likely currently leads the Giants in receptions, with 33 catches to Malik Nabers ' 29. As Nabers continues to recover from the ACL injury he suffered last season, he might accrue more volume. But Likely is ahead right now and has proved to be a key part of this new Giants offense.

 
 

 Tennessee Titans 
 Original prediction: Cornerback Alontae Taylor will allow 1.4 yards per coverage snap or worse, per NFL Next Gen Stats.

 Why it's on target: Taylor is right on target at 1.4. Should that continue, this would be disappointing for the Titans after they signed Taylor in free agency following a 1.0 yards-per-coverage-snap season in 2025. But Taylor was at 1.6 in 2023 and 2024, which is a big reason I made this prediction. For context, the average for an outside cornerback is 1.1.

 

 

 Still a chance ... 
 

 Arizona Cardinals 
 Original prediction: The Cardinals will go 1-16.

 

 Why there's still a chance: I don't think this will hit anymore, especially since the Cardinals won their opener . But I won't quite throw this out yet because Arizona's remaining schedule is an absolute gauntlet. There could be winnable games against the Commanders, Jets and Saints down the road, but if the Cardinals can't win any of those, I could get the backdoor cover.

 
 

 Atlanta Falcons 
 Original prediction: Safety Xavier Watts will be a first- or second-team All-Pro.

 

 Why there's still a chance: Watts has one interception, one forced fumble and a half-sack as part of a Falcons defense that has been better than expected. He has allowed 0.8 yards per coverage snap -- higher than average for a safety, though I don't put a lot of stock in that number for safeties considering the variety and complexity of assignments at that position. This is a long shot, but you never know -- if Watts goes on an interception run, anything could happen.

 
 

 Baltimore Ravens 
 Original prediction: The Ravens' defense will rank in the top four in EPA per play.

 

 Why there's still a chance: Baltimore ranks 17th through five games. That's not ideal for making the top four, but it doesn't put the Ravens out of the running just yet, as we've seen their defenses turn it around in the second half of the season in recent years. Considering the talent the Ravens have and that they are playing under a new coach with a defensive background in Jesse Minter, I think it's at least feasible. Trey Hendrickson , who ranks sixth in pass rush win rate at edge, has missed the past two games due to a broken finger that required surgery . If Baltimore can get him back, that should help.

 
 

 Carolina Panthers 
 Original prediction: The Panthers will finish last in the NFC South.
 Why there's still a chance: Considering how well Carolina's offense has played, I sincerely doubt that I will be correct on this. But this is the NFC South, and you just never know. The Panthers are only 1.5 games out of last place, and I have a strong opinion of cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson , so their absences could really sting.

 

 

 
 

 Cincinnati Bengals 
 Original prediction: Running back Chase Brown will record at least 15 total touchdowns.

 

 Why there's still a chance: With only one score thus far, this prediction is off to a pretty rough start. But a big part of why I backed Brown was the Bengals having the easiest schedule in the NFL. The beginning of that schedule wasn't easy, and it gets lighter from here, so there should be plenty more touchdowns to come.

 
 

 Cleveland Browns 
 Original prediction: Quarterback Taylen Green will start at least four games.

 

 Why there's still a chance: The odds have dropped. I had figured the Browns would already be on to Shedeur Sanders by this point. Even though Deshaun Watson hasn't been quite as bad as expected, I still think that the Browns will make the move to Sanders relatively soon and that an end-of-year stint for Green remains in play.

 
 

 Dallas Cowboys 
 Original prediction: Kicker Brandon Aubrey will record the most field goals over expected, per NFL Next Gen Stats.

 

 Why there's still a chance: Aubrey is off to a slower start than I would have guessed, with 1.3 field goals made over expectation. That ranks 13th, and he has missed a PAT, too. But there's still plenty of time for him to move to the top.

 
 

 Denver Broncos 
 Original prediction: Cornerback Riley Moss will command a $17 million-per-year contract after this season, either with the Broncos or someone else.

 

 Why there's still a chance: Moss missed Week 5 with a rib injury, but he has allowed 1.1 yards per coverage snap (average) this season, per NFL Next Gen Stats. He picked off Trevor Lawrence in Denver's Week 2 win over the Jaguars but was also burned badly by Konata Mumpfield on a double move for a 48-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter against the Rams in Week 3 . I still feel good about this one, though.

 
 

 Detroit Lions 
 Original prediction:  Edge rusher  Aidan Hutchinson will win Defensive Player of the Year.

 

 Why there's still a chance: Four sacks and a 66th percentile pass rush win rate at edge isn't a bad start, but he's going to have to pick it up to fulfill this prediction. He has the talent level to do it, but the fact that the rest of the Lions' defense is looking so weak is going to hurt Hutchinson's sack total, which in turn will hurt his DPOY chances.

 
 

 

 Green Bay Packers 
 Original prediction:  Quarterback  Jordan Love will finish in the top three in MVP voting.

 

 Why there's still a chance: I was prepared to throw this one out ... until Week 5, when Love posted a 94 QBR in the Packers' 31-7 dismantling…

title: Super Bowl LXI odds: All 32 teams' odds to win the championship

full_text:
After beginning the season as the clear Super Bowl favorites at +500, the  Los Angeles Rams ' grip on the top spot has loosened significantly. title: Removing 'a dark cloud': How the Ravens' clutch play ended a 581-game streak
summary: Baltimore became the first team to win a game down by eight or more points in the final minute in four years.
full_text:
ATLANTA -- After receiving a game ball in the locker room for his game-ending interception, Baltimore Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton wanted to provide perspective to Sunday night's 30-23 overtime win over the Atlanta Falcons . 
 
 "The last couple of years, like ever since I've been here, that's a game that we would lose," Hamilton told his teammates and coaches. "This win right here, I feel like is us." 
 
 Hamilton was referring to the frustrating reputation that the Ravens had built with years of fourth-quarter collapses and coming up short in close games. But after an improbable comeback with backup quarterback Tyler Huntley , Baltimore believes there is a reversal of fortune happening after a clutch performance rarely seen in the NFL. 
 
 The Ravens became the first team in four years to win a game down by eight or more points in the final minute, breaking the 581-game losing streak for teams in that situation, according to ESPN Research. 
 
 "We talk about being at your best when your best is needed, and just like, [the team had] no flinch, no panic," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said. "That's a big step for us. And if we let it be, it can be a launch point for us to really, really get this thing rolling." 
 
 Baltimore had previously struggled in close games. From 2023 to 2025, the Ravens were 9-15 (.375) in games decided by seven points or fewer, which was the sixth-worst mark in the league over that span. 
 
 This season, Baltimore has won three straight games that have been determined by a one-score margin. In Week 3, Tyler Loop 's 56-yard field goal as time expired lifted the Ravens to a 34-31 win over the Dallas Cowboys in Rio. In Week 4, Malaki Starks ' leaping recovery of an onside kick sealed Baltimore's 24-18 victory over the Tennessee Titans . And on Sunday night, Hamilton's interception of Tua Tagovailoa closed out the game in overtime. 
 
 
 
 Minter pointed out how this string of nail-biters followed a 24-17 loss to the New Orleans Saints , a game in which Baltimore gave up 15 points in the fourth quarter. 
 
 "Confidence is gained by going through things and going through things together," Minter said. "And I don't know if we have the results of the last three weeks if the Saints game doesn't happen. So I think there's always ways you can take losses like that. You can learn from them and really, really try to improve and get better and look at the things that you did well and build on things." 
 
 On Sunday night, here is how the Ravens went from trailing 23-15 late in the fourth quarter to winning 30-23 over the course of four drives: 
 
 
 In a hurry-up offense, Huntley quickly moved Baltimore 71 yards in one minute, 51 seconds, completing all six of his passes to four different receivers. The Ravens tied the game at 23 when Huntley hit Devontez Walker for a 7-yard touchdown with 40 seconds remaining and running back Derrick Henry rushed for a two-point conversion. 
 On the last drive of the fourth quarter, Ravens outside linebacker Tavius Robinson beat two blockers off the right edge and hit Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr ., which forced him to sit out overtime with a rib injury. 
 After electing to take the ball first in overtime, Baltimore marched 68 yards on 14 plays, marking the longest touchdown drive in overtime in eight years. Huntley capped the possession by getting into the end zone on a 1-yard sneak. 
 Down 30-23, the Falcons' chance of coming back ended with Hamilton's first interception of the season. Hamilton felt Tagovailoa was trying to look him off, but he just watched his eyes to get the pick. 
 
 
 "I have said it a thousand times before, but big-time players make big-time plays in big-time games," Ravens defensive end Calais Campbell said. "And Kyle Hamilton is the best of us."  
 
 For nearly three quarters, it didn't seem like this was going to be a watershed moment for Baltimore. With quarterback  Lamar Jackson out with an ankle injury, the Ravens couldn't consistently finish off drives, totaling one touchdown, three field goals and four punts on the first nine possessions. Tight end Mark Andrews watched his fumble turn into a Falcons defensive touchdown and then failed to hold on to a two-point conversion that would have tied the game at 17 in the third quarter. The Baltimore defense couldn't get off the field, allowing Atlanta to convert nine of its first 15 third downs (60%).  
 
 "We were able to overcome adversity," Andrews said. "In some years past, we may not have been able to do that." 
 
 It marked the first time the Ravens had come back from a deficit of eight points or more in the final minute since 2021, when Baltimore beat the Indianapolis Colts  31-25 in overtime in Week 5. 
 
 "That is just us getting over some sort of hump or dark cloud," Hamilton said. "I am excited for the future."

title: How Bills QB Josh Allen has become a star on and off the field
summary: The Buffalo QB is racking up the endorsements and leaning on his Hollywood wife for advice.
full_text:
Editors note: This story was published ahead of the Bills' 37-34 overtime win against the Rams on Monday. 

 ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. -- Here's a dirty little secret of the advertising industry: Professional athletes can be divas too.

 Athletes have been pitching products in TV commercials for almost as long as there have been TV commercials. They act. They sing. They dance. They toss their game-worn jerseys to well-meaning kids who have reminded them of their long-lost innocence and they laugh -- holding the product they're sponsoring label out, of course -- as choirs sing infectious jingles about how all the regular people at home wish they could be a little bit more like their heroes.

 One thing they don't do all that often in commercials is, well, play sports. There are plenty of reasons why this is the case, but one that's less talked about is that some athletes and their agents come on set with established constraints. It's why so many commercials for sports drinks and athletic wear consist of sluggers pointing their bats to the camera and basketball players setting up for slow-motion free throws.

 

 It's the way it is. Unless you're working with Josh Allen .

 "Some athletes will be like 'I'll give you three throws' or 'I'll kick the ball four times' or 'I'll run at no more than 50%' or whatever," said Alex Bower, former creative director at TBWA/Chiat/Day who wrote Allen's 2024 Gatorade campaign. "Josh, we shot him in L.A., it was a hot day. He gave us a lot of takes of him running lines and throwing the ball full pelt. He committed. We kind of used his shots heavily in the edit because it looked real because he was giving it 100%."

 Allen, the Buffalo Bills quarterback and betting favorite to win the NFL's MVP award (+280 on DraftKings entering Week 5), is a commercial star. He has endorsed Nike, New Era, New Balance, Nationwide and Natrol Sleep, and that's just the part of his portfolio that begins with "N." As the Bills (3-1) prepare for their "Monday Night Football" showdown at the Los Angeles Rams (2-2) at SoFi Stadium ( 8:15 p.m. ET, ESPN ), the prospect of having to perform in Hollywood for a national TV audience will hardly be novel for Allen -- who in addition to his commercial work is also CEO of his own production studio and is married to an Academy Award nominated Marvel superhero actress Hailee Steinfeld.

 "I just try to be myself," Allen said when asked if there's a trick to being a successful commercial actor. "I just kinda wing it."

 

 

 It's a Wonderful life 

 Wonderful Pistachios had its pick of three days.

 Between Allen's commitments to his new marriage, newborn daughter, practices, workouts and other work ventures, he had only six to eight hours on one of three summer days to be in Los Angeles to film a quartet of TV spots, which are set to debut during Monday's game.

 As Allen points out in the ads, his family owns a pistachio farm, making the partnership with Wonderful as much a business endeavor as a pitchman job. But ask Wonderful's chief creative officer Bobby Pearce and executive creative director Steve Yee, and they'll tell you Allen's behavior on set hardly portrays that of someone viewing this relationship transactionally.

 "He wasn't the kind of athlete or celebrity who as soon as he's done with his shot he's running back to his trailer," Yee told ESPN. "He's hanging out with us and sitting amongst us at Video Village. He's just really cool and chill."

 "He's just curious," Pearce adds. "He wants to look at the process. He's like 'Did I do that right? Did I give you what you need?'"

 

 If anything, the Wonderful cohort points toward Allen being a little too friendly on set. He gets to know cast and crew. He banters. In Year 1 of their partnership, Allen and his co-star spent so much time laughing with each other that the producers had to ask them to settle down.

 It would be one thing if this experience was unique to Wonderful. But it really isn't.

 "It's almost like he became buds with people on set a little bit, people we've worked with. Which is kind of unusual," Bower said. "Athletes, or talents in general, tend to be quite cloistered and separated off. It makes sense why that would be the case. But in the small moments between takes [Allen] seemed to be joking around and being friendly with regular people that were on set."

 "People will ask me after they know what I do 'Is this person really as nice as they seem on television?'" adds Rebekah Lyle, chief marketing officer for Vytalogy Wellness, parent company for Natrol. "I think Josh is one of those individuals where I'm always proud to say 'yes.' I think the person you imagine of who he would be is really genuinely who you get to interact with when you're with him on set."

 

 Allen's backstory says it all 

 Allen's family doesn't own a Gatorade bottling plant, so that partnership trades a little bit more in Allen's status as a football star. To Bower, Allen's origin story of emailing more than 1,000 college coaches and coordinators seeking a scholarship but received only two offers was his everyman hook before ending up at Wyoming.

 The campaign didn't traffic in mythological boasts about Allen's arm strength. Gatorade bet on Allen's persistence resonating with viewers who also believe greatness lies within them.

 

 Natrol went the other way. It identified Allen as a busy husband and father with a hectic life who prioritizes sleep and wellness, a superstar avatar for the workday public.

 And while Wonderful had no problem leaning into the farmer image, it also values him as a celebrity who it believes transcends sports. Pearce jokes that Wonderful founder Stewart Resnick knows only two athletes by name: Allen and LeBron James.

 Commercial shoots are hectic. Allen's most recent Wonderful shoot was interrupted first by a Bills superfan attempting to sneak onto set by posing as an ESPN reporter (his comically large collection of Bills hats and pins gave him away) and later by a police lockdown nearby that sealed off the 2-mile radius outside the studio and made it impossible for production assistants to go out on coffee runs.

 Amid all that, Allen played. Pearce swears by his theory that Allen took acting lessons between Year 1 and Year 2 of working with Wonderful. (He didn't, but he says his wife helped him out.) In one of the soon-to-be-released ads, Allen didn't know he would have to react to a surprise reveal of a blocking dummy wearing a jockstrap. Per Pearce, Allen's improvised reaction made it to the final edit.

 According to the Forbes list of the world's highest paid athletes in 2026, only Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes makes more money in off-field earnings ($28 million) than Allen does ($17.5 million) among NFL players. Per the Forbes report, no other NFL player made more than $5 million in off-field earnings. When factoring out international soccer stars and athletes who compete in individual sports like golf and tennis, Allen ranks as the 10th-highest paid athlete by off-field earnings in major American team sports.

 

 Factor in Allen's $55.1 million salary and Forbes has him ranked 22nd in the world for 2026, right between Ravens QB Lamar Jackson and YouTube star turned boxer Jake Paul.

 Based on internal research shared with ESPN, the ads are effective. Wonderful commissioned a third-party survey of 2,647 participants to evaluate the commercials. Two-thirds of participants rated Allen as a good fit for the brand and 41% of viewers said the ads made them more likely to purchase Wonderful Pistachios.

 Then there's the effect Allen had on the folks he worked with. Yee keeps a bobblehead of Allen riding a tractor in his office and a framed photo of Allen with the cast and crew on his desk.

 "What comes across for me with Josh is he looks like he's having fun," Yee says, trying to sum up why he's proud of the ads. "I think he is. That's a difference. A lot of times when a camera turns on, people freeze up. He's cool as a…
